body:
Closes #24.

The server could add a workspace but not remove one, so an agent that set a worktree up had to hand the teardown back to the user in the app. `remove-workspace` is the Project screen's `Remove` action reached over MCP.

## The tool

`path` to a workspace, plus all three of `GitService::removeWorktree()`'s flags — `force_delete_worktree`, `delete_branch`, `force_delete_branch`.

**Every flag is stated on every call.** An unstated flag read as false decides a destruction the agent never answered either way, and it is `remove-project`'s existing shape for the same reason. Two refusals enforce it:

- leaving any flag out — `The delete branch field is required.`
- `force_delete_branch` beside `delete_branch: false` — `force_delete_branch requires delete_branch to be true.`, rather than the silent drop git would give that pairing

## Which gate it sits behind

`RegistersWhenWritable` + `#[IsDestructive]`, **not** `IsShellCommandExecutionTool`.

The line that trait draws is *whose* command runs. The four tools behind it run something the user authored — a workflow's steps, a configured launch command. This spawns a fixed `git worktree remove`, exactly as `add-workspace` spawns a fixed `git worktree add`, and `remove-project` already removes *every* worktree of a project from behind the write gate alone. Gating the narrower tool harder would have been incoherent, and would have meant a fifth `McpActionPendingApprovalType` plus a new arm in the approval modal's `rawData()`, which renders a workflow file or a launch command — a removal is neither. The client-side destructive annotation is what asks the user, and `remove-workspace` joins the `#[Instructions]` confirm-list beside `remove-project`.

## Which workspaces it will take

The Project screen hides `Remove` for the primary workspace and for `ready`, `working` and `pending`. That rule moves into `WorkspaceStatus::allowsRemoval()` and is now read by both the page's `->hidden()` and the tool, so a tool call cannot reach past a button the app hides — the same shape as `allowsWorkflowRequiring()` for runs. `is_primary` stays checked beside it by each caller, not being a status concern.

The refusal is split three ways because the routes out differ:

| refused | told |
| --- | --- |
| primary | it is the project's own directory — no route |
| `ready` | call `override-workspace-status` to suspend it first |
| `pending` / `working` | wait for the run to finish |

Naming the override tool in that last case would send the agent to a second refusal, since `override-workspace-status` declines an in-flight workspace too.

Dirtiness is left to git. Our `git_status` is computed separately from git's own removal check, which also counts untracked files and submodule state, so a pre-check could disagree with it in both directions. Git's stderr surfaces through `GitOperationFailed`, and `force_delete_worktree` is what lifts its `--force` rule.

Nothing outside the git worktree records a workspace — `projects.yaml` keeps no list, and per-workspace state lives in `.laborforest/ignored/` inside the worktree — so a removal leaves nothing to clean up.

## Incidental

Two things outside the issue's literal scope, both small. `path` is validated `required|string` — without it a call omitting `path` was a `TypeError` rather than an MCP error. And `tests/Feature/ProjectPageTest.php` gains cases pinning `primary`, `working`, `pending`, `error` and `unknown`: the existing pair covered only `ready` and `suspended`, which would have left the `->hidden()` rewrite unguarded.

## Docs

`docs/mcp.md` gains the table row and a removal section, and three stale counts are corrected (`fourteen` → fifteen, `leaves ten` → eleven, `the twelve that change something` → thirteen). `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are updated together and verified byte-identical.

## Testing

16 new cases across `tests/Feature/LaborForestServerTest.php` and `tests/Feature/ProjectPageTest.php`, covering both registration gates, each flag reaching git, all five refusals, and the statuses the Project page offers the action for. The `ProjectPageTest` additions pin `primary`/`working`/`pending`/`error`/`unknown` — the existing pair only covered `ready` and `suspended`, which would have left the `->hidden()` rewrite unguarded.

`composer test` — **970 passed**, and `vendor/bin/pint --dirty` clean. Fork PRs land as `action_required` until a maintainer approves the workflow run, so that local run is the only evidence this branch is green until you do.

author: rzaman8677
body:
## Summary

Implements `backend/core/knowledge_retriever.py` per Phase 2 Task 3 in `docs/PHASE1_SUMMARY.md`, providing the real context that `AgentWorkflow._retrieve_knowledge` currently stubs out as:

```python
{"relevant_docs": [], "similar_tickets": [], "faq_items": []}
```

`KnowledgeRetriever` exposes three methods that map onto those three keys:

- **`search_knowledge_base(query, top_k=5)`** -> candidates for `relevant_docs`. Returns `{"title", "content", "source", "score"}` dicts, ranked by score descending, capped at `top_k`.
- **`get_similar_tickets(ticket, candidate_tickets=None, top_k=5)`** -> candidates for `similar_tickets`. Since there's no ticket store/DB yet, this never queries anything on its own: `candidate_tickets=None` (or empty) returns `[]`. When candidates are supplied, similarity is a simple heuristic — subject/description keyword Jaccard overlap plus a bonus for sharing the same classification category — returning `{"ticket_id", "similarity_score", "subject"}` dicts, ranked.
- **`retrieve_for_classification(category, top_k=5)`** -> candidates for `faq_items`. Accepts a `ClassificationCategory` (reused from `backend/core/ticket_processor.py`, not redefined) or its raw string value.

This PR intentionally does **not** touch `agent_workflow.py` — wiring `KnowledgeRetriever` into `_retrieve_knowledge` is left to a separate PR, per the task instructions.

## MCP-optional design

Phase 2 Task 2 (`backend/integrations/mcp_layer.py`, an `MCPRegistry`/`execute_plugin` system) is being built in parallel and doesn't exist in this branch yet. `KnowledgeRetriever` never imports that module directly — it only accepts an already-constructed `mcp_registry` object in its constructor:

- If `mcp_registry` is provided, `search_knowledge_base` and `retrieve_for_classification` call `mcp_registry.execute_plugin("knowledge_base", {...})` and normalize whatever shape comes back (list of dicts, or a dict with a `results`/`documents`/`items`/`data` key) into this module's documented shape.
- If `mcp_registry` is `None`, or the call fails for *any* reason (missing method, missing module, plugin exception) it falls back to a local, dependency-free implementation — guarded with `try/except (ImportError, AttributeError)` plus a broad `Exception` safety net so a half-finished or flaky MCP layer can never crash retrieval:
  - `search_knowledge_base` falls back to simple keyword-overlap search over documents supplied via `load_documents()` — no ML/embedding dependency, clearly documented as a fallback, not the production search path.
  - `retrieve_for_classification` falls back to a small built-in FAQ dict keyed by `ClassificationCategory`, with every item tagged `"source": "builtin_fallback"` so it's never mistaken for real KB content.
  - `get_similar_tickets` doesn't call MCP at all (no ticket-similarity plugin contract exists) and always uses the local heuristic described above.

Net effect: this class is genuinely useful standalone today (zero external services, zero network calls anywhere in it), and will start returning real knowledge-base results automatically the moment a caller constructs an `MCPRegistry` and passes it in here — no changes needed in this file, and no required merge order relative to the MCP layer PR.

Also included, per the Phase 2 spec's "caching for frequently accessed docs" and "ranking and filtering" requirements:
- A small bounded in-memory LRU cache (`_cache`, capped via `cache_size`, oldest evicted) keyed by `(query, top_k)` for `search_knowledge_base`.
- Results from every method are sorted by score/relevance descending before truncating to `top_k`.

## Testing

Added `tests/core/test_knowledge_retriever.py` (23 tests, all passing) covering:
- Local fallback search returns ranked, relevant results for loaded documents, respects `top_k`, and handles empty query/no documents.
- `mcp_registry=None` end-to-end with no errors.
- A mocked `mcp_registry` (`Mock()` with `execute_plugin` configured) is called with the expected payload and its output (list or dict shape) is normalized correctly.
- A missing `execute_plugin` method (`AttributeError`) and a raising plugin (arbitrary `Exception`) both fall back cleanly instead of crashing.
- `get_similar_tickets` returns `[]` with no candidates, excludes the ticket itself, and ranks supplied candidates sensibly.
- `retrieve_for_classification` returns builtin items tagged `"source": "builtin_fallback"`, accepts both enum and string categories, and uses the MCP path when available.
- Cache behavior: repeated identical calls store once (`len(retriever._cache) == 1`), different queries cache separately, the underlying local search is invoked only once for two identical calls, and the cache is bounded/evicts.

```
$ python -m py_compile backend/core/knowledge_retriever.py
$ python -m pytest tests/core/test_knowledge_retriever.py -v
======================== 23 passed in 0.03s ========================
```

(Note: this repo's `requirements.txt` pins a legacy `logging==0.5.1.2` package that isn't installable on Python 3.9/3.10+ and isn't actually needed — `backend/core/knowledge_retriever.py` only uses the stdlib `logging` module. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change, left untouched here.)

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m py_compile backend/core/knowledge_retriever.py`
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/core/test_knowledge_retriever.py -v` (23 passed)
- [x] No real network calls anywhere in the new module or its tests

author: thezupzup
body:
Closes #442.

## Goal

Turn Linthra's existing offline Flatpak design into a regression-tested guarantee: after `flatpak-builder` fetches the manifest-declared sources, the actual build must succeed without downloading anything else, and without being able to hide behind a developer cache, a previous module build, or a host build tree.

The packaging already had most of the right pieces. This PR audits those pieces and makes future drift fail CI rather than changing runtime behavior.

## Automatic guard

Adds `test/tooling/flatpak_offline_build_test.dart`, which runs in the normal Flutter test suite and performs static/offline validation only (no subprocess execution). It checks that:

**Dependency resolution**
- the authoritative template keeps `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` and builds with `--no-pub`;
- the generated `linthra` module runs `setup-flutter.sh` **before** `flutter build ... --no-pub`;
- the generated Flutter setup script resolves dependencies with `flutter pub get --offline`;
- every hosted package/version in `pubspec.lock` has exactly one generated pub-cache archive, and its SHA-256 equals that package's `description.sha256`;
- each hosted-hash entry is an `inline` source landing in `.pub-cache/hosted-hashes/pub.dev`, where `pub get --offline` reads it, with contents equal to the lockfile hash.

**Content addressing**
- every remote `archive` or `file` source carries its **own** valid SHA-256;
- every remote `git` source pins a full commit hash, so a mutable tag cannot be repointed upstream between the two phases;
- a later source's hash cannot accidentally satisfy an earlier source mapping;
- source mappings are recognised whatever order their keys appear in, and a trailing comment cannot hide a key's value.

**Native inputs that CMake would otherwise fetch**
- the SQLite archive URL and hash are read from the committed `sqlite3_flutter_libs` CMake patch, and that exact archive must be staged in FetchContent's own download directory (`build/linux/<arch>/release/_deps/sqlite3-subbuild/sqlite3-populate-prefix/src`);
- the same destination rule applies to media_kit's mimalloc input;
- coverage is required for every architecture the **Flutter SDK module** declares, currently `x86_64` and `aarch64`, so dropping both architectures' entries together cannot shrink the requirement;
- the `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<NAME>` seam and `MIMALLOC_USE_STATIC_LIBS OFF` remain in CMake.

**Build-time network**
- a network grant appears only in the top-level runtime `finish-args`, never in build options for the app or a generated module, in either the joined (`--share=network`) or split (`--share`, then `network`) form that Flatpak's GLib option parser accepts.

**Nothing audited is an orphan**
- the generated files under audit are the ones the `linthra` module actually includes, so a lingering generated file cannot pass for a staged one.

**It fails closed**
- YAML flow style, anchors and aliases are rejected outright rather than skipped, because the line-oriented checks above cannot interpret them. An unreadable manifest fails instead of silently passing.

This keeps `pubspec.lock` and the generated manifest authoritative instead of maintaining a second hand-written list.

## End-to-end smoke

Adds:

```bash
bash scripts/flatpak_offline_build_smoke.sh
```

The script splits validation into two phases against the generated manifest:

1. `flatpak-builder --download-only` fetches only declared sources into its source cache;
2. the output build directory is removed and a full build runs with **both** `--disable-cache` and `--disable-download`.

`--disable-cache` forces every module build command to execute again instead of restoring a previous module result. The source cache populated by phase 1 remains available. `--disable-download` then requires those declared sources to be sufficient for the uncached rebuild.

The app module stages the checkout with `type: dir, path: ..` and no skip list, so a host `build/`, `.dart_tool/` or `.pub-cache/` tree would reach the sandbox as **source**, which neither phase 2 flag stops. The script therefore refuses to start when any of those sit at the repository root, naming them and printing the exact `rm -rf`. It deletes nothing itself.

A hidden `pub get`, CMake `FetchContent`, curl/wget, or other undeclared fetch therefore cannot be masked by module-cache reuse, by a host build tree, or by Linthra's runtime `--share=network` permission.

## Documentation

Adds `docs/flatpak-offline-build.md` with the source-fetch/build boundary, hash and destination rules, SQLite/mimalloc handling, the clean-source-tree requirement, the regeneration flow, and clean-cache release/Flathub validation.

## Scope

The final PR changes only:

- `docs/flatpak-offline-build.md`
- `scripts/flatpak_offline_build_smoke.sh`
- `test/tooling/flatpak_offline_build_test.dart`

No runtime permission, Android behavior, provider code, generated manifest, dependency version, or production application code is changed.

**Still requires a Linux machine for the final real Flatpak smoke:** this execution environment has neither `flatpak` nor `flatpak-builder` nor the runtimes needed for the complete `download-only` -> `disable-cache + disable-download` build. Everything above is static and unit-level validation. Note the smoke will now refuse to run until `build/`, `.dart_tool/` and `.pub-cache/` are cleared from the repository root.

author: ciresnave-bot
body:
Item 2 of the agreed order, in its own PR so the correction has its own record.
Independent of #36/#37/#38 — based on `main`, no shared files.

## This is not a stale number

ROADMAP quoted `30 files total = 14 REBUILT`. **Every one of those file numbers
is correct.** Re-measured: 14 rebuild, 5 are unreadable, and the `1 SPM + 13 BPE`
breakdown matches exactly.

It is the **right number of the wrong construct** — a different failure from
staleness, and it deserves different words.

## Six files, one vocabulary

Six of the thirty are one SmolLM2 vocabulary at six quantizations. A
quantization changes the weights and leaves `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` untouched, so
those six exercise the tokenizer path **once**. Adding quantizations grows "30"
without growing coverage at all.

```
30 files / 17 vocabularies      (8 files duplicate a vocabulary already present)
14 of 30 files rebuild  ->  but only 9 of 17 VOCABULARIES
```

## The equivalence relation, stated

Two files are the same vocabulary **iff their `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` arrays are
identical — same length, same ordered contents.** Not tokens+merges, not
tokens+special-tokens; those give different totals on these same files. A count
whose relation is unstated is a number, not a measurement.

**And the relation is doing work — here is the control:** `starcoder` and SmolLM2
both have exactly **49152** tokens and **different** digests. A census keyed on
vocabulary *size* would have merged them and reported 16.

## Two vocabularies split, and the first assertion was wrong to forbid it

```
151936   qwen2 (pre=qwen2) rebuilds          qwen35 (pre=qwen35) refused
 32000   TinyLlama Q4_0 (llama, no pre) rebuilds
         llama-spm (llama, pre=default)      refused
```

The census originally asserted this **could not happen**, and failed on its first
run. **The assertion was wrong, not the corpus.** Support is keyed on the *rule*,
deliberately — the same reasoning that refuses `qwen35` despite it differing from
`qwen2` on 0 of 130 cases.

So *"this vocabulary is supported"* is ill-formed. The invariant kept instead:
every split must be **explained** by a differing `model`/`pre`, and a split where
two files share a rule and disagree anyway still fails — that would be identical
inputs producing different outcomes.

## Measured, previously inferred from size

`qwen2` ≡ `qwen35` and `gpt-neox` ≡ `mpt` carry byte-identical token lists. The
argument for refusing them is unchanged — vocabulary identity does not imply rule
identity — but its premise is now measured rather than assumed.

## Three corrections to my own reporting

Recorded because **two of them flattered the point I was making**:

1. I said the corpus was **29 files**. It is **30** at `C:\Models`; 29 was the
   `gguf-corpus` subdirectory. The count was right for a root I had not stated —
   and I nearly filed *"30 is wrong"* as a correction. It was not.
2. I said *"9 SmolLM2 quantizations = 1 vocabulary"*, read off filenames. It is
   **six**, plus three that fail to parse entirely (`unknown tensor dtype`). The
   inferred version was the one that agreed with the caveat I was answering.
3. The split-groups assertion above.

## The instrument

`tests/gguf_corpus_vocab_census.rs`, `#[ignore]`d behind `LIGHTBULB_GGUF_CORPUS`.
It asserts a non-empty corpus, and that a file with an **unreadable** vocabulary
is **not** counted as a vocabulary — the direction that would otherwise flatter
the number.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01JtTf3315ahKPPyBiYugnPh

## Summary by Sourcery

Correct the roadmap’s tokenizer corpus measurement by reporting vocabulary coverage separately from file counts and adding an executable census to enforce the distinction.

Enhancements:
- Document GGUF tokenizer corpus coverage by distinguishing file counts from distinct vocabularies and measuring vocabulary identity by ordered token-list contents.
- Clarify that tokenizer rebuild support is rule-dependent, allowing vocabulary groups to split when their model or pre-tokenizer rules differ while detecting unexplained inconsistent outcomes.

Documentation:
- Update the roadmap with measured corpus coverage, duplicate-vocabulary counts, rebuild coverage, vocabulary equivalence criteria, and rule-based split behavior.

Tests:
- Add an ignored, opt-in GGUF corpus census that reports readable and unreadable files, groups files by vocabulary, measures rebuild coverage, and asserts that split outcomes are explained by differing tokenizer rules.

author: elie222
body:
## Why Fixes #499: cancelling a run (or archiving a group) was marking the run cancelled and releasing leases, but orphaned Chromium/shell work in the computer sandbox could keep running. Box cancel also had cross-process fencing races that could either skip teardown or kill a newer run's browser. ## What changed - Scope background launch markers by `computerId-runId-launchId` and cancel matching run work before screen release. - Keep the execution lease until cancel teardown finishes; pass `screenLeaseId` into `releaseScreen`. - Supervisor kills primary Chromium only when a screen index was actually released. - Box: publish a remote screen lease with flock + monotonic fence; cancel stops browsers only when the cancel lease still owns the fence (atomic check/stop/clear). Claim fails closed if lease publish fails. Local release no longer bypasses a newer remote fence. - E2B/Daytona/Box: cancel primary browser work; portable kill matches browser **argv0**, not cmdline substrings (avoids killing `node --engine=chromium`). - Group archive returns execution run/fence metadata and cancels run work before screen release. ## How tested - `pnpm exec vitest run --root . packages/adapters/src/box-sandbox.test.ts packages/adapters/src/computer-idle.test.ts` (33 passed) - CI on the PR (will re-run on this push) No UI changes; no issue comments.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Stopping a computer-backed run now also cancels its associated background work. * Releasing a primary screen during cancellation now stops the related browser process without affecting the desktop session. * Background tasks are isolated by run, preventing cancellation from affecting work belonging to other runs. * Cancellation behavior now works consistently across supported sandbox environments. * Screen ownership checks help prevent an earlier run from stopping a replacement run’s browser session. * Stale screen leases no longer clear or stop active replacement sessions.

## ぎふやDM：リクエストDMがアプリに出ない
`dm_notify` の会話取得が primary 受信箱のみだった。Instagramの**メッセージリクエストは別フォルダ扱い**のため、`folder=requests/pending/page` も試して会話IDでマージするよう変更（未対応folderはエラーを握りつぶし、取れた分だけ使う）。取得内訳もログ出力。
※IG APIの仕様上、相手に一度も返信していないリクエストはポーリングで出ないことがあります。その場合はInstagramアプリでリクエストを承認すると通常会話として次巡回で一覧に載ります（diagで会話数を確認できます）。

## 三条「おすすめ3」に直近と同じ品が出る
根本原因：予約投稿(GAS)が**品名を保存しておらず**、`schedList_` がキャプションの先頭行（三条フィードは毎回同じ挨拶「こんにちは」）を `name` として返していた。そのためアプリの重複除外(`recentNames`→品名フィルタ)が一切効かず、直近投稿と同じ品がおすすめに再出現していた。
修正：予約投稿シートに**M列（品名）**を追加保存し、`schedList_` はM列を正として返す（旧行は従来のフォールバック）。列A〜Lは投稿エンジン(`post_reservations`)と互換のまま＝投稿処理に影響なし。以降の予約から重複除外が正しく効きます。

body:
## 問題

`requestLink` 與 `adminCreateOrganizerCandidate` 都是**先寫入再寄信**，中間沒有 try/catch。寄信一失敗，寫入留著、稽核那一行跳過、呼叫端拿到 500。

實測（本機 D1 直接讀）：

```
organizer_event_candidates: id=bab940a3-…  tentative_name="test"  status="draft"
login_tokens:              navie434@…  audience=organizer   ← 已鑄出
preview_mail_sink:         邀請信沒寄出
audit_log:                 沒有 organizer_event.created
```

三個後果：

- **孤兒候選活動。** 沒有 `organizer_event.created` 稽核列，事後查不出是誰建的。畫面說失敗，管理者重試會再建一筆同名候選——`tentative_name` 沒有唯一限制。
- **登入額度被燒掉。** token 已落地卻沒有人拿得到，而它算進 `countLoginTokensSince("email", …)`，所以寄信中斷會把地址鎖在自己的登入之外。
- **preview／本機的收件人名單是固定的**，名單外的地址是被拒絕的輸入，不是伺服器故障，但 mailer 的 throw 讓它長得像故障（`functions/_portal.ts:327` → `guard()` → 500「伺服器發生錯誤。」）。

## 改法

新增選用相依 `mailRecipientAllowed`，在**任何寫入之前**問「這個環境寄得到這個地址嗎」。

只有 `PREVIEW_MAIL_SINK=d1` 的環境提供它。**production 維持 undefined**——它的 mailer 接受任何地址，沒有東西可答，而且 `requestLink` 對所有地址回同一個 202 的反列舉設計（`circle-portal-handlers.ts` 的 `// Always the same answer: an attacker must not learn which inboxes exist.`）必須原封不動。新的 400 在 production 到不了，這由型別與 wiring 保證，不是靠約定。

- **建立活動**：名單外的地址在候選活動存在之前就回 400，什麼都沒寫。
- **索取登入連結**：同上，不鑄 token，額度不受影響。
- **`organizer_event.created` 移到寄信之前**，因為候選活動在那個時間點確實已經建立。寄信失敗改記 `organizer_event.invitation_failed`，**活動保留**，回應帶 `invitationSent: false`。

  活動保留是刻意的：Mailgun 一次抖動不該讓主辦把已經填好的東西丟掉，而「回報整批失敗」正是造成重複建立的原因。
- **登入連結寄失敗時刪掉該 token**，讓它不再佔用額度。

## 介面提示

就是那個 400 的訊息本身，沒有另外加橫幅、徽章或常駐提示——它只在使用者撞到的那一步出現，而且會改變他接下來的動作：

```
這個測試環境不會寄信到這個地址。
```

**不列出可用地址。** `PREVIEW_TEST_RECIPIENTS` 是公開的，但 `PREVIEW_SANDBOX_RECIPIENTS` 是 secret，裝的是真實個人信箱；列名單會把它漏出去。要怎麼加地址寫在 runbook，不寫進畫面。

寄信失敗那條走既有的 notice：`活動已建立，但邀請信沒有寄到 <address>。`

## 驗證

本機實跑原始情境（`/organizer` 建立活動、負責人填 Gmail）：

```
建立活動     -> 400 {"error":"這個測試環境不會寄信到這個地址。"}
索取登入連結 -> 400 {"error":"這個測試環境不會寄信到這個地址。"}

candidates                    0 -> 0
login_tokens (該地址)          0 筆
```

瀏覽器實開也確認畫面顯示的是那句話，不再是「伺服器發生錯誤。」

新增 4 個測試：名單外的地址不鑄 token／不建活動、寄信失敗後 token 被回收且額度可再用、活動在邀請失敗後仍在且稽核有 `organizer_event.created` + `organizer_event.invitation_failed`。既有那條「不論信箱存不存在都回同樣的 202」的測試未改動且仍然通過。

Gate：`npm test` **577 pass / 0 fail**、`npx eslint .`、`npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` 全綠。

## 與 #183 的關係

獨立，可各自合併。[#183](https://github.com/dekkmarsvin/tw_doujin_event/pull/183) 讓本機有第二個 `.test` 地址；本 PR 處理寄不出去時的行為。兩者都由 [#171](https://github.com/dekkmarsvin/tw_doujin_event/issues/171) 的實測帶出來。

author: importcpp
body:
## What does this PR do?

`agent_task_queue.result` stored the entire `/complete` request struct, marshalled verbatim, while every reader parsed it back through a different three-field type. The two definitions only overlapped on `output` — the one field anyone actually read — so the drift was latent rather than actively broken. But the same blob carried `session_id` and absolute `work_dir` paths straight out to every UI caller, and `autopilot_run.result` inherited a verbatim copy of it.

This PR makes a single versioned envelope, `CompletionResultV1{version, summary, artifact_ids}`, the only persisted shape, with a strict parser at the write boundary and a tolerant adapter on the read path. Transport-only fields stay in their own columns and top-level API fields instead of riding along inside the result blob.

There is no behavior change for the three existing consumers (the fallback comment, the chat outcome, and quick-create): they produce equivalent results under both legacy and v1 input, which is the core acceptance criterion here.

## Related Issue

No GitHub issue — this is internal refactoring work tracked as CODI-11 in our Multica workspace. The repository issue templates target user-facing bug reports and feature requests, which do not fit this change.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Refactor / code improvement (no behavior change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] CI / infrastructure

## Changes Made

- `server/pkg/protocol/completion.go` (new): defines `CompletionResultV1` and both boundary functions. `ParseCompletionResult` is deliberately unforgiving once a payload declares a version — malformed JSON, an unknown version, a missing summary, or a bad artifact id is a 400, never a quiet fall back to legacy. A payload carrying no envelope at all reports `ErrLegacyCompletionResult` so the caller normalizes from `output`.
- `ReadStoredResult` is the tolerant half: an unparseable stored row degrades to `null` rather than being re-read under legacy rules or echoed back as a raw blob. Historical legacy rows normalize through the same lifting path.
- `summary` must be present but may be the empty string. A tool-only chat turn is a legal silent completion, and collapsing "absent" into "empty" would hide producer bugs. An explicit JSON `null` is rejected, because unmarshalling it into a Go string is a silent no-op.
- `artifact_ids` normalizes missing, `null`, and `[]` to a non-nil slice. Bad elements are rejected rather than sanitized, since editing an identifier changes which object it names.
- `server/internal/daemon/client.go`: the daemon builds `result.summary` and the compatibility `output` field from one string through a single constructor, so the dual write cannot diverge. The server still validates that the two agree, to catch a forged producer.
- `server/internal/handler/daemon.go`, `handler/agent.go`, `handler/autopilot.go`, `service/task.go`: read paths moved onto the shared adapter. `ContextExhaustedCompletion` now reads the canonical summary, so v1 and legacy daemons classify an exhausted run identically.
- `packages/core/api/schemas.ts`, `types/agent.ts`, `types/autopilot.ts`: the frontend accepts both shapes through one union and normalizes to `CompletionResult`, degrading per field so a malformed result cannot take its task row down. Wires `parseWithFallback` into the task and autopilot read paths that were previously returning bare casts.
- `apps/mobile/data/schemas.ts`: mobile's `AgentTaskSchema` typed `result` as `z.unknown()`, which stopped satisfying `z.ZodType<AgentTask>` once the shared type narrowed. It now mirrors the same two-branch normalization. Mobile takes only types and pure functions from `packages/core`, so the schema is copied rather than imported, with a comment pointing at the core original.
- Drops the dead `pr_url` field, which no daemon ever sent and no server ever consumed. Note that the `pr_url` in `server/internal/service/builtin_skills_test.go:237` is an unrelated issue-metadata concern locked by MUL-5442; it shares only the name and is intentionally left alone.

A server predating this change ignores the unknown `result` key and consumes `output`, so no capability negotiation is required.

## How to Test

1. `(cd server && go test ./pkg/protocol/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/handler/...)`
2. `pnpm typecheck`
3. `pnpm test`
4. `pnpm exec turbo typecheck lint test --filter=@multica/mobile` (this is what mobile-verify runs; `packages/core/types/**` changes trigger it)

Suggested review order: `server/pkg/protocol/completion.go` for the contract, then the write boundary, then the read paths, then the frontend schema.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have run tests locally and they pass
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [ ] If this change affects the UI, I have included before/after screenshots
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes
- [ ] If I added a new runtime / coding tool / UI tab, I synced the change to **landing copy** and **relevant docs**
- [ ] If this PR touches Chinese product copy, I checked it against `conventions.zh.mdx`
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above
- [x] I will address all reviewer comments before requesting merge

Notes on the unchecked boxes: there is no UI change to screenshot — no component reads `task.result` directly, so what changed is the parsing contract rather than anything rendered. No new runtime, tool, or tab was added, and no Chinese product copy was touched.

## Risks

Two limitations worth stating plainly rather than leaving for a reviewer to find:

- `apps/desktop/src/main/runtime-config-loader.test.ts` does not run in my sandbox, because the Electron binary cannot be downloaded without network egress. I have not executed that file. It is unrelated to this change — my commits touch no `apps/desktop` files, and checking out the base commit `2e2974510` reproduces the identical error. CI has network access and will run it normally.
- `pnpm test` reports 9 pre-existing failures in `packages/core` across `workspace/mutations`, `projects/mutations`, `issues/mutations`, and `realtime/use-realtime-sync-ws-instance`. These are not caused by this PR: running the same suite on a clean checkout of `main` (`d4a712abf`) produces exactly the same 9 failures. Every CI check on this PR is green.

## AI Disclosure

**AI tool used:** Multica Agent, Claude Code

**Prompt / approach:** The change was produced by a Multica agent working the CODI-11 issue in our workspace, then reviewed across three rounds against an independent agent before implementation. The final rebase onto `main`, verification, and PR authoring were done with Claude Code. Verification was run rather than assumed; the two limitations above are reported as measured, including the suite I could not execute locally.

body:
### Description

In `whisper/whisper-streaming/packages/whisper_streaming/whisper_online.py`, `ASRBase.__init__` passes three arguments to `load_model`:

```python
# line 42
self.model = self.load_model(modelsize, cache_dir, model_dir)

# line 44 — the stub a new backend is meant to implement
def load_model(self, modelsize, cache_dir):
    raise NotImplementedError("must be implemented in the child class")
```

The stub only declares two. Both concrete backends in the file already take the third:

| line | definition |
|---|---|
| 44 | `ASRBase.load_model(self, modelsize, cache_dir)` ← the odd one out |
| 61 | `WhisperTimestampedASR.load_model(self, modelsize=None, cache_dir=None, model_dir=None)` |
| 107 | `FasterWhisperASR.load_model(self, modelsize=None, cache_dir=None, model_dir=None)` |

So the stub documents a contract the base class itself violates. A backend written against it — the stub is the only signature a subclass author sees — breaks in `ASRBase.__init__`:

```
TypeError: load_model() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given
```

Verified by rebuilding each `load_model` signature from the repo file with `ast` and replaying the `__init__` call through `inspect.Signature.bind`:

```
ASRBase                load_model(self, modelsize, cache_dir)                           -> TypeError: too many positional arguments
WhisperTimestampedASR  load_model(self, modelsize=None, cache_dir=None, model_dir=None) -> OK
FasterWhisperASR       load_model(self, modelsize=None, cache_dir=None, model_dir=None) -> OK
```

### Changes

One line: give the `ASRBase.load_model` stub the same signature as its two overrides. Nothing else in the file changes, and no existing backend is affected.

`ruff format --check` (v0.11.6, the pinned pre-commit version) reports the file already formatted, and `ruff check` yields identical findings before and after (two pre-existing `E741`).

body:
## What

Issue #15, pulled into v0.0.2: on every change, every supported Gatling release is started for real, runs the probe simulation, and the decoder is held to the report that run generated for itself and to the other runs. The recorded corpus proves the decoder against the past; this proves it against a Gatling that ran a minute ago.

- `.github/workflows/gatling-canary.yml`: reusable from `ci.yml` (job `canary`), startable by hand from the Actions tab with any version list, and weekly. JDK 17 + sbt with a cache, the stub, one sbt run per version, then the canary tests with `-count=1`; a run in which no test passed fails.
- `gatling/text/canary_test.go` (`//go:build canary`): per version, the header must name the version asked for; counts and mean rate must equal `js/global_stats.json` and `js/stats.json` exactly; runs must be identical as masked multisets; the list must cover both bounds of `SupportedVersions`, so widening the range without running it fails. A version above the range decodes unverified and is named in the job summary as a candidate — the range is never widened by a machine. Without `PARSEC_CANARY_RUNS` the tests skip with a reason.
- The report and cross-run checks moved to `helpers_test.go` under `integration || canary`; the corpus suite is unchanged.

## Evidence

Run locally end to end from the workflow's own steps — stub, Gatling 3.11.5 and 3.12.0 under sbt, then the canary tests: both versions matched their own report (36 requests, 18/18, 2 groups, 6/6 users, 6 errors, span 4 s) and were identical as a multiset (70 lines). Lint: 0 issues with every build tag. Coverage unchanged: `gatling` 100%, `gatling/text` 97.3%.

## For the reviewer

- Gatling 3.13.0 and later write the binary format (milestone v0.0.5); they are not on the default list — the "newest release" probe of #15 becomes meaningful when both codecs exist. Recorded in the spec's Assumptions and research R14.
- The constitution's gate table needs a `canary` row: an amendment for its own PR.
- Stacked on #25; rebase-merge only, `docs(speckit)` first.

Closes #15

body:
Yukon submission `4ded9637-38cf-4626-9f75-f13137c64c53` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-gemma4-26b-a4b-engine at `1e713b8cafe33bf4d7764d38e3ccb29599e13390`.

Current best score: 2.38577112847741. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5
Harness: Claude Code

# CONST-SCALAR-MEMO-001 -- the forward stops rebuilding its constant bfloat16 scalars through a conversion node on every call

**Base.** `1e713b8c` -- the current crown, submission `5eef22c4`, composite
**2.38577**. This branch is that commit plus one commit. One file
changes; nothing else in the tree is touched.

## THE MECHANISM

`MLXArray(Float, dtype: .bfloat16)` is **not** a host-side construction. The
mlx-swift initializer routes it to `init(bfloat16:)`, whose body is

```text
  let v_mlx = mlx_array_new_float(Float32(value))
  var v_bfloat = mlx_array_new()
  mlx_astype(&v_bfloat, v_mlx, DType.bfloat16.cmlxDtype, stream.ctx)
```

-- a real one-element conversion node that becomes its own dispatch when the
graph is evaluated. `Float.asMLXArray(dtype:)` reaches that same initializer,
and so does the `MLXArray * Float` operator, which is defined as
`lhs * rhs.asMLXArray(dtype: lhs.dtype)`.

Three scalars on the scored road are pure functions of the checkpoint config
and are rebuilt through that node on **every forward call**:

| site | scalar | reached |
|---|---|---|
| `Gemma4FusedScaledEmbedding.apply` -- the `embed_scale` kernel input | `embedScale` = `sqrt(hiddenSize)` | once per prefill call and once per decode step, at the top of the trunk |
| the token-PLE plane | `sqrt(hiddenSizePerLayerInput)` | same call, immediately after |
| `embedTokensForDrafter` | `sqrt(hiddenSize)` | the drafter's target-embedding input under the v1.1 speculative protocol |

This ticket memoizes them on `(bit pattern, dtype)` behind an explicit lock and
returns the evaluated array instead. **Deleted: one conversion node per scalar
per forward call.** Nothing is added -- no wider load, no wider store, no extra
arithmetic, no new kernel and no new road.

## WHY IT IS EXACT

The cached array is produced by calling **the incumbent's own**
`asMLXArray(dtype:)`, on the same `Float`, for the same dtype. It is therefore
bit-identical to the array the incumbent would have built on that call, and the
consuming `mlx_multiply` and custom-kernel dispatch see the same operand values
in the same positions.

The dtype is never chosen by this ticket. At the kernel site it is the literal
`.bfloat16` the incumbent already passed. At the two multiply sites it is
`lhs.dtype`, which is exactly what the `MLXArray * Float` operator itself
passes, so the conversion that happens is the conversion that happened before.

A cached entry is a read-only **input** and is never a mutated output, which is
why sharing one across graphs and across steps is safe. This is the same
argument the tree already relies on for
`CBv2ComposedPrefillSDPAV1.bfloat16LowestScalar`, its negative-zero twin, and
its two causal-mask tables.

No shape, stride, dispatch, grid, threadgroup, allocation or dtype changes.
**This ticket only deletes work.**

## THREAD SAFETY

The table is guarded by an explicit `NSLock`. The build runs with **no lock
held**, so a concurrent prompt pass is never stalled behind an evaluation, and
the insert re-checks the table: a pass that built the same scalar concurrently
keeps the first entry, which is the same value from the same operation either
way. The table is bounded -- dropped wholesale past `maxEntries` -- so an
unexpected scalar stream cannot grow it without limit.

## WHY THIS SITE CLASS AND NOT ANOTHER

The remaining per-call small-array constructions on this tree were swept and
most are already memoized or dark:

* `CBv2ComposedPrefillSDPAV1` -- its causal mask, its mask bias and its two
  bf16 constants are already built once; its softmax `paramsArray` was memoized
  by the incumbent crown.
* `CBv2AttentionV1.boolMask` and `spanMask` build index vectors per call, but
  they are reached only through the attention-softcap and vision-span paths,
  and this checkpoint declares `final_logit_softcapping` only -- no attention
  softcap, no image spans on this benchmark. Not shipped: they do not fire.
* `RaggedTwoPassDecodeAttentionV1`'s five `startArray` and three `paramsArray`
  sites are decode-side and depend on the live `starts` vector, so they are not
  invariant given their inputs. The one that is -- the all-zeros
  `startArray` -- is on the decode road where this technique already measured
  at zero on three ranked samples. Not shipped.
* `LogitsPipelineV2`, `SamplerV2` and `TokenConstraintSamplerV2` build larger
  per-call arrays, but the ranked geometry is greedy argmax and does not reach
  them. Not shipped.

What is left is the class above: a scalar that is constant for the life of the
process, rebuilt through a conversion **dispatch**, at the top of every forward.

## GATE

Three arms, one GPU hold, on this base:

* `ctl` -- the crown, built from unmodified sources in the same worktree
* `cand` -- this branch, switch at its default
* `k0` -- the same `cand` binary with `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_CONST_SCALAR_MEMO=0`

| check | result |
|---|---|
| **RCPTOK** warm decode receipts, 3 runs x 3 arms | **1 distinct** -- `ctl`, `cand` and `k0` all `fb2e31028fd7eb2b3724f97c677fca34` |
| **VECOK** decode probe-vector signature | **1 distinct** over cand / ctl / kill -- `795e0ff71d65c886` on all three |
| **TOKOK** prefill token plane | `cand=8f574624234b4505` `ctl=8f574624234b4505` -- **identical**, and this is the arm that matters here, because the largest of the three sites is reached once per prefill call |
| **MARKOK** engage-mark census | `cand` gains exactly `['const-scalar-memo']`, loses nothing; `kill == ctl`. The control census carries both `scaled-embedding` and `scaled-embedding-decode`, i.e. the memoized site is reached on the prompt plane AND on the decode cell |
| **SRCOK** metallib + kernel-source files | metallib `37013fcef2a24f99`, identical across arms; 0 kernel-source-bearing files changed vs tip; one file changed: `Gemma4Text.swift` |
| **R18FLOOR** paired timing draw | decode p50 `ctl=16.630` `cand=16.655` `kill=16.637` ms (`+0.15%`, with the kill arm between the two, i.e. the spread is the instrument). **Informational only** (doctrine R9): this dev part is not the scoring machine, the gate is the 0.90 decode floor, and this ticket's sites are weighted to the prompt plane, which this draw does not price |

Gate `CSM` PASS, 36m07s, one GPU hold, on tip `1e713b8c`.

`k0` is the strong form of the switch test: it is not a second build that ought
to behave like the base, it is the SAME binary as `cand` with one environment
variable set, and with the switch off every site calls the incumbent

Twenty-ninth drive-down PR, off master. The worst function under the shared pin — `parseWaitArgs` in `src/wait/args.ts` — and the shared max comes down from 25.30 to 25.08.

## What changed

- **`src/wait/args.ts`** — `parseWaitArgs` (cc 25, 92%) was one loop with every flag of `agendo wait` inline, the same shape `parseLaunchArgs` had before #94, and gets the same treatment. The options accumulate in a `WaitDraft`; `takeToken` handles one token (a toggle from a table, `--`, a value flag through a setter table, or a positional through `takePositional`, which is where a dashed non-flag is refused); `setScope` and `setDuration` are the two setters with a refusal of their own; `checkStates` is the tail check that `--state` / `--not` name a state and are not both given. `parseDuration`'s `switch` is a unit table, since the regex admits exactly those units and the `default` arm could never run. Same flags, same messages, same exit codes, same defaults.
- **`test/waitArgs.test.ts`** (8 tests) — `parseDuration` unit by unit; then every flag beside the next: the defaults, the toggles and ids with `--` escaping what follows, the value flags with an empty `--prefix` kept raw, `--repo`/`--path` refusing a missing or flag-shaped value, a bad duration naming the flag and what it got, the state checks and the both-given refusal, and a dashed token that is not a flag. author: 7sageer
body:
## Related Issue

No linked issue — found during an internal telemetry code audit.

## Problem

The default `kimi -p` path (v2 print runner) had two telemetry gaps:

1. It ignored the `KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` environment variable: `run-v2-print.ts` only consulted the `telemetry` config key, while the v1 print path and kap-server also honor the env var — three entry points, two behaviors.
2. Crash telemetry was silently lost: `main.ts` installs the process-wide crash handlers on the v1 default telemetry client, but the v2 print path never initializes that client, so no sink was ever attached. `crash` events sat in the in-memory queue and were dropped when the process exited. `system_metrics` coverage was missing for the same reason.

## What changed

- The v2 print runner now computes the telemetry switch with the shared `shouldEnableTelemetry` helper (config `telemetry` key **and** `KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`), exported from the `@moonshot-ai/kimi-telemetry` entry.
- When telemetry is enabled, the v2 print runner also initializes the v1 telemetry pipeline with the same parameters as `initializeCliTelemetry`, so the process-wide crash handlers and the system-metrics collector work in v2 print mode. `first_launch` is deliberately tracked only on the v2 side to avoid double-sending; crash phase transitions (`runtime` / `shutdown`) and the v1 pipeline shutdown during cleanup now mirror the v1 print path.
- Tests: the env-var case asserts neither the cloud appender nor the v1 pipeline is initialized; the default case asserts the v1 init parameters, session context sync, crash phases, and shutdown.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [ ] I have linked a related issue (external PRs: the issue must have a maintainer's `/approve`).

author: vjpixel
body:
## Problema (#7212)

`.claude/hooks/inject-session-id.mjs` injeta `--session-id` só em comando **standalone**. Comando **encadeado** (`&&`/`;`/`|`/multi-linha) que casa com um dos scripts-alvo (`session-registry.ts`, `overnight-session-marker.ts`, `resolve-{develop,overnight}-plan-path.ts`) simplesmente não recebia a flag e rodava sem ela — o subcomando falhava alto por dentro (`--session-id ausente`, exit 1), mas esse erro:

1. competia por atenção com a saída de outros comandos do mesmo bloco, ou
2. era engolido por completo quando o bloco redirecionava (`> /dev/null 2>&1`).

**Reprodução ao vivo, mesma rodada que despachou esta issue** (`/diaria-overnight 260902b`), duas ocorrências:

1. `npx tsx scripts/overnight-session-marker.ts --start 2>&1 | tail -3` — erro apareceu, mas truncado/perdido no meio da saída do `tail`.
2. `for i in 7175 7176 7177; do npx tsx scripts/lib/session-registry.ts unclaim-issue --kind overnight --issue $i > /dev/null 2>&1; echo "unclaim $i"; done` — as 3 chamadas falharam por completo em silêncio; a única saída visível foi a do `echo`, indistinguível de sucesso. As 3 issues ficaram reivindicadas por engano até serem refeitas standalone.

## Fix

`detectChainedSessionIdRisk(command)` (função pura nova) detecta exatamente esse caso — comando encadeado + alvo injetável + sem `--session-id` explícito — e o hook agora emite `PreToolUse` `deny` em vez de deixar a chamada passar sem a flag. Um `deny` é impossível de engolir com redirect — é o "grito" que a issue pede, em vez de deixar o subcomando gritar sozinho e torcer pra alguém ouvir.

`matchesInjectableTarget()` foi extraído de `needsSessionId()` pra reusar a lógica de casamento de alvo sem herdar o early-return de `isChainedCommand` — esse early-return existe pra decidir SE injeta (nunca em encadeado), não pra decidir SE bloqueia (agora sim, em encadeado).

**Não afrouxa `isChainedCommand`** — a detecção de encadeamento continua exatamente a mesma (#5751 item 18). O que muda é só a reação: antes "deixa passar sem a flag, silenciosamente"; agora "bloqueia, alto e cedo".

## Testes (#633)

`test/inject-session-id-hook.test.ts`:
- Novo `describe("detectChainedSessionIdRisk (#7212)")` com as duas reproduções REAIS da issue (`| tail -3` e o `for` loop com `> /dev/null 2>&1`) + casos negativos (standalone, já com `--session-id`, alvo não-injetável, `list-active`).
- 3 novos testes e2e via stdin real no harness (`spawnSync`) reproduzindo os dois incidentes e confirmando `deny`/`updatedInput: undefined`.
- 2 testes pré-existentes ("resolve-*-plan-path.ts encadeado → nenhum stdout emitido") tiveram a asserção atualizada pra refletir o novo comportamento (deny em vez de silêncio) — mudança de comportamento intencional, documentada no próprio teste.

`npx tsc --noEmit` limpo. `npx tsx --test test/inject-session-id-hook.test.ts test/lib-boundary.test.ts` → 81/81 passam. `scripts/which-set-guards.ts` não aponta nenhum guard de conjunto afetado.

## Preflight (#5327 item 3 / regra 14)

`gh pr list --state open --search "7212"` vazio, `git log origin/master --grep "#7212"` vazio, `check-issue-duplicate-preflight.ts --issue 7212` → `not-in-master`. Sem duplicidade.

## Self-review pendente

Hook pós-`gh pr create` de review multi-agente **não foi executado** por instrução explícita do dispatch — anotado aqui conforme regra 8 de `context/overnight-dispatch-rules.md`. Self-review manual (regra 7) feito, achados abaixo como comentários inline.

Closes #7212

body:
## Summary

Pressing "Done today" on a habit goal that had already ended (due Sep 2, pressed on Sep 3) created a check-in for today, which sits outside the goal window: the card kept saying `0 of 1 days` while the streak jumped to `1 day`.

Habit check-ins now apply to `habitCheckInDay(goal, now, tz)` = `min(today, last day of the goal window)`, used by both the `toggleHabitCheckIn` action and `goalProgress` (so `todayChecked` / streak are evaluated for the same day). Toggling also deletes any stray check-ins dated after that day, which cleans up the one the user already recorded.

`GoalProgress.ended` is new (`now >= windowEnd`); `habitButtonLabel(progress)` renders "Mark done (late)" / "Undo" for ended goals instead of "Done today" / "Undo today", and the streak text/tile is hidden once a goal has ended, since a streak only makes sense for a running goal.

Period goals (week/month/year) are unaffected — their window always contains today.

author: 0xbrsm
body:
## Summary

`trade_event(game, valuation_of, gate)` called every seat's `valuation` fresh at event time — one forward per seat per lane per turn, the one place HexNet's batched collector stopped batching (5.8x slower collection with trading on). That is not the trading design's §8 shape: seats publish at their own decisions, the event only reads.

- `hexset.trading.trade_event(game, gate)` drops `valuation_of` and reads `game.valuations` directly, already fixed for the whole event by the time it runs.
- `Game.publish(seat, vector)` is the one way to set a seat's vector: validates length and range (`hexset.trading.checked_valuation`, moved out of `hexset.server.webplay`'s own copy) and records nothing else. `Game.traders` is `Game.gates`, gate-only — publishing is a separate act, not something `trade_event` asks a seated object for.
- `hexset.trading.publish_valuation(game, seat, trader)` is the "ask, then publish" driver convenience: `hexset.arena.play`, `hexset.record.record_game`, `hexset.bench.aivat`'s replay (a line-for-line twin of `arena.play`, so it stays bit-identical), and `hexset.gym`'s auto-played opponents all call it right after the acting seat's own action. The server's embedded bots publish the same way from `hexset.server.api.act()`; a human seat is unaffected, still publishing only through `PUT .../valuation`.
- `hexset.onnx_record.CONTRACT_VERSION` → `"5"` (missed when `RECORD_FIELDS` changed in the one-event-trading PR; `RECORD_CONTRACTS` already only allowed `"5"`).

## Census split

Both fixtures re-baseline by construction, checked before writing the new ones:

| preset | result |
|---|---|
| `heximax` | changed |
| `heximax-omni` | changed |
| `heximax-notrade` | **byte-identical** |
| `search2` | changed |
| `search2-notrade` | **byte-identical** |

## Readouts (re-run, not reused)

**(iii) Strength** — `heximax` vs `search2`, 800 blocked, seed 42000, 26 workers: **485/800 = 60.6%** [57.2, 64.0], paired VP **+0.929** [+0.759, +1.100]. Bar (point ≥ 50%, Wilson lower > 45%) **met**.

**(v) Cost** — mirror table, 3 games/arm, seeds 0/1/2, one process: **1.57x** `search2` ms/move (ceiling 2x), 1.37x calls/move. Trades/turn over the lineup (iii) plays (`[heximax, heximax, search2, search2]`, blocked, 6 games): mean **0.127**, max 1, 450 events — same order as the pre-fix 0.151 reading, no runaway trading.

Both written to `docs/readouts/one-event-trading/publish-*.json`, README updated.

author: rodnrr
body:
Finding a shelter, pantry or clinic is only half the problem if the person cannot physically get there. Three commits: the transportation layer from the brief, then real bus-stop data on top of it, then three more county feeds.

## 1. "Get There" on every listing

`src/components/shared/GetThere.tsx` + `src/lib/transport.ts`, rendered in `ResourceSheet` (compact) and on `/resources/:id` (card).

Six tiles: 🚌 public transit · 🚶 walking · 🚲 bicycle · 🚗 driving hand the trip to Google Maps with the destination prefilled (Apple Maps as a secondary link on Apple devices); 🚕 ride assistance and ♿ accessible transport open the finder.

- **Replaces** the single "Directions" action that sat in `ResourceSheet`'s footer grid — driving is one of the four tiles, so nothing is lost.
- `canRouteTo()` reproduces the existing gate: a `confidential_address` or `phone_intake` listing gets **no** map links and **no** destination carried into the finder.
- No routing backend, deliberately — the map app has the live timetable.

## 2. `/transportation`

The transportation directory and the Ride Assistance Finder on one route. `?to=<resourceId>` prefills the destination; `?mode=wheelchair` preselects accessible transport. Added to the sitemap, the homepage grid, and the footer.

**Deliberately not a `CategoryPage`.** Transportation programmes are service-area-scoped rather than point-located: several have no coordinates, and `fetchCategoryResources()` requires `is_map_ready` plus non-null lat/lng. Routing this through `categories.ts` would hide exactly the listings the page exists to surface.

## 3. The matching engine

`src/lib/rideOptions.ts`. Five plain questions ranked against `ride:`-prefixed tags. Same discipline as `resourceFaq.ts`: **nothing is invented** (every reason is assembled from a stored field), **unknown means "maybe"** (a programme recording no area/mode/eligibility is never excluded on that basis), and **qualification is never asserted** — the strongest claim is "you may qualify", beside the published requirement. `ride:notice:enrollment` is load-bearing: someone who needs a ride in the next hour will not get it from a programme that certifies riders over three weeks.

**Privacy.** The eligibility step asks about income, disability, Medicaid and veteran status. Those answers live in React state for the visit and nowhere else: no Supabase write, no URL parameter, no persisted store. Per the brief, saving them is an opt-in on an account someone created, never a default.

## 4. Nearest bus stop, from four counties' static GTFS

The maintainer supplied published GTFS bundles for four agencies, so the layer now answers "can I get here on the bus?" — with no API key and no realtime feed, because a stop's location changes on service-change dates rather than by the minute.

| Migration | Agency | County | Stops | Routes | Feed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 042 | — | — | — | — | DDL only |
| 043 | HART | Hillsborough | 2,245 | 32 | `2608.1` → 2027-01-02 |
| 044 | MCAT | Manatee | 928 | 16 | `20260814` → 2027-06-04 |
| 045 | Miami-Dade Transit | Miami-Dade | 6,973 | 122 | derived → 2027-12-31 |
| 046 | GoPasco | Pasco | 945 | 14 | `20260828` → 2031-12-13 |

No PostGIS: the app scans a small bounding box and reuses `geo.ts` for exact distance, so there is only ever one distance implementation in play. `scripts/build-transit-sql.ts` turns a bundle into the migration, so provenance is reproducible and a feed refresh is a re-run rather than hand-editing.

### What the data shows

| | Hillsborough | Miami-Dade | Pasco | Manatee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Listings on live | 21 | 25 | 2 | **0** |
| Within 400 m of a stop | 11 | 23 | 0 | — |
| Flag wrong today | 11 | 5 | 0 | — |

All 21 Hillsborough listings say `public_transit_accessible = false` — including First Baptist Progress Village, **17 metres** from a stop on Route 8. The map renders that column as a "Near transit" facet, so the filter isn't empty, it's wrong, and it hides listings from the people filtering on it.

**Miami-Dade mostly confirms rather than corrects:** 18 of the 19 hand-set TRUE flags from migration 032 measure inside 400 m, most within 100. The one exception is 400.4 m and is left alone — none of this ever lowers a flag. Good result for hand-entered data.

**Pasco has no Sunday service at any of its 945 stops.** A Sunday meal service there cannot be reached by bus by anyone without a car, and the rows now say so.

**The negative is the valuable half.** Hillsborough's four parks are 7–11 miles from any stop; Pasco's two campgrounds are 1.5 and 3.8. It's computed at read time rather than stored, so it can't go stale against a feed that has moved on.

**Manatee loads stops nothing yet matches** — there are no public Manatee listings on live. Worth loading anyway: without it the app can't distinguish "no feed" from "no transit".

### Coverage is gated per county, not by distance

`AGENCY_BY_COUNTY` lists the four counties with a loaded feed. PSTA, LYNX and Broward County Transit are **not** loaded. Distance alone stopped being sufficient once Pasco landed: GoPasco borders Pinellas, so a Tarpon Springs listing can sit 2 km from a GoPasco stop while being served all day by PSTA — "nearest stop: GoPasco, 2 km" there is a partial answer dressed as a complete one.

So a county with no loaded feed renders nothing, and a city that doesn't resolve to a county gets *partial*: a genuinely walkable stop still shows (positive evidence), but the "nearest stop is 8 miles away" line is suppressed, because that one asserts an absence. `COUNTY_BY_CITY` was extended until all 40 distinct cities on live resolve.

Two further silences, both deliberate: an **expired feed** (`feed_valid_until`), and a **confidential-address or phone-intake listing** — naming the nearest cross street to a DV shelter would leak the location the rest of the panel is careful not to publish.

**The backfill only ever raises the flag.** No branch writes `FALSE`; each feed covers one county, so a FALSE would assert "no bus" about an address the feed was never meant to describe. `resources_updated_at` is disabled across the UPDATE (idiom from 037/040) so a derived-data backfill can't manufacture freshness a human never earned.

**One thing the app has never said:** HART's own `fare_attributes.txt` prices the **TECO Line Streetcar (800) and the airport SkyConnect at $0.00**. `is_fare_free` is set only from an explicit 0.00 — a NULL fare is unknown, not free. The other three feeds ship no usable fare data, so their routes land NULL.

### Importer changes each feed forced

- **GoPasco publishes no `calendar.txt` at all** — 1,657 explicit `calendar_dates` rows out to 2031, which the importer rejected outright. It now infers a day pattern from the dates a service actually runs over the next four weeks, but only for services `calendar.txt` is silent about. Where a weekly pattern exists it wins: HART adds its *Sunday* service on Labor Day, a Monday, and folding that in would mark Sunday-only stops as having weekday service.
- **Miami-Dade omits `feed_info.txt`** — both fields fall back: validity to the latest active calendar end date, version to a hash over the files describing the network (not `stop_times`, since a timetable tweak should update rows in place rather than look like a new feed). A NULL version would make the trailing `DELETE` a permanent no-op and stops would accumulate forever.

HART's generated SQL was verified byte-identical after these changes, so the first feed didn't regress.

### Two bugs found while building it

1. **Fixed:** HART right-aligns single-digit hours (`' 5:01:41'`), so an anchored `\d+` pattern rejected them and silently dropped every departure before 10am — making the first bus of the day look like a mid-morning one on *every* stop. Caught by cross-checking one stop against the raw file; the runbook carries a verify query that would catch a regression.
2. **Not fixed, logged:** several live listings share one rounded

author: romanize
body:
Stacked on #15 (AGX-17), which is stacked on #13 (AGX-16) and #12 (AGX-15). Base
this on `agx-17-claude-transcript-discovery`; review the AGX-18 commit only.

## What this resolves

AGX-17 shipped two deliberate under-claims and named this ticket as the fix.

- `awaiting-permission` was unreachable. A permission prompt and a running tool
  are byte-identical on disk — an assistant `tool_use` with no `tool_result`
  after it — so both read as `progressing`.
- `progressing` under-claimed `idle`, because a recent write proves something
  wrote recently, not that anything is running now.

Both need evidence a transcript cannot carry. Claude Code keeps it beside the
transcripts, in `<store>/sessions/<pid>.json`: the pid, the session, when it
registered, and what that session is doing right now. `waiting` is the provider
itself declaring a human is being waited on.

## The liveness rule, and why both halves are needed

Registry entries are never cleaned up, so a file long outlives its process. Pids
recycle, so a live pid is not the process the entry meant. Neither half is
evidence alone. An entry counts only if the pid is alive **and** the process
holding it started no later than the entry's own epoch `startedAt` — a recycled
pid was necessarily issued after the entry was written, and that is the only
thing separating them. The captured fixture shows the invariant: `startedAt`
lands 1669ms *after* the process it describes actually began.

An undatable pid is refused rather than assumed innocent: it is precisely the
pid a recycled one is indistinguishable from.

## Fixture provenance

`fixtures/claude-session-registry.json` is a real entry copied from
`~/.claude/sessions/71484.json` on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.259) while that
session was running. Only payloads were replaced: the cwd, the derived session
name, and the session id — swapped for the one the AGX-17 transcript fixtures
carry, so the two captures describe one session. Every key, type and value the
parser reads is as Claude Code wrote it.

The status vocabulary is captured too, from the binary rather than a file:
2.1.259 carries `var je=["busy","shell","idle","waiting"]` guarded by
`je.includes(e)?e:void 0`. That is both the set and the CLI's own handling of a
status it does not know, so an unrecognised status degrades here exactly as it
does there — the entry survives without a status rather than being thrown away
along with its pid and its dates. The same binary reduces its statuses as
`busy -> active, waiting -> blocked, everything else -> idle`, which is why a
live but `idle` or `shell` session is not reported as working.

Fixtures are now prettier-ignored. Reformatting a capture makes it a file this
repository wrote rather than one a provider did.

## Decisions worth scrutinising

**`waiting` promotes only a `progressing` transcript.** It is the provider's
word for blocked on a human and covers being asked a question as much as being
asked for permission — its `waitingFor` field is free-form display text ("input
needed", "dialog open"), typed as nothing more than a string, so it cannot
narrow the two. The promotion is therefore confined to the one reading the
transcript genuinely cannot make. A transcript that already says a turn ended
keeps `awaiting-input`, rather than spending the loudest state in the product on
a session merely waiting to be spoken to.

**The platform split is not a preference.** The deployment image is
`node:24-bookworm-slim`, which ships no `ps` at all (verified in that exact
image). A `ps`-based probe would return `null` for every pid in production while
passing every test on a developer's Mac — status derivation silently disabled
exactly where it runs. Linux reads `/proc`, part of the kernel and needing no
package; macOS, which has no `/proc` and which Node cannot `sysctl`, spawns `ps`
as argv with no shell. Both branches are covered by a suite that probes its own
process, and both were run: macOS locally and Linux via `pnpm docker:test`.

**Nothing parses `procStart`,** though the entry carries it and it holds the
very fact the check wants. It is the process start rendered in UTC with **no
zone marker**, so reading it as a date lands hours off wherever the machine is
not on UTC (three hours, here). The code asks the kernel instead.

**Probe ordering.** `ProcessProbe` asks liveness first and the start time
second, so a process exiting between the two cannot be dated and the race
resolves to "not verified". It can cost a true claim and cannot manufacture a
false one.

**A 2s recycle tolerance** absorbs probe resolution only — `ps` reports whole
seconds, and a genuine entry is written a beat after its process exists. It is
not slack for a recycled pid, which would have to be re-issued within two
seconds of the original entry to slip through.

**Residual risk, stated rather than hidden:** a registry file copied between
machines (an rsynced store) names a pid that means nothing here. The `startedAt`
check defends against it only partially — an unrelated live process would have
to have started before the entry was written. Worth a follow-up if stores are
ever synced.

**Status is still derived once and still pure.** Finding out is I/O, so
discovery does it and reports `running` on the discovered session; `status`
stays a function of four values with `now` supplied by the caller, and no
elapsed-time rule reads a clock behind anyone's back. `store-discovery` ors the
adapter's verified answer with the sessions this server spawned itself: a
session started in somebody's terminal is invisible to the server's own process
table, and is exactly the session a watcher exists to report.

## Degradation

AGX-17's posture is kept everywhere. A store with no registry says nothing. An
entry that cannot be parsed is dropped silently — these files are rewritten on
every status change, so a torn read is transient and a complaint would flap. A
registry that refuses to be read *is* reported, because the directory is mode
0700 and a daemon running as the wrong user would otherwise lose every
permission prompt in silence. In every unverified case the answer is the
conservative one AGX-17 already gave.

## Checks

`pnpm check` green (build, lint, typecheck, 161 tests). `pnpm docker:test` green
on Linux: 165 tests, including the `/proc` probe and the database integration
suite that skips itself outside a container.

author: steipete
body:
Closes #136939

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice acknowledges ordinary conversation without answering, or stops delivering later answers after an interrupted or rejected speech response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early wake-name path used a sliding transcript tail and fuzzy matching on unfinished words, so its acknowledgment could disagree with the final admission decision. It now retains the original prefix and reserves fuzzy matching for final transcripts.

Voice output ownership now survives audio clearing, encoder errors, and Discord's synchronous error-to-Idle transition until the provider response terminates. Already-completed buffered audio releases immediately. OpenAI speech-request rejection goes through the existing terminal response owner, including live validation errors that omit `event_id` but identify the pending `response` field. The shared harness admits the outgoing request before `response.created`, so a rejection cannot disappear before an owner exists. Redundant `audioStarted` and duplicate rejection cleanup paths are removed.

## User Impact

Ordinary words and mid-sentence names no longer trigger misleading early acknowledgments. Following answers can speak after cancellation, encoder failure, or request rejection without reconnecting; old terminal events cannot prematurely release new speech. No configuration, model selection, schema, or protocol-version changes are required.

## Evidence

- The full changed-code check passes (format, types, lint, plugin boundaries, dependency, storage, import-cycle, and authorization guards). A clean rebase onto current main preserves the exact patch.
- 186 tests across 11 owner/sibling files pass, including Discord consults, wake-name handling, real Opus encoding/player errors, OpenAI events/tools/response control, and the shared session harness.
- Added regressions failed before the corresponding fixes. The real Discord player reproduces error -> Idle before Node's pipeline callback; the repaired owner retains the current answer until provider completion.
- Live OpenAI WebSocket proof: the original code received a real `invalid_request_error` for `response.tool_choice` with no event ID and emitted no terminal outcome. The candidate emitted `failed` then `completed`, received 16,000 audio bytes, matched the synthetic phrase, and kept the same connection open.
- Compared directly with OSS Codex at `38ba8cdceb536aa55af7db132d6bc830da8c0129`: [response-create queue](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/38ba8cdceb536aa55af7db132d6bc830da8c0129/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L365) and [terminal response handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/38ba8cdceb536aa55af7db132d6bc830da8c0129/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L2328). The repair follows terminal ownership and queue release while retaining OpenClaw's successful-response-only tool execution boundary.
- Installed `@discordjs/voice` 0.19.2 source confirms synchronous error-to-Idle behavior. Independent autoreview found the initial Idle-ordering gap; the real-player regression and owner repair addressed it, and the final P0–P2 review is clean.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-consults.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-playback.integration.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-playback.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-transcript.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime-turns.wake-name-followup.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-events.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-tools.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-response-control.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-terminal-outcomes.test.ts src/talk/realtime-session-harness.test.ts
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live --no-quiet extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.live.test.ts -t 'speaks again'
node scripts/check-changed.mjs
```

Production LOC: +49/-39 (net +10). Tests/support: +425/-64. The growth is the live-proven optional event-ID attribution contract and admission of a request before server acceptance; duplicate terminal cleanup and playback state were removed first. Regression introduction is not established; the failures were reproduced against current-main baseline `41419be40bbb17e5eed318992c8e3bf1aee6199b`.

Proof scope: live OpenAI provider plus real Discord codec/player and manager-boundary tests. A new end-to-end Discord room roundtrip is not claimed.

author: tongx-blip
body: ## Problem Tong: *"我只要annotate的功能标注图片，并attach mark就会出现这个问题"* — every annotated screenshot came back with the red retry badge on its chip, so the annotation could never be attached. The badge is `AnnotationUploadRetry`, which renders when `annotationUploadStatus$ === "failed"`. That is the **annotated copy**, not the original upload — a failed original upload removes the chip entirely and toasts. ## Cause Flattening reached for the original with an ``. That made it the only step in the feature that needed the CDN's permission: the annotation editor renders the very same URL as a plain `` (`image-annotation-editor.tsx` → `useResolvedAttachmentUrl`), and a plain `` negotiates nothing. So the image a user had just finished drawing on could still be refused at flatten time — and an image element reports that as a bare `error` event with no status, no headers and no reason. ## Fix - **Read the bytes with `fetch`, decode through an object URL.** A `blob:` URL is same-origin by definition, so the canvas is never tainted and `toBlob` stays readable without asking the CDN for anything. A refusal now arrives with its HTTP status attached. - **Stop discarding the error.** Five steps land on the one `failed` state — the original going missing, the read, the decode, the encode, the upload — and `rendered.error` was dropped, so the badge was the only evidence any of them happened. Logged as a *warning*: the marks survive on the chip and the badge retries in place, so this is a recoverable condition the user is already being shown. ## Why this was never caught `window.Image` is stubbed in tests to report `load` for **any** src, including one the browser would have refused, and the canvas is fully mocked. The whole "can this app actually read these pixels" question had no coverage, which is how a failure that reproduced on every annotated screenshot stayed green. Two new cases close that. Verified both ways — they **fail** against the old `crossOrigin` loader and **pass** against this one: ``` × attaches marks when the original image is only readable as bytes × offers a retry when the original image cannot be read Tests 2 failed | 15 passed (17) ← old loader Tests 17 passed (17) ← this branch ``` ## Checks prettier clean · platform `check-types` clean · eslint clean on the changed files · `image-annotation.test.tsx` 17/17 · `chat-draft` + `attachment-chips` 80/80. `knip` and repo-wide `check-types` were excluded locally in this 3.9 GB sandbox (`LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=knip,check-types`, not `--no-verify`); CI runs both. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: eljoakodelxd
body:
## What failed, measured and not assumed

On 02-09-2026 a session created from a source landed on the default branch and **was paralysed in its shell from its first turn**. The guard denied every `Edit`, `Write` and `Bash` call while the checkout sat there — **including the `git checkout -b` that would leave**. It could not run `date` either.

It escaped only because it happened to hold API tools that do not go through a shell. **A session without them has no first move at all**, and that is the shape every new agent arrives in, on every copy.

A rail that traps the sessions it is meant to guide gets worked around until it protects nothing (§8).

## The fix, one command wide

A lone branch-creating checkout passes: one segment, no chaining, no redirection, no substitution, and a name that is not the default branch.

Everything else from there stays denied. `Edit` and `Write` carry no command field, so they can never reach the escape even by accident.

## The bench was measuring the far end

It had 23 cases and **all 23 exercised the segment scanner**. The `branch == main` half of the hook — the half that failed — had **zero coverage**, because the bench runs from whatever branch the session is already on. A bench on the near end measures nothing about the far one.

Fifteen new cases run against a fixture repository standing on the default branch, so there is no test seam inside the hook. **The three escape cases run red without this fix** — verified before it was written.

## Verification this round

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/test-guard-main.sh` | 38 cases, green |
| all 15 benches | green |
| `tools/index.sh --check` · `tools/sections.sh --check` | ok |
| personal data | the diff was read line by line; the only address in it is the fixture's dummy `b@b` |

## Prose account (§8)

`CLAUDE.md` rule 1: **+21 words**, and they say what a reader could not otherwise know — that from the default branch there is exactly one way out. The rest of the new prose is comment inside the hook and the bench, which is where the *why* of a rail belongs.

## Scope

One release, one change. This copy also carries an unrelated encoding fix to the same file that has not travelled upstream yet; it is deliberately left out so this pull request stays one thing.

## Problem

Assistant messages that contain only tool calls were serialized with `"content": null`. Some OpenAI-compatible proxies reject that or respond with an empty, never-ending stream (hang). See #1.

## Change

- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts` (`convertMessages`): assistant messages now always start from `content: ""` instead of `compat.requiresAssistantAfterToolResult ? "" : null`. This generalizes the existing provider-specific workaround to all providers. `""` is semantically equivalent for tool-call-only messages and universally accepted; the skip logic for content-less assistant messages treats `""` and `null` identically, so nothing else changes.
- Regression test `packages/ai/test/openai-completions-assistant-content.test.ts`: asserts `content === ""` for tool-call-only assistant payloads, both without and with following tool results; also guards that content-less assistants without tool calls are still skipped.
- Changelog entry under `[Unreleased]`.
