body:
Seven layouts ported from byungjunjang/slide-master were still on the pre-6.1 contract (`native_structure_mode: template`, `01_cover`-style layout ids, a `<id>-master` master id, an English-only `summary`). This branch moves all seven onto the v6.1.0 structured contract, registers them through the tool, and documents the roster.

Branch is current with `main` (`ee98302` — PRs #4, #5 and #6 are all in; it was fast-forwarded onto `42d8068` for the work, then `main` moved and was merged in). One commit per layout, plus one for the index and roster, plus that merge.

## What changed, per layout

Common to all seven: pages renumbered to the structured naming (`02_chapter.svg` → `03_chapter.svg`, `03_content.svg` → `04_content.svg`, `04_ending.svg` → `05_ending.svg`), `native_structure_mode` moved from `template` to `structured`, master id moved to the underscore form (`<id>-master` → `<id>_master`), each page's `data-pptx-layout` dropped its file-number prefix for the bare page type (`01_cover` → `cover`), frontmatter gained the full trilingual set (`summary` / `summary_ko` / `summary_zh_tw`, `display_name` / `display_name_ko` / `display_name_zh_tw`), and a root `README.md` was added with provenance, migration notes, and gaps.

| Layout | Commit | Pages | Layout-specific notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `academic_defense` | `3fe6a73` | 5 | Header band with accent bar, key-message strip, two-column card agenda, full-bleed chapter divider. |
| `government_blue` | `0620ec5` | 5 | Gradient planes; inline `style="stop-color:…"` presentation replaced with real SVG attributes. |
| `government_red` | `579e5d2` | 5 | Two-tone accent chrome, agenda with statistic callouts; same inline-style cleanup. |
| `medical_university` | `0d13f1b` | 5 | Header band, card agenda, cross and pulse-trace accents. |
| `psychology_attachment` | `e3de9df` | 5 | `{{COVER_BG_IMAGE}}` promoted from a comment to a typed full-canvas `picture` slot. **See open question 1.** |
| `ai_ops` | `cf9666f` | **6** | `reference_style.svg` promoted to a real sixth page, `06_architecture_overview.svg`; page type `reference_style` → `architecture_overview`; all sample telecom copy replaced by slots. **See open question 2.** |
| `pixel_retro` | `4680e8d` | 5 | Dark plane, neon dual rules, pixel-block corners, stat-strip agenda, three-card closing. |
| index + roster | `0119f26` | — | `layouts_index.json` regenerated via `register_template.py` (never hand-edited); `templates/layouts/README.md` gains a Roster section. |

## Two open questions for Daren — please decide; unchanged here

**1. `psychology_attachment` — the cover picture carrier is faded to 25 %.**
`{{COVER_BG_IMAGE}}` existed in the legacy file only as a comment naming an optional background image. It is now a typed full-canvas `picture` slot carrying the shared 1 × 1 PNG at `opacity="0.25"` — the alpha the legacy spec prescribed. The reason it lives on the carrier rather than as an overlay: a Slide placeholder always paints above Layout atoms, so z-order alone cannot put the ring field over a cover photograph. Consequence: **any photo a deck drops into that slot renders at 25 % alpha and cannot be turned up from the Slide side.** Keep the legacy intent, or make the slot opaque and lose the ring field showing through?

**2. `ai_ops` — the chapter watermark is gone.**
The legacy chapter page painted a 160 px watermark echo of `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}` behind/over the 80 × 80 badge. One marker owns one slot, so the number now lives once, in the badge. In the legacy file the watermark sat under the badge, so nothing legible was lost — but the decorative echo is gone. Accept the loss, or reintroduce the watermark as a Layout-owned decorative atom (which means it stops tracking `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}` and becomes fixed art)?

body:
## What

Critique rounds 1 and 2 of the W4e cockpit (plan `~/.claude/plans/twinkly-bouncing-nest.md`, slice J). After #952 went live, three independent critics reviewed the served build against the reference with the parity packet (`C:/tmp/w4e-critique`): kimi-critic (15 items, verdict 7/10 to the reference), opus-critic (15 items, verdict 3/10 away), Codex sol (no result: the worker asked for an operator login). Every accepted item was re-verified on the reference's pixels before it was applied; the rejected ones are named with the reason.

Applied (measured against `ocs-workspace.png`):

- **Ribbon tabs**: the active tab is the band colour with 2px #00b4ff lines top and bottom (x=254: y 1-2 and 25-26, fill #2a2a2a); the strip starts at x 40 and runs on a 17px padding so Draw centres near x 278 and Manage near 630 as on the reference. Both critics had this wrong in different ways; the pixels settled it.
- **Large tools**: labels sit at the bottom of the 78px block (the reference centres "Line" at y 97).
- **Layers panel**: layer rows 104px so the panel lands at the reference's width; the four panels to its right re-register.
- **Properties combos**: one column on the reference's 21px pitch (y 47 / 68 / 89).
- **Document tab**: the 1px #00b4ff top edge (y 126) and a close glyph at its right, which is real (back to Start).
- **View cube**: the reference's 96px ring, 56px #9ec2d6 disc with the TOP face, compass letters in the annulus; WCS under it.
- **Properties pane**: rows and section heads at ROW_H 26; a new Drawing section fills the column with the document's own facts (name, entities, polylines, block inserts, 3D faces, layers, layers shown, extents, width, height, source), from the intake and one pass over its vertices, dashes for anything absent. This was Opus's biggest lever: the lower two thirds of the pane read as unfinished.
- **Ink**: secondary #949494 (4.7:1 on #2a2a2a) and disabled #767676 (3.2:1), a deliberate improvement on the reference's #696969 at 2.6:1; status text #9a9a9a (5:1) with muted honesty tints; the surface switch and the command-line controls quiet at rest; pressed tools and toggles get a container state (layer rows keep the bulb).
- **Tour card**: the cockpit's register (12.5px title, 11px body, 20px chips, Next in the Model blue, 260px) instead of the landing page's.

Rejected, with reasons: carets on large tools and on the view-mode readout (no menus exist; a caret would fake one), a radius on the doc tab (the reference has none), pin/close controls on the pane title and a collapsible pane (a real feature, round 3), collapsing the status bar's honesty segments (kept visible, muted), hiding History (it is live).

## Measured

Dev loop, 1920x940, rail on, `scripts/overlay_parity.py`: every reference edge still delta 0; chrome-region difference 4.84% (gate 6%; 4.45% before this PR, the pane's new rows add legitimate content the reference draws differently), whole frame 10.54%.

## Verification

- Units: site / composer / cadedit suites plus the new `propertiesDockDrawing.test.jsx` (extents fold, dashes, section presence); `check:app-wiring`, `check:unified-pins`; bundle within the reseeded baseline (numbers in the comment before merge).
- Managed local proof with `VITE_CAD_EDIT=1` and kimi-critic: recorded as comments before merge.
- Staging: verify by marker (`dock-drawing`), 1920x940 shot with the rail on, `overlay_parity.py` numbers in the plan record.

body:
## Original Swagger linter

- linter code: [UnSupportedPatchProperties](https://github.com/Azure/azure-openapi-validator/blob/main/packages/rulesets/src/spectral/functions/validate-patch-body-param-properties.ts)
- linter doc: [un-supported-patch-properties.md](https://github.com/Azure/azure-openapi-validator/blob/main/docs/un-supported-patch-properties.md)

The original rule performs these checks on every ARM Swagger PATCH operation:

- [x] Rejects writable top-level `id`.
- [x] Rejects writable top-level `name`.
- [x] Rejects writable top-level `type`.
- [x] Rejects writable top-level `location`.
- [x] Rejects writable `properties.provisioningState`.
- [x] Exempts `readOnly: true` properties.
- [x] Exempts properties whose `x-ms-mutability` excludes `update`.

## How the Swagger linter works

The ARM Spectral ruleset selects PATCH operations under both `paths` and `x-ms-paths` with resolved references enabled. `validatePatchBodyParamProperties` finds the first body parameter, resolves its schema through `getProperties`, checks the configured top-level denylist, then separately resolves the `properties` bag and checks `provisioningState`. Every failure targets the PATCH body parameter rather than the individual schema property.

For each selected property, the validator treats `readOnly: true` or an `x-ms-mutability` array without `update` as exempt. Spectral's resolved traversal can drop annotations that are siblings of `$ref`; the migration corpus confirmed false positives for referenced read-only `provisioningState` and immutable `location` properties. The TypeSpec rule intentionally preserves the authored lifecycle semantics instead of reproducing that validator defect. Swagger also reports emitted occurrences, while one authored TypeSpec property can be reused across operations and versions.

## Source TypeSpec lintdiff rule

- Validator rule ID: `UnSupportedPatchProperties`
- Local lintdiff rule: `unsupported-patch-properties`
- Canonical validator slug: `un-supported-patch-properties`
- Source branch: `feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties`
- Merged source revision: `de8d12e0244eb128604d2c4208f19325837fa852`
- Source repair PR: #5386
- Source worktree: `C:\dev\worktrees\lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties`
- Source state: clean; there were no uncommitted rule changes
- Source rule: [`unsupported-patch-properties.ts`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/src/rules/unsupported-patch-properties.ts)

The user marked this source rule done after its provider-namespace ownership repair merged. Promotion did not modify the lintdiff source, fixtures, snapshots, package metadata, or documentation.

## Destination analysis

The rule belongs in `@azure-tools/typespec-azure-resource-manager`. Its semantics are ARM RPC-Patch-V1-02, every fixture uses ARM service shapes, catalog metadata says `applicability: ARM` and `sources: ["arm"]`, and the validation report infers the resource-manager ruleset. Azure Core is not a plausible destination because the rule is not shared data-plane guidance.

Existing official rules do not duplicate this behavior. `arm-resource-patch` rejects fields absent from the resource but permits envelope fields such as `name`, `type`, and `location`; custom ARM PATCH templates also accept arbitrary patch models. The promoted rule therefore closes the documented official coverage gap rather than changing an existing rule.

The official name is `no-unsupported-patch-properties`, following the TypeSpec `no-<thing>` convention instead of retaining the validator's historical casing and wording. The rule is explicitly registered as `false` in the resource-manager ruleset so promotion does not immediately add diagnostics to existing service specifications.

## How the promoted TypeSpec linter works

When enabled in the ARM ruleset, the rule visits operations and selects HTTP PATCH requests with bodies. The official implementation deliberately omits the lintdiff source's provider-namespace guard: lintdiff enables ARM and data-plane rules together and must self-scope, while the destination ARM ruleset already supplies this applicability boundary. This matches neighboring operation-based ARM rules and avoids suppressing diagnostics solely because provider decoration is absent or malformed.

The rule unwraps nullable single-model bodies while leaving scalar and multi-model unions compliant. For the PATCH model and nested `properties` model, it walks inherited properties, resolves their `application/json` encoded names, and uses HTTP metadata plus PATCH request visibility to determine whether each property reaches the payload. Lifecycle visibility distinguishes writable properties from read-only or create-only properties. Diagnostics target authored project properties; library-originated properties fall back to the operation. This avoids emitting duplicate diagnostics for generated Swagger occurrences while preserving actionable source locations.

Promotion-specific adaptations are the official rule name, removal of the lintdiff-only applicability guard, canonical documentation URL, and package registration. Property-selection, visibility, and diagnostic semantics remain aligned with the source rule.

## Fixture-to-native test mapping

| Original lintdiff fixture | Native vitest case | Coverage note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`patch-with-id-name/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/patch-with-id-name/main.tsp) | `it("reports writable id, name, and type properties")` | Three direct writable top-level reserved properties and diagnostic cardinality. |
| [`nested-arm-namespace/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/nested-arm-namespace/main.tsp) | `it("reports unsupported properties in nested ARM namespaces")` | Nested namespace ownership regression from the merged source repair. |
| [`global-operation-compliant/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/global-operation-compliant/main.tsp) | `it("does not require provider namespace decoration when the ARM rule is enabled")` | Destination adaptation: the ARM ruleset owns applicability, so the official rule does not retain lintdiff's mixed-ruleset guard. |
| [`patch-with-location-provisioning-state/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/patch-with-location-provisioning-state/main.tsp) | `it("reports writable location and properties.provisioningState on a nullable body")` | Nullable body unwrapping plus top-level and nested violations. |
| [`encoded-inherited-properties/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/encoded-inherited-properties/main.tsp) | `it("reports inherited properties by their encoded JSON names")` | Inherited properties, encoded JSON names, nested inheritance, and three diagnostics. |
| [`readonly-immutable-properties-compliant/main.tsp`](https://github.com/Azure/typespec-azure/blob/feature/lintdiff-un-supported-patch-properties/packages/typespec-lintdiff/test/fixtures/UnSupportedPatchProperties/readonly-immutable-properties-compliant/main.tsp) | `it("accepts read-only and immutable reserved properties")` | Read-only identity and provisioning state plus create-only location. |

author: stylique123
body:
`generate-blueprint/index.ts` is **8,179 lines** and carries **83 inline mirrors** of shared code, because an edge function cannot import `@twinai/shared`. Drift between a mirror and its original is not hypothetical: **#644 shipped a half-applied fix earlier tonight** because the edge copy had diverged, and production reads the edge copy.

## A name grep gets this wrong

A name-mention grep says 15 mirrors have no test. **That number is wrong.** Nine are exercised *through a caller* — `asksForBrollInline` has no test naming it, but `unsupplyableShotCountInline`'s parity test evaluates the source slice containing it. Same mention-versus-call trap the repo has hit twice before.

Resolving the call graph among mirrors and taking the transitive closure from the tests that name one:

| | |
|---|---|
| inline mirrors | 83 |
| named directly by a test | 44 |
| reached transitively | 33 |
| **exercised** | **77** |
| reached by nothing | **6** |

Of those six, only **two** have a shared original they can drift from:

- `renderContentHistoryInline` → `packages/shared/src/contentHistory.ts`
- `resolveSubjectSourceInline` → `packages/shared/src/script/subjectSource.ts` (with its two constants)

The other four are edge-only — untested, but with no second copy, so not a parity risk. The two that matter are guarded here.

## `resolveSubjectSource` is not a byte copy, and my first draft assumed it was

The inline takes a **boolean** rather than the knowledge array (the edge resolves `evidenceLevel` earlier, from rows the shared copy never sees) and names the verdict fields in **snake_case** because they are persisted. Deep equality fails on both counts and says nothing about drift.

So the test compares the **decision** and the **instruction text** — the half the writer actually reads, where a drift is invisible in every verdict field and still changes the script.

## Verification

- 15 tests, **mutation-checked against real drift**: rewording the inline content-history header fails 4; widening the inline experience set to include `'advice'` fails 2. Edge source restored byte-identical after both.
- `tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` clean.
- Gate classifier: **STATIC** (`required=0`) — one new test file, no matrix required.

body:
zabuno.com canlıya alındıktan sonra üretim ilk kez **dışarıdan** kontrol edildi. Altı paketin göçleri uygulanmış, şema sağlam, hiçbir yerde 500 yok. Ama iki şey yerelde çalışıp üretimde çalışmıyordu.

## 1. Üretim hangi commit'i sunduğunu söyleyemiyordu

```html
<meta name="zabuno-build-revision" content="">
```

Bu depo `preview-truth` kapısını tam olarak *"baktığım şey gerçekten yazdığım kod mu"* sorusu için kurmuştu. Üretimde o soru **cevapsızdı**: deploy `.image.env`'e yalnız imaj etiketini yazıyor, konteynere hiçbir revizyon geçmiyordu.

**Geri alma da kördü** — eski bir SHA etiketine dönüldüğünde sayfada hangisinin canlı olduğunu söyleyen hiçbir şey yoktu.

## 2. `robots.txt` üretimde ölüydü

`ShowRobotsController` var, rota kayıtlı, yerelde 200; üretimde **404**. Sebep tek satır:

```nginx
location = /robots.txt  { access_log off; log_not_found off; }
```

Tam eşleşmeli blokta ne `try_files` var ne PHP'ye aktarım — nginx isteği statik dosya olarak arıyor, bulamıyor, **Laravel'e hiç ulaşmıyor**. Yerelde `artisan serve` çalıştığı ve nginx devrede olmadığı için kusur yalnız canlıda görünüyordu.

## Aynı sınıf, üçüncü kez

İkisi de **koddan değil, kodun taşındığı yoldan** kaynaklanıyor. Depo bunu daha önce yazmıştı: *"sorun kodda değil aktarımdaydı."* İkisi de artık `DeploymentContractTest` içinde dondurulmuş ve **mutasyonla** doğrulanmış.

## Kontrol edilip sağlam çıkanlar

author: rios0rios0
body:
**Stacked on #296** — targeted at its branch so the diff shows only this work. GitHub retargets it to `main` when #296 merges.

Ruby was the one ecosystem left without a way to honour the *allowing* direction of `allow_major_updates`. Bundler has no flag meaning "raise the bounds in the Gemfile" — `bundle update` resolves inside whatever is declared, and `--major` only lifts bundler's own ceiling, not the repository's. So `gem "rails", "~> 6.0"` stayed on 6.x for ever however the key was set, while every other ecosystem had a native answer:

| Ecosystem | Raises the manifest with |
|---|---|
| dart | `pub upgrade --major-versions` |
| python | `pdm update --unconstrained` |
| javascript | `pnpm update --latest` / `npm-check-updates` |
| **ruby** | **nothing — hence this** |

## What it does

Four moves around `bundle update`, the manifest ones emitted by one shared fragment, `support.GemfileConstraintScript`:

1. **Widen.** Every pessimistic constraint on a `gem` line — `~> X.Y[.Z]` — becomes `>= X.Y[.Z]`, so the resolution may cross the major. A copy of the manifest is kept outside the clone.
2. **Resolve.** `bundle update`, now free to take the new major.
3. **Re-tighten.** The manifest is rewritten from the copy: a constraint whose gem resolved past the bound it expressed becomes `~>` the resolved version at the precision the repository wrote — `~> 6.0` becomes `~> 7.1`, `~> 6.0.1` becomes `~> 7.1.3` — and a constraint whose gem stayed inside its bound, or whose gem the lockfile does not list, is put back untouched.
4. **Re-lock.** `bundle update` resolved against the widened manifest, so `Gemfile.lock`'s `DEPENDENCIES` block records `rails (>= 6.0)` beside a Gemfile that now says `~> 7.1`, and a `--frozen`/`--deployment` install refuses that mismatch. `bundle lock` reconciles the two: every locked version already satisfies the raised bound, so it rewrites `DEPENDENCIES` and moves nothing.

The widening is a means, not the result. What the repository keeps is a *raised* bound, which is the contract `pub upgrade --major-versions` and `npm-check-updates` honour too: the operator survives the bump. A `>=` left behind would be permanent — turning the key off again would restore nothing, and every later resolution by any tool would be free to take the next major.

## When the resolution fails

The manifest is restored from the copy and `bundle update` retried within the bounds the repository declared. A conflict between two new majors therefore degrades to the smaller upgrade rather than shipping a dropped ceiling beside a stale `Gemfile.lock` — which a `--frozen` or `--deployment` install would refuse — or producing no upgrade at all.

## What it deliberately does not touch

- **Anything that is not a `gem` line.** The rewrite is anchored on the call, not on the operator, so the `ruby "~> 3.2"` directive (a statement about the interpreter, the same kind of thing as `.ruby-version`), commented-out declarations and bundler `plugin` lines are out of reach by construction. A constraint carried onto a continuation line keeps its ceiling — the conservative outcome, and a shape a Gemfile almost never has.
- **Exact pins** (`gem "rails", "6.0.1"`) — a deliberate pin.
- **Explicit ceilings** (`"< 7"`, `"<= 6.9"`) — the repository saying no in as many words. A compound `"~> 6.0", "< 7"` resolves inside the ceiling and comes back exactly as written.
- **`.gemspec`** — its constraints describe what *consumers* of the library must tolerate, not what this application may resolve to.

## The description follows the flag

`GeneratePRDescription` now takes `allowMajorUpdates`, as dart's does: with majors allowed the body names the raised constraints and adds a `- [ ] Review the constraint changes in `Gemfile`` checklist item; with majors refused it says `bundle update --minor` re-resolved the lockfile within the current majors and points at nothing that is not in the diff.

## Refusing is unchanged

No manifest edit happens when `allow_major_updates: false` — that direction still uses bundler's own ceiling, `--minor`, and a test asserts none of the three functions is emitted.

## Tests

- **Widening** — seventeen Gemfile shapes run through the emitted bash: both quote styles, no space after the operator, a pre-release suffix, trailing options, a parenthesised call, a group-indented line, and every shape that must *not* change — exact pin, explicit ceiling, already-open, unconstrained, prose mentioning the operator, the `ruby` directive, a commented-out declaration, a bundler plugin, a continuation line.
- **Re-tightening** — sixteen rows run the whole cycle against a fixture lockfile with nested dependencies, a platform-suffixed version and a `DEPENDENCIES` block: one-, two- and three-segment bounds raised at their own precision, bounds the gem stayed inside left byte-identical, a gem missing from the lock put back, spacing normalised only when a bound moves, and the `ruby` directive surviving the cycle. Plus: no working file left behind for `git add -A`, and a no-op without a prior widening.
- **Restore** — the manifest comes back byte-identical, and the call is a no-op without a prior widening.
- **Ordering** — widening precedes `bundle update`, re-tightening follows it, and the re-lock comes last; a `contains` assertion cannot express any of them.
- **Description** — both directions of `GeneratePRDescription`.

`golangci-lint` 0 issues against the shared config (run locally against the pre-rebase dependency set, since the rebased `langforge`/`cliforge`/`testkit` require Go 1.27.1; CI runs the current one). Full suite green apart from `TestWriteGoUpgradeCommands`, a pre-existing stub hard-coding `#!/bin/bash` that fails on any machine without one; it fails identically on the base branch.

body:
🎯 **What:** Enforce an upper bound check (`num_headers > 10000`) on `num_headers` when deserializing cache object metadata in `src/content/llcache.c`.

⚠️ **Risk:** Invalid or maliciously crafted cache metadata files with an arbitrarily large `num_headers` could cause excessive memory allocation during header parsing loops or out-of-bounds reads/writes.

🛡️ **Solution:** Check `num_headers > 10000` after parsing with `sscanf()`. If `num_headers` exceeds 10,000, `llcache_process_metadata()` immediately rejects the metadata with `NSERROR_INVALID` and cleans up safely. Unit test added in `src/test/llcache.c` verifies the fix.

author: alyssa-cntp
body:
**Merge when the PR head shows `73b6a19`.**

## What you were seeing

The top-ups **were** in Total output. The problem is that the **Bagging panel header showed that total over a list containing only the bags.**

On 2 September:

| | |
|---|---|
| panel header | `18 217.0 kg` |
| the rows beneath it | `17 925.0 kg` |
| the gap | **292.0 kg** — top-ups into 1 September bags, shown in a separate panel further down |

Read the header and the top-ups looked double-counted. Read the rows and they looked missing. The arithmetic was correct throughout; the panel asserted an answer its own contents contradicted, which is why the totals did not justify what the note claimed.

## The fix

- **The header now shows the bags' own weight**, so it matches the rows beneath it.
- **The panel foots with the sum in view:** `Bagged out` + `Half-bag top-ups — added into older bags` = `Total output` — the same figure the mass balance uses. Only when there is a top-up to add; otherwise the bags' total *is* the output and a second identical number is noise.
- The top-up line says those bags were bagged on an earlier day and are not in the count above, which is why the bag count does not move when the kilograms do.
- The per-shift block's `N bags · X kg` now reads `X kg out`, since that figure includes the shift's top-ups while the count does not.

Nothing about how output is calculated changed. `bagsOutputKg` and the mass balance are untouched — this is the panel showing its working.

## Verification

`scripts/verify-output-panel-totals.py` — 14 checks against the 2 September figures, including the 292 kg gap the old header left, plus the no-top-up, top-ups-only and bag-count cases. All passing.

`next build` clean, 227/227, exit 0. Type errors 38 — unchanged from `main`.

## Also in that PDF

`TOTAL INPUT 18 581.0` against `TOTAL OUTPUT 18 217.0` — a shortfall of **364 kg, −1.96%**, so it flags outside ±1%. That is a real balance question for the day rather than a display one: worth checking against the bucket elevator left in the tower, which is excluded from output by design.

## 這個 PR 做了什麼

新增一份國小四年級數學互動教材：四上第 1 單元「一億以內的數」。

依 108 課綱（南一版四上第 1 單元）的**章節架構**自行編寫，內容全部原創，沒有複製任何出版社或平台的教材。單檔 HTML、無外部相依，可離線開啟。

## 檔案異動

- 新增 `lessons/國小四年級數學/四上1_一億以內的數.html`
- `lessons/lessons.js`：在陣列最前面登錄一筆
- `README.md`：收錄表補一列，開頭敘述由「給中學生」改為「給國小～國中學生」
- `lessons/國二數學/學習紀錄.html`：`SEC` 小節對照表加上新單元

## 教材結構

- 1-1 認識大數：十萬／百萬／千萬／一億、數位表、四位一撇的讀法、中間的 0
- 1-2 換算與比大小：幾萬 ⇄ 數字、幾個一萬／幾個十萬、比大小兩步驟
- 1-3 大數的計算：同單位加減、乘 10/100/1000、拆 0 相乘、生活應用題
- 單元總測驗 10 題，交卷計分，8 題過關

每節有觀念卡（公式框／提示／常錯警告）、可展開詳解的例題、4 題即時對答案的練習。

## 額外的互動小工具

1-1 內建「輸入數字，看它怎麼唸」：輸入 0～99999999 的整數，即時顯示中文讀法，並自動畫出對應的數位表。純 JS，無外部相依。

## 學習紀錄

沿用既有機制：`localStorage` key `study_log_v1`，`CH` 常數為「四上1 一億以內的數」，雲端上傳網址一樣只從 `localStorage` 讀，不寫死在檔案裡。

## 驗證

- 所有練習題與測驗題的答案、算式都用 Node 逐題驗算過（含換算、加減、乘法、排序、最接近一億）

- 教材內嵌 JS 通過 `node --check`
- `lessons.js` 載入後陣列長度 10，第一筆為新教材

原本想參考的均一頁面（`junyiacademy.org/topics/n-m4a-c01`）在此環境被網路政策擋住，無法讀取；單元名稱是透過搜尋結果確認的，內容為原創編寫。

author: aronk11
body:
A kubeconfig context with `auth-provider: oidc` could not be used at all:

```
Could not read default: no Auth Provider found for name "oidc"
```

That message describes the binary, not the cluster. client-go still ships the
OIDC provider, but providers register themselves in an `init`, and Correlux
never imported the package — so no amount of fixing the kubeconfig helped.

One blank import in `internal/kube/client`, which is the package that
authenticates and therefore the honest place for the only side-effect import in
the codebase. It also pulls in the azure and gcp stubs, so those contexts now
report which exec plugin to install instead of claiming no provider exists.

Three tests: an OIDC context is never rejected for lack of a provider, a
provider Kubernetes itself removed explains what to use instead, and an unknown
provider is still an error — the last one so the first two cannot pass
vacuously.

Not reproduced end to end against the reporting cluster: that context is not in
the kubeconfig on this machine. The mechanism is not in doubt — without the
import, every `auth-provider: oidc` context fails with exactly this message.

The listed description said the plugin detects "prompt injections" and
shows "a verdict you can acknowledge", which overstates what it does.
dsh-trust-check discloses capability *shapes* (capabilities, literal
destinations, install scripts, prompt/skill/patch registrations) with
file:line evidence — it never judges whether content is malicious, and
"nothing detected" is not a safety claim.

New copy matches the project README: static capability disclosure,
code-determined, zero-token, evidence-backed, explicitly not a security
verdict. One yml file changed; READMEs regenerate on merge.

author: gr8monk3ys
body:
`trackEvent` has been exported since the analytics component was written and **was never once called**. The site measured page views and nothing else, so a visitor opening a demo, sending the contact form, or asking for a tool report left no trace distinguishable from someone bouncing off the homepage.

That matters more here than it usually would. `PRODUCT.md` now records the primary user as an **open decision** — the audience assumption in the copy is validated by nothing — and the three live demos are the only proof on the site a visitor can check without talking to anyone. They were producing no signal at all.

## Now measured, all three consent-gated

| Event | Category | Label |
|---|---|---|
| `demo_opened` | `proof` | which demo |
| `contact_submitted` | `conversion` | the service interest |
| `tool_report_requested` | `conversion` | which tool |

## One structural fix it required

`trackEvent` and `trackPageView` move to `src/lib/analytics.ts`. They lived inside the Google Analytics component, which `AppChrome` imports **lazily** so `next/script` and the gtag loader stay out of the initial bundle. Importing a helper from there would have dragged all of that back into every page that measures anything. The old path re-exports them.

The helpers no-op without consent **and** without `gtag` on the window. Both checks are load-bearing: gtag can linger after a visitor withdraws consent inside a single page view.

## Verified in a browser, and the first version of that test was wrong

Unit tests prove the helper fires; they cannot prove a real click reaches it through consent gating and the lazy boundary. So `tests/e2e/analytics.spec.ts` clicks a real demo link on the homepage: with consent it records exactly one `demo_opened` in the `proof` category, with consent refused it records nothing.

Getting the negative case honest took two attempts, which is worth stating. Aborting the outbound request **still commits a navigation**, which re-runs Playwright's init script and resets the recorder — so the "records nothing" assertion passed while proving nothing at all. The click's default is cancelled instead, and the test now asserts the page stayed put before checking the recorder is empty.

The 10 unit cases drive consent through real `localStorage` rather than mocking `hasAnalyticsConsent`, so they also prove `analytics.ts` and `cookieConsent.ts` agree on the stored shape. A mock would pass even if that contract drifted.

`type-check` clean · eslint clean · **101 unit at 100%** on all four metrics · 14 integration · **21/21 e2e** · `next build` clean.

## What this does and does not do

It does not answer who your audience is. It makes the question answerable — nothing could while no action was recorded.

author: macnite
body:
### Motivation

- Remove the long-standing split between `MealInput` and `RecipeImport` so both entry points use one pipeline driven by an explicit intent (`MEAL` | `RECIPE`).
- Ensure recipe extractions use the same, stronger component resolution as quick-meal runs and never rely on model-invented nutrition for recipes.
- Make the per-ingredient candidate chooser consistently available on AI draft recipes and apply reviewer choices before a draft becomes ACTIVE.

### Description

- Data model and migration: add `AiIngestionInput` (merged input table), copy legacy `MealInput` / `RecipeImport` rows into it, repoint `AiJob` → `ingestionInputId`, and promote legacy checkbox flags into the new input (`intent` + `logAfterConfirm`). In-flight `RUNNING` jobs are deterministically requeued (`RUNNING` → `QUEUED`) so workers resume from the migrated input. (See `prisma/schema.prisma` and `prisma/migrations/20260903000000_unify_ai_ingestion/migration.sql`.)
- Single queue path: collapse the two entry points to use `AI_INGESTION` jobs and a shared queue function (`queueAiIngestion`), and route both server actions through it (`meal-ai-actions.ts`, `ai-ingestion-actions.ts`).
- Unified extraction and resolution: introduce `src/server/ai-ingestion.ts` which runs a single merged extraction for recipe intent, fetches URL instructions when requested, resolves every component via the existing `resolveComponent()` chain, and stores the extraction + diagnostics as a draft; the resolver gained an explicit `allowModelEstimates` flag so `RECIPE` runs disallow model-estimated nutrition while `MEAL` runs keep it. (`component-resolver.ts`, `ai-jobs.ts`, `ai-types.ts`.)
- Review UI and confirm flow: moved the per-ingredient `ComponentChoice` into the recipe draft page so every AI draft recipe shows one row per ingredient with candidates and the explicit skip option; confirming applies reviewer selections then flips the recipe to `ACTIVE` and — when `logAfterConfirm` was requested — logs exactly one portion automatically. (`src/app/recipes/[id]/page.tsx`, `recipes.ts`, `recipe-actions.ts`.)
- Routing & intent: derive completion destinations from the stored intent rather than old `entityType` + metadata. `MEAL` → `/ai-review/<id>`, `RECIPE` → `/recipes/<id>`. (`ai-types.ts`, `completion-redirect` usage.)
- Housekeeping: removed legacy standalone files for the old recipe import/ingredient-resolution pipeline (`ingredient-resolution.*`, `recipe-import.*`) and adapted tests and admin surfaces to the unified model; added missing i18n keys for `MODEL_VISION_UNSUPPORTED` and updated `servingsHint` text.

What was removed or replaced: the legacy recipe-import module and its action, the separate ingredient-resolution resolver, and associated tests that were superseded by the unified flow (these deletions were done deliberately after wiring the new pipeline).

### Testing

- Ran lint (`npm run lint`) and typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) — both succeed in this environment.
- Ran the full unit/integration suite (`npm test` / Vitest): all tests passed locally after updates (reported: ~432 tests passed, 9 skipped at the final run in this workspace).
- Built the app (`npm run build`) successfully; server pages compiled and static pages generated in the local build run.
- e2e / migration note: end-to-end acceptance (Playwright) and the migration that needs a real Postgres instance were exercised where possible, but creating a Docker Postgres container is not available in this execution environment (docker not present), so CI should run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and the e2e suite with the standard PostgreSQL service as documented in the brief; the migration script requeues any `RUNNING` jobs so in-flight jobs resume deterministically.

If you want, I can open the PR text for review and list the exact files removed versus kept in a checklist for reviewers.

author: samuelstefano
body:
## Correção de uma afirmação errada minha, da PR #507

Escrevi no `ARCHITECTURE.md` e no comentário de `roleFromIdentity` que o gate de `email_verified` era fail-closed a ponto de "num projeto sem confirmação de e-mail ninguém virar root". **Isso está errado.**

O GoTrue do Supabase, com **"Confirm email" desligado**, cria a conta **já confirmada** — `email_confirmed_at` preenchido e `user_metadata.email_verified: true`. O claim chega `true` e o gate deixa passar.

Consequência prática: enquanto o cadastro for aberto e a confirmação estiver off, **quem souber um e-mail da allowlist `COCKPIT_ROOT_EMAILS` continua se cadastrando com ele e virando root**. A checagem no código não fecha esse buraco sozinha.

## O que muda

Só texto. O comportamento da #507 continua correto e útil como defesa em profundidade (cobre "sessão existe sem e-mail confirmado" e impede o relay de confiar cegamente no claim), mas a documentação agora diz o que de fato protege: **ligar "Confirm email" no projeto `deck-relay`**. Enquanto isso não estiver ligado, `COCKPIT_ROOT_EMAILS` deve ser tratado como segredo.

## Validação

`tsc --noEmit` limpo; `vitest run` em `shared/identity.test.ts` e `relay/` verde. Nenhuma mudança de comportamento.

author: tolu-ex
body:
Nine commits. The through-line is that almost everything here was found by **running the game and measuring it**, not by reading the code — several were bugs that read perfectly well in source.

## Three bugs, found by exercising it (`e054d2a`)

A debugging pass over the whole tree. Static reading found nothing; all three came out of running it.

**Two bins could be collected at once, by an arm that serves one.** `RoundManager` accumulated `anyCollecting` *while walking the bin array*, so a bin at index 0 was tested before the loop reached a bin at index 13 already mid-lift. The 0.9 s cooldown didn't cover the gap — a lift cycle runs ~5.5 s. The second bin scored, `playArmCycle()` returned false because the mechanism was busy, and **the bin emptied itself with no arm anywhere near it.** Reproduced at 2 simultaneous, 1 after the fix, collection still working. Now also gated on `truck.armBusy`, so a bin can never start a cycle the arm can't perform.

**The hydraulic ram walked out of its barrel.** `slider()` captured `node.position.clone()` as home at construction, and a new `TruckMechanism` is built on every re-bind — which happens on every switch back from the bike. A switch made mid-cycle took the *displaced* rod position as its new home. Measured drift: **0.23 m per switch, linear and unbounded, 1.38 m after six.** The boom was unaffected (`rotator` writes an absolute angle) and the tailgate ram was unaffected (it already cached home on the node — which is the fix, now applied to `slider`). Zero drift across eight interrupted switches.

**A failed world build soft-locked the game.** `_transitionTo` had no `try/finally`, so anything throwing between the fades left `transitioning` true, input locked and the overlay at full opacity: a black screen with no way out and nothing explaining it. Now guarded with a hub fallback and a `finally` that returns control regardless. After a simulated failure it recovers to the hub, lifts the fade, and drives at 57.6 km/h. **This one matters most given a weekly agent is about to start editing world builders — it's exactly how a bad edit would present.**

## Shading and line work (`15addcd`)

The truck reading as "blocks upon blocks" was not the model. Sampled off the rendered frame, the body's roof and flank came back at **luma 131.5 and 130.8 of 255 — 0.7% apart**, and a modelled rib measured 131.5 against 131.7 for the panel beside it. 605 nodes of detail rendering as one silhouette.

Ambient was 0.52 of a 1.49 budget with hemisphere at 0.42 — **63% of the light directionless**, carrying no shape information. The toon ramp's stops at 0.62/0.82/1.0 then quantised what survived into one band. Now 0.22 + 0.28 + 0.85 by day, ramp 0.40/0.70/1.0; green spread went from **1.7 luma to 43.1**.

Shading alone was never enough: a poster carries form with flat colour *and line*, and there was none. Outlines by inverted hull, which suits a model made of hundreds of separate meshes — every rib and shut line gets a contour. Expansion is in view space scaled by distance so lines hold constant pixel width; node scales run 0.186–1.066 and expanding locally would have made a gripper pad's outline five times heavier than the body's.

## Title screen, music, sound control (`26b3dc2`, `3dfa6c7`, `7120182`)

The intro painted an opaque gradient over the viewport; `main.js` had always rendered a frame of the hub behind it that nobody saw. Now a poster over the living world, with attract mode sweeping a front three-quarter of the truck. Type went from centred and tracked `+2px` on a 900-weight face to a left-anchored masthead at `-0.035em`.

Music is synthesised like the rest of the audio — four bars in D at 82 BPM, scheduled against the audio clock because `setInterval` drift is audible as a stumbling rhythm. No asset, no licensing question on a public repo.

Plus a **visible sound toggle**: the page autoplayed music with no control anyone could see, and `M` is neither shown nor bound until the round starts. A remembered mute now creates no `AudioContext` at all.

## Ile-Ife, rebuilt (`c094367`)

The world was a dirt road across bare laterite, sixty palms, loose rocks, and a cone-on-a-drum that a source comment called *"the iconic wide conical OAU-style roof"*. Nobody had checked. Haarlem got canal houses and a windmill, Singapore got supertrees — the one African world got a generic idea of a continent.

Rebuilt on Arieh Sharon's 1960s modernist campus: teaching slabs on pilotis, egg-crate brise-soleil screens, covered walkways, Oduduwa Hall under a folded roof, a paved boulevard and planted roundabout, broad-canopy shade trees. The rebuild also caught that `createTree` is a stacked cone — a conifer — so the first pass had put Northern European pines on a Nigerian campus.

**The massing is an impression, not a survey.** If any of it is wrong, it should be corrected by someone who knows the campus.

## Dead code (`ceb375d`)

104 deletions: `PALETTE.truck` (orphaned by the GLB swap), five dead palette keys, `createTulip`, `POSTER`, two uncalled methods, unused imports, the last shadow plumbing, three `roughness` options routed to a material that ignores them.

Worth flagging: **three symbols the audit flagged were live code.** `WORLD_BOUNDS` and `HUB_PORTAL_RADIUS` are each used four or five times *inside* `HubWorld.js`, and `stdMat` is used by `mesh()`. An unused-*exports* audit flags all three because it only counts external references — they needed the export removed, not the constant.

## Dragon and backlog (`4b82859`, `beb2582`)

A dragon circles the hub as scenery. Every link samples the same flight path at a progressively older time, so the serpentine curve and banking fall out of the path with no keyframes. The trap: spacing is `lag × speed`, so guessing the lag flies the body apart — it's derived from segment length over path speed. Recoloured scarlet with a horn crown after reference images.

`IMPROVEMENTS.md` is the queue a weekly scheduled agent works from — topmost unchecked item, one per PR. Its rules come from what went wrong here: never invent CV copy, never depict a real place from assumption, verify on screen not in the diff, never push to main.

## Verification

- **6,300-frame randomised fuzz** across all seven worlds, 9 arm and 4 tip cycles — no NaN in position, heading, speed, roll, steer, sideslip or yaw rate; no bounds escapes; no exceptions
- **28 world loads**: geometries, textures, programs flat. **36 real transitions** plus 12 overlapping requests against the guard: counts identical across three passes (834 / 834 / 834)
- All seven worlds: 13,624 meshes, **0 missing materials**, byte-identical renders across repeated builds and reverse visit order
- Truck 57.6 km/h, 17.2° steer, 18.9 m radius, rolls **out** +5.2°; bike 25.9 km/h, 5.5° steer, 0.47 g, leans **in** −25.2° (`atan(0.47) = 25.2°`, so the bank is physical)
- Audio measured off the master bus: theme 0.0118 RMS, muted 0.0004, stopped 0.0 on Start
- No console errors

## Still open

`cvData.js` holds placeholder copy — that's yours to write, and the agent is explicitly forbidden from touching it. No touch controls, so the game is unplayable on a phone. Not yet deployed.

author: nelsongan
body:
## The report

> if i press in it looks this [the dish] however for example i feel like wait no the normal thosai seems more fitting i press the back button, thinking it will bring me back to previous menu [the results] but instead it brings me to the home page of the app, so it's quite troublesome having to redo the entire flow

## Why

`/log` is a `transparentModal`, so a `push` from inside it stacks a second presentation on the sheet. `openFood` avoided that with `router.replace`, which put the dish on the stack above Today and left it standing there. The comment recorded the cost as deliberate:

> The cost is that back from the dish lands on the day rather than the results, which is the right trade for pick a dish, set the portion, done.

It is the one place in the app where a search cannot be come back to. `/log/search` already exists as a page precisely so that it can be, and is reached from an unreadable snap; the sheet's inline field just never went through it.

## The change

A search pick replaces the sheet with `/log/search` carrying the query, then pushes the dish over it. Both queue in one flush, so the user still sees the sheet go and the dish arrive; the stack underneath is now `[tabs, log/search, log/food/[id]]`.

The barcode scanner keeps the old `replace`. A code is one dish and one answer, with no search to return to.

`FoodSearchPanel` gained the two halves that make it rebuildable: `onPick` hands out the search, `restore` takes it back. `tracked` travels with the query because `Food Searched` fires 1,200ms after a query settles and a panel picked from inside that window unmounts with the timer pending — seeding on the words alone loses exactly the searches that found their answer fastest, and not seeding double-counts the slow ones. Both directions are pinned by tests.

`autoFocus` is off when a query arrives: that page mounts *under* the dish, and what the user comes back to is a list to read.

## Verified on the iOS simulator

- sheet → search → dish → back: the results, with the query, no keyboard
- back again: Today
- edge swipe from the dish: the results
- dish → Add: unwinds to Today and writes the row
- `/log/search` with no query: still opens the keyboard

`pnpm check` green (71 suites, 758 tests).

## Not in scope

`RecipePanel`'s `onOpen` has the identical `replace` shape, so backing out of a recipe opened from the sheet lands on Today rather than the recipes tab. Left alone deliberately — noting it so it is not rediscovered.

author: keycode17
body:
Two requests, plus a latent sync bug the first one exposed.

## Delete one entry

There was only *Delete all entries*. The editor header now shows a trash icon on a saved entry; it asks — *Delete this entry? Its photos go with it.* — with **Delete** / **Keep**, then closes the editor, returns to the diary and syncs.

Underneath, `entries` gains `deleted_at`. Deleting soft-deletes and bumps `updated_at`, so the next sync pushes a tombstone; once acknowledged the row and its tags, stickers and photo references are dropped. Every read path skips soft-deleted rows meanwhile.

**The latent bug:** the protocol and the server already handled `deleted_at_ms`, but the device never sent one and ignored any it received — an entry deleted on one phone stayed on every other. A pulled tombstone now removes the local entry and everything hanging off it.

The confirmation uses the existing toast prompt, which was composed *under* the composer and could never be seen while editing. It now sits above it.

## The ratio slider reaches landscape

It was linear in height/width from 0.5 to 2.0: square sat a third of the way along, landscape had a third of the track and stopped at 2:1, and it read as portrait-only. It is now logarithmic and symmetric — 3:1 · 1:1 · 1:3 — with the ends labelled and the current shape shown.

The four frame handles gain content descriptions (a11y, and it lets the harness find them).

## Verified on the emulator

- Trash → prompt → Delete: 3 entries → 2; still 2 after a cold restart; **server tombstones 7 → 8** after the sync the delete triggers.
- Slider tapped near its left end → label `2.48:1` → placed box w/h 2.29.

Tests: two new Rust tests (a soft-deleted entry goes out as a tombstone and then leaves the store; a pulled tombstone forgets the entry and its children).

author: epistex0
body:
Bảng baseline trong `CLAUDE.md` neo vào `f45ba365`+wt của nhánh `docs/flow-maps-and-demo-fixes`. SHA đó **không tồn tại**.

## Cơ chế

Repo merge kiểu `--squash --delete-branch` (§CI). Squash sinh commit mới, nhánh bị xoá — nên mọi SHA của nhánh feature chết ngay khi PR merge. Kiểm cả dãy lịch sử của bảng thì **bảy trong tám SHA cũng vậy**; chỉ `f9fc3a18` còn sống, vì nó vốn là commit squash trên `main`.

Hệ quả: bảng đọc được số nhưng không tra lại được số ấy đo trên cây nào. `CLAUDE.md` tự nói *"bảng rot còn tệ hơn không có bảng"* — đây đúng là dạng rot đó, chỉ ở phần con trỏ thay vì phần số.

## Đã làm

Đo lại thật **cả bảy gate** tại `9bb41f94` (HEAD của `main`) thay vì chỉ sửa con trỏ — đổi SHA mà không đo sẽ khiến số chưa xác minh trông như đã xác minh tại SHA mới. Kết quả trùng khít số cũ, xác nhận squash không đổi nội dung:

| Gate | Kết quả |
|---|---|
| `ruff check src tests` | All checks passed! |
| `ruff format --check src tests` | 600 files already formatted |
| `pytest` | 3295 passed, 2 skipped (240.58s) |
| `pnpm run lint` | 0 error, 2 warning — `inbox/page.tsx:97`, `AiChat.tsx:588` |
| `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` | sạch (exit 0) |
| `pnpm test` | 498 passed (53 file) |
| `pnpm run build` | xanh |

`pytest` mất ~240s thay vì ~156s là chênh do tải máy lúc đo, không phải hồi quy: số test không đổi.

## Thay đổi

- Bảng neo lại vào `9bb41f94` trên `main`, ngày đo 2026-09-03.
- Thêm **luật neo SHA** ngay trong §Baseline: đo trên nhánh thì ghi nhánh, nhưng tới lúc PR merge phải đổi sang SHA squash trên `main`. Không có luật này thì chỗ vừa sửa sẽ rot lại theo đúng cơ chế cũ ngay ở lần cập nhật sau.
- Dãy SHA lịch sử giữ nguyên làm xu hướng, kèm ghi chú rằng chúng không còn là con trỏ.
- `CLAUDE.md` lên v6.

## Phạm vi

Chỉ `CLAUDE.md`, không chạm code. Số đo không đổi (3295 + 498 = **3.793**). **§`Authority` giữ nguyên** — không có thay đổi nào cần owner duyệt lại theo §Protocol evolution.

body:
Two commits, both prompted by the `unauthored_node` finding that shipped in 3.4.0 actually pointing at something.

## `caf5b103` — doctor reports what you can act on

Measured on this repo's own bundle: **23 of doctor's 25 findings were `unadvised_sensitive`, and every one named a task already `done`.** The advice each carries — attach a lens — is unreachable on a closed, gated node, so the report read as a wall with the two actionable findings sitting inside it. A report is read as a worklist whether or not it was written as one.

`unadvised_sensitive` now skips a node whose status is `done`. Type, sensitivity floor, lens presence and the severity split (security `warn`, softer floors `info`) are untouched.

Three calls inside the contract, each carrying a probe:

- **`done` is the ONLY exclusion.** A node in `verify` can still take a lens before its gate; excluding it would hide a finding while it is still actionable.
- **An absent status is not closed** (`R:BLINDCLOSE`). Hiding a finding on a malformed node is the failure this rule guards against, not an instance of it.
- **The closed findings are dropped, not tallied.** A summary line is still a line the reader has to decide to ignore.

On this bundle: **25 findings → 1**, and the survivor is the real `edge_unresolved` defect the noise had been burying.

## `62e157f3` — v3-final-collateral, authored from the work it shipped

Scaffolded 2026-08-11 by `add/3.0.0` and driven to six closed tasks without its CARD or EXIT ever being filled in. Nothing asked: `freeze` did not refuse a template Milestone until `authoring-beat-named` shipped that guard, and `placeholders_in` reads only RULES/ASSUMPTIONS/CHECKS, which a Milestone body does not have. `status` had been pointing at it as live work for three weeks.

**Deletion was considered and rejected on inspection.** Six tasks declare `milestone: v3-final-collateral` and all six are `done`, so removing the node would have traded one warning for six dangling edges. Authored retrospectively from what those six shipped, closed 6/6, archived — the `why:` says out loud that it was written after the fact.

## Verification

`1116 passed, 7 skipped` across both test roots. Task `doctor-nudges-what-you-can-act-on` gated PASS on `runs/1.md` at `freshness: fresh`; `ENGINE_MD5` re-aimed and all four engine twins synced.

One note for the reviewer: my first fixture called `add.doctor(root / ".add")`, which returns `[]` — `doctor` takes the **project** root. That is the "green anchor proving nothing" shape, and it surfaced only because a check asserting *preserved* behaviour was failing when it should have passed.

author: zohaibsundrali
body:
> Depends on **#79** (QA module) — this branch is cut from it. Merge #79 first.

## The process HR had no way to run

`hr` holds thirty-five permissions and had no way to run the one process an HR function exists to run. `employee_profiles.performance` has been a jsonb column since migration 015, described as *"cached rollups (optional)"* — **a place to put an answer, with no process to produce one.** Nothing has ever written to it.

## A review is private until it is shared

This is the rule the whole module turns on.

```
draft  →  submitted  →  shared
   ↑          ↑            ↑
reviewer   reviewer       HR
is writing  finished    decides it's ready
```

A half-written assessment is **not feedback** — it is a draft its author would edit if they knew it was being read. The subject cannot see it until somebody decides it is ready.

Enforced **twice, independently**: the route filters on status, *and* the RLS read policy carries the same clause. These tables are reachable from the browser through PostgREST like every other table here, so a route check alone would be advisory.

## Submitting and sharing are different acts by different people

The reviewer says *"I have finished"*. HR says *"this should be read"*. Collapsing them would mean either HR editing somebody's words, or a reviewer publishing without review. The route refuses a submit from anybody but the author, and a share from anybody without `review.view_all`.

## Nobody reviews themselves

A `CHECK`, not a convention. Self-assessment is a different feature with a different shape, and letting it through this table would make *"who said this"* unanswerable. The reviewer is always the token's own id — `reviewerUserId` is read from the body **nowhere** in the route, and the option is not offered in the picker either.

## A closed cycle still allows sharing

The trigger permits exactly that one edit. **Closing ends the writing, not the reading** — an HR lead who closes the cycle and then shares the reviews is doing the normal thing, and a lock that blocked it would force them to reopen the cycle just to finish.

## Two things left deliberately empty

**No rating is invented.** Nullable, no default. A `3` nobody chose averages into every report as if it meant something. The screen shows an em-dash rather than `0.00` where nothing is rated, and the form's hint says so.

**A goal outlives the cycle that set it.** `cycle_id` is nullable with `ON DELETE SET NULL` — a goal set in one review is often still open in the next, and tying it to the cycle would delete it with the cycle or make it look finished when the cycle closes.

## Permissions

| Key | Roles |
|---|---|
| `review_cycle.manage`, `review.view_all` | owner, admin, hr |
| `review.write`, `goal.manage` | owner, admin, hr, manager, team_lead |
| `review.view_own` | every staff role |

Writing a review is **wider** than running the cycle — a manager and a team lead assess the people they work with. But neither gets `review.view_all`: **a reviewer reads what they wrote**, which RLS grants on *authorship* rather than on a key. Reading everybody's assessment of everybody is a different thing, and it belongs with HR.

## Screens

- **My Reviews** — in both shells, one component. Shared reviews and your goals. The empty state says outright that reviews still being written are not shown, so an absent review does not read as a bug.
- **Performance** (People) — cycles, their progress, and the submit/share workflow.

## Verification

- **2399 tests, 76 files, green.** `next build` OK, `next lint` clean.
- **Mutation tested: ten mutations, all killed** — including dropping the `'shared'` clause from the subject's read policy (the privacy rule), letting the body name the reviewer, letting anyone share, and gating the Performance section on a key every staff role holds (the front door).
- New `tests/performanceReviews.test.js` (32 tests).

## ⚠️ Migrations

Run **`083`** then **`084`**, after 082.

- `083` — three tables, one view, one trigger, six policies. Fully additive; nothing backfilled.
- `084` — mirror re-sync, **409 rows over 89 keys**, upsert only.

## Still open

`productivity.view_own`, `monitoring.view_own` and `team.view_own` have no screen; `reports_to` is still empty (data, not code); Features #7–#10 remain (ATS, capacity, assets, contracts).

## Summary

Bounded theorem note + exact runner + cache on the low-energy content of the coarse-lattice staggered sector: **two tastes of one four-component Dirac field, vector-like, with a single isotropic velocity and a free massless Dirac equal-time propagator.** It settles a reading question raised on PR #7844 during the vacuum panel: the 2x2x1 magnetic cell has band function `H4^2 = (6 + 2 cos Q1 + 2 cos Q2 + 2 cos 2Q3) I` with exactly two 4-fold nodes, which the 2x2x2 cell folds onto its single 8-fold point, so the landed count of eight is right and the four-dimensional factor of "spin(2) x taste(4)" is a chirality pair times a taste pair (`X = -i m1 m2 m3 = I x T` exactly): `8 = 2 (Weyl) x 2 (chiralities) x 2 (tastes)`, net chirality zero.

- `docs/EMERGENT_LORENTZ_INVARIANCE_AT_THE_DIRAC_POINT_AND_THE_TASTE_CENSUS_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-09-03.md` (329 lines)
- `scripts/emergent_lorentz_invariance_at_the_dirac_point_and_the_taste_census_check_2026_09_03.py` (`TOTAL: PASS=18 FAIL=0`, 3.7 s)
- `logs/runner-cache/emergent_lorentz_invariance_at_the_dirac_point_and_the_taste_census_check_2026_09_03.txt`

## Theorems

- **T1** the magnetic cell and its two nodes (exact band function; exhaustive scan; the folding identity).
- **T2** the chirality census: `2R + 2L` Weyl, `N_f = 2` four-component Dirac, vector-like (Nielsen-Ninomiya); the relabelling of PR #7844's factorisation (a correction of reading, not of any number); torus zero-mode counts 8, 0, 8 from `4 | L`.
- **T3** the exact dispersion `E(pi+p)^2 = |p|^2 - (1/12) sum p_a^4 + (1/360) sum p_a^6 + O(p^8)`: one velocity `v -> 1` in every direction, every taste, both chiralities, no free parameter; the leading anisotropy is the unique quartic cubic invariant, spread `|p|^2/36`; the taste-mixing term is `O(p^2)` and a spin singlet.
- **T4** the propagator: `P_vu = 0` exactly off the one-odd-component set (an identity of the projector), and `|P_vu| |r|^3 -> (4/pi^2)|nhat_a|`, the free massless Dirac equal-time kernel in three spatial dimensions, matched to `0.1 %` at `|r| = 60` to `90` on a `288^3` momentum grid.

- No chiral sector; no generations from tastes (`N_f = 2` identical copies); not a proof of Lorentz symmetry of correlators (isotropy of the one-particle dispersion and one equal-time kernel only); coarse lattice only (the fine `(4,2,2)` pattern's tetragonal anisotropy is not examined). author: trekin-geoalert
body:
load_results, download_results_file and download_aoi_file join the other processings-table
actions. The fork that made load_results look awkward dissolves on the way: it branches to
enter_template, which is that controller's own method, so there is no cross-controller call left
to design around. _open_template was a one-line forwarder to exactly that and is deleted.

This corrects the plan, not just the code. The WAL assigned these three to a ResultService in
Phase D. That is the wrong home for them: they read the table selection, read the tiles/local
radio and prompt for a working directory, all of which is controller work. What Phase D should
move is ResultsLoader in layer_utils - the requests, the layer building, the styles - which these
delegate to. Both WAL entries now say so.

The start-fork item is closed rather than deferred, with the reason recorded. Moving that fork
requires moving template_to_run, which planned_processing_selection_error calls, which
update_processing_cost calls - and one of *that* method's callers is AreaCalculatorService, a
service, which cannot compute a template and should not know templates exist. Threading the
parameter through it, or duplicating the rule, both make the design worse than leaving it.
template_to_run reaches into no other service, so it is not a layering violation; the seam that
made the item urgent was deleted in 2c.

Eleven tests. The behavioral suite already drives the happy path end to end but never reaches the
guards, and two of them encode decisions that look like inconsistencies worth "fixing":

Tiles must NOT require a working directory. That route adds a remote layer and writes nothing, so
gating it would stop a user with no directory from viewing results they can perfectly well view.
The test asks for tiles with the directory check failing, so restoring the gate fails loudly.

download_aoi_file deliberately has no status check, unlike the other two. An AOI exists as soon as
the processing does, and it is most wanted when the run failed - often *because* it failed.
Aligning it with its neighbours would remove the feature's main use.

## Manual test
Double-click a finished processing: with "tiles" selected the result layer appears; with "local
file" it downloads into the working directory first. Double-click a planned processing (template)
row and it opens the template instead of loading anything. Try either on a failed processing:
refused with "only the results of correctly finished processing can be loaded". With no working
directory configured, the local route asks for one and "Later" cancels the load - but the tiles
route must still work without one. From the context menu, "Save result" writes the GeoJSON, and
"Download AOI" works even for a failed processing, asking for a directory first. Regression
surface: the Download button and double-click share this handler, so check both.

## Summary

- document the safe admission boundary for the indexed-vector phase of #9 without enabling distributed indexed routing
- add an executable Lance IVF regression proving that default adaptive probes change semantics under fragment-local execution
- verify fixed probe counts in the counterexample and lock default probes, fixed probes, refinement, and partial coverage to `FINAL_SEARCH` for this phase

Lance uses adaptive IVF probing when `nprobs` is omitted. body:
## 病因

日曆的現在時間線用 `.now` 這個類別，而卡片上「今天到期」的日期是 `class="dd now"`，兩者撞名。

```css
.now{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;height:0;border-top:2px solid var(--bad);z-index:5}
.now::before{...紅點...}
```

這條規則套到卡片的日期元素上，就變成一條橫貫整個畫面的紅線加一顆紅點。而且 `.t` / `.col` / `.cols` 都沒有 `position`，所以 `left:0;right:0` 一路算到視窗，「今天」那兩個字才會跑到側邊欄上面。有幾件今天到期的任務就有幾條線。

## 修法

現在時間線改名 `.nowline`。順手修了同一類的另一處：日曆表頭的 `.dn` 與 `.wd` 也是裸類別，會套到統計那格的 `<em class="dn">`（專注時間的增減百分比），改成 `.chead` 底下才生效。

## 驗證

`drag.test.js` 加的不是單點測試，是通則：掃出卡片會輸出的所有類別（`now`、`over`、`live`、`pA`…共 20 個），跟 CSS 裡所有「裸類別且 `position` 為 `absolute`/`fixed`」的規則（7 個）比對，撞名就失敗並指名是哪一個。

驗證過它會抓到這個 bug——把 `.nowline` 改回 `.now` 再跑，測試失敗並印出「卡片用的類別跟會脫離文件流的裸 CSS 規則撞名了：now」。

四支都通過：

```
node worklog/test/board.test.js && node worklog/test/migrate.test.js && \
node worklog/test/drag.test.js && node worklog/test/perf.test.js
```

僅改動 `index.html` 與測試，`Code.gs` 未變。

author: cb1kenobi
body:
Batch A of the overnight run. Three tickets that all live in the same surface — `src/components/docs/*`, `globals.css`, and the markdown pipeline — so they share one build and one verification pass.

## TI-10 — typography, prose, code blocks

The registry carries **2,034 fenced code blocks** (1,372 JavaScript, 609 Alloy XML, the rest HTML/JSON/shell) and none were highlighted, because no highlighter was installed.

- **Shiki**, constructed synchronously from static grammar imports on the JavaScript RegExp engine rather than the oniguruma WASM one. Both matter more since TI-25 made these on-demand renders: the highlighter is built inside the serverless function now. 6ms to construct, 33ms to render every prose field on the worst page in the corpus.
- **Highlighting runs after sanitizing.** Shiki colours each token with an inline `style`, and `renderMarkdown` also renders third-party module READMEs — letting its output through the sanitizer would mean allowing `span[style]` for whoever wrote that README. Callouts work the same way, so neither needed the sanitizer loosened by a single tag.
- **The palette corrects itself.** GitHub's themes were designed against GitHub's backgrounds; three colours the corpus produces missed AA on `--color-surface`, worst the dark comment grey at **2.77:1**. Every foreground is now nudged at construction until it clears 4.5:1, and `check:contrast` covers the syntax palette and asserts the surface constants still match `globals.css`.
- Callouts use GitHub's alert syntax (`> [!NOTE]`), plus `DEPRECATED` which this ticket asks for and GitHub lacks. No content uses them yet — they are for TI-32 and the guides, covered by tests rather than by content.
- Copy buttons enhance the DOM after mount, so a reader without JavaScript sees selectable code rather than a dead button.

### 320px

Verified across twelve pages. Three causes, none of them the code blocks everyone suspected:

| cause | cost |
|---|---|
| member headings had `break-words` but no `min-w-0` | 324px in a 288px column |
| inline `<code>` holding a fully-qualified identifier | wider than the viewport |
| ti.map's apidoc has a bare 74-char URL as plain text | 283px on its own |

All twelve pages now measure **0px** of horizontal overflow at 320px.

## TI-26 — API page rendering

Audited against all nine criteria on a running build. Inherited markers, platform badges, deprecation, `since`, sanitized prose, resolved cross-references and scrolling tables were already correct. Two were not:

- **Duplicate ids.** `Titanium.UI.Window` has a method `open()` and an event `open`, both emitting `id="open"` — invalid HTML, and the event was not deep-linkable at all. `toc.tsx` had already documented that 41 types declare a property and an event under one name; the anchors never followed. Anchors are now allocated per page across all three groups and keyed on the *member*, not its name. The first group keeps the bare anchor so cross-references from other pages still land somewhere sensible; later ones take a suffix. Nine SDK and module pages now carry 0 duplicates where two did.
- **Unresolved cross-references** (`<PullView>`, `<Ti.UI.Component.property>`) are source defects, not rendering ones. Left for TI-60 rather than papered over.

## TI-27 — version switcher

Twenty versions have been reachable since TI-25 with no way between them.

Real links in a `<details>`, so it works with scripting off. Each option is existence-checked against that version's compiled index, and the ones with nowhere to land are marked rather than hidden or linked into a 404 — measured against the only two types where this happens, `Titanium.UI.iOS.ButtonConfiguration` (added after 12.5.0) and `Titanium.UI.iOS.SystemButtonStyle` (removed after it).

**Not done here:** the module half. Modules version independently per platform — ti.map is android 5.7.0 and iOS 7.3.1 simultaneously — and module routes carry no platform segment today, so that wants settling against TI-31's URL shape rather than guessing.

## Checks

190 tests, lint, tsc, contrast gate, and the offline build all pass. Static output 72.8MB and the docs function 37MB, both still well inside the caps TI-25 established.

author: victor-zzh
body:
## 背景
成员筛选此前只能从团队页「管理密钥」带 `?member_id=` 跳进来，密钥页上没有筛选入口——换个成员看、或者看看没归属的 key，都只能回团队页再跳一次。

## 改动
常驻筛选栏（搜索框 + 三个下拉 + 「清除筛选」）：

| 维度 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 名称/前缀 | 250ms 防抖，复用列表已有的 keyword 谓词（name / key_hint / id） |
| 分组 | 取「我可用的分组」，与新建密钥同源；已下架分组上的存量 key 在不筛选时仍在列表里 |
| 成员 | 全部 / 各成员 / 未归属（哨兵 `__unassigned__`，语义同账号页 `UNGROUPED_GROUP_FILTER`）。**主账号没有成员时整个选择器不渲染**，普通用户界面不变 |
| 状态 | 启用 / 停用 / 已过期 |

**状态口径**跟表格展示对齐——表格里过期优先于启用/停用显示（`displayStatus = isExpired ? 'expired' : status`），所以 `active`/`disabled` 都排除已过期，`expired` 不看 status（停用且过期的 key 在表格里同样显示「已过期」，筛选也应能选出它）。

后端 `ListFilter` 增 `GroupID` / `Status` / `MemberUnassigned`，连同原有成员筛选统一收进 `applyAPIKeyFilters`；`member_id` 与 `member_unassigned` 同时给出时以 `member_id` 为准。查询参数走 dto 校验，`status` 只接受 `active|disabled|expired`，非法值 400。

团队页跳转仍带 `?member_id=`，现在只是把成员筛选**预置**好；「清除筛选」会一并把 URL 参数去掉，否则 URL→筛选的同步会把成员装回来。该同步用**渲染期修正状态**而非 `useEffect`——少一次带旧筛选的渲染，也不触发 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` 告警。

顺带去掉三个筛选下拉里与 `aria-label` 重复的 `sr-only` Label（读屏会把标签词念两遍），与用量页的写法对齐。

## 验证
- store 层 11 例表驱动测试：各维度、叠加（成员+分组 / 成员+状态 / 关键词+分组）、`member_id` 优先级、越权隔离（别人的 key 任何筛选都不出现）。
- 本地起真实二进制跑 HTTP 冒烟 **19/19**：6 把样本 key 覆盖两成员/两分组/过期/停用，逐条比对返回集合；含非法 status → 400、分页 `total` 跟随筛选。
- Playwright 走查：筛选栏渲染、成员筛选、成员+分组组合、搜索防抖、状态=已过期、清除筛选、团队页深链预置、同路由再导航（点侧边栏「我的密钥」）后筛选正确重置。
- `go test ./...` 全绿、`make lint`、type-check、vitest 五包一致。

author: humiley
body:
The company publishes all of this in SharePoint already — an **OUR LIBRARY** board of seven tiles, a **WIKI** page on the HR site, and a **Knowledge Hub** on the Learning Management System site. None of it was reachable from the portal, so people left the portal to find any of it.

Three pages under a new **Library** app that every account can open (no `data-roles` — a wiki nobody below manager can read is not a wiki):

| Page | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Our Library** | The board, in the order SharePoint publishes it |
| **Company Wiki** | The wiki page, plus its document library browsed in place |
| **Knowledge Hub** | The same for the LMS site, with the L&D links an admin already maintains for the dashboard rather than a second list of them |

## Nothing here stores a document

The board carries links, and the two hub pages read the libraries live through Microsoft Graph with the reader's **own delegated token** — the same resolver a project's Documents tab uses (`_pmSpToken` / `_pmSpCtx` / `_pmSpResolve`, reused, not re-implemented).

SharePoint stays the single source and **its** permissions still decide what each person sees, because the request is made as the reader: a folder somebody cannot open in SharePoint is a folder they cannot open here. The cost is that browsing needs a live Microsoft session, and the pages say so rather than rendering an empty list.

That last part is most of the work. *"You are not signed in"*, *"no library is configured"*, *"that address is not SharePoint"*, *"SharePoint did not answer"* and *"this folder is empty"* are **one blank list on screen and five different facts**, only one of which the reader can act on — so each says its own sentence, and only the fixable one offers a button.

## A file name is a link

A file row is an `<a href target="_blank" rel="noopener">`, not a button calling `window.open`. The two look identical and only one gives the reader the destination on hover, middle-click, ctrl-click, and a right-click menu with *open in new tab* and *copy link address*. SharePoint's own viewer then previews or downloads it; the portal stays open behind. A folder means two things and is not asked to guess: the row opens it **here** (breadcrumbs), the arrow beside it opens the same folder **in SharePoint**.

## Five tiles ship with no link, on purpose

IT Knowledge Page · PMO – Project Template · Project Management Hub · Learning Management System · Training Hub.

Those addresses were never given, and a guessed link that 404s wastes more time than a tile saying it needs one. They render **marked, not hidden** — a board that silently drops a row reads as "we do not have one". A manager fills them in at **HR Admin → Company Portal**.

## Server side

Four addresses and two content lists, and every way that breaks is quiet:

- `wikiPageUrl` / `wikiSpUrl` / `knowledgePageUrl` / `knowledgeSpUrl` — admin-only to change like every other integration URL, read back to everyone (staff are who the wiki is *for*), and defaulted in **`_APPR_SETTING_DEFAULTS` as well as `_portal_get`**. A GET default the save path does not know about 403s a manager for a change nobody made, because the form echoes back what it was sent.
- `library` / `wiki` join `PORTAL_KEYS` as list content beside `resources`, so they go through the same `_crm_sanitize` strip every company-wide list gets.

## Tests

- **`tests/test_library_settings.py`** (7) — the round-trip, including the manager-echo case and the admin-only refusal.
- **`tests/library_docs_panel.js`** (41, wired into CI) — the panels themselves, which nothing else can reach: no development machine has a Microsoft session, so every local look falls into the demo branch and the listing code never runs — and a render that throws is an empty panel that reads as *"there are no documents"*.

It also pins the escaping. A file name is chosen by anyone who can upload to the library and lands inside a JS string inside an `onclick` attribute; `_tkEscA` escapes `&` and `"` only, so `foo'+alert(1)+'.pdf` closed the string and ran. `_libArg` escapes for both parsers, and the test **executes the handler a browser would build**: the injected call must not fire *and* the name must arrive unchanged — over-escaping would open the wrong folder for `Q3 forecast's.xlsx`, and nobody would call that a fix.

## Verified

Full `pytest` suite, every i18n gate (`vi_duplicate_keys`, `missing`, `ortho-scan`, `ortho-platform`, `domwrites`), `check_index_js`, `no_duplicate_functions`, and the adjacent JS gates. Both languages and mobile checked in the browser. `hml-pwa-v734`, above `main` (v733) and every open PR.

author: dariomory
body:
Fixes #2

`hitTestLayer` rejected any pixel with alpha below 10. A text raster is mostly transparent between the glyphs, so unless you grabbed a letter stroke exactly, the layer slipped out from under the cursor. Text layers are now picked by their bounding box instead.

```diff
+    // Text rasters are mostly transparent between glyphs, so a per-pixel alpha
+    // test makes them slip out from under the cursor. Their bounding box is the
+    // grabbable area instead.
+    if (layer.kind === "text" || layer.role === "text") return layer;
```

Image and paint layers keep the per-pixel test, so clicking through the transparent part of a photo layer still behaves as before.

**Trade-off worth knowing:** a text layer now captures clicks across its whole box, gaps included. Picking a layer underneath means clicking outside the text bounds. That is the usual bargain for making text grabbable, and it is the behaviour the issue asks for.

## Verification

Driven in a browser against the running editor: place a text layer, switch to Move, drag starting from a gap *between* two letters, then sample the canvas. The origin reads white and the drop point reads dark, so the layer followed the drag. Before the change that same drag did nothing.

`pnpm test` (21) and `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` are clean.

Branched off `master` and independent of #13, so the two can merge in either order.

author: kevin-patyk
body:
Resolves https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/29104.

In `get_arithmetic_field`, `Operator::Plus` branch had an explicit `(Decimal, Decimal)` arm returning `Decimal(DEC128_MAX_PREC, max_scale)`, but `(Decimal, integer)` fell through to the `try_get_supertype` catch-all. This returns the decimal's original precision whenever the integer's max value fits (`i8::MAX` fits in `Decimal(18, 4)`, so the planner reported `Decimal(18, 4)`. 

However, the engine always emits `DEC128_MAX_PREC` for decimal addition, giving `Decimal(38, 4)`. The fix adds a `(Decimal, Integer)` arm to the `Plus` branch that mirrors the engine and is consistent with the existing `(Decimal, Decimal)` arm.
