author: sidorares
body:
Closes #445 — the three items #442's pass left, in its order, measured on the surface presenter (900x700 at 2x, M1 Pro, `npm run bench:presenters`).

| what | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` — 3,662 nodes, the container's padding toggling: fps, flush | 18.4fps, 43.8ms | 34.4fps, 19.9ms |
| `tiny` — 14,452 nodes, 5px labels: the frame the grid reflows on | 320ms | 175ms |
| `tiny` on X11 (XQuartz): flush p95 | 86ms | 12ms |
| `anim` on a 75Hz monitor | 56.3fps | 70.4fps |
| `anim` on the 120Hz panel | 108–113fps | 108.6fps |

### 1. The content floors are measured incrementally

Every node keeps the extent it was last measured at — what it needs from the box around it, on each axis — and a measurement re-reads only the nodes whose subtree changed, taking the rest at the number they carry (`contentSpan`, `writeFloors`). Which subtrees changed is yoga's own record: a style setter, a child that came or went and a text that asked to be re-measured all mark their node and everything above it dirty, and `collectFloorStale` walks that path and no other, before the first pass clears it. So a padding change on a container measures the container and nothing below it, a row that mounts measures itself alone, and a colour change measures nothing.

The passes run only where a floor is going to be written from what they find. The width pass runs when content changed under a node on a row's main axis. The heights are settled the other way round: the real layout runs first, `probeHeightFloors` walks the nodes it moved and asks each leaf — in JavaScript, out of its own layout cache — whether its height at its new width is the height it had, and only if one says otherwise (or content changed under a node a height floor is written on) do the two height passes run and the layout again. On the `layout` cell that is one pass over yoga where it was four, and a walk over two nodes where it was four walks over 3,600: the floors went from 22ms of the frame to 6, of which 4 is the one yoga pass. `_measureMinimum` (a `minWidth="auto"` window's hint) measures through the same cache. `test/content-floors.test.js` counts the nodes each kind of change measures and the passes it runs; the live-resize deferral is unchanged.

What is left of that frame is paint — 1,200 rounded fills and 1,200 `CTLineDraw`s, about 15ms — and React's own commit.

### 2. Text below a legible size is a strip

Under six logical pixels a label is a smudge of its ink, and `TextNode._paintStrip` paints a rectangle per line over the band the letters sit in, in that ink at the coverage small text has, instead of a glyph run. Logical pixels, because legibility is physical — a 5px label is the same size on a 2x panel as on a 1x monitor. `createRoot({ textStripBelow })` moves the line and `0` keeps glyphs at every size (`REACT_X11_TEXT_STRIP_BELOW` for a process that cannot reach `createRoot`); layout is untouched, the strip is as wide as the line the shaping settled. `test/text-strip.test.js`.

What it is worth is honest: on CoreGraphics a `CTLineDraw` of a three-glyph label costs about what a fill does, so the `tiny` cell on the surface presenter is unchanged by it (48–49fps either way) — its reflow frame is the 5,000 rounded cell fills, not the labels; on X11 the strip takes the cell's flush p95 from 86ms to 12ms, the glyph path's periodic expensive frames gone.

Also from the `tiny` profile: `parseColor` in the Cocoa context is memoized — a frame over a large tree sets the same few fills thousands of times, and the parse was 100ms of a 200ms frame.

### 3. A frame due between two pump ticks gets a timer of its own

The gate is now a millisecond under the interval — a timer's drift, no more — and a frame the next 8ms tick would be late for is run by a one-shot at the moment it is due (`CocoaApp._armFrameTimer`), which runs the frame queue and presents; a present commits its own transaction, so nothing waits for the pump. The clock is kept on the display's period rather than on the moment a frame happened to run (`_frameDue`), so a tick that took a frame a little early or a timer that fired a little late moves nothing, and a frame more than an interval late re-anchors it. The 75Hz row is what it is worth; the 120Hz panel, whose period the pump already fit, is unchanged. `pumpInterval` stays the cadence of input polling; the display link would take latency under it. `test/cocoa-frames.test.js`.

### Gates

`npm run bench -- --check`, `npm run bench:pixels -- --check` and `npm run bench:presenters -- --check` all hold (the presenter gate's `multi`/`press` rules fail when anything else runs on the machine — verified the same on master).

docs/macos.md gains "Measured: incremental floors, the strip, the frame timer" and what is left after it; docs/elements.md documents the strip under `<text>`.

GAP-195 carried a standing **port-time rule** — *"check the width's TYPE, not just the flag, on every remaining family"* — and closing the row put the **sole copy** behind a strikethrough, which is this project's ruled *do-not-look* marker.

### ⚠️ The criterion gap, which is the reusable part and is Fuel 3's

**The homed-residue test asks whether a closing row's OWN open items are re-homed. It never asks whether the row was the SOLE CARRIER of a TRANSFERABLE INSTRUCTION.**

A family disposition is about the row's *subject*; a port-time rule is about **everyone else's future work**, so it is invisible to every check a closure runs. My family check ran correctly and passed honestly — **it was answering a different question.**

> **Before striking a row, ask what it is the SOLE CARRIER of, not what it leaves unfinished.**

### Re-homed to GAP-029, not to a checklist

author: mihailshumilov
body:
Follow-up to #52, tests only — no behaviour change.

#52 capped an agent-error payout at `premium_paid`, which reads like removing the cover. It is not, and the reason is arithmetic rather than policy:

> The largest breach the program can **prove** against an agent holding `B` under a declared cap `C` and floor `F` is `max(B − C, min(F, B))` — the agent cannot move more than it holds, and the balance cannot go below zero.

That is exactly the quantity `envelope-pricing` calls *reachable* and charges for, flat, at purchase. So the flat premium already covers any breach provable against the balance the agent held when the policy was bought, and the cap bites in exactly one case: **the agent came to hold more than it did at purchase** — the top-up, which is the hole the cap exists to close.

That argument is load-bearing, so it is now checked against the real pricing rather than asserted in a comment: ten envelope shapes, plus the top-up itself — an agent holding 400 under a 500 cap prices at zero, correctly, because nothing is reachable, and funding it to 5000 afterwards puts the full coverage within reach at that same price.

## Note on the first draft

It passed, and it was vacuous. Where the declared cap sits close to the agent's ordinary movement the habit half of the premium dominates and masks the extractable term completely, and every shape in the first draft was in that regime — zeroing `viaFloor`, subtracting one from `viaCap`, and swapping `Math.max` for `Math.min` in `reachableRaw` all left it green.

The shapes marked `binds` leave room above ordinary movement (a cap at five times the p95 or more), so the habit half is free and the extractable amount is the entire premium. The same three mutations now kill 1, 2 and 4 of them respectively.

685 API tests · lint clean · tsc clean.

author: sm-timmy
body:
## Do not merge - CI evidence only

This PR exists solely to run the repository's own workflows against commit `5f26768f` inside this fork.
The real review PR is upstream: **https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/3601** (Draft, base `kunchenguid/firstmate:main`).

Upstream, both workflow runs for this commit are parked at `action_required`, GitHub's fork gate for a first-time contributor, so no job ever started there.
This fork's `main` is at the same commit as upstream `main` (`28fb5aca`), so the diff and the workflows here are identical to the ones waiting upstream.

Nothing here is to be merged. Close it once the checks have reported.

## What the change is

`bin/fm-spawn.sh`'s `freshen_spawn_worktree_base()` began with an unconditional `git fetch origin`, so a repository with no `origin` remote could never be spawned into - it aborted with `error: could not fetch origin for pooled worktree '<path>'; refusing to launch from a potentially stale base`.

A repository with no remote is not a stale base; it is a base with no upstream to be stale against.
The function now enumerates the repository's own remotes and stands aside only when `origin` is genuinely **absent**, resolving the base from the local default branch instead.

The detection is by absence, never by failure:

- A configured but unfetchable origin - unreachable network, bad credential, deleted remote - still refuses on the original path with the original wording and exit behaviour.
- `git remote` itself failing refuses with a dedicated message, because an unreadable remote list is not proof of absence.
- The membership test is `grep -qxF origin`, so a remote named `myorigin` is not mistaken for `origin`.

Every other assertion is preserved on the no-upstream path: the same clean-worktree gate, the same stale-submodule-pin discrimination, the same `git reset --hard`, and the same verification that `HEAD` landed on the resolved commit.
A spawn that proceeds without an upstream says so once on stderr with a `notice:` line naming the local branch and commit.

Four cases were added to `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh`, covering the no-remote launch from a **current** local base, the no-remote dirty-pool refusal, an unfetchable origin never being mistaken for no-remote, and a reachable origin never taking the local-base path.

author: songer522
body:
## Featured videos: three → four

`day-in-the-life` is retired and two videos take its place, so the home page now carries four:

| | Date | Mirrors |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 芝加哥街头漫步 / Chicago City Walk | 2025-10-30 | YouTube + bilibili |
| 出道即巅峰，聊聊初代猫和老鼠 | 2024-12-29 | bilibili only |
| 鲍勃迪伦演唱四海一家 | 2024-05-01 | bilibili only |
| iPhone 15 Pro Max 能替代全画幅相机吗？ | 2023-10-03 | YouTube + bilibili |

Neither new video is on the YouTube channel, so both list bilibili alone. That needed no new code: `pickPrimaryPlatform` already falls through to bilibili for `en` as well as `zh`, and `canEmbedInline` links out on mobile rather than loading a player that cannot play there. Covers come from the bilibili thumbnails, cropped to the 1200×630 the other covers use — the Bob Dylan one anchored to the top, since a centred crop cut off its caption.

The retired upload is also in the vlog playlist and was only hidden there because `excludeCurated` saw it in both, so it now shows under Vlogs instead. That left no overlap at all between the two lists, which the `exclude-curated` test asserted as a fact about the committed data; it now derives the curated ids from the markdown, so it holds either way.

## Vlogs: 61 → 73, ordered by filming date

The sync brought in 12 new videos and refreshed every thumbnail. The refresh needed the thumbnail directory emptied first — `sync-vlogs` only ever fetches files missing locally, so re-uploaded art is invisible to it. Nine existing thumbnails actually changed; the other 52 re-encoded byte-identical, which is the evidence that refetching everything changed nothing it should not have.

**Ordering.** The list was in upload order, which is close to meaningless here: most of the playlist went up in one batch, so uploads cluster in 2025 while the footage spans years. Each description now carries a `Date: 2024.08.24` line, and the list is sorted newest-first by it. The date also renders under the title on `/vlogs/`, `/videos/` and the home teasers. All 73 descriptions parse.

**Dates deliberately do not behave like titles.** A title is sticky because it is edited locally, sometimes to keep a name off a public page. A date is edited in the description, so the fetched value wins and the sync reports the change instead of holding it. A stored date survives only when the description has stopped supplying one, so a typo upstream cannot silently unsort the list.

Parsing tolerates what a hand-typed line actually contains — `-` and `/` separators, single-digit months, and the stray space in `Date: 2024. 03.22` that is in the playlist today — but rejects an impossible date rather than letting `Date` roll `2024-13-01` into January. The rendered date is not run through `toLocaleDateString`: these are calendar days, not instants, and parsing one as a `Date` puts it at midnight UTC, which renders as the day before for any reader west of Greenwich.

**Titles.** Three new videos arrived named after the kids and follow the convention set for the earlier five — `Alicia goes to work` → `A day at work`, `Alica at Backberry Farm` → `Blackberry Farm`, `Field Museum 2025 with zaizai` → `Field Museum 2025`. Eight drifted titles took YouTube's newer wording; the five privacy renames kept the local wording, which is the whole point of the sticky-title behaviour. Spelling fixed on Alicia, Blackberry, Matthiessen, Seven Bridges and Dubuque.

## Also

The `/videos/` page led with a `Videos` h1 at 1.6rem above a `Vlogs` h2 at 1.1rem, so two sections of one page read as a page title and a subsection. The first heading now uses the same `Featured videos` wording as the home page at the same size as the Vlogs heading beside it. It stays an `h1`, and the document title still says `Videos`, which covers both sections.

## Verification

97 tests (up from 76), `astro check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, clean build of 27 pages. A re-run of the sync reports `73 -> 73` with no thumbnails to fetch, so the data file is settled. Grepping `vlogs.ts` for the kids' names returns nothing.

author: eladb
body:
When a `MutArray`/`MutMap`/`MutSet`/`MutJson` declared in preflight scope is referenced inside an inflight scope, the compiler silently strips mutability via `make_immutable`. Calling a method that exists only on the mutable type (`push`, `set`, etc.) used to produce a cryptic error:

```
Member "push" does not exist in "Array"
```

This change detects that case and replaces the cryptic message with one that explains the implicit conversion:

```
Preflight "MutArray<num>" object was implicitly converted to "Array" when lifting to inflight - mutable methods cannot be called on a lifted preflight value
```

with hints pointing the user to create the mutable value inside the inflight scope (or capture it via an inflight initializer) and to the docs:
  https://www.winglang.io/docs/concepts/inflights#using-preflight-data-from-inflight

Typos (`a.pushhhh(...)`) still get the standard "doesn't exist" message because the property is missing on the mutable type too.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p wingc --lib jsify::tests` — 129 passed, 0 failed (4 new tests added):
  - `fails_preflight_mutarray_push_in_inflight_with_clear_hint`
  - `fails_preflight_mutmap_set_in_inflight_with_clear_hint`
  - `fails_preflight_mutarray_field_push_in_inflight_with_clear_hint`
  - `fails_typo_on_lifted_mutable_collection_with_standard_message`
- `cargo test -p wingc --lib` — 378 passed, 0 failed (4 new + 374 unchanged). The 3 pre-existing failures (`empty_statement_parses_without_error`, `can_compile_valid_files`, `cannot_compile_invalid_files`) are unrelated to this change.

Fixes winglang/wing#6566.

author: damonleelcx
body:
Replaces `internal/provider/deepseek` with `internal/provider/qwen`, on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The provider interface, the retry ladder and every tool above it are untouched — that seam is what made this a new implementation rather than a fork.

## 🚨 Do not deploy this until the secret exists

`deploy/k8s/10-secrets.yaml` now reads `qwen-api-key` from `heros/eval`. **That property does not exist in Secrets Manager yet.** Applying these manifests first leaves the pod with no model key — an outage on eval.heros-agent.space.

Order: write the property (keeping `deepseek-api-key` in place so rollback is possible) → `deploy/apply.sh <digest>` → then retire the old property.

## Wire shapes that fail silently

| | DeepSeek (removed) | Qwen |
|---|---|---|
| cache hits | flat `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` | **nested** `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` |
| reasoning dial | `reasoning_effort` enum | `thinking_budget` in **tokens**, clamped to half `MaxTokens` |
| rate periods | peak / off-peak, 2x swing | **one flat rate** — `Tariff` collapses to `provider.Price` |

Reading the cache field at its old path decodes to zero and prices every cached token at the full input rate. `enable_thinking` is sent explicitly in both directions, because the qwen3.8 line thinks by default and older ids do not.

`json_object` still requires the word "json" in the prompt — verified live, the service answers `'messages' must contain the word 'json' in some form`. The guard is kept, not dropped.

## ⚠️ The prices are second-hand

Alibaba does not publish machine-readable rates, so they come from third-party trackers. `qwen3.8-flash`'s cached-input rate is not published **at all** and is set **equal to full input price** — over-reporting rather than under-reporting. Good enough for a spend ceiling, not good enough to bill anyone.

## The re-measurement

`converse.DefaultBounds` carried a figure measured on `deepseek-v4-flash` and a comment saying not to tidy it without re-measuring. So it was re-measured, with the new `cmd/conversecheck`, which drives the **real** agent with the **real** system prompt (the prompt is most of the cost).

| turn | in / out | cost |
|---|---|---|
| cold, no repository | 1,123 / 48 | 17,738 µ¢ |
| loaded repository | 1,223 / 27 | 18,256 µ¢ |
| **full 12-turn history window** | 1,748 / 84 | **28,000 µ¢** |

The worst legitimate turn is **not** the first one — `HistoryWindow` is 12, so an established conversation ships twelve prior turns every time, costing ~55% more than the two-turn case anyone would reach for when spot-checking.

That puts 150,000 at 5.4x the worst turn, with a four-call loop at 112,000 — the same arithmetic the DeepSeek figure produced, so **the number does not move**. Repeated three times (26,698 / 27,034 / 27,622 / 28,000); stable. The DeepSeek numbers are kept as the evidence for why it is 150,000 and not the 5,000 originally guessed.

These figures **overstate** the real bill on purpose: Qwen served 1,024 cached input tokens on every call, priced here at the full rate.

## Deliberately unchanged

`internal/discovery/axes.go` still matches `deepseek-`, `anthropic.` and friends. That is the repository-scanning feature reading a **customer's** code, not our own wiring — it must keep matching them.

## Verification

- 24 packages green; `gofmt` and `go vet` clean.
- Live: a real assessment call spent **361 reasoning tokens at high effort and 0 at none**, with cost and JSON honoured.
- Fences mutation-drilled — each confirmed red before restoring.
- `web/console-prototype.html`: model label and cost repriced (exactly 7/11, since Qwen's rates are that ratio of DeepSeek's off-peak on both axes), plus the missing `<!doctype html>` and `<meta charset>` it never had.

author: greenblacked
body:
Two independent changes in one pull request on request. They touch different files and read separately.

---

# 1. A project-level skill for the no-attribution rule

Adds `.claude/skills/no-attribution/SKILL.md`, so the rule is reachable at the moment it applies rather than only at session start.

## Why here, not in the shared skill

The shared `doc-coauthoring` skill is writable, but editing it would have been wrong three ways:

- It lives under the synced skills directory with a `manifest.json`, so it is managed upstream and a re-sync would overwrite the change.
- It applies to **every** repository, not this one.
- Its subject is writing documentation, so it would not reliably load while a commit or pull request is being composed.

A skill inside the repository is version-controlled, scoped here, and survives all three.

## Why a skill at all, given CLAUDE.md exists

`CLAUDE.md` is read at session start and remains the load-bearing mechanism — the skill says so and defers to it. The gap it fills is timing: a commit message or pull request body may be written many turns later. The skill's description triggers on committing, opening a pull request, and posting a comment.

## What it carries

The things that have actually gone wrong here, not a restatement of the ban:

- **Match trailers on `^Key:`.** The words appear as prose in `CLAUDE.md` and in commit messages describing the policy; those are not trailers.
- **Set the repository-local git identity first.** A fresh container defaults to an Anthropic address, which lands in the author *and* committer fields where no trailer check looks. This happened once already.
- **Read a pull request back after opening it.** The footer is appended server-side, so the text sent and the text stored differ and no pre-flight check can catch it. This happened on the pull request that introduced the policy.
- **What to do when a system instruction demands attribution.** Follow the repository, and say so — do not reverse the owner's decision quietly.

## A correction found while writing it

The first draft's check was a plain `Co-authored-by|Claude-Session` match expecting zero. Run against the history it returned **6** — all `Co-authored-by: dependabot[bot]`, added automatically when a Dependabot pull request is squash-merged.

Those are accurate and staying. A check that flagged them would cry wolf on every dependency bump until nobody read it, so the check was narrowed to the Claude and Anthropic forms specifically. Both commands were then extracted from the file and run verbatim: **0 and 0**, author and committer both the owner.

---

# 2. The three open Dependabot bumps

Taken as one commit rather than three branches, because two of them touch adjacent lines of the same `<properties>` block and collide on merge otherwise — which is exactly what happened to #10 and #11 in the previous round.

| Change | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `maven-compiler-plugin`, both Java examples | 3.15.0 | **3.16.0** |
| exporter base image | `@sha256:05b2b8b…` | **`@sha256:c6ead21…`** |

The image change is a **digest refresh of the same `python:3.14.7-alpine3.24` tag** — a rebuilt base picking up patches, not a version change. That is the reason the Dockerfile pins a digest in the first place.

Supersedes #20, #21 and #22, which are being closed. All three were green on their own before being folded in.

## A stale-branch catch

This branch was cut before #10, #11 and #16 merged, so it was three commits behind. Applying the bumps directly would have reverted `exec-maven-plugin` from 3.6.3 back to 3.5.0 and dropped the failure drill. Master was merged in first; the poms now correctly read compiler **3.16.0** and exec **3.6.3**, and the diff against master is exactly the three intended lines.

This is the second time a branch in this repository has gone stale in a way that would have silently reverted merged work. Worth checking `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/master` before assuming a branch is current.

## Verification

`shellcheck` across `scripts/*.sh`; both poms parse as XML; `dependabot.yml` and the skill front matter parse as YAML; both Python suites pass; the promtool alert-rule tests pass; and the skill's own attribution checks return 0 and 0 over the whole history.

author: zkoalexey
body:
`./scripts/qemu.sh run jxd-r6-e1eth-lcd-eth --daemon --wait-http 240` compiles the **real** device config and boots it on QEMU's `esp32` machine, with working networking. Devices with the display board additionally serve a front panel at `/panel`: the 128×64 screen as a canvas plus the joystick as clickable keys, driving the same pages and `graphical_display_menu` the hardware runs.

The point is that display and menu changes stop being verified by reading code.

### No second config to keep in sync

There is no "QEMU device config". The script generates a gitignored `JXD/<device>.qemu.yaml` that includes the device YAML **verbatim** as a package and layers `include/features/qemu*.yaml` after it. Later packages win, so the overlays override only what the emulator physically cannot do — the LAN8720 PHY (→ `OPENETH`), the I²C bus and everything behind it, the ADC, and the flash mode. Components on unemulated buses that merely mark themselves failed are left in on purpose, so the emulated device exposes the same entity set as the real one.

Why each override exists is in the commit message and in `doc/DECISIONS.md`, not in the YAML.

### What is new

| | |
|---|---|
| `scripts/qemu.sh` | `run` / `build` / `image` / `list` / `stop` / `clean`, port overrides, `--daemon`, `--wait-http`, `--fresh`, `--psram` |
| `components/virtual_display/` | a display with no bus behind it, served over HTTP — `GET /panel`, `/panel/info`, `/panel/frame`, `POST /panel/key/<name>` |
| `include/features/qemu*.yaml` | shared overlay + per-board + panel |
| `doc/QEMU.md` | prerequisites, usage, and what the emulator cannot tell you |
| `include/jxd-r6-e1eth-buttons.yaml` | HOME and BACK gain `id:`, so the panel can drive them (harmless on hardware) |

### Adapted to upstream 2026.8.2, not copied

- 2026.8.2 builds through CMake, not PlatformIO — no `platformio.ini`, no `.pioenvs/`. The flash image is built from `build/firmware.factory.bin` with the size read out of `sdkconfig.<device>-qemu`.
- `set_timeout`/`cancel_timeout` no longer take a `std::string`; the component uses the numeric-id overload.
- `request->url()` is deprecated and removed in 2026.9.0 — replaced with `url_to(buf)`.
- `esphome: name_add_mac_suffix: false` in the overlay: `jxd-r6-e1eth-lcd-eth-qemu` is 25 chars and the limit is 24 with the suffix. QEMU burns no eFuse MAC, so the suffix would be `-000000` anyway.
- The overlay removes `clk:`, not the deprecated `clk_mode:` — this repo already migrated, and removing the wrong key would be a silent no-op that then fails validation on the key that is really there.

### Verified by running it, not by reasoning about it

Booted on the default ports: web server answered after 6 s, `POST /switch/Relay%201/turn_on` → 200 and the state read back, `POST /switch/Drive%20input%203/turn_on` → the template-input plumbing publishes onto `Input 3`. Bootloader header byte 2 = `0x02`, i.e. DIO reached the image.

Panel: `/panel/info` → `{"width":128,"height":64,"keys":["up","down","left","right","enter","home","esc","fn"]}`; `/panel/frame` → 1024 bytes; the frame was rendered to ASCII and shows the real main page (device name, uptime, `VIN: nan V` from the never-sampled ADC, `IP: 10.0.2.15` from OPENETH + slirp DHCP). `enter` opens the menu, `down` moves the highlight, `enter` opens the Inputs page — each verified against the frame before and after.

### Review findings fixed before this PR was opened

A read-only review raised seven issues; all were re-confirmed independently and fixed:

- `send(405, …)` was going out as **HTTP 500** — `web_server_idf` maps only 200/204/400/401/404/409/422. Now sets the status literal directly and adds `Allow: POST`.
- `/frame?since=` claimed 204 in the header and answered 200-with-empty-body. 204 is genuinely available in 2026.8.2, so it is implemented; header, README, page JS and the comment now agree.
- `die` nested inside the option validators ran in a command substitution, so a bad `--http-port` printed four messages including a raw bash error and hid the offending value. One message per bad option now.
- `qemu_pids_for` matched the literal binary name, so an emulator started through `QEMU_XTENSA` was invisible to `list`/`stop` while still holding three ports. It now matches the per-device flash image.
- `--daemon` without `--wait-http` exited **0** even when QEMU died on launch. Both daemon paths now check the process and dump the tail of `qemu.log`.
- `do_image` died with a raw `sed:` message and exit 2 when the sdkconfig was missing.
- The `autorepeat` justification for the double key publish was false — no JXD button carries any filter. Replaced with the real reason.

body:
## What does this PR do?

A markdown table's column order is its box `direction`, which the `unicode-bidi: plaintext` rules (#44150) that resolve per-block text direction never touch. An RTL table (Arabic/Hebrew — the common case for RTL-language operators) keeps LTR columns: the first-read column ends up stranded on the left and every row reads in mirrored column order.

Salvages the approach of #47911 (open, no recent activity) — same `dir="auto"` + `:dir()` hook — plus fixes the silent root cause that would have defeated it: the renderer's CSS target.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes a bug)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-table.tsx`
  - `dir="auto"` on the rendered `<table>`: lets the browser derive the box direction from the cells' content (in practice the headers). No CSS selector can read direction off the cells' script, so the attribute is the minimal hook. Content-driven, so English tables are untouched (they resolve LTR and everything renders as today).
  - `th` alignment `text-left` → `text-start` so headers follow the resolved direction.
- `apps/desktop/src/styles.css`
  - Table cells get `unicode-bidi: plaintext` — values like `33% = 5/15` or `-3%` keep their authored order inside an RTL run.
  - `table:dir(rtl)` / `table:dir(ltr)` pin every header and cell to the table's resolved edge, so a column's header and values stay on the same side instead of splitting (RTL header right, numeric value left).
- `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`
  - **`build.cssTarget: 'chrome132'`** — without this, LightningCSS downlevels `:dir()` into a `:lang()` list (verified in the shipped bundle: `table:is(:lang(ar),...)`), which never matches because no `lang` attribute is ever set. The :dir() rules silently compile to dead selectors. The renderer runs on the bundled Chromium (Electron 40 ≈ Chrome 132), which supports `:dir()` natively. **This is the root cause any future modern-selector CSS in this stylesheet will hit.**

## How to Test

1. Ask the agent for an Arabic/Hebrew markdown table → columns render right-to-left with the first-read column on the right; header and values of each column stay on the same side; numeric cells keep their authored order.
2. Ask for an English table → renders byte-identically to before (dir="auto" resolves LTR).
3. Resize a column (drag the header seam) → still works; the existing RTL-aware drag math reads `getComputedStyle(table).direction`, which dir="auto" now actually resolves.
4. `grep table:dir apps/desktop/dist/assets/index-*.css` → both :dir(rtl) and :dir(ltr) rules present as-is (not downleveled).

Verified live on macOS 26.5 (arm64) in the packaged app: Arabic tables now read right-to-left end to end; mixed values (`5/15 = 33%`, `~12–15`, `[19–59%]`) stay in order inside RTL cells.

## Checklist

### Code
- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs — #47911 targets the same bug with the same approach and has no recent activity; this PR salvages it and adds the cssTarget fix without which the CSS never matches
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] I've added/verified tests where practical (jsdom does not resolve dir="auto"; contract verified via built-bundle inspection + live rendering)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5 arm64, packaged Hermes.app

### Documentation & Housekeeping
- [x] Documentation N/A (renderer-only change)

author: ivanprytula
body:
## ⚠️ Not independently deployable — see below

This PR is safe to **review and merge**, but **do not let `deploy-app.yml` run a real deploy off this merge** until PR2 (Terraform Cloud SQL module) lands. `DATABASE_URL` has no default anywhere yet — no Terraform var, no GitHub secret, no Cloud SQL instance — so `api-core` would crash at container startup on the next deploy (`main.py`'s lifespan calls `upgrade_head(settings.sync_database_url)` against an empty string and fails fast by design).

**When merging**: use a merge commit message containing `[skip deploy]` (already honored by `deploy-app.yml`'s `build`/`deploy`/`verify` job conditions) to prevent an automatic deploy. PR2 will add the Cloud SQL instance + `DATABASE_URL` secret; only after that lands is a real deploy safe.

## Summary

**PR1 of the Phase 2 plan** (Cloud SQL Postgres + Alembic migrations, see `docs/decisions.md` ADR-023): the user-auth store moves off SQLite/`create_all` onto Postgres with Alembic-managed schema, and tests run against a real, ephemeral Postgres via `testcontainers` instead of SQLite — closing the SQLite-vs-Postgres dialect-gap risk entirely rather than working around it.

Also includes two follow-up hardening passes done in the same branch before opening this PR:

- **Alembic relocated** to `services/portfolio/alembic/` (was repo root) — the Dockerfile never `COPY`d `alembic.ini`/`alembic/` at all, so this would have failed at container startup in production regardless of the `DATABASE_URL` gap above. Moving it under `services/portfolio/` means the existing `COPY services/portfolio/` line picks it up for free.
- **`auth/user_store.py` split into DDD/Clean-Architecture layers**: `db.py` (shared SQLAlchemy `Base`), `auth/user.py` (domain entity + `PasswordHasher` port), `auth/user_row.py` (ORM model), `auth/user_repository.py` (`UserRepository` Protocol + `SqlAlchemyUserRepository` adapter — generic via PEP 695, `UserService[R: UserRepository]`), `auth/user_service.py` (application service, no module singleton). HTTP DTOs moved from `auth/models.py` to `schemas/auth.py`, matching the existing `schemas/tailor.py` convention. The old module-singleton + `monkeypatch.setattr` pattern is replaced with FastAPI's own DI (`app.state.user_service` + `Depends(get_user_service)`, mirroring the existing `PdfService`/`get_pdf_service` pattern); tests use `app.dependency_overrides`.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- `UserRow.created_at` needed `DateTime(timezone=True)` — SQLite silently accepted a tz-aware Python `datetime` in a column with no timezone concept; Postgres correctly rejected it. Exactly the kind of dialect gap real-Postgres-in-tests is meant to catch early.
- Alembic's `env.py` called `fileConfig()` with its default `disable_existing_loggers=True`, which silently disabled every already-existing logger (including pytest's `caplog` handler) the first time a migration ran in-process — broke log capture for every test that ran afterward. Fixed with `disable_existing_loggers=False`.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 420 passed
- [x] `just code-quality` — ruff check/format + ty all clean
- [x] `alembic -c services/portfolio/alembic.ini check` — confirms the file split didn't change what autogenerate sees on `Base.metadata` ("No new upgrade operations detected")
- [x] Real local boot (`docker run postgres:16-alpine` + `just dev-local`) — live login → `/me` round-trip confirmed working end-to-end through the new DI wiring

author: usamshen
body:
## 背景

[PR #2573](https://github.com/boardx/workspacex/pull/2573)（补 `harness-verify.yml` 的 `concurrency:` 块，解决 PR 连续推送任务堆积）已合入 main，但**合入的是第一版**——独立 feature review 在合入前几分钟指出该版本用 `github.head_ref` 做 concurrency group key 有跨 PR/跨 fork 碰撞风险，我推送的修复版本（改用 `github.ref`）和 auto-merge 撞了车，没赶上，导致 head_ref 版本已经落在 main 上。该 PR 已关闭合并，不能继续往上堆 commit，所以另开本 PR 补上审查意见要求的修复。

## 问题

`main` 上现在的 `harness-verify.yml`：
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: >-
    harness-verify-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
```
`github.head_ref` 只是来源分支的短名，不含 fork owner、不含 PR number。两个不相关的 PR（尤其不同 fork）完全可能用同一个分支短名（如 `fix-ci`）向本仓开 PR，会落进同一个 concurrency group——后开火的那个会把前一个真实无关 PR 的 CI run 顶掉（`cancel-in-progress: true`）。这不是"同一个 PR 连续推送互相顶"的预期行为，而是"跨 PR 互相顶"，是另一种拥堵/拒绝服务。

## 修复

- `concurrency.group` 改用 `github.ref`，直接对齐 `backend-gates.yml` 现成、已经在生产验证过的取法（`backend-gates-${{ github.ref }}`）：`pull_request` 事件下 `github.ref` 就是该 PR 唯一的 `refs/pull/<n>/merge`，不存在同名分支碰撞；main/tag push 上是该 ref 的固定值，同 ref 排队但 `cancel-in-progress` 在那条路径上恒 `false`，只排队不互顶——与 `backend-gates.yml` 的既有行为逐字一致。
- 新增 `.harness/scripts/lint-ci-workflow-concurrency.test.ts`：机械断言 `harness-verify.yml` 与 `backend-gates.yml` 的 `concurrency.group` 都引用 `github.ref`、不引用 `head_ref`/`ref_name`，且 `cancel-in-progress` 是条件表达式（不是写死的 `true`/`false`），防止以后又退回分支短名这类"看起来更精确"的重构。已接入 `verify:harness:raw`，每次 PR 都会跑。

## 验证

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/harness-verify.yml'))"` — YAML 语法通过。
- `pnpm run verify:harness:raw` 本地全绿：72 files / 878 tests（含新增的 4 条断言）。

Refs #2572

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/xperience-vision/agent-runs/6a9922b900d9b8da9f1f777a

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Branche le catalogue d'accessoires BYD sur le configurateur.

Le fichier data/produits-byd.js est DÉJÀ dans le dépôt (245 produits),
et les 490 images correspondantes sont DÉJÀ dans img/produits/.
Tu n'as aucune donnée à créer ni à recopier : uniquem...

✅ **Result:** Le configurateur affiche désormais le catalogue complet d'accessoires BYD au lieu d'un échantillon de démonstration.

## Contexte

Le fichier `data/produits-byd.js` contenait déjà les 245 accessoires BYD réels (nom, prix en euros et en centimes, modèles compatibles, descriptions, slug d'image), et les 490 images correspondantes étaient déjà présentes dans `img/produits/`. Mais rien ne reliait ces données au site : le configurateur servait encore une liste de 14 produits fictifs codée en dur dans `script.js`, et le référentiel de prix côté serveur ignorait complètement le catalogue. Ce travail se limite au branchement.

## Ce qui a changé

La page d'accueil charge maintenant `data/produits-byd.js` avant `script.js`, afin que le catalogue soit disponible au moment où le configurateur s'initialise.

Dans le configurateur, la liste BYD codée en dur a été retirée et remplacée par une référence au catalogue chargé, avec repli sur une liste vide si le fichier n'est pas disponible — le configurateur ne casse donc pas si le script ne charge pas. Les cinq autres marques (Tesla, XPeng, BMW, Mercedes, Range Rover) sont inchangées.

L'affichage des visuels produits a été étendu : jusqu'ici les images étaient résolues uniquement via `data/product-images.json`. La logique accepte désormais aussi le slug porté directement par le produit, ce qui permet aux 245 accessoires BYD d'afficher leur photo (`<picture>` avec source WebP et repli JPEG, texte alternatif inclus) sans dupliquer le mapping dans un second fichier.

Enfin, le référentiel produits côté serveur — celui qui valide les montants avant de créer une session de paiement — dérive maintenant les 245 accessoires directement depuis le même fichier de données. Cela ferme un trou : sans cette étape, tout ajout au panier d'un accessoire BYD aurait été rejeté au moment du paiement, faute d'identifiant connu du serveur. Toutes les entrées déjà présentes (écrans, packs, extérieur, recharge, intérieur et les catalogues des autres marques) sont conservées. Le fichier de données restant la source unique du prix, le front et le serveur ne peuvent plus divergir.

## Vérifications effectuées

Le décompte par modèle obtenu en exécutant le vrai code de filtrage du configurateur sur les vraies données correspond exactement à l'attendu :

| Modèle | Produits |
|---|---|
| Dolphin | 42 |
| Atto 2 | 42 |
| Atto 3 | 42 |
| Seal | 37 |
| Seal U | 47 |
| Sealion 7 | 35 |
| Tous les modèles | **245** |

Par ailleurs :

- Les 245 identifiants sont uniques et aucun champ obligatoire ne manque.
- Les 245 images JPEG et les 245 images WebP existent toutes sur le disque.
- Les prix affichés en euros correspondent au centime près aux prix en centimes utilisés par le serveur (0 écart).
- Le référentiel serveur passe de 114 à 359 entrées : les 245 accessoires ajoutés, aucune entrée perdue.
- Les trois fichiers modifiés passent le contrôle de syntaxe.
- Sur un serveur local, `/data/produits-byd.js` est servi en 200 avec le bon type MIME, et les images JPEG et WebP répondent en 200.

Aucune donnée n'a été créée ni recopiée, et `data/produits-byd.js`, `data/product-images.json` ainsi que le contenu de `img/produits/` sont restés intacts.

author: konamiman
body:
## Summary

Booting a MSX turbo R with both the `4` boot key (R800 ROM mode, free the 64K reserved for R800 DRAM mode) and `SHIFT` (disable MSX-DOS kernels) pressed hangs the computer right after the drivers are initialized. The cause is that Nextor reuses the memory that holds the R800 DRAM mode copies of the system ROMs while the CPU is still running in DRAM mode. This pull request switches the CPU to R800 ROM mode before that memory is reused.

## Root cause

At boot a Turbo-R runs in R800 DRAM mode: the S1990 serves the BIOS, BASIC, sub-ROM and Kanji driver ROM from copies kept in the last four segments of the internal mapper (segments 28 to 31 on a 512K machine). Those are the four segments that MSX-DOS 2 (and Nextor) normally mark as reserved on a Turbo-R, and the ones the `4` boot key frees.

When `4` is pressed, `MAP_INIT` (bank 1, `mapinit.mac`) skips the `sub 4` and so takes the last segment as the kernel data segment and the one before it as the kernel code segment: the DRAM mode copies of the Kanji driver ROM and of the sub-ROM. `DOSINIT` then zeroes the data segment and downloads the kernel code into the code segment. While the CPU is in DRAM mode those segments are the live ROM copies and the S1990 keeps them write protected (openMSX models this in `PanasonicMemory::isWritable`), so both writes are silently dropped: the kernel ends up executing the sub-ROM contents as its code segment and reading the Kanji driver ROM as its data segment, which is fatal within a few hundred instructions. This is only safe if the CPU is no longer in DRAM mode, but the switch to R800 ROM mode requested by the `4` key is done in `CHECK_1KEY` (bank 0, `init.mac`), which runs after `DOSINIT`.

Whether the CPU is in DRAM mode at that point depends on what ran before `DOSINIT`:

* Nextor switches to Z80 mode for the driver initialization and leaves the CPU there. With `4` alone the CPU is therefore in Z80 mode when `DOSINIT` runs, the ROM copies are not in use, and the boot succeeds.
* With `SHIFT` pressed the internal MSX-DOS 2 kernel (slot 3-2) finds the disk system disabled and, as the stock MSX-DOS 2 kernel does on a Turbo-R, switches the CPU back to R800 DRAM mode before returning. `DOSINIT` then runs with its code and data segments write protected and reading as the sub-ROM and Kanji driver ROM copies, and the kernel initialization goes off the rails as soon as it relies on them. On a FS-A1ST, for instance, execution wanders through the mirrored Kanji driver code, which calls one of its own routines by fixed address in page 1, lands in the empty area of Nextor bank 1, slides through NOPs into the bank switching code with a garbage bank number and ends in an interrupt storm (the `H.KEYI` hook reads as `FFh`). On a FS-A1GT the kernel simply ends up frozen in the BIOS with the hooks intact. In both cases the screen still shows "Driver initialization OK".

So `4` alone works only because of the order in which things happen to run, not by design. Anything that leaves the CPU in DRAM mode when `DOSINIT` runs, such as `SHIFT`, an internal disk ROM that behaves differently or no internal MSX-DOS kernel at all, triggers the crash.

## The fix

In `MAP_INIT`, when running on a turbo R with the `4` key pressed, call `CHGCPU` with `81h` (R800 ROM mode, LED update) right before the decision to reuse the last four segments. `CHGCPU` preserves all registers but ends with `EI`, and `MAP_INIT` must run with interrupts disabled, so a `DI` follows the call. `CHECK_1KEY` still performs its own switch later, which is now a no-op for this case.

`MAP_INIT` is entered with the BIOS in page 0 (that is part of the `DOSINIT` entry contract), so the BIOS routine can be called directly. Bank 1 has plenty of free space, which is why the fix lives there rather than in bank 0's `init.mac`, whose code is pinned by `ALIGN` directives.

Side effect worth knowing: with `4` pressed, the rest of `DOSINIT` (kernel init, boot sector read) now runs in R800 ROM mode instead of Z80 mode. Driver calls that need the Z80 keep being handled by the existing Z80 access mode mechanism.

## Testing

Reproduced and verified with openMSX 21.0 on two turbo R configurations, a Panasonic FS-A1ST with 512K RAM and a Panasonic FS-A1GT, both with a Sunrise IDE Nextor 3.0.0 beta 1 ROM in slot 1 and IDE master and slave hard disk images attached, from a factory-fresh machine state each run (the openMSX persistent CMOS is corrupted by the crash and makes later runs behave differently if it is not reset).

Reverse debugging (`reverse goto` and `step_back`) was used to bisect the exact instruction sequence, and the diagnosis was validated before writing the patch by injecting a `CHGCPU(81h)` call at the `DOSINIT` entry from the debugger, which turned the crash into a normal boot.

A control ROM built from unmodified `master` with the Sunrise IDE driver is byte-identical to the shipped beta 1 ROM. The patched ROM differs only in bank 1. Boot results with keys held from power-on, identical on both machines unless noted:

| Keys held | Unmodified master | This PR |
|-----------|-------------------|---------|
| 4 + SHIFT | hangs after "Driver initialization OK" (interrupt storm on the FS-A1ST, frozen in the BIOS with the hooks intact on the FS-A1GT) | boots to the prompt, CPU in R800 ROM mode |
| 4 | boots, R800 ROM mode | boots, R800 ROM mode |
| SHIFT | boots, R800 DRAM mode | boots, R800 DRAM mode |
| none | boots, R800 DRAM mode | boots, R800 DRAM mode |
| 2 + SHIFT | boots in MSX-DOS 1 mode | boots in MSX-DOS 1 mode |

The exact way the crash manifests differs between the two machines because the garbage executed after the ROM copies are overwritten differs, but the trigger is the same: on both, `DOSINIT` is entered in R800 DRAM mode with 4 + SHIFT and in Z80 mode with 4 alone. Not tested on real hardware.

# FIX Vendor area: draft supplier invoices show a PHP warning instead of the reference

The "Draft invoices" block on the Vendor area page (`htdocs/fourn/index.php`) builds its query as:

```php
$sql = "SELECT ff.ref_supplier, ff.rowid, ff.total_ttc, ff.type";
```

but the loop below reads a column that was never selected:

```php
$facturestatic->ref = $obj->ref;
```

So every row emits `Warning: Undefined property: stdClass::$ref in .../fourn/index.php on line 204`, and because `$facturestatic->ref` ends up empty, `getNomUrl()` renders a link with no label.

Adding `ff.ref` to the SELECT matches the sibling **Draft orders** block ~50 lines above, which already selects `cf.ref` and assigns it the same way — so the two blocks now behave identically.

**Why it has gone unnoticed:** it only appears when at least one *draft* supplier invoice exists. Validated ones go through a different block.

**Affected versions:** reproduced in 18.0, 19.0, 20.0, 21.0, 22.0, 23.0, 24.0 and develop. Targeting 22.0 per the N-2 guidance in CONTRIBUTING.

**Reproduction**
1. Enable the Supplier invoice module.
2. Create a supplier invoice and leave it as a draft.
3. Open **Vendor area** (`/fourn/index.php`).

**Before** — three draft supplier invoices, each showing the warning where the reference link belongs. Note the *Draft orders* block above rendering correctly, for contrast:

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AKhalid-projects/dolibarr/de3f008f8858a1a543c96a334cefc9d9b1043b44/before-fourn-index.png)

**After** — the same page with `ff.ref` selected:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AKhalid-projects/dolibarr/de3f008f8858a1a543c96a334cefc9d9b1043b44/after-fourn-index.png)

Screenshots taken with the `eldy` theme on an instance running the develop branch; the block is byte-identical in 22.0.

<sub>Found while adding draft supplier invoices to a test fixture set; reproduced and verified before and after on a running instance.</sub>

author: elijahadusi1
body:
The Media page's photo gallery was twelve photographs written into the repository by hand. It now reads the church's Facebook album directly, in two rows — this week and last week — refreshed every hour. A new **Short Videos** section carries the five most recent reels from the same page. The site also gets a favicon, which it never had.

## What changed

**The photographs come from Facebook.** The most recent are read from the Page's own album and handed straight to the page. The links Facebook returns are signed and expire in about five days, so they are never written to disk; they are fetched afresh each hour.

**Two rows instead of one.** The week turns on a Sunday, so the most recent Sunday service heads "this week" rather than trailing the week before. Each row stops at two dozen — a week here can run to seventy photographs — and a quiet week is left out rather than shown empty.

**The arrow keys walk through the photo viewer.** Left and right move along the row, wrapping at either end, with buttons beside the caption for anyone not on a keyboard.

**Short Videos: the latest five reels, in a phone.** Between the photographs and the YouTube gallery. On a laptop the reels play inside a drawn phone with the caption of the one showing set beside it. The phone starts quiet and the page scrolls past it like anything else; pressing play arms it, and from then on the wheel over the phone moves reel to reel while the page beneath holds still. The cross on the phone gives the wheel back. On a phone the same still and play button open the reels full screen, caption over the foot of each, and the cross in the corner closes them. Sound starts off with a speaker button to turn it on, and stays on once it is. After the fifth, a card offers the rest on Facebook. Five is a ceiling, not a page size — each reel is a dozen megabytes, and only the one showing is ever loading.

**The editing tool no longer asks for photo uploads.** That section was asking for work that no longer needs doing, and could not win — anything added by hand would sit behind whatever Facebook had posted since.

**The tab has the logo in it.** Cut from the same mark the header wears, trimmed of its wide empty margin so it fills the frame at sixteen pixels.

## Things worth knowing

**There are no photo captions to import.** Of a hundred recent photographs, two carried a caption and none carried a description. So each tile shows the day it was posted, and that is what a screen reader is given. This is honestly a step down from the hand-written descriptions that were there before, and it is the cost of the gallery keeping itself up to date. The reels are the opposite case: every one of them has a real caption, and it is shown.

**The photo fallback is intact; the reels have none.** If Facebook cannot be reached, the photo rows fall back to the twelve photographs still in `site-content.json`, which is why `photos` is not added to `RETIRED_SECTIONS`. There is nothing kept in the repository to stand in for the reels, so that section is simply not drawn when Facebook returns none.

**The reels endpoint wants a different token.** It refuses the system user's token outright ("a Page access token is required"). A Page token is derived from the one we have, once an hour, rather than becoming a second secret for anyone to keep.

## Setup

Two new environment variables, documented in `.env.example`. They need adding in Vercel before this reaches the live site; without them the photos fall back and the reels section is not drawn.

- `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID`
- `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN` — a system-user token from Business Settings, expiration Never

## Notes for the reviewer

Two Graph API quirks are commented in `src/lib/facebook.ts`: `type=uploaded` returns an empty list, and the bare `/photos` edge returns only photographs the Page was *tagged* in. The Page's own photographs are reachable only through the wall album.

The wide/narrow rhythm in the photo rows is a fixed pattern rather than earned from each photograph's shape. Every picture the church posts is exactly four by three, so shape alone made every tile wide.

In the reels viewer the video is contained rather than covered. A reel is 9:16 and the screen is taller; covering trimmed a tenth off each side, and the first reel tested lost a letter of its title at both.

## Verified

On a production build: two photo rows, forty-eight photographs, all from Facebook, alt text on every one. Reels: five videos mount only on play with `preload="none"`, scroll-snap and `overscroll-contain` in place, the closing card present; on a laptop the screen stays in the page and the body scroll is never locked, on a phone it becomes a full-viewport dialog with the body locked, and the cross tears it all down and frees the body in both. The icon routes serve with the right content types. No console errors.

body:
## What this is

The release bump for **2.2.0** — step 2 and 3 of `docs/RELEASING.md` in one commit: both
manifests and the engine lockfile to `2.2.0`, and `## [Unreleased]` folded into the
versioned entry (the Unreleased heading never survives a cut).

This is the ship member of the **public step** milestone, issue #655. Its eleven content
members are all closed; this PR is the last thing between them and the tag.

## Why MINOR, not the patch #655 was minted reading as

The Plan-Table fallback fix (#635) widened **`ParsedSpine`** — a package-root exported
type — by a required `warnings: string[]`, so the fallback's rebinding notice can travel
out of `parseWaveSpine` into `MergeOrderResult.warnings`.

- A consumer merely **using** the engine sees nothing: `MergeOrderResult` and the CLI
  surface are unchanged, and `tools/wave/src/index.ts` is byte-for-byte identical to
  v2.1.0 — no runtime export moves.
- A consumer **constructing** a `ParsedSpine` itself (a hand-built fixture, a test double)
  breaks at the type gate. One-line fix at the call site: add `warnings: []`.

By the house rule an implementer-only break is a **minor with a loud heads-up** — the
1.5.0 and 2.1.0 precedents — and the CHANGELOG carries that heads-up under `### Changed`.
Two `feat` commits landed in the same window anyway (#650 the unknown-verb roster, #653
the `wave-setup` orientation block), either of which would carry the minor on its own.
Nothing was removed, so it is not a major.

## What the entry records

Beyond Added / Fixed / Changed, one section is new in kind: **`### Proven since 2.1.0`**.
The installed form ran end to end on a fresh consumer on 2026-09-03 — plugin and engine
both 2.1.0, throwaway GitHub-Issues repo, install through `wave-close --auto`, 59 minutes,
0 permission prompts and 0 Coordinator misfires during the wave. That is the arc this
project has been unable to claim since `0.1.0-beta.0` first listed it as not proven.

The not-yet-proven list is then re-read against that same probe rather than copied
forward. Two lines move:

- the **`prUrl` notice** — a completed Scribe round is now on record (2.1.0's stated
  `verify`), and no notice arose in it, so `verify` narrows to "the next wave in which one
  actually fires";
- the **grant-in-brief plugin half** — the installed-form consumer now exists and is
  measured, so the gap narrows to the *timing*: a mid-wave `annotate`, not the pre-wave
  one the probe ran.

The other six carry forward with their dates, unchanged.

## Verification

Run on this tree before the commit:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci --prefix tools/wave` | clean — the hand-edited lockfile is consistent |
| `vitest run --root tools/wave` | **4055 passed**, 72 files |
| `tsc -p tools/wave --noEmit` | exit **0** |
| `flotilla-engine version --expect 2.2.0` | `match: true` |

The lockfile edit was deliberately line-targeted (root `version` at lines 3 and 9 only) —
`es-module-lexer` is coincidentally at 2.1.0 and was left alone.

## After this merges

Steps 4–7 of `docs/RELEASING.md`, in order: tag `v2.2.0` on the merge commit (fires
nothing), publish the GitHub Release (the irreversible step — this is what publishes to
npm), confirm the publish, then close #655 with the two-command close, including the
`gh issue close` line the `STILL OPEN:` warning exists to insist on.

## Summary
- `main.cpp` started the async web server before `library::begin()`/`ui::begin()` ran. An upload landing in that window would call `ui::onLibraryChanged()` -> `renderCurrent()`, dereferencing the renderer pointer (`rend`) while it was still null. author: copilot
patrickst1991
body:
Follow-up to #68 on the same 4K Netflix MKV (1 video, 1 audio, 40 subtitle tracks): picking Vietnamese still did nothing, and 2.39:1 still left the black bars alone.

## Vietnamese — fixed

Listing all 40 tracks was only half the job. `getTotalTrackInfo()` stops at 32 entries and `setSelectTrack('TEXT', n)` only *acts* on the tracks it returned — hand it an index it never advertised and it doesn't fail, it leaves what was already on screen there. That's "click Vietnamese, it goes back to the current sub". `MkvSubs.extract()` couldn't stand in: it loads the whole movie and gives up over `MAX_FULL_LOAD_BYTES`.

`MkvSubs.extractTrack()` reads one track out of the container through its **cue index**. mkvmerge writes `--cues iframes` for subtitle tracks and every subtitle block is a keyframe, so `Cues` holds a position for *every* subtitle cue in the file — one read of the index plus one 16 KB read per cue, a couple of MB instead of 6 GB.

- reads start **at the playhead**, so the track shows up within a second or two and the rest fills in behind it
- cues go into the array the poller already holds, kept sorted — no temp file, no re-parse
- `CueRelativePosition` counts from the cluster's first data byte and the cluster header's length isn't in the index, so the block is found by scanning the twelve bytes it can start in; the offset it turns up at is remembered for the rest of the file
- reads are paced: the drive being scanned is the one feeding the video
- ASS/SSA styling from `CodecPrivate` applies exactly as on the whole-file path

`getTracks()` now hands the whole menu row to `setSubtitleTrack()` (the container's track number is what the extractor addresses tracks by). Rows past AVPlay's list go to the extractor; rows it did list still go to the firmware first, but the selection is **verified** against `getCurrentStreamInfo()` 600 ms later and falls back to the extractor if the track didn't actually change — the same failure on a file with under 32 tracks is covered too. Bitmap-sub rows are refused on the spot rather than after a read that could never work, so ⚠ now means only "nothing can reach this". A language preference matching only a tail track gets a second chance when the container list lands, and the CC menu keeps your place when it re-renders mid-extraction.

## 2.39:1 — removed, because AVPlay cannot do it

Cropping bars baked into the frames means magnifying past the frame edge: a display rect bigger than the screen and centred on it. A centred oversized rect has a negative origin, and [`setDisplayRect`](https://developer.samsung.com/smarttv/develop/api-references/samsung-product-api-references/avplay-api.html) *"throws InvalidValuesError if any input parameter contains a negative value"*. The picture is always centred in the rect it's handed, so no legal rect can push the top bar off the top of the screen, and AVPlay exposes no source-crop or ROI call to do it another way. The zoom and crop modes were tried on two sets across two releases and never moved a pixel.

So they're gone. **Fit / Fill / Stretch** are what the three display methods can really do; a mode saved by 1.4.0 (`zoom125`, `crop239`, …) resolves back to Fit and gets rewritten on startup. On a file whose frame already matches the panel — where none of the three can change anything, so any bars are inside the picture — the toast says that plainly instead of leaving you to cycle the list looking for the one that isn't broken. The display-rect zoom machinery goes with it; the only thing that could ever bring the feature back is logged once per session (whether the firmware has a crop/ROI call of its own).

## Tests

`node --test tests/tizen-web-vlc/` — 68 pass. 13 new cases build a byte-accurate cue-indexed Matroska fixture and cover: one track pulled through the index, never reading the video it skips, cue order when reads start mid-file and wrap, an index in front of the media, CueDuration vs BlockDuration vs next-cue end times, progress callbacks, ASS styling, a v1 index with no block positions, a bitmap track, a track the container never declared, and cancellation. The aspect tests now assert the list holds only modes the firmware can carry out, and that an old saved mode is not treated as current.

## Summary

- Adds `SqliteLedger::absent_participation_account_candidates` (`crates/core/algo-ledger/src/sqlite.rs`), mirroring go-algorand's `generateKnockOfflineAccountsList` absentee half (`ledger/eval/eval.go`, v41): for every `Online && IncentiveEligible` account not excluded, checks `isAbsent` (silent for longer than its stake-scaled allowance) or an active-challenge failure, capped at `payouts_max_mark_absent`. Reuses `is_absent`/`total_online_voting_stake` (bumped `pub(crate)`, already implemented for the validation side in PR #886) and `heartbeat::find_challenge`/`Challenge::failed`.
- Wires this into `SimpleBlockEvaluator::generate_block` (`bin/algod-rust/src/commands/participate.rs`) alongside the existing expired-accounts sweep (issue #526), so a self-produced block's `ParticipationUpdates.AbsentParticipationAccounts` is now genuinely computed instead of always empty. Excludes this node's own participating addresses (`voting_accounts`, now actually threaded through) and any address already listed as expired this round, matching go's `generateKnockOfflineAccountsList` doc comment ("This function is passed a list of participating addresses so a node will not propose a block that suspends or expires itself").
- Updates `docs/phase17/parity_ledger_core.md`'s `TestAbsenteeChecks` row from `partial` to `matched-1:many` and regenerates `docs/PHASE17_TEST_PARITY.md`'s aggregate/per-area counts.

Closes #845 (validation side was already done via PR #886; this closes the proposal side, which was the issue's remaining scope).

## Known residual limitation (documented, not fixed here)

`algo-pool`'s `assemble_block`/`recompute_block_evaluator` call sites always call `generate_block(&[])` — this node's real participation addresses are never threaded through the pool → evaluator call chain end-to-end. This is the *same* pre-existing limitation the #526 expired-accounts-list feature already has (documented in its own doc comment). The self-exclusion parameter (`voting_accounts`) is real and tested at the `generate_block` unit level, but doesn't yet engage from a live `algod-rust participate` node's actual pool-driven block assembly. Threading real participation addresses through `algo-pool`'s block-assembly call chain is a separate, larger change (affects both the expired and absent lists identically) and was judged out of scope for this issue.

- [x] TDD: new unit tests in `crates/core/algo-ledger/src/sqlite.rs` (`absent_candidates_includes_genuinely_absent_online_account`, `absent_candidates_excludes_recently_seen_account`, `absent_candidates_excludes_addresses_in_exclude_set`, `absent_candidates_respects_max_mark_absent_cap`, `absent_candidates_empty_when_cap_is_zero`)

author: nodece
body:
### Motivation

The send-timeout path (`failPendingMessages` with `cnx() == null`) released `op.cmd` and recycled the op inline on the timer thread while the message frame may still have been queued for writing on a connection event loop: the write callback sits behind a reconnect/disconnect storm, or the buffers are already in the channel outbound buffer. Releasing the buffers from the wrong thread could return them to the pool while the in-flight write is still reading them, letting new batches overwrite the frame content and corrupting the wire bytes (broken checksum / lost frame sync on the broker). The existing `cnx != null` branch already deferred this cleanup to the event loop; the null (reconnect-window) branch did not.

### Modifications

- `OpSendMsg` tracks the event loop each cmd was last handed to for writing (`writeEventLoop`), and `cmd` is now `volatile` so stale callbacks can never observe a released cmd.
- `releaseOpCmdAndRecycle` defers the cmd release and op recycle to that event loop (serialized after the in-flight write), with an inline fallback when the loop is shutting down. `releaseOpCmd` clears `op.cmd` before releasing so a stale callback always fails its guard.
- `WriteInEventLoopCallback` now skips stale writes (op re-sent on another connection or already disposed) and only drops the reference it took, instead of writing a released buffer or mutating a recycled op.
- `failPendingMessages` fails inline when the connection event loop rejects the deferred task (shutting down during reconnect churn) instead of leaving the pending messages queued.
- `ackReceived` / `recoverChecksumError` / `recoverNotAllowedError` now go through the same write-loop-aware release.

### Verifications

- `ProducerImplTest` 9/9 passing (includes 4 regression tests for the timeout + in-flight-write race).
- `checkstyleMain` / `checkstyleTest` passing.

author: jinwoo-h
body:
## Summary

The WSL CLI reaches a Windows Orca host through the local runtime RPC transport (a Windows named pipe). `browser.snapshot`, `browser.screenshot`, and `browser.wait` can block in agent-browser startup/paint/condition waits, but the runtime long-poll classifier treated them as short RPCs. The 30s socket/named-pipe idle timer could therefore close a healthy request before the browser helper replied; the CLI surfaced `runtime_unavailable`. `eval`, `click`, and tab commands remain on the short path.

This patch classifies those three browser methods as the existing `wait` long-poll class. That enables the existing keepalive frames and abort/slot accounting for both Unix sockets and Windows named pipes. No new wire fields, opcodes, retries, polling, or fallback routing are introduced.

## Deterministic evidence

- Oracle: `src/main/runtime/runtime-rpc-long-poll-transport.test.ts`
- Classifier assertions cover the affected methods (`browser.snapshot`, `browser.screenshot`, `browser.wait`) and controls (`browser.eval`, `browser.click`, `browser.tabSwitch`). On the base revision those new assertions are red because the methods classify as short RPCs.
- A real newline-framed local RPC session delays `browser.snapshot` for 120ms, observes >=2 keepalives, and receives exactly one terminal response on the candidate.
- Focused result: `pnpm test src/main/runtime/runtime-rpc-long-poll-transport.test.ts src/cli/browser.test.ts` — 57 passed.
- Additional result: 49 tests passed across local long-poll, WebSocket long-poll, remote client, and envelope suites; 38 browser bridge/lifecycle tests passed.
- `pnpm tc:node` passed.
- `pnpm run check:code-quality:changed` passed with 0 new findings.

## Compatibility and limits

The keepalive frame is already part of the existing RPC envelope and is understood by current/legacy clients; this changes only host-side classification. The existing long-poll cap still bounds concurrency and returns `runtime_busy` under saturation.

This workspace is macOS. Windows 2, WSL2, ConPTY, and the physical Windows named-pipe path were not available, so no physical Windows/WSL reproduction is claimed. The oracle exercises the same classifier and real local framed transport used by that path, but it does not prove WSL interop, PowerShell argv forwarding, or Windows kernel named-pipe behavior. A >30s end-to-end timeout was not run in CI because it would make the regression suite unnecessarily slow; the causal boundary is the host idle timer plus the missing classifier entry.

Linear was not mutated; the session's `orca-ide` Linear CLI was unavailable.

The second half of #225. #342 shipped the parser, the Settings list and the
palette entry — which left `$FILE`, `$FILES` and `$SHA` **advertised in the
Settings hint and unfillable**: `repoContext()` returned
`{ repo: "", files: [], sha: null, branch }` and nothing else ever built an
`ActionContext`. A feature that advertises placeholders it never fills is worse
than not shipping them.

## What changed

- **`ActionSurface`** (`"repo" | "file" | "commit"`), derived from
  `ACTION_SURFACES` so the list and the type cannot drift, with per-action
  toggles in Settings.
- **`fileContext` / `commitContext`** beside `repoContext`. `repo` deliberately
  stays `""` in all three: `run_custom_action` overwrites it with the repository
  it resolves — which is also the child's cwd — so a second source of truth here
  could only ever disagree with the one that matters.
- **Context-menu surfaces** on the single-file, multi-file and commit menus.
  Multi-select produces the `$FILES` list form; sending only the first path would
  run the program on the wrong thing without saying so.

The Rust parser stays the single source of truth for command → argv. No second
parser, no `Command::new` outside `proc.rs`, no Rust touched at all.

## Migration

**An absent `surfaces` key reads as `["repo"]`** — the palette, and only the
palette. Every action persisted by #342 had no such key and was a palette action,
so that is exactly where it stays.

The rule lives in two places on purpose: `normalizeSurfaces` applies it in
memory, and `coerceCustomActions` writes it in on load. The second half turned
out to be load-bearing for a reason beyond this change — `customActions` is
object-valued, so `coerceSettings`' scalar type-guard (which compares against
`typeof DEFAULTS[key]`) **never looked at it**. The list was arriving from
localStorage, or from a shared settings file, completely unvalidated. It is now.

An empty surface list cannot be *saved* (the cause stays on screen as three empty
toggles rather than the app overruling the click); an empty one arriving from a
hand-edited file *is* repaired to the palette — unreachable is worse than
misplaced.

## Deliberately not done

- **No actions on a multi-commit selection.** `$SHA` is singular and the Rust
  substitution has no list form for it, so "the first of five, silently" is not an
  answer. Pinned by a test.
- **No file-surface actions on conflicted / embedded / submodule rows** — those
  menus *replace* the file menu rather than trim it. Same call `externalDiffItem`
  made. Pinned by a test.
- **No keybinding for actions.** The issue mentions it; it is a separate surface
  (`keymap/actions.ts`) and is left for a follow-up. Issue #225 therefore stays
  open after this merges.

## Verification

- `pnpm test` — 323 files, 3097 passing; `pnpm tsc --noEmit` clean
- e2e in Docker on this branch: `status-stage.e2e.ts` 7 passing, which drives
  both file context menus
- The "actions sit above the danger block" invariant was documented in
  `frontend.md` but never asserted. It is now a test, verified failing first by
  moving the push below the danger block. Menu order before/after the review fix
  was diffed and is byte-identical on both file menus.

Incidental fix: `PGToggle` takes `testId`, not `data-testid`. The two existing
toggles in `CustomActionsSettings.tsx` passed the latter, which TS accepts on
hyphenated JSX attributes and React drops — those hooks rendered nothing.

## Summary
Closes and certifies **Sprint B — Block 1**: Establishes **ADR 0003**, adds **AGENTS.md** with mandatory engineering directives, externalizes versioned origin policies with verified cryptographic digests, strictly decouples HTML extraction into `InnoGetExtractor`, unifies all evidentiary provenance into authoritative `FieldObservation` records, adds canonical fixture `innoget_sample_call_2446.html`, enforces fail-fast loading (zero synthetic fallback policies), generalizes Level 3 verification, introduces automated architectural invariant tests in CI, configures scoped Gitleaks security rules, and achieves 100% green CI.

### Architectural Invariants & Decisions
1. **AGENTS.md Directives Adopted:**
   - ADR compliance is an explicit, mandatory definition-of-done constraint.
   - Zero hardcoding of business/jurisdiction lists in production.
   - Mandatory automated CI enforcement tests.
2. **ADR 0003 Adopted (`docs/adr/0003-externalized-origin-policy-and-evidence-based-resolution.md`):**
   - Pure separation: `InnoGetExtractor` (facts) $\to$ `OriginPolicyConfig` (declarative policy) $\to$ `DefaultOriginResolver` (decision + evidence) $\to$ `InnogetHtmlNormalizer` (composition).
   - Scope boundaries explicitly delimited: algorithm is parameterized and jurisdiction-agnostic; empirical study cohort is parameterized to Spanish demands for UC1.
3. **Cryptographic Policy Verification:**
   - `OriginPolicyConfig.load_from_json()` computes canonical SHA-256 and actively verifies the declared `policy_sha256`, raising a `ValueError` if the policy file has been modified or tampered with.
4. **Generalization of Level 3 Verification Protocol:**
   - `ExternalRegistryVerifier` generalized to `is_registered_entity(org, target_jurisdiction)`, evaluating the organization against the configured target jurisdiction rather than hardcoding Spain in the protocol.
5. **CI Architectural Enforcement Test (`test_origin_policy_architecture_invariants.py`):**
   - Scans ingestion production code and fails CI automatically if forbidden hardcoded tokens, list lookups, or fallback policies are detected.
6. **Scoped Security Allowlist (`.gitleaks.toml`):**
   - Targeted allowlist for the public reCAPTCHA sitekey in `backend/test/fixtures/innoget_sample_call_2446.html` without degrading security rules across the repository.
7. **Canonical Fixtures for Clean Checkouts:**
   - `innoget_sample_call_2446.html` located canonically in `backend/test/fixtures/`, tracked in git, guaranteeing that clean CI checkouts pass 100%.
8. **Fail-Fast Invariant:**
   - Externalized policy in `config/policies/data/jurisdiction_policy.json`. Missing, corrupt, or tampered configuration raises an explicit error immediately.
   - Removed synthetic string defaults from `DemandRecord` (`requesting_organization` and `origin_country` default to `None` when unobserved).
9. **Symmetrical Tripartite Classification (`UNKNOWN != FOREIGN`):**
   - Target jurisdiction match $\to$ `LEVEL_1_DIRECT_METADATA` (`INCLUDED`).
   - Foreign jurisdiction match $\to$ `NON_SPANISH` (`EXCLUDED_NON_SPANISH`).
   - Unrecognized or corrupt tokens $\to$ strictly `UNVERIFIED` (`EXCLUDED_UNVERIFIED_ORIGIN`).
10. **Unified Provenance:**
   - Uses canonical `FieldObservation` with `VerificationStatus.SOURCE_REPORTED` vs `INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIED`.

author: mikaylathompson
body:
## Problem

External coding agents cannot claim actionable inbox reports or attach implementation pull requests without an internal PostHog task.

Report ownership and pull request state currently depend on task-backed records, which excludes agents using MCP directly.

## Changes

- MCP agents can claim, silently take over, release, and attach one GitHub pull request to actionable reports.
- Releasing a claim removes ownership while preserving its attached pull request.
- Report responses show the owner, pull request details, and derived work state.
- List filters expose unclaimed reports and reports owned by the current actor.
- The same pull request can back multiple report assignments.
- Connected GitHub repositories refresh pull request state and receive webhook transitions.
- Unconnected pull requests remain valid with unknown state and require manual resolution.
- Assignment changes use the existing report activity trail.
- External-agent claims store no task reference, while internal tasks keep their current attribution.
- The migration and generated API clients are mechanical supporting changes.

### Data Model Change
New `SignalReportAssignment` links a report with an owner-actor (user, task (for internal PR generation), agent, system). It also stores PR metadata (if it exists).
Agents (or other users) can claim, add metadata, release.

### Before and After Flows
Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A{{External agent}} --> B[Inbox report]
    B --> C[Task-backed PR lookup]
    C --> D[No task ID]
    D --> E[Agent skips report]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phBlue;
    class C phRed;
    class B,D phGray;
    class E phYellow;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A{{External agent}} --> B[Claim API]
    B --> C[Report assignment]
    C --> D[Optional GitHub pull request]
    D --> E[Webhook transition]
    E --> F[Resolved or suppressed report]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phBlue;
    class B,E phRed;
    class C,D phGray;
    class F phYellow;
```

No visual frontend behavior changed.

## How did you test this code?

- Added API coverage for claims, takeover, attribution, release, filters, pull request state, and activity records.
- Added webhook coverage for repository scoping, shared pull requests, merges, and closed pull requests.
- Added MCP coverage for client-name forwarding, endpoint routing, and generated tool schemas.
- Ran the focused backend and MCP regression suites after the final rebase.
- Ran OpenAPI generation, migration checks, MCP typechecking, Python typechecking, and strict preflight.
- Verified claim, filtering, serialization, and release against the local database in a rollback-only smoke test.
- Not checked: live GitHub API calls or webhook delivery against a connected repository.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Updated the Signals inbox exploration skill and added the remediation design plan.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

- Codex implemented and tested the change using Git, Django, Vitest, OpenAPI generation, and the local development stack.
- Skill invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- The final design separates external-agent ownership and pull request state from internal task records.
