Gerichte laatste UI/UX-ronde zonder redesign en zonder een nieuwe postbuildlaag.

## Wijzigingen
- mobiele uurtabel: geen geneste verticale scroll meer; 8-uurs preview met toegankelijke uitklapactie
- headerhiërarchie: Mijn locatie primair; verversen/weergave visueel secundair
- Nachtzicht: `Indicatie` wordt `Zichtscore`; lange zichtadviescopy links uitgelijnd binnen het bestaande gecentreerde blok
- redundante `10+ km` zichtuitleg teruggebracht tot `Goed zicht.`
- mobiele horizontale padding aangescherpt op ≤430 px
- top/bottom/left/right safe-area hardening voor mobiel en minibar
- bestaande desktopcentrering, scrollbarstyling en Nachtzicht-grid behouden

## Belangrijke correctie uit verificatie
De finale UI-shell ondersteunt bewust alleen Automatisch, Licht en Donker; de oude rode stand wordt gemigreerd naar Auto. Daarom wordt in deze PR géén rode themastand of contrastpatch opnieuw geïntroduceerd.

## Verificatie
De bestaande final-visual-polish-laag is uitgebreid in plaats van nog een patchlaag toe te voegen. De verifier bewaakt ook dat de verwijderde rode stand niet terugkomt. De browsertest dekt 320, 390, 430, 1100, 1366, 1440, 1600 en 1920 px, mobile expand/collapse, ARIA-scrollgedrag, overflow, headerhiërarchie en Nachtzicht-regressies.

author: tonqian
body:
## 改了什么

DESIGN-V3「第 3 批之后的附加 PR：回边重入等待环体收束」，stacked 在 #24 之上。这是早于本次清理的引擎行为，轮次表让它可见（Codex 在 #18 第十九轮指出）。

- `reenter()` 不再直接重置回边下游：记成 `PendingReentry { target, affected }`（按 target 去重——同一轮里两个评委都打回只推进一轮）；调度循环每一轮先应用 `affected` 里没有 `running` 节点的重入（在 `pickReady()` 与 `running.size === 0` 的收束判断之前）；`pickReady()` 跳过待重入范围内的节点，环体不会在即将被重置的一轮上再烧一个会话；`maxReentries` / `onExhausted` 在真正重置时才计数；取消与整运行失败作废排队中的重入。
- 后果之一：触发回边的节点自己也在 `affected` 且仍在 `running`，所以所有重入都走排队路径（下一次调度轮应用），没有快慢两条路径可漂移。
- `runner.test.ts` 新夹具「输入 → 写码 → {快评委, 慢评委} → 汇总 → 输出」（快评委的「不通过」出口回边到写码）：「环体里还有节点在跑时回边重入挂起」（慢评委的第 1 次报告落在第 0 轮、第 2 次落在第 1 轮，第 1 轮全部 `startedAt ≥` 慢评委第 0 轮 `finishedAt`，`(node, round)` 唯一，无行残留 running）、「挂起期间被取消：这次重入作废，没有任何第 2 轮」——两条在旧代码上都失败，后者在旧代码上表现为运行已被宣告结束而慢评委的会话仍在执行。
- AGENTS.md「The workflow graph is not a DAG」、DESIGN.md 引擎 spec 的回边段、REVIEW.md 同步。

## 跑了哪些命令

- [x] `npm run check`（typecheck + lint + fmt:check + vitest）
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] e2e：`npx playwright test e2e/parallel-runs.spec.ts e2e/runs.spec.ts e2e/parallel-ui.spec.ts`（本分支 worktree 自带空 `data/`，临时配置起在 3596）
- [x] 付费冒烟：`smoke-graph`（扇出 / 汇总 / 回边，在本分支 worktree 自己的库上跑）——结果见下

## 验收结果

- `npm run check`：46 个文件 384 个用例通过、1 个按条件跳过（无 `_reference/` 的 worktree）；`npm run build` 通过。
- e2e：`parallel-runs` / `runs` / `parallel-ui` 三个 spec **11/11**（本分支 worktree 空 `data/`，3596）。
- `smoke-graph`（本分支 worktree 自己的库）：运行成功；6 个节点共 11 行轮次、最大轮次 1、无行残留 running——回边重入在真实扇出 / 汇总 / 回边图上按新语义完成。

## 对照 .github/REVIEW.md 自查了哪几条

- 5：重入排队按 runId 隔离（运行级结构）；取消 / 整运行失败作废排队；运行不会带着在跑的会话被宣告结束。
- 8：新用例只依赖 mock 的 runActionNode 与内存库；两条都验证过在旧代码上失败。
- 9：AGENTS.md / DESIGN.md / REVIEW.md 同一 PR。
- 10：不立 ADR——不是新取舍，是把 ADR-0009 已定语义（回边重入整个环体一起推进一轮）在并发下做对。

author: jonassaa
body:
The forge half of #233. The identity half shipped in #335 / #340; this is the
constraint called out in the issue's own comment thread:

> `useForgeStore.ts:42-60` persists `logins: Record<string, string>`, host →
> login, **singular**. Two GitHub accounts is not expressible today even before
> identities exist.

## Old vs new persisted shape (`pg-forge-hosts`)

```jsonc
// BEFORE — one login per host
{ "hostKinds": { "github.com": "GitHub" },
  "logins":    { "github.com": "jonassaa" } }

// AFTER — host → many, exactly one active
{ "hostKinds": { "github.com": "GitHub" },
  "accounts":  { "github.com": [
      { "id": null,       "login": "work",     "active": false },
      { "id": "acc-mfx-2","login": "personal", "active": true  } ] } }
```

## Why the slot lives in the credential username

The persisted map was not the only constraint. A token is stored under one
credential key per host, so "add a second account" would have overwritten the
first token and "switch active" would have been a lie. The host key must stay
shared — it is what keeps an API token off the git-transport credential for the
same host — so the slot moved into the `username=` field, the only remaining part
of the key: `credential_username(None) == "platypusgit-forge"`,
`Some(id) == "platypusgit-forge:<id>"`.

The id is opaque rather than the login because a forge login can be renamed while
the token stays valid, and a login-keyed entry would orphan it.

`active` is a flag rather than a `host → id` pointer because a pointer can dangle
and is ambiguous (`null` meaning both "the legacy slot" and "nothing recorded").
`parseHosts` normalises "none flagged" and "two flagged" to exactly one.

## Migration — the part that had to be right

The old `logins[host]` lands on **`id: null` and nothing else**, which is
byte-identical to the `platypusgit-forge` username a released build already wrote
real tokens under. Any other id would point at a slot that has never held
anything, and a user who never signed out would come back signed out. Nothing
ever *mints* `null`; it only arrives from migration. `""`, `null` and `undefined`
all collapse to that same slot rather than minting a third.

`parseHosts` is pure and takes the raw string, so it is testable without
localStorage. 30 tests cover: legacy single host, multiple hosts, empty `logins`,
a login that is not a non-empty string, absent blob, corrupt JSON, a blob parsing
to `42` / `null` / `"string"`, `{}`, non-object `hostKinds`, none-flagged,
two-flagged, duplicate id, non-array account list, and both keys present at once.

## Blast radius

`lib.rs`, `error.rs` and `src/lib/types.ts` are **untouched** — no new Tauri
command, no `invoke_handler!` change, no new `AppError` variant, no TS-union
drift. Every token-using command gained an `account: Option<String>` where absent
means the pre-#233 slot. No command returns a token. `credential_input` now
line-safety-checks the *computed* username, so an account id carrying `\n` cannot
inject `host=`.

## Verification

- `pnpm test` — 322 files, 3116 passing; `pnpm tsc --noEmit` clean; e2e tsc clean
- `cargo test` — 84 suites, 1161 passing, including
  `the_legacy_slot_username_is_byte_identical_to_what_shipped` and
  `an_account_id_with_a_newline_cannot_reach_the_credential_protocol`
- e2e in Docker on this branch: `pulls.e2e.ts` 5 passing

## Two things to weigh

- **`var(--row-step)`:** the account rows reuse `ForgeSettings`' local `Row`,
  whose fixed padding matches `screens/Settings.tsx`' own `Row`. Making only the
  forge rows density-aware would leave them a different height from their siblings
  in the same panel — it belongs on both helpers at once, or neither. Flagged
  rather than silently skipped.
- **Not built:** a saved identity *referencing* a forge account. It is expressible
  for the first time now, but two questions need settling first — whether applying
  an identity also switches the host's active forge account (which would silently
  change what a Pulls refresh lists), and what a dangling reference renders as.

Part of #233

author: sam0urr
body:
`web/method.html` has been on main since the methods-page branch landed. `story.html` and `method.html` already link to each other and back to the map — but the map linked only to the story.

So a reader who opened the map and never went via the story had **no route to the methodology at all**. That is the wrong way round: the map is the page that makes the claims the methodology qualifies.

The link sits in the intro paragraph beside the existing story link, and reuses the wording `story.html` already uses for the same destination ("How the index is built") rather than inventing a third label for one page.

## The check

`verify.py` now asserts all three pages reach each other, rather than asserting this one anchor exists. The gap was not that a particular link was missing — it was that nothing asserted the pages form a connected set, so a future page can be added and silently linked from nowhere. Confirmed the check fails with the link removed.

author: naveen-raj-sivasamy
body:
## The bug

\`ensureReportConfigsForCategories_\` (merged in #1) checked "does a Report Config already exist under this category's name" and stubbed one for every category missing a match. That meant the **first** Save Categories after v1.25.0 shipped would retroactively stub a config for **every pre-existing category at once**, not just a newly added one — a burst of extra rows appended to \`_ReportConfigs\` in the same write/lock as \`_Categories\`' own save.

Two full-workbook-recalculating writes back to back on one save is exactly what this codebase's own existing comments already flag as the cause of the "stuck on Saving for everyone" issue fixed earlier — and matches what was just reported: cache-clear/Manage Fields feeling stuck or not populating right after touching Categories.

## The fix

Diffs the just-saved categories map against what \`_Categories\` held **before** the save, and only stubs a config for a category name that's genuinely new to *this* save. "Whatever category gets added" now means an actual add — one small append, same size as any other single-category edit — never a retroactive backfill against everything already there.

## If you already hit this

Check \`_ReportConfigs\` for stray auto-created rows (Enabled = FALSE, no recipients) under categories you didn't just add — safe to delete, nothing references them yet.

author: sic-em
body:
Changing the app icon did nothing in a packaged build. Windows draws the taskbar button from the shortcut matching the app's AppUserModelID, and that shortcut points at Vesper.exe, so `window.setIcon` was never going to show up. Dev sets a different AppUserModelID, which is why it looked like it worked. The window is frameless too, so there was no title bar icon to fall back on.

Each variant now ships an .ico, and picking one rewrites the Start Menu, Desktop, and pinned taskbar shortcuts, keeping their AppUserModelID and target intact. The stored pick is reapplied on launch, since an installer update recreates the shortcuts with the default artwork.

The taskbar button only rereads its icon when the app starts, so Settings now asks whether to restart after a pick, over a new `app:relaunch` channel. That prompt is Windows only, because the macOS Dock swaps live.

Verified on a packaged build: the .ico files land in app.asar.unpacked, both the computed asar path and its unpacked rewrite exist, and rewriting a copy of the real Start Menu shortcut moved its icon from Vesper.exe to the variant while preserving the AppUserModelID and target.

Closes #38

author: seb7152
body:
> ⚠️ **Changement cassant** — le token en chemin d'URL du MCP (`https://mcp.<DOMAIN>/<API_TOKEN>/...`) n'est plus accepté (`401`). Tout client configuré ainsi doit basculer le token dans l'en-tête `Authorization: Bearer`. Voir §4.

## Problème

L'API n'acceptait qu'une seule clé : `API_TOKEN` d'environnement, comparée en `!==`, sans scope ni expiration. Elle est copiée dans n8n, Claude Code, Codex et le compose — la révoquer, c'est éditer l'environnement, redémarrer, et tout reconfigurer d'un coup. Et elle donne lecture **et** écriture sur tout le vault, `10_Context/Perso/` compris.

Déclencheur : accéder au vault depuis un PC pro où les MCP custom ne sont pas disponibles.

## 1. Tokens applicatifs (`tokens.js`)

Sur le patron de `webhooks.js` : JSON sous `/data` (hors vault synchronisé), écriture atomique, **SHA-256 seul** — une fuite du fichier ne donne rien d'exploitable — et comparaison en temps constant.

Chaque token porte `scopes` (`read`/`write`/`admin`), `path_allow`/`path_deny`, une expiration optionnelle, et `last_used_at`/`last_used_ip`.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"PC boulot","scopes":["read"],
       "path_allow":["20_Projects/Pro","30_Knowledge"],
       "path_deny":["10_Context/Perso"],
       "expires_at":"2026-12-01"}' \
  https://obsidian-api.<DOMAIN>/api/tokens
```

### L'enforcement REST

Centralisé dans deux middlewares plutôt que dispersé par route, pour qu'un nouvel endpoint ne puisse pas le contourner par oubli.

| Surface | Comportement |
|---|---|
| Chemin dans l'URL | `403` avec le chemin fautif |
| Chemins dans le corps (batch, folders, move) | Rejet de **toute** la requête — pas de traitement partiel silencieux |
| Suppression / déplacement de dossier | L'arborescence entière doit être dans le périmètre — un ancêtre navigable ne suffit pas |
| Listings (`/api/files`, `/api/search`, `/api/directory`, `/api/projects`) | Filtrage **silencieux** : un token restreint ne peut pas sonder l'existence de ce qu'il ne peut pas lire |
| `/api/query` | **Refusé** aux tokens restreints par chemin |
| `/api/webhooks`, `/api/tokens` | `admin` requis |

Six décisions qui méritent justification :

**Les chemins sont canonicalisés avant d'être autorisés.** L'autorisation porte sur le chemin tel qu'il arrive, alors que le système de fichiers ne le voit qu'une fois `path.join()` passé dessus. Comparé brut, `20_Projects/Pro/../../10_Context/Perso/x.md` commence par un préfixe autorisé et lit `/vault/10_Context/Perso/x.md` — la cible ne quitte pas le vault, donc le garde-fou anti-traversée des routes la laisse passer aussi. `.` et `..` sont donc résolus, et un chemin qui remonte au-dessus de la racine, ou qui contient un antislash, est refusé : le vault est POSIX, où `\` est un caractère de nom de fichier ordinaire, donc le lire comme séparateur élargit les `path_allow` et le lire comme texte élargit les `path_deny` — refuser est la seule lecture qui échoue du bon côté.

**Une opération récursive doit prouver toute son arborescence.** Les cibles de dossier passaient par le prédicat de navigation, qui tolère volontairement un ancêtre d'un préfixe autorisé pour qu'un token puisse descendre depuis la racine. Supprimer n'est pas naviguer : un token autorisé sur `20_Projects/Pro/Sub` pouvait effacer `20_Projects/Pro` et tous ses frères, des fichiers qu'il ne pouvait même pas lire. Chaque cible nomme désormais le contrôle dont elle a besoin — `file`, `tree`, `browse` — au lieu de le déduire de la forme de la valeur.

**Le SQL est refusé, pas filtré.** `SELECT group_concat(path) FROM files` fuite du contenu sans jamais renvoyer de colonne `path`. Filtrer les lignes aurait donné une fausse sécurité.

**Webhooks en `admin`.** Un webhook avec `include_body` exfiltre n'importe quel fichier vers une URL arbitraire.

**Pas de rerank pour les tokens restreints.** Le reranker cloud tourne *dans* l'index, donc avant le filtre : un token bridé pouvait faire expédier chez Jina des passages interdits. Gap révélé par le merge de la recherche hybride.

**Navigation vs lecture.** Un dossier menant à un préfixe autorisé reste navigable (sinon impossible de descendre depuis la racine), sans que ses fichiers deviennent lisibles.

Corrections au passage : `/api/files/batch`, `/api/query` et `/api/links/check` sont des lectures en POST — un token `read` en était exclu à tort. Les préfixes matchent par segment entier : `10_Context/Perso` ne couvre jamais `10_Context/Perso2`. Un préfixe non canonicalisable est refusé à la création plutôt que silencieusement ignoré : un `path_deny` perdu, c'est un token plus large que celui demandé. Et `expires_at` doit être une date qui existe : `9999-99-99` passait le contrôle de forme, se comparait lexicographiquement et n'expirait donc jamais — borné sur le papier, permanent en pratique.

## 2. Le MCP accepte les tokens nommés

Chaque client peut désormais avoir sa propre clé au lieu de partager `API_TOKEN` : « Claude Code portable », « Codex bureau », « n8n ». Révoquer celle du portable ne touche pas les autres, sans redémarrage.

Le conteneur MCP ne monte aucun volume et ne peut donc pas lire `/data/tokens.json` — et réimplémenter hachage, expiration et révocation en Python ferait une seconde implémentation à garder synchrone. Il passe par un `POST /api/tokens/verify` (admin), avec le même cache 45 s que le lookup userinfo existant. Conséquence assumée : un token révoqué reste actif au plus 45 s, exactement le compromis déjà accepté côté OAuth.

**Le point qui compte.** Le MCP appelle le REST en root : les scopes et chemins d'un token n'y sont donc **pas** appliqués. Accepter un token restreint l'authentifierait sans honorer ses limites — il *paraîtrait* cloisonné tout en étant root, ce qui est pire que la situation actuelle. Le MCP n'accepte donc que des tokens déjà équivalents à root (non restreints, avec `write`) et **refuse** tout ce qui est plus étroit avec un `403` qui l'explique et renvoie vers le REST.

Ce que ça apporte : un nom, une expiration, une trace d'usage, et la révocation client par client. Ce que ça n'apporte pas : le cloisonnement à travers le MCP — il faudrait transmettre le credential de l'appelant à chaque requête, ce qui est un autre chantier et n'est pas revendiqué ici.

## 3. Gestion des tokens depuis MCP, derrière un rôle OAuth

Une identité OAuth doit porter **`OAUTH_ADMIN_ROLE`** (défaut `obsidian:admin`) en plus d'`obsidian:access` pour appeler `list_api_tokens`, `create_api_token` ou `revoke_api_token`. Un token du magasin doit porter le scope `admin`.

Toutes les branches d'authentification convergent maintenant vers un unique `_forward()` portant un drapeau `is_admin` : le gate ne peut plus être contourné en ajoutant une branche d'auth et en l'oubliant. Ça le resserre au passage — avant, n'importe quel porteur du token statique pouvait gérer les credentials.

**Où vit le contrôle.** Dans `AuthMiddleware` : il bufferise le corps, y cherche un `tools/call` visant un de ces outils, et renvoie `403` avant que la requête n'atteigne l'app. Volontairement **pas** un contextvar posé autour de l'appel applicatif — en HTTP streamable, un tool peut s'exécuter dans une tâche créée avant la requête courante, donc le principal serait perdu ou hérité de la requête précédente.

## 4. Suppression du token en chemin d'URL

Un secret dans une URL est écrit dans tous les logs de proxy et d'accès qu'il traverse, atterrit dans l'historique et les `Referer`, et ne peut être effacé d'aucun d'eux. Le code annonçait déjà cette suppression. Le Bearer statique reste, comparaison en `hmac.compare_digest`.

## Déploiement

`docker-compose.yml` télécharge les sources une par une : `tokens.js` ajouté à la liste (sans ça le conteneur plante sur le `require`), plus `TOKENS_CONFIG_PATH` et `OAUTH_ADMIN_ROLE`.

## Vérification

- **105 tests** : 29 sur `tokens.js`, 19 sur `AuthMiddleware` (harnais ASGI pilotant le vrai middleware, `/oidc/v1/userinfo` e

author: jardo-51
body:
Stacked on #26. That PR retries the picker's open when it stalls, but couldn't pin down *why* it stalls — so the retry papers over a failure it re-triggers on every attempt. This finds the cause and removes it.

Root cause is written up in detail on #22, so in short: when the target message renders near the top of the pane, its toolbar sits under the pinned-message banner, and the banner overlaps the "More reactions" entry. The open force-clicks that entry — but a forced click only waives the actionability check, it doesn't click *through* a cover; the browser still delivers the event to whatever is topmost at the point, which is the banner. Clicking the banner scrolls the pane to the pinned message (weeks back), so the picker never opens **and** the pane is left displaced, which cascades into "message not found" for every later id in a batch.

## The fix

Dispatch the click on the entry element itself instead of clicking at its coordinates. `locator.dispatchEvent('click', …)` hands the event straight to the button whatever overlaps it, so the banner never sees it. The entry is already singled out by its `data-tid`, so the target is known — hit-testing was only in the way.

One line changes; the rest of the diff is the comment explaining why.

## Why the retry alone didn't help

Each retry re-hovers the same message at the same top position and force-clicks the same banner again. Worse, the first banner-click already moved the pane, so the retry's re-hover (`scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`) times out — the "the toolbar did not come back up" second error. The retry from #26 is still worth keeping for genuine stalls (an empty emoji grid, a frame that never renders); this just stops the banner from being one of them.

## Validation

Reproduced deterministically with a probe that repeats the open path faithfully (real emoji click + pill, batch, one shared finder). Before: the second message that lands under the banner fails at "no picker followed", the pane jumps from the `1788…` id range to `1784…` (the pinned message), and the next five ids all fail their history walk. After switching the entry click to `dispatchEvent`: every message that lands under the banner opens the picker, the pane never leaves the `1788…` range, and the cascade is gone. `elementFromPoint` at the entry's centre confirms the banner is the covering element (`data-tid="pinned-message-banner"`), and the entry-click step drops from ~200–1600 ms (a forced click resolving against a cover) to ~40 ms.

author: frdyx
body:
Track A **PR2** extracts the hook-firing core out of `commands/hooks.mjs` (1258 lines) into `template/maddu/runtime/lib/harness/` so the Codex, Hermes and OpenHands adapters can share it. The campaign calls it the highest-risk slice and isolates it precisely because it is refactor-only: **nothing Claude Code observes may change.**

This is that PR's success condition — `node scripts/test/harness-hook-core.mjs` — landed **before the refactor exists**, and written by the supervisor rather than the implementer.

That ordering is the whole point. The goal's own constraints say *"the implementing actor never writes its own suite"*, and a suite written afterwards can only describe what the new code happens to do. This one describes what the current code does, so the refactor has something to be wrong against.

## What it locks

The surface Claude Code actually consumes — never internals:

- every `hooks fire` exits 0; the hook may never fail a tool call
- stdout is empty or strictly parseable JSON (Claude Code parses it as context)
- `PreToolUse` discriminates three ways: **silent / nudge / deny**
- a throw at either seam, and malformed stdin, are contained silently
- `SessionStart` announces a well-formed minted session id
- `SessionEnd` is silent and idempotent

Everything runs through `node bin/maddu.mjs hooks fire <event>` with canned stdin against a throwaway fixture. **No internal import, no function name, and no path from inside `hooks.mjs` appears anywhere in the suite** — so the extraction is free to move any of it and this still means the same thing afterwards.

## Behavior was probed, not assumed

Before writing a single assertion I ran the real thing and recorded what it does:

| input | today |
|---|---|
| non-mutating tool (`Read`) | silent |
| mutating tool (`Edit`), standard governance | **nudge** |
| mutating tool (`Edit`), strict governance | **deny** |
| malformed stdin | silent, exit 0 |
| throw at `bootstrap` / `handler` seam | silent, exit 0 |

That three-way split is the anti-vacuity core: a gate that always denied, or always kept quiet, could not produce all three. Two further controls sit above it — the verdict reader is shown to discriminate on synthetic input before it is trusted, and the throw seam is shown to be **inert without `MADDU_SELF_TEST`**, so "silent" under the seam is containment working rather than the case failing to run.

## Mutation-tested

A lock-in suite proves nothing unless it would catch a change. Three regressions a refactor could plausibly introduce, applied one at a time to `commands/hooks.mjs`:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| a stray `console.log` leaks into the stdout Claude Code parses | **caught** — 8 assertions red |
| the deny path degrades to an advisory | **caught** — 1 red |
| a contained failure becomes a non-zero exit | **caught** — 3 red |

Source restored byte-identical after each, tree verified clean.

**On method:** the first attempt at the third mutation reported MISSED. The right response was to inspect the mutation, not to conclude the suite had a gap — I had gated the injected exit on an env var the suite never sets, so it was inert. A mutation that cannot fire proves nothing about the suite that missed it. Same failure family as a grep that cannot match.

## Scope

| | |
|---|---|
| `harness-hook-core` | 17 pass · 0 fail · 3.8s |
| version bump | none — `scripts/` does not ship and no consumer behavior changes |
| what remains | PR2 itself, which must go to an actor who did **not** write this suite |

author: quintinshaw
body:
## Summary

`openasr serve --parent-pid` now joins the same graceful shutdown path as Ctrl-C / SIGTERM instead of calling `process::exit`, so ggml Metal backends drop before process teardown.

## Why

When Desktop 0.1.22 aborted on system-audio start, the sidecar logged `parent process N is gone` and then immediately:

```
ggml-metal-device.m:917: GGML_ASSERT([rsets->data count] == 0) failed
```

`crates/openasr-cli/src/parent_watchdog.rs` used `std::process::exit(0)`. That skips Rust `Drop`, so atexit-time Metal device teardown still saw residency sets held by a live backend. There was no existing serve graceful-shutdown hook in `openasr-server` (`axum::serve` is awaited without `with_graceful_shutdown`). This PR does not touch `openasr-server`; the CLI wraps that future and cancels it.

## Changes

- Parent-loss watchdog signals a oneshot instead of `process::exit`.
- `openasr serve` awaits that signal together with Ctrl-C and SIGTERM, then returns so `NativeExecutionServices` / ggml backends drop before the process exits.
- Unit test: a dead child pid fires the oneshot without exiting the test process.
- Manual: isolated `OPENASR_HOME`, `openasr serve --no-model --parent-pid <parent>`, kill parent after Metal init (`use residency sets = true`). Child exits in ~3s. Log has `parent process ... is gone` and no `GGML_ASSERT`.

## Tests run

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p openasr-cli` (289 passed, 4 skipped)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --doc`
- [ ] `cargo deny check`

## Manual smoke checks

- Isolated `OPENASR_HOME`; `openasr serve --addr 127.0.0.1:0 --backend native --no-model --parent-pid <sleep>`; kill parent after `ggml_metal_rsets_init`. Child exits; log has no `GGML_ASSERT`.

## Model-family changes (when applicable)

- [ ] I followed the root `AGENTS.md` model-family onboarding entry point and
      ran `cargo xtask family conformance --profile-id <profile-id>`.
- [ ] I stated `core-only`, `staged release candidate`, or `public-ready`; any
      staged/public-ready work completes Model Onboarding Step 5 without
      hand-editing generated catalog/registry truth.
- [ ] Real-weight quality/performance claims have artifact-backed evidence;
      otherwise they are explicitly listed as unverified.

## Docs updated

- [x] README or docs updated, if behavior or limitations changed.
- [x] No docs overclaim current capabilities.

## Scope / non-goals

- Does not change `openasr-server`. Cancelling the CLI-awaited `axum::serve` future is the shutdown signal.
- Does not fix the macOS system-audio `__rust_foreign_exception` abort (separate PR).

## Artifact confirmation

- [x] I did not commit model weights, large binaries, generated artifacts, secrets, or private audio.
- [x] I did not add vendored runtime sources outside `crates/openasr-core/third_party/openasr-ggml`.

author: gtapps
body:
## Summary

A hermit asked to install something in its container could only see `Dockerfile.hermit` and the compose file, so that is what it edited: the one channel a later `hermit-evolve` can drop. This adds a `docker-customize` skill that routes the request at the point the choice is made, and gives humans the same map in `docs/always-on.md`.

Writing it surfaced a documented behavior that does not hold: `docker.packages` is baked into `Dockerfile.hermit` by `packagesBlock()` at **template render** time (`scripts/render-docker-templates.ts:70`), while `hermit-docker update` only runs `docker compose build` against the on-disk file (`state-templates/bin/hermit-docker:490`). Setting the config value installs nothing, and no operator-facing command closes the gap: `/docker-setup` re-runs the wizard, `hermit-evolve` is the upgrade path, and a bare re-render overwrites compose, the Dockerfile and the entrypoint in place (which is why evolve 3-way merges instead). Since the container runs as `USER claude` with `cap_drop: ALL`, a package can only enter through the image, so the apt channel is one step: add the `RUN apt-get` layer to `Dockerfile.hermit`, then `hermit-docker update`.

Closes #956.

## Changes

**New skill** — `plugins/claude-code-hermit/skills/docker-customize/SKILL.md`, model-invocable, three channels in order:

| Need | Where it lives | Applies | Survives evolve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| apt package | a `RUN apt-get` layer in `Dockerfile.hermit` | `.claude-code-hermit/bin/hermit-docker update` | the edit marks the file `customized-kept`, so evolve keeps it and stops applying upstream changes; re-check after an upgrade |
| binary, `pip`/`npm -g`, env, dir, side service | `docker-entrypoint.hermit-local.sh` (`HERMIT_ENTRY_PHASE`), files under `.claude.local/` | `hermit-docker restart`, no rebuild | yes, upgrades never touch the sidecar |
| volume, port, capability, base image | one commented block in compose or `Dockerfile.hermit` | rebuild or restart | 3-way merged with a `.bak` **when a baseline exists and upstream moved**; otherwise left alone with no backup |

**Docs** — `always-on.md` gains § Customizing the container (the table above) replacing the one-paragraph sidecar note; `upgrading.md` § Project Customizations gains a `**Container**` bullet pointing at it; `troubleshooting.md:147` corrected, it claimed a rebuild applied a `docker.packages` change.

## Behavior delta

```
BEFORE: operator: "install gog in the container"
        ─> hermit hand-edits Dockerfile.hermit + compose (only channel it can see)
        ─> next hermit-evolve merges the rendered templates; the block can be dropped
        ─> gog gone, integrations dark until someone diagnoses it

AFTER:  operator: "install gog in the container"
        ─> docker-customize triggers
        ─> apt package?            ─> a RUN apt-get layer in Dockerfile.hermit, rebuild.
                                      Config alone installs nothing.
        ─> binary / env / service? ─> docker-entrypoint.hermit-local.sh, files under
                                      .claude.local/, runs now + every boot, no rebuild,
                                      never touched by evolve
        ─> only compose/Dockerfile? ─> one commented block, evolve 3-way merges it,
                                       re-check after every evolve
        ─> humans get the same map in docs/always-on.md
```

## Blast radius

- **Released surfaces touched:** `docs/always-on.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` (repo-side, read on GitHub). `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.
- **Unreleased surfaces touched:** the new `docker-customize` skill. No state template, no script, no hook, no config schema, no version floor.
- **Downstream operators:** nothing to do. No migration, no config change, no rebuild; existing container customizations are untouched. They stop being told a `docker.packages` edit plus a rebuild installs anything, and get one place that says where each kind of change belongs. Arrives on the next `/plugin update` after a release.
- **Downstream hermits:** one more always-listed skill description (the budget guard sits at 7191 B against its 8600 B ceiling). On a container-install request the hermit now picks the sidecar instead of the Dockerfile, so what it installs survives the next evolve.
- **Merge-class note:** editing `Dockerfile.hermit` moves it to `customized-kept`, so upstream Dockerfile changes stop reaching that hermit until the operator re-syncs. Both the skill and the docs say so. The clean fix is an operator layer for the Dockerfile (the entrypoint already has one via `docker-entrypoint.hermit-local.sh`, and `hermit-docker:46` already passes a second compose `-f`); the plan fences that out, tracked in #961.
- **Known gaps, deliberately out of scope:** the #955 evolve merge bug is unfixed, so a hermit that *already* hand-edited its Dockerfile stays exposed. `skills/hermit-settings/SKILL.md:361` still prints `Rebuild your container to apply` after a `docker.packages` edit — the same wrong claim corrected in the three docs here; the plan fenced `hermit-settings docker` off.
- **Per-actor ledger:** grok wrote the skill and the three doc edits from the frozen plan. `/code-review high --fix` found the apt-package contract was factually wrong and applied 8 fixes (sidecar `${PROJECT_DIR}` anchoring, `chmod +x` + `PATH`, `bash -n` ordering, conditional `.bak` claim, `docker compose config -q`, `hermit-docker update` side effects). Operator kept the `troubleshooting.md` fix, then rejected a first attempt at the apt-package routing that sent operators to `/docker-setup` or the next `hermit-evolve` — neither is an apply path; `39e642e4` replaced it with a record-then-write-then-rebuild pair, then `073ab806` cut it to one step after the operator questioned whether the `docker.packages` half earned its keep: tracing `evolve-plan.ts:330-375` and `classifyOne:159-179` showed a hand-added `RUN` layer already survives evolve as `customized-kept`, so the config half bought only the `unmodified` classification. The consequences are now stated rather than engineered around. The plan file records each corrected contract. I reverted code-review's `CHANGELOG.md` edit, since the plan reserves that for `/commit`.

## Test plan

Plan's Closing verification, re-run by me in the worktree after the last edit — all four rows exit 0:

```
0  head -5 skills/docker-customize/SKILL.md | grep -q '^name: docker-customize$' && ! grep -q 'disable-model-invocation' … && ! grep -Eq '#95[56]|PROP-' …
0  [ "$(grep -c '^### Customizing the container' docs/always-on.md)" = 1 ] && [ "$(grep -c 'Customize boot in' docs/always-on.md)" = 0 ]
0  [ "$(grep -c '^\- \*\*Container\*\*' docs/upgrading.md)" = 1 ]
0  bun test --parallel --timeout=45000
```

The last line is the CI spine from `.github/workflows/test-hooks.yml:72-73`.

body:
The first freely positioned UI in the app: a small, draggable window hosting one running external command's live output — ping and tail -f were the motivating cases, since neither should have to permanently cover content the way the Details sidebar (the obvious reuse candidate) would.

- `toolWindow`: bordered Box (top border row = title bar) + scrollable TextView, implementing Draw/MouseHandler/InputHandler directly
- Drag-to-move with the mouse — verified against tview's actual `Application.fireMouseActions`/`MouseMove` source (not guessed) that `event.Buttons()` reliably reports the held button during a move
- Alt+arrow keys move the focused window; plain arrows still scroll the content — **live-verified in a real terminal via tmux**, not just unit-tested, since Alt-key encoding varies across terminals
- Non-modal, multi-instance: each window is its own dynamically added/removed Pages entry — panel and other tool windows stay usable
- `openToolCommand(title, name, args)`: the general-purpose launcher future Toolbox entries will reuse; stdout+stderr merged via `io.Pipe` so neither is silently dropped; closing (Escape) cancels the process via `exec.CommandContext`
- "Ping (test)" under a new "Tools" context-menu section is this slice's own placeholder proof of concept — the real Toolbox (networking/hardware departments, see feature_ideas.txt) replaces it later

**Tested:** `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` (793 passed, +10 new), `gofmt -l .` clean. **Live-verified in tmux** against a real ping process: drag-to-move mid-stream (output kept flowing uninterrupted), all four Alt+arrow directions, a plain arrow *not* moving the window, and — checked via `ps -ef` inside the tmux session — that closing the window with Escape actually kills the running ping process, not just the window.

author: johnnyyammine
body:
## The mismatched right edges

Reported as "the first paragraph doesn't go to the same length as the second". It was not paragraph against paragraph — it was the **summary quote** against the body:

| Block | Right edge | Sized as |
|---|---|---|
| Summary quote | 980 | `80ch` at 15.5px = 780px |
| Every body paragraph | 957 | `78ch` at 15px = 737px |

`ch` is the natural unit for a reading measure, but it is relative to each element's *own* font-size. Two blocks with near-identical `ch` counts and different font sizes landed 23px apart.

Ragged text hid this completely. #17 justified the prose, which turns every block's right edge into a hard line — and two hard lines 23px apart read as a mistake rather than as two deliberate measures.

Both now share one absolute measure:

```css
:root { --measure: 46rem; }   /* the 78ch the body already had */
```

Summary, paragraphs, lists and blockquotes all end on the same pixel — verified at 936 for all four.

## Further left

The page padding is already the left edge, so the only two terms left to spend were the rail width and the gap:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rail (above 1180) | 188px | 176px |
| Rail (below 1180) | 172px | 158px |
| Gap (above 1180) | 40px | 32px |
| Gap (below 1180) | 28px | 22px |

The article starts **20px further left at 1000px** and **28px further left above 1180**.

**This is close to the limit.** Any further shift has to come out of the rail, and below about 158px the longer entries begin wrapping to three lines — which makes the rail taller and bulkier, the opposite of what it was narrowed for. At 158px every entry still fits in two lines except two formula citations carrying a parenthesised year.

## Verification

```
        rail            article.left   para.right   summary.right
1000    [20, 178]  158       200           936           936
1280    [20, 196]  176       228           964           964
1440    [40, 216]  176       248           984           984
1600   [120, 296]  176       328          1064          1064
```

- Justification and hyphenation still active above 700px, off at 390px.
- Full sweep of all twelve concept pages at 1500 / 1150 / 950 / 390px: no horizontal scroll, no console errors.
- 45 tests pass; build reports `0 warnings, 0 errors`.

author: yonggyu
body:
이슈 #316 의 **1번(검수자가 원고를 여는 경로)만** 다룬다. 2·3·4번은 다른 PR 이다.

## 무엇을 열었나

`GET /api/v1/admin/reviews/{storyId}` (`readReviewManuscript`) — 큐의 형제 자리다.

큐(`listReviewQueue`)는 **무엇을 볼 차례인가**를 답하고 원고 본문을 담지 않는다. `ReviewQueueItem` 이 스스로 *"원문 열람은 **감사가 걸린 다른 문**"* 이라고 적었지만 **그 문이 계약에 없었다.** 그대로면 관리자는 제목과 상태만 보고 승인/반려한다.

## 담은 것

| 담은 것 | 왜 |
|---|---|
| 제목 · 한 줄 소개 · 세계관 소개 · 상태 · 가시성 · 생성 시각 | 기본 정보 |
| 작성자 **표시명** | §13-7. `player_ref` 는 나가지 않는다 (I-3). 설정 안 했으면 `null` — 이름을 지어내지 않는다 |
| **세계관 프롬프트 원문** | UGC 원고의 본체. 매 턴 모델에 들어가는 문장이다 |
| 캐릭터 이름 + **페르소나 프롬프트** | 작품 상세는 감추지만 검수는 반대다 — 안 보고 한 승인은 절반만 본 승인이다 |
| 챕터 번호 · 제목 · 최소/최대 턴 | 이야기의 뼈대 |
| 엔딩 번호 · 라벨 · **에필로그 원문** · 기본/비밀 | 독자가 마지막에 읽는 작성자의 문장이다 |
| 자동 검수 요약 — 판정 · **카테고리** · 시각 | R8.5 · R8.7. 걸린 항목은 담지 않는다 (S-11) |

**가장 마지막 버전을 본다** (R8.8) — 판정과 열람이 다른 버전을 보면 승인된 적 없는 원고가 열린다.
**상태로 거르지 않는다** — 방금 판정한 작품을 다시 열 수 없게 된다.

## 뺀 것과 이유

- **미리보기 3턴 — 데이터에 도달할 길이 없다.** 먼저 확인했다: §13-5 대로 미리보기는 임시 `draft`·`private` **작품**과 그 위의 테스트 세션을 만들고(`PreviewController` → `publishNew`), 제출은 **별개의 작품**을 발행한다(`SubmissionService`). 원고가 기억하는 작품 id 는 제출된 쪽 하나이며 미리보기 작품은 아무 데도 연결되지 않은 채 파기 대상이 된다(§13-37, B-61). **없는 것을 지어내지 않았다** — §13-61 에 적었고 **후속 이슈 후보**로 올린다(미리보기 세션을 원고에 연결 + 파기 정책 재검토).
- 진입/엔딩 조건식 — 판정 로직이지 사람이 읽는 문장이 아니다.
- `player_ref`(I-3) · 검수 이력 전체(#316-③) · 신고 내역(#316-②) · 초상/커버 이미지(#315 가 아직 안 열림).

## 감사 기록 — 기존 장치를 그대로 썼다

| 기록 | 어디에 | 실패하면 |
|---|---|---|
| 관리자 행위 (R14.5) | `admin_audit_log` — `AdminAccessGuard.recordAction("admin.review.manuscript", …)` | 행위를 막지 않는다 |
| **원문 열람** (R12.3, S-5) | `access_audit_log` — `AccessAuditRecorder.record(…, STORY_DRAFT, storyId)` | **원문이 나가지 않는다** |

`AuditedResource.STORY_DRAFT` 는 *"검수 전 UGC 원고"* 로 이미 정의돼 있었고 **이 문이 그 값의 첫 사용처다.** 새로 만들지 않았다.
순서는 ① 작품을 찾고 ② 열람을 기록하고 ③ 원문을 읽는다 — ①을 미루면 없는 작품의 열람이 쌓이고, ②를 미루면 기록되지 않는 열람 경로가 생긴다.

세 조건(S-4)은 `listReviewQueue` 와 같게 `requireAdmin` 한 줄로 선다.

## 모듈 경계

`admin → authoring :: review → catalog :: publish · catalog :: query` — 허용 의존 안이다. admin 은 catalog 의 Repository·Entity 를 직접 잡지 않는다. 표시명은 `common/spi` 의 `AuthorDisplayNameQuery`(ADR-0002 형태), 열람 감사는 `common/spi` 의 `AccessAuditRecorder`. 스키마 간 JOIN 없음 — catalog 안에서만 읽고 promptlog 는 SPI 너머다.

## 문서

- `docs/openapi.yaml` — `/api/v1/admin/reviews` 와 `.../verdict` **사이**에 경로 하나, `ReviewQueueItem` 근처에 스키마 다섯(`ReviewManuscript` · `ManuscriptCharacter` · `ManuscriptChapter` · `ManuscriptEnding` · `AutoCheckSummary`). `x-notice-exempt` 는 형제 관리자 응답과 같은 이유로 붙였다(관리자 화면이라 사전 고지 대상이 아니다).
- `docs/corrections.md` — **§13-61 (신규)** 만 더했다. 다른 절은 건드리지 않았다.

## `docs/internal/` 부재

이 기계에 `docs/internal/` 이 없어 **R 조항 원문을 대조하지 못했다.** 값·정책을 지어내지 않았고, 근거는 레포 안의 기존 코드·계약·`docs/corrections.md` 와 오케스트레이터의 결정표다. 새로 정한 정책 값은 없다.

## 검증

- `./gradlew test` — **746개 통과**
- `./gradlew integrationTest` — **548개 통과** (`AdminReviewApiIntegrationTests` 12/12, 그중 신규 5)

신규 테스트: `SEC4_without_a_step_up_the_manuscript_is_not_visible` · `S13_61_the_manuscript_carries_what_a_verdict_needs` · `R12_3_reading_a_manuscript_is_audited` · `I3_the_manuscript_carries_no_player_ref`(`doesNotContain` 로 식별자 누출까지) · `S13_61_an_unknown_story_has_no_manuscript`(404 이고 **열람 기록도 남지 않는다**).

`src/main/**` 추가 305줄.

### 위키 갱신 필요

- `50-API/*` — 관리자 검수에 **원고 열람** 경로가 생겼다. 큐/판정과 나란히 두고, "큐는 무엇을 볼 차례인가, 상세는 무엇을 보고 판정하는가"의 구분을 적는다.
- `60-Domain/*` (UGC 검수) — 검수자가 보는 것의 목록과 **미리보기 3턴이 왜 빠졌는지**(§13-61).
- `00-Overview/current-status` — #316-① 완료, ②③④ 잔여. 기준 커밋·날짜 갱신.
- `00-Overview/doc-code-drift` — `AuditedResource.STORY_DRAFT` 가 정의만 있고 쓰이지 않던 상태가 해소됨.

author: smitdonda
body:
Found by driving the editor in a browser, then reproduced in core with no React in the picture.

## The bug

Setting a column's **Width %** to 70 beside a 50 gave you **58**. Typing 70 again gave 62, then 65 — the number crept towards the one you asked for and never arrived.

```
start            [ 50, 50 ]
patch 70 once    [ 58, 42 ]   ← you asked for 70
patch 70 again   [ 62, 38 ]
and again        [ 65, 35 ]
setColumnWidths  [ 70, 30 ]   ← the op that was right all along
```

## Why

The field patched `width` like any other prop, which left the row summing to **120%** for an instant. `normalize` repairs that by scaling every column proportionally — 70 and 50 both × 100/120 — which is exactly right for a malformed imported document and exactly wrong as the answer to somebody deliberately setting one column.

`setColumnWidths` had the correct behaviour all along. The Inspector simply was not using it.

## The fix

Width is now handled as what it actually is: not the column's own business, but the row's. Your column gets the value you typed, the siblings absorb the remainder in proportion to what they had, rounding drift lands on the widest sibling, and the whole row is written at once.

Asking for 100 gives **95**, because every sibling keeps the field's own 5% minimum. A column squeezed to zero is one you cannot see, and therefore cannot click on to undo what you just did.

Every other column prop goes through the unchanged path.

## Verified

Two regression tests — typing 70 gives `[70, 30]` and stays there when repeated; asking for 100 never drops a sibling below 5 and the row still totals 100. 487 tests, typecheck and lint clean. Re-checked in the real playground afterwards: 70 renders 70/30, repeating does not creep, 100 renders 95/5.

author: sisshiki1969
body:
## Summary

Two independent changes, one commit each.

**`Add region-reusing match/search API`** — monoruby matches in a hot loop and currently pays an `onig_region_new` / `onig_region_free` per match through the `Captures`-returning API. This adds:

- `Regex::match_at_with_region(&[u8], at, &mut Region)` — anchored match via `onig_match`, no forward search. Returns the byte offset of the match **end** (`onig_match` returns a length, so `at + len`).
- `Regex::search_with_region(&[u8], from, &mut Region)` — forward search via `onig_search`. Returns the byte offset of the match **start**.
- `Regex::onig_result` — private helper mapping a return code to `Ok(Some)` / `Ok(None)` on `ONIG_MISMATCH` / `Err`.

Both take a caller-owned `&mut Region` reused across calls, so the register array only grows once. `Region::new` becomes `pub` for that; `Region` already exposes `len` / `pos` / `clear`, so registers can be read back without going through `Captures`.

Note on anchoring: `\A` and `^` anchor at the start of the haystack, not at `at`. A caller wanting CRuby `StringScanner` semantics passes the suffix as the haystack with `at == 0`.

**`Track Onigmo sources in build.rs rerun-if-changed`** — a build fix, not related to the API above.

`build.rs` printed `cargo:rerun-if-changed=.gitmodules`, and emitting any `rerun-if-changed` turns off cargo's default of rebuilding when anything in the package changes. The C sources handed to `cc` were therefore untracked, and 4db1266 (pointing the submodule at cruby-compat) changed only the gitlink — so cargo considered the build script fresh and kept a `libonigmo.a` built *before* those fixes landed. That is why `nested_quantifier_not_reduced` and `word_class_matches_join_control` fail on a tree that has the fixes checked out.

The fix lists every compiled `.c` plus the headers they include. The headers matter: bindgen's `CargoCallbacks` only registers what `wrapper.h` pulls in, and the `CR_Word` change lives in `enc/unicode/name2ctype.h`. Explicit paths rather than watching the `onigmo` directory, so churn under `onigmo/.git` doesn't rebuild the whole C library.

## Test plan

- `cargo test`: 15/15 lib tests and 11/11 doctests pass. Both previously-failing tests pass once the C library actually rebuilds.
- New API verified with a temporary integration test (not committed): match-end offset, anchored match at a non-zero `at`, group registers via `region.pos(0/1/2)`, `Ok(None)` on mismatch, and `search_with_region` returning the match start.
- Build tracking verified both directions: two consecutive `cargo build`s do not re-run the build script (which also confirms no non-existent path is listed, since a missing path would force a rerun every time), and touching `onigmo/enc/unicode/name2ctype.h` does rebuild `libonigmo.a`.

author: hotell
body:
## Summary

The font subsetting plugin silently subset **nothing** on rspack whenever the app used a named runtime chunk. This fixes the root cause, lowers the supported rspack floor to `>=2.0.0` behind a capability guard, and adds unit tests that pin both behaviours.

## The bug

`getRuntimeSpec()` passed `compilation.entrypoints.keys()` to `moduleGraph.getUsedExports()` as a stand-in for runtime names. Those two coincide only when the runtime chunk is *unnamed*. As soon as an app sets `entry.runtime` or `optimization.runtimeChunk`, they diverge — `getUsedExports()` then returns `false` for every module, the plugin concludes no icons are used, and every font ships un-subset.

| `runtime` passed to `getUsedExports` | result |
| --- | --- |
| `['atoms']` (entrypoint name) | `false` ❌ |
| `['shared-runtime']` (chunk runtime) | `["GamesFilled"]` ✅ |

This was never an rspack version issue — it reproduces identically on 2.0.1 and 2.1.10.

The fix derives the runtime spec from `chunk.runtime` across `compilation.chunks`, handling both the `string` and `Set<string>` shapes. Entrypoint names are kept only as a last-resort fallback.

New `namedRuntimeChunk` fixture, measured on both bundlers:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| emitted font bytes | 2,818,416 B | **1,164 B** |

## rspack 2.0.x support

Peer range lowered `>=2.1.0` → `>=2.0.0`. The only 2.1-only API the plugin touches is `moduleGraph.getProvidedExports()` ([rspack#14349](https://github.com/web-infra-dev/rspack/pull/14349)), which is needed solely to resolve icons reached through a namespace import (`import * as ...`). `getUsedExports()` — the hot path for named imports — landed in 2.0.0 ([rspack#13519](https://github.com/web-infra-dev/rspack/pull/13519)).

So on 2.0.x the plugin now feature-detects: named imports subset normally, namespace imports are left un-subset and a build **warning** explains why and points at the upgrade. Previously this path threw `TypeError: getProvidedExports is not a function`.

Verified manually on rspack 2.0.1:

| fixture | bytes | warning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `atoms` | 1,164 B | — |
| `namedRuntimeChunk` | 1,164 B | — |
| `atomsImportStar` | 2,818,416 B | emitted, build succeeds |

## Tests

The existing integration suites only observe emitted bytes, so they can't assert *which* runtime was queried, nor simulate an absent API. Added `test/plugin.test.ts`, which drives `apply()` against a fake compiler — no bundler required:

1. rspack path queries the chunk runtime, not the entrypoint
2. webpack path queries with `undefined` (merge across all runtimes)
3. missing `getProvidedExports` → warns and skips, no throw
4. namespace imports subset when the API is present
5. named imports subset without the API

Both regressions confirmed caught by reintroducing them:

- revert the runtime fix → `expected [['main']] to deeply equal [['shared-runtime']]`
- remove the guard → `TypeError: getProvidedExports is not a function`

## Validation

- Unit 5/5, conformance, webpack 6/6, rspack 6/6, lint clean

## Caveat worth flagging

CI still only exercises rspack 2.1.10, so the `>=2.0.0` floor is verified manually here rather than continuously. The unit tests cover the capability-guard logic, but not a real 2.0.x build. Pinning a second aliased rspack in CI is possible (~40 MB of extra native binaries) if reviewers would rather have that guarantee than the manual check.


## Follow-up: namespace-import fallout is now scoped to the package

Review surfaced a second, worse bug in the capability guard above. Skipping only the *offending module* let its siblings subset the package's shared fonts down to their own glyphs, deleting the ones the namespace import needed — a green build shipping broken glyphs, rather than the merely-larger font the warning claimed.

Reproduced as a failing unit test before fixing:

```
AssertionError: expected [ { name: 'Regular.ttf', size: 660 } ] to deeply equal []
```

`resolveUsedIconExports` now returns an `UNRESOLVABLE_NAMESPACE_IMPORT` sentinel rather than a bare `null`, so the caller can tell "contributes nothing" apart from "glyphs are real but unknowable". The latter poisons its `pkgLibPath`, which is dropped before subsetting, leaving that package's fonts whole. Scoped per-package rather than per-compilation, since multiple `@fluentui/react-icons` instances are supported and poisoning one shouldn't disable the others.

Also applied to `getProvidedExports()` returning `null`/boolean (`optimization.providedExports` disabled) — identical failure mode. The warning now names the affected package and covers both causes.

Not expressible as an integration fixture: CI runs rspack 2.1.10, where `getProvidedExports` exists and the bug is unreachable.

Unit tests now 6/6; webpack 6/6, rspack 6/6, conformance and lint unchanged.

## Summary

The "Open in app" / install icon in the browser still showed the old mark, even though the in-app UI and favicon updated. The manifest icon `src`s were versioned (`?v=oct6`), but the manifest `<link>` in `index.html` had no query, so Chrome kept serving the **cached old `manifest.json`** and never saw the new icon URLs. - `frontend/index.html`: `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.json">` → `href="/manifest.json?v=oct6"`.

author: lloydsmart
body:
## Summary

Implement the OPNsense signing milestone for UniFi certificate renewal while preserving both private-key boundaries.

- add a narrow OPNsense Trust API client limited to CA listing, CSR signing, and public CRT retrieval
- load OPNsense API credentials only from defensive private secret files
- constrain all application-controlled security-sensitive file reads beneath the fixed `/run/secrets` root
- use fixed credential names (`opnsense-api-key` / `opnsense-api-secret`) and basename-only custom CA selection
- pin and validate the trusted secrets directory and open contained files relative to its directory descriptor
- enforce verified HTTPS, TLS 1.2+, hostname verification, and redirect rejection
- derive OPNsense `key_type` from a freshly re-inspected CSR rather than inheriting Aruba's hard-coded value
- support RSA 2048/3072/4096 deliberately; current UniFi RSA-4096 produces `"4096"`
- retrieve only the public signed certificate
- validate returned certificate subject, SAN identity, SPKI continuity, validity, lifetime, Basic Constraints, EKU, Key Usage, and native offline CA path
- record unsupported CSR SAN identity types so URI/email identities cannot pass unnoticed
- update README to reflect implemented OPNsense signing/validation while leaving UniFi installation and live verification out of scope

## Security properties

The UniFi private key remains entirely inside the UniFi environment. Only an already-validated public CSR is sent to OPNsense.

The OPNsense CA private key remains entirely inside OPNsense. This client uses only:

- `GET /api/trust/cert/ca_list`
- `POST /api/trust/cert/add` with `action: sign_csr`
- `POST /api/trust/cert/generate_file/<uuid>/crt`

It does not use `/api/trust/cert/search` and never requests private-key, P12, or PFX material.

Credential files are fixed beneath `/run/secrets` and must be owner/root-only readable (`0400`/`0600`); group/world-readable credential files are rejected. Optional custom CA files are selected by a validated single basename beneath the same trusted root and may remain normally readable, e.g. `0644`. Arbitrary absolute paths, traversal, nested paths, and path separators are rejected before filesystem access.

Returned certificates are treated as untrusted until validation succeeds. SPKI SHA-256 must exactly match the freshly inspected CSR. The leaf must have Basic Constraints `CA=false`, exactly `serverAuth` EKU, and when Key Usage is present it must include `digitalSignature` and prohibit certificate/CRL signing.

## GitHub Advanced Security remediation

The initial PR analysis reported four CodeQL `py/path-injection` findings in `src/secure_file.py`. Commit `6e112b90d84ec61dacf429684fd4a76ba22d6c5c` removed arbitrary path selection and introduced the fixed `/run/secrets` trust boundary with validated basename selection and descriptor-relative file opening.

On the refreshed GitHub Advanced Security analysis, all four original findings became outdated and were automatically resolved by the GHAS bot; no replacement path-injection findings were created.

## Validation

- `ruff check .` — passed
- `ruff format --check .` — passed
- `pytest` — **252 passed**
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Markdown lint — passed
- Gitleaks working-tree scan — no leaks found
- Gitleaks reachable-history scan — no leaks found
- dependency audit — all four lock files passed with no known vulnerabilities
- shell syntax checks — passed
- dependency/lock files unchanged
- GitHub Actions on current head — Python tests, Python lint, Markdown lint, and Security scanning all passed
- commit `58f21b88e67d6f81362271fc4b01c54dfd55c1db` is cryptographically signed and verified by GitHub
- remediation commit `6e112b90d84ec61dacf429684fd4a76ba22d6c5c` is cryptographically signed and verified by GitHub

## Out of scope

- UniFi certificate import
- UniFi restart/reload
- live HTTPS endpoint verification
- exact live DER verification after installation
- Docker/host orchestration
- threshold-based unattended renewal
- key rotation
- keystore permission hardening tracked in #3

Closes #7

author: iurdivad-netizen
body:
Two changes, one purpose: the decision the game is built around now resolves as loudly as it builds.

The resolution is animated. Three phases build a moment a beat at a time and then the outcome arrived as a line of text. Now the ball flies on the same canvas the moment was read on — into the net, the keeper's committed dive, the post, or out to the man the pass picked — for under a second before the overlay comes down. The pause the match screen already took after a decision absorbs it, so the rhythm of a match is unchanged, and nothing is revealed early: the outcome is decided before the first frame draws. The keeper strip now agrees with the picture during the resolution, and the whole thing is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion with the banner carrying the same fact. Shootout kicks play the same ending.

The game has sound. A synthesized Web Audio layer — no files, nothing to 404: a crowd bed for the whole match that swells as a chance builds, a beat per line of story, the options' reveal, an audible clock that gains weight as the window drains (never at the untimed pace — an audible clock is the pressure that setting removes), the keeper's commit, kick-off and full-time whistles, and an outcome cue landing on the animation's impact frame. Background goals roar and concessions groan from the commentary feed; the engine debounces the roar so a goal never sounds twice. Every cue restates something already on screen, so the new Sound switch (in settings, on by default, saved with the rest, additive for old saves) is genuinely binary: off loses atmosphere, never information.

author: stefanosbalaskas
body:
Add a transparent paired-fold comparison layer for matched eye-event validation results without treating cross-validation folds as independent inferential replicates.

- add `PairedModelDifferences` and `paired_model_metric_differences()`
- require identical fold coverage across all compared models
- preserve first-seen model order for deterministic pair construction
- retain raw `model_a - model_b` deltas for every metric
- add direction-normalized improvement where positive always means model A performed better
- register higher-is-better and lower-is-better metric directions explicitly
- report mean/median/SD/min/max raw deltas plus win/tie/loss counts
- allow metric-level missingness, so deterministic I-VT calibration comparisons remain unavailable rather than fabricated
- explicitly record that no cross-validation p-values or confidence intervals are produced and folds are not treated as independent replicates
- embed paired summary/fold deltas/design in RA and MN Lund benchmark reports, and therefore their suite child artifacts
- expose the API publicly
- add regression tests for directionality, missing calibration, tie tolerance, duplicate rows, identical fold coverage, and Lund report integration
- add a Methods page and API documentation

No empirical performance values are added. The new outputs are descriptive matched-fold diagnostics for future frozen benchmark reports.

author: takanashisatou
body:
## Summary

Three related correctness fixes plus the three cover game tests that were disabled with `required = false`.

### Multiparallel (thread) merging — `RecipeLogic`

* The intra-recipe parallel block in the multiparallel loop scaled only `inputs` / `outputs`. EU/t and tick fluids stayed at 1x, so a machine could do up to `MultiParallelCount` times the work for a single recipe's cost. `MultiParallelCount` is a thread count and every thread already pays for its own recipe, so the block is removed and the budget counts threads.
* `mergeTwoRecipes` primed the Lombok lazy `getInputEUt()` / `getOutputEUt()` fields *before* the tick contents were merged, which cached the first thread's EU/t forever — the merged recipe then billed one thread's power for all of them.
* Merged `parallels` are summed with saturation instead of wrapping.

### Chanced outputs

* `ChanceLogic.OR` computed `times * chance` as an `int`. Chanced outputs are rolled once per run batch, so `times = parallels * batchParallels`; above ~430k runs of a 50% output the product wrapped around and silently dropped most of the outputs (1M runs produced 70504 instead of 500000).
* The roll count itself (`RecipeRunner`) and the parallel counts in `ModifierFunction` are saturating now, so they can no longer wrap to zero or to a negative count — a negative count makes `AND` / `FIRST` / `XOR` skip every roll. `MultiblockDisplayText` uses the same saturating product for its output rate line.

Known remaining limitation: `OR` still materialises the guaranteed part as one list entry per produced unit, so an absurd parallel count (the 1e9 caps some addon machines use) with chanced outputs can exhaust memory. Fixing that means scaling a single `Content` instead, which needs the capability inside `ChanceLogic#roll` and changes how outputs are inserted, so it is left out of this PR.

### `AdvancedActivityDetectorCover`

Once a machine went idle, `RecipeLogic` cleared progress and duration, the cover returned early on `maxProgress == 0` and kept its last signal forever — a stopped machine reported activity indefinitely. It now clears the output in that case.

## Tests

`:modules:gtm-reborn:runGameTestServer` — all 100 required tests pass. The three previously optional tests are required now:

* `testAdvancedActivityDetectorCover` and `testAdvancedActivityDetectorCoverGoesOffWhenIdle`: the template's electrolyzer is UEV, which overclocks water electrolysis down to ~2 ticks, so the cover's 20 tick sampling caught `progress == 0` at random. Both tests pin the overclock tier, which keeps the reported progress stable. The idle test fails without the cover fix (lamp stays lit for 200 ticks).
* `generatesEnergyAtDayTest` / `doesntGenerateEnergyAtDayWhenBlockedTest`: the automated test server generates a normal overworld and places every structure deep underground, so no template can offer sky access. Both tests now build their machine in open air above their own test area and pin the weather. The blocked variant waits for the light engine before covering the machine, and both wipe the spot first, since only the structure itself is cleaned up between runs.
* New `ChanceLogicTest` locks the overflow fixes: both cases fail on the old math (70504 outputs instead of 500000, and parallels wrapping to 0).

author: ecomlabnz
body:
A month at a glance, an agenda beneath it, and any single day on its own — over the dates the register already owns.

## What is on it

Decision deadlines, tasks, visa / passport / certificate expiries, invoices due, quotes running out, warnings about to lapse — and, which the Alerts page never showed, **what has already happened**: when a matter was lodged, and when it was decided. A calendar that cannot show last month is half a calendar.

## It holds nothing of its own

The practice decided against appointments, so every entry belongs to a record and is changed on that record — moving a visa expiry on a calendar would not change when the visa expires.

**Guarded, not merely intended.** A test walks both files for any write statement and fails on one; it also asserts there is no `appointments` table and no `POST` route on the page.

## The legend is the filter

One row of keys under the month, each with a colour and this month's count. Click a key and that kind comes off the month. Not a legend nobody reads sitting beside a filter nobody finds.

**Everyone or Mine.** "Mine" narrows to matters and tasks assigned to you. Client dates — visas, passports, certificates — belong to a *client*, not to a member of staff, so they step aside in that view rather than being listed under somebody's name. This is the seed of the per-user calendars the practice asked to keep possible: **a filter value, not a second page.**

## Modular by construction

Each kind of date is a source in a registry — a label, a colour, and a function returning events between two dates. Adding a new kind is one entry in that list, not an edit to a query eleven things depend on. A source that fails is dropped and logged rather than taking the page down: a calendar missing one kind of date is still a calendar; a blank page is not.

## No script at all

Every control is a link — months, filters, days — which the content-security policy would require in any case. Below **780px** the grid steps aside and the agenda takes over: seven columns do not fit a phone.

## The month arithmetic is its own file

So the awkward cases could be tested directly, and they were:

| Case | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| A month starting on **Sunday** | Six leading blanks, not none — `getUTCDay()` counts from Sunday, so this is the case a naive implementation gets exactly wrong |
| A 31-day month starting on **Saturday** | Six rows, not five — a five-row assumption loses the last days |
| Leap Februaries | Including the 1900 (not a leap year) and 2000 (is one) century rule |
| **Every day appears exactly once** | A day dropped from a grid is a deadline nobody sees |

Verified in Chromium with scripting off: September (5 weeks), November — starts on a Sunday (6 weeks, 30 days), August (6 weeks, 31 days), source filters, Mine (27 events → 17, client dates correctly absent), one-day view, and a malformed month falling back to the current one. No sideways scroll at any width; no page errors.

## The navigation bar

Its ceiling moves from eight items to nine to make room — **on a measurement, not as an allowance.** The nine-item bar holds a single line at every width from 780px (where the mobile nav takes over) to 1680px, checked in Chromium. The comment records the measurement so the next addition measures again.

The alternative was demoting Alerts into a group, which the register's own rule keeps one glance away — a decision already made and still right.

---

**Four mutations, four failures:** drop the last day of the grid, start weeks on Sunday, let a failing source take the page down, apply the owner filter to client dates.

Full suite green: 85 files, 1291 tests. Typecheck clean.

author: mithtech-is
body:
## What
Fixes `variant.tier_price.set` returning **HTTP 500 `B2bPriceTier with id "" not found`** whenever an existing tier bracket is re-priced.

## Root cause
The update branch called `b2b.updatePriceTiers(existing.id, { ...fields })` — a positional `(id, data)` form. MedusaService-generated `update*` methods take a **single** `{ id, ...fields }` object (or an array), so the id string was consumed as the data payload → `data.id` undefined → the `id ""` error. Create/delete branches used the correct signatures, so ladders could be created but never updated.

## Fix
`updatePriceTiers([{ id: existing.id, value, max_quantity }])` — matches host `tier-price-list.ts` usage.

## Verification (demo stack, E2E)
- Base pricing unaffected: Standard Selling 911 → variant price 91100 paise ✅
- Wholesale Item Price 656 → Medusa PriceTier min_q=50 = **65600** ✅
- Frappe outbound Medusync Log: **Success** (was Failed HTTP 500) ✅
- Retry cron auto-recovered the previously-failed events after redeploy ✅

author: bluntexe
body:
## Summary
- Moves venue gallery images off Prisma's `Venue.galleryImages` (legacy `xiv-venues` MinIO bucket) onto xvm-api's own image storage (`xvm-api-media` bucket, multipart upload, server-side validation + WebP re-encoding)
- Adds `uploadVenueImage`/`deleteVenueImage`/`VenueImage` to `lib/api/xvm-api.ts`, mirroring the existing unused `uploadRoomImage`/`deleteRoomImage` pattern
- Rewrites `/api/venues/[venueId]/gallery`: POST/DELETE/GET proxy to xvm-api instead of a presigned-URL dance; the GET (not in the original plan — see below) gives the settings page a live source for the current image list. All three verbs now wrapped in `withRateLimit`.
- Rewires `GalleryManager` (single multipart upload instead of a 3-step client dance), the settings page that hosts it, and adds a client-side 8 MB pre-check before upload so an oversized file doesn't round-trip to the server for a 413
- Adds `backfill-gallery-images.js`, a one-time ops script migrating existing venues' old-bucket images into xvm-api, so admin (Settings) and public-page views don't permanently diverge for venues that had a gallery before this shipped
- **Public venue page (`/venues/[slug]`) migrated too**, now that xvm-api#71 exists: name/description/banner/gallery/location come from `GET /public/venues/{venue_id}` exclusively, no Prisma fallback. A venue not connected to xvm-api, or a failed request, gets a degraded page (those sections omitted) rather than serving Prisma's stale copy as current — same principle `settings/route.ts` already applies to visibility fields. `generateMetadata` (SEO) migrated the same way. What's genuinely left on Prisma — events list, follow/membership counts, `ownerId`, the `settings` JSON (tags/hours) — has no xvm-api equivalent at all; that's a different resource, not more of the same gap.

## Resolved: deletes now propagate to the public page
Previously an accepted gap (see history below) — closed once [xvm-api#71](https://github.com/xiv-venue-manager/xvm-api/pull/71) shipped the public endpoint requested in #69. Live-verified the full chain: uploaded a test image and description via xvm-api directly, confirmed both render on the public page; deleted the image, confirmed it disappears from the public page too — the exact regression Allegro's review caught, now fixed end to end rather than documented as accepted.

## Process notes
Executed via subagent-driven-development against a written plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-gallery-xvm-api-cutover.md`) — fresh implementer + spec-compliance review + code-quality review per task, with real fix-and-re-review loops (found and fixed: missing try/catch on DELETE's JSON parsing, stale error state not clearing on delete). Mid-execution, Task 5's investigation surfaced a real gap the original plan didn't anticipate (no read path once Prisma stops being written to) — added as Task 5b, same review rigor. A final whole-implementation review then surfaced a production consequence (existing venues' galleries would appear empty in Settings until backfilled) — added as Task 7.

Allegro's review then caught two more real issues, fixed as follow-up commits: the public-page-delete gap (first patched with a rejected Prisma-write approach — wrong direction for a Prisma-removal migration — then properly resolved once she shipped #71), and a backfill idempotency bug (count comparison instead of per-image tracking — a partial failure would re-upload and duplicate already-succeeded images on retry). The idempotency fix was re-verified with a real partial-failure exercise (one broken URL mixed with two working ones) against the shared dev xvm-api instance, confirmed no duplicates on retry, then fully reverted.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean (whole project)
- [x] `eslint` clean on all changed files
- [x] Live-tested against local dev + the shared dev xvm-api instance: upload → appears immediately → confirmed served from `xvm-api-media` bucket as `.webp` → persists across reload → delete → persists (gone) across reload
- [x] Backfill script: dry-run (0 matching local venues, clean empty-result pass) + two real exercises against the shared dev instance — a full-success case, and a partial-failure/retry case proving the new per-image idempotency (2 of 3 uploaded, one deliberately broken URL; re-run retried only the failed one, confirmed via xvm-api that no duplicates landed) — both fully reverted afterward
- [x] Public page migration: set description + uploaded an image via xvm-api directly, confirmed both render on `/venues/[slug]`; deleted the image, confirmed it disappears from the public page too — reverted afterward

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- xvm-api#70: whether xvm-api's venue id should become the sole venue identifier dashboard-wide (exploratory, not committed work)
- Backfill script has not been run against the shared dev or prod xvm-api instance for real venues — that's a separate, explicit decision when we are ready

body: Adds a play/pause background-music button, bottom-left, persistent across every page (mounted once in the root layout so client-side navigation doesn't restart it). ## A scope note on how this request got here You linked a specific YouTube video to use as BGM. Two things made me not just rip it: - **I genuinely can't** — YouTube is egress-blocked from this sandbox, and neither `yt-dlp` nor `ffmpeg` exist here (same constraint as the circuit-frames video earlier). - **More importantly**: looping someone's actual song as sitewide background music is a much more central use of copyrighted audio than the flyover video's decorative, silent background role was. Your own README already holds this project to a "no official misuse" standard from an earlier audit pass. I flagged this and you picked the royalty-free/CC-licensed route instead. So this PR ships the full player, wired and tested, with a **placeholder** audio slot — no real track included. `frontend/public/audio/README.md` has sourcing links (YouTube Audio Library, Pixabay Music) and next steps. ## What's built - `BgmPlayer` (client component) — small button, bottom-left, hover/focus reveals the track title + artist in a pill to the right. - **Never pretends to autoplay.** Browsers block audio-with-sound autoplay without a user gesture; this starts paused always, and a rejected `play()` (blocked, or the placeholder file 404ing) falls back to the paused state cleanly rather than getting stuck showing "playing." - Track title is in the button's own `aria-label`, not just the hover tooltip (which is `aria-hidden`) — a screen reader user gets the same info a sighted hovering user does. - `data/bgm.ts` holds the title/artist/path — swap in real values once you've dropped a licensed file at `public/audio/bgm.mp3`. ## Verification - `tsc`/`next build` clean. - Playwright against a production build: confirmed `aria-pressed` stays `false` (not stuck) when the placeholder audio file 404s, the hover tooltip renders correctly, and — checked specifically since the landing hero also anchors content to the bottom of the viewport — no visual collision between the two. Both use fixed, viewport-relative offsets rather than content-relative ones, so the ~24px gap between them holds regardless of viewport height. ## Still needs from you Source a license-clear track (or your own), drop it at `frontend/public/audio/bgm.mp3`, and update `frontend/data/bgm.ts` with the real title/artist. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01XHEHHdZJtpUij8spYeMgX4 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01XHEHHdZJtpUij8spYeMgX4)_ --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > UI-only addition with no auth, API, or data-model changes; main follow-up is choosing a license-clear audio asset before production. > > **Overview** > Adds a **sitewide background music control** mounted once in the root layout so it survives client-side navigation without restarting playback. > > The new `BgmPlayer` client component is a fixed bottom-left play/pause button with a looping `

Throwaway native CI for the Linux x64 CPU and Windows x64 CPU live STT gates in #845. **Not product code. Do not merge as a shipping feature.**

PR #850 already merged the macOS Metal spike report. Apple Silicon QEMU SIGILLs on `doctor`/`serve`; PE32+ cannot run here. These jobs are the native proof.

## What the jobs do
Matrix: `ubuntu-latest`, `windows-latest` only (no macOS minutes). After caching the pinned v0.1.0 CPU archive and Q8 GGUF (`d9a01898…3812d`, 699,872,960 bytes):

1. `nemo-speech doctor` (CPU device must appear)
2. `serve --host 127.0.0.1 --no-ui --device cpu` with `NEMO_SPEECH_HTTP_API_KEY` (not argv)
3. `GET /ready` (`device=cpu`)
4. One websocket `/v1/realtime` turn on the checked-in 16 kHz mono PCM16 fixture (100 ms frames): delta + completed, first-partial ≤ 1.5 s, stop-to-final ≤ 1.5 s
5. 300 s max-pace RTF ≤ 1.0 and sidecar RSS < 2.5 GiB

## Out of scope
- No `electron/`, `src/`, `test/`, or `scripts/package*` changes
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` untouched
- GGUF and runtime archives are not in git
