body: **Do not merge until Stephen reviews.** Auto-bet stays **OFF**. No live orders were placed. SharpMoney not touched. KalshiBB was not modified. ## Audit Traced the +EV alert → match → click-to-bet / auto-bet → `place_order` path against BookieBeats / KalshiBB rules already encoded in this repo (away = `−hdp`, limit at the displayed `price_cents`, Over = YES / Under = NO). `NDGopher/KalshiBB` is not a public repo this agent can clone; comparison is against those known-good rules and the comments that describe BB order-price semantics. ### What was already correct - Alert `line` / qualifier for spreads is home-centric: **away is always `−hdp`** (`side_handicap` / `_pick_qualifier_line_for_side`). - Totals: Over → YES, Under → NO. - `place_order` already submitted `type=limit` with `yes_price` / `no_price` at the alert’s `price_cents` (BookieBeats `price` field, before fees). `post_only=False` is the intended taker-limit (fill at limit or better, never a market order). - Auto-bet default is `False`. PLive take cards never auto-bet. ### Regressions / holes (PRs #1 / #2 / #3 made these more visible) 1. **Kalshi cards vanished without a private key.** `find_submarket` → `get_market_by_ticker` always signed GETs. With no key the signature is `MISSING_KEY` and the public market GET 401s, so matching fails and unmatched rows are omitted from the live list (PR #1 hide-unmatched). Cards should use Odds-API + **public** Kalshi market data. Credentials are only for orders. Confirmed: `GET https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets` returns 200 unsigned. 2. **Odds-API href is often the market ticker** (`…-DET1` / `…-143`). `handle_new_alert` treated it as the **event** ticker and `build_market_ticker` appended the line again (`…-143-143`). Wrong ticker / wrong market. 3. **Click-to-bet rematch** could rebuild a different market and read `side` from a market dict that has no `side` field. Removed. Missing identity now refuses. 4. **Missing price used 50¢** for contract size (`expected_price_cents or 50`) on manual and auto paths. 5. **PLive cards still showed BET / BET MAX**, which would POST `/api/place_bet` with a `PLIVE|…` ticker. PR #2 (PLive ML idx1) does not change Kalshi order construction. PR #3 (soccer / conservative PLive join) does not change Kalshi side/line rules. ## Fixes (fail closed) - `execution_guard.py`: refuse if ticker, side, line, event, or price is missing or mismatched. Away invert, stale/rebuilt ticker, wrong family, PLive venue, credentials-for-orders-only. - Public unsigned GET for markets / orderbook when no key is loaded; 401/403 signed GET retries unsigned. - `place_order` returns immediately without credentials. Payload is always `type=limit` at the displayed cents (`yes_price` / `no_price`). - Manual and auto endpoints run the same identity gate and rebuild-and-compare the ticker. No rematch. No 50¢ fallback. - Frontend: `canPlaceKalshiBet` hides click-to-bet on PLive / unmatched cards. ## Tests Fixtures in `tests/test_execution_guard.py`: - wrong-side (spread YES on opponent ticker, Under as YES, ML YES on opponent) - wrong-line (spread −2.5 vs −1.5 ticker, total 8.5 vs 7) - away-side inversion (Tigers must be −1.5, not +1.5) - stale / mismatched ticker and event mismatch - limit price is the displayed cents; no market order - missing fields and PLive refuse - public GET headers empty without a key; `place_order` refused - market-href does not double-suffix the totals ticker - auto-bet switch stays OFF `python3 -m pytest tests/test_execution_guard.py` — 18 passed. ## Locks unchanged - Auto-bet **OFF** - minSharp **3** (default) - No SharpMoney - No live orders from this agent

author: patcartelli
body:
## What

Record anything with the camera toggle off. The take library row says "Camera: recorded no frames — this take has no picture-in-picture", for a take that never asked for a camera at all.

`helper/src/AnchorsDoc.swift` wrote `anchors.camera` unconditionally — `{present: false}` whenever no camera was requested. `schema/anchors-2.schema.json` already says *absent* means no camera was even attempted and `present:false` means one was requested (or considered) but yielded nothing; `app/src/takes.ts`'s `cameraSummary` and `app/src/renderer.ts` already read it that way. The write side just never gave them the absence to produce. `helper/test/anchors/main.swift` check 1 and `app/test/take-list.test.ts` were pinning opposite claims — both green, contradictory — which is how this survived.

## How

- **`anchorsDocument`** gains a `requested: Bool` parameter. The `camera` block is omitted entirely when `false`; when `true`, it's written exactly as before (`present:true` with measurements, or `present:false` with none).
- **`CaptureSession`** records `wantCamera` once, in `begin`, from `start`'s own argument — `camera == nil` alone can't distinguish "never asked" from "asked, got nothing" — and threads it into `writeSidecars`'s call to `anchorsDocument`.
- The STC-286 case is deliberately untouched: `requested: true, camera: nil` (a device that opened and delivered zero frames) still produces `present:false`. That's the one thing this fix must not silence, and it now has its own test case.
- **`helper/test/anchors/main.swift`**: check 1 was pinning the old, wrong behaviour ("a camera block is always written") — it now asserts absence when nothing was requested. A new case exercises "requested, no track" directly. Both new documents validate against `schema/anchors-2.schema.json` in `helper/test/anchors.test.ts`, same as the existing cases.

Nothing on the TS side changes — `takes.ts` and the schema already expected this.

## Verification

**This session cannot compile Swift** (Linux container, no `swiftc`) — nothing here ran locally. All three typecheck passes clean and the full Linux-safe unit suite (323 tests) unaffected and green, but neither touches the changed files.

**CI's macOS runner is the actual verifier for this change, and it's now green**: `helper/test/anchors.test.ts` compiled `AnchorsDoc.swift` + `main.swift` for real and validated all four built documents against `schema/anchors-2.schema.json`, including the new "requested, no track" case and the corrected "no camera requested → block absent" case.

## Acceptance (from the ticket)

- [x] A display-only recording lists with no camera line — `anchorsDocument(requested: false)` omits the block; `main.swift` check 1 asserts it and CI confirmed.
- [x] A camera-requested take that delivered nothing still says "recorded no frames" (STC-286) — `main.swift`'s new "requested, no track" case; CI confirmed present:false is preserved.
- [x] `npm test` green, including anchors-2 schema validation of both documents — CI green on the macOS runner.

## What this adds

Implements the AI-1 Global Research & Evidence Director as a first-class, deterministic runtime governance layer on top of the existing DeepResearchEngine truth/evidence pipeline.

### AI-1 packet contract
- exact 15-section AI-1 research packet in the required order
- user-goal + requested-deliverable preservation
- relevant domain discovery from runtime planner/specialist lanes
- evidence-linked experts plus research traditions as test targets (never fame-based truth)
- strongest-source ranking with source hierarchy, relevance, quality and access-depth disclosure
- claim-evidence matrix with support, contradiction, source quality, mechanism/applicability and A-E grading
- strict C/D/E non-promotion to fact
- active contradiction/counter-search status
- theory component retain/reject decomposition
- explicit MISSING SOURCE / FULL TEXT REQUIRED / MISSING DATA / NOT VERIFIED / UNKNOWN states
- cross-agent alerts for AI-2 / AI-3 / AI-4
- second-pass tasks ranked by Importance × Expected Information Gain
- packet confidence /100 explicitly scoped to research-packet/process completeness, never truth/profitability/success probability
- exact blockers preventing a higher score

### Runtime integration
`AgentManager.research()` attaches the AI-1 packet after the core engine finishes its existing citation, A-E claim verification, evidence-axis, contradiction, source-integrity and other truth gates. It is additive/backward-compatible and cannot manufacture or upgrade evidence.

### Tests / CI
Adds focused adversarial tests for exact section contract/order, missing-source fail-closed behavior, shallow-reading honesty, C/D/E promotion prevention, cross-agent routing, EIG ranking, trading-framework neutrality, and backward compatibility.

Adds a dedicated PR CI workflow that compiles the integration and executes the AI-1 contract tests. Existing Foundation Tests also run on this PR.

author: rebel-jonghewk
body:
## Summary of Changes

### Summary

Adds `torch.rbln.physical_layout(tensor)`: where an RBLN tensor's bytes physically sit on the device, one `PhysicalShard(node_id, chiplet_id, nbytes, device_addr, shape)` per device area, plus the logical shape/dtype and the physical shape/dtype/itemsize of the allocation's transform. It is the input for per-chiplet KV cache sizing (`nbytes_per_chiplet()` divided by the compile-time block hint gives bytes per block per chiplet) and for placement diagnostics (a 4-way head split reports `(4, 4, 1, 128, 2048)` per shard; a 4-way replication reports the full shape four times).

Backed by the librbln C ABI `rbln_get_memory_info()` — `MemoryInfo.device_areas` added in rebellions-sw/rebel_compiler#13405 (ABI 4) — through a new `_C._get_memory_info` binding. No `rebel._C` import on the torch side.

### Details

- **`_C._get_memory_info(tensor)`** (`csrc/rbln/Module.cpp`) — validates the tensor with the same rule as `bind_device_memory` (RBLN tensor covering its whole storage), calls `c10::rbln::get_memory_info(data_ptr())` (`require_runtime` guard), and returns `physical_shape`, `physical_dtype` and `device_areas` as one dict per area keyed like `PhysicalShard`, so Python builds `PhysicalShard(**area)`. `physical_dtype` is a real `torch.dtype` via `getTHPDtype` from the new `c10::rbln::to_scalar_type()` (inverse of `to_rbln_dtype()`), or `None` for a dtype torch lacks — DLFloat16, the usual fp16/bf16 on-device storage.

- **`torch.rbln.physical_layout()`** (`memory.py`) — wraps the dict into `PhysicalLayout(logical_shape, logical_dtype, physical_shape, physical_dtype, physical_itemsize, shards)`. `physical_itemsize` is derived from an area (`nbytes / prod(shape)`), so it is set even when `physical_dtype` is `None`. A tensor whose allocation is not bound yet (no torch op or graph has touched it, no `bind_device_memory`) raises `no device memory yet`. A flat 1:1 binding has no transform: every `physical_*` field and each shard's `shape` is `None`.

- **Timing** — the physical view exists only after the allocation is bound, so the KV sizing flow reads the layout after warm-up and before releasing the tensor. A dynamic (`mark_dynamic`) dim is reported as the concrete value bound at that point, since the runtime regenerates the transform with resolved sizes.

- **Tests** (`test/rbln/test_physical_layout.py`) — API visible and CPU tensor rejected as plain tests; the device tests go through `instantiate_device_type_tests(only_for="privateuse1")`: bound flat buffer is one shard with `physical_* is None`; compiled-op output covers its bytes and every shard satisfies `prod(shape) × physical_itemsize == nbytes`; unbound tensor and interior view raise. `test_cpp_RBLNFunctionsTest.ToScalarTypeInvertsToRblnDtype` pins the dtype inverse.

### Next Steps

- vllm-rbln: replace the per-artifact `kv_cache_memory_profile()` merge with `physical_layout(kv).nbytes_per_chiplet()` after warm-up (dynamic KV proposal).
- Per-shard `slice_axes` (axis/begin/end) is not exposed; the sliced shape covers sizing and placement. Add it next to `shape` if the KV connector needs it.
- `lintrunner` was not run locally (init download timed out); `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` and `clang-format` pass on the changed files.
- `c10::rbln::get_memory_info()` now logs its cost at debug instead of warn, since `physical_layout()` calls it on purpose; the header note still tells hot-path callers to prefer `get_torch_device_id()`.

---

## Related Issues / Tickets

* Related to rebellions-sw/rebel_compiler#13405 (required: `MemoryInfo.device_areas`, `RBLN_ABI_CURRENT` 4)

---

## Type of Change

- [x] `feature` — New capability or functionality
- [x] `core` — Changes to RBLN backend, device layer, C++ extension, op registration, or `torch.compile` integration

---

## Affected Modules

- [x] C++ extension (`torch_rbln/csrc`)
- [x] Memory

---

## How to Test (if applicable)

1. Build against a rebel_compiler that includes rebellions-sw/rebel_compiler#13405.
2. Run `pytest test/rbln/test_physical_layout.py` on an RBLN device.
3. Expected: 6 passed. On REBEL a compiled matmul output reports one shard per chiplet it was placed on, each with `prod(shape) × physical_itemsize == nbytes`.

---

## Checklist

* [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) format
* [ ] This PR is linked to a corresponding issue — see [Contributing to torch-rbln](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/torch-rbln/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)
* [x] Linting passes — see [Linting](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/torch-rbln/blob/main/docs/LINTING.md)
* [ ] All CI tests pass — see [CI/CD Workflows](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/torch-rbln/blob/main/docs/WORKFLOWS.md)
* [x] The test method is described, and the expected result is clearly stated (if applicable)
* [ ] Relevant documentation has been updated (if applicable)

---

## Notes

body:
### What does this PR do?

Whenever resource creating controllers (Monitors/SLOs/Dashboards/DDGR) reconciles that fail with a permanent (4xx) API error now back off to the existing force-sync cadence (default 60m) instead of retrying every 5s forever. Transient errors (5xx, network, 429) keep the fast 5s retry.

**4xx** responses are **client-side errors**. The request itself was invalid (bad query, bad field, etc.), so retrying the exact same request isn't going to produce a different result. It's a permanent failure until the spec changes, so hammering it every 5s is for nothing.

### Motivation

Fixes #3422: a handful of misconfigured `DatadogMonitor`/`DatadogSLO` resources could get retried every 5s indefinitely which is noisy.

author: golyakoff
body:
Part of golyakoff/ago-root#367. One of three repositories; `ago-calendar` follows, and `ago-chat` lands last because it carries an EF migration that must sequence behind [ago-chat#153](https://github.com/golyakoff/ago-chat/pull/153).

## The gap

`/api/v1/module-tasks` was `AllowAnonymous()` and took `SiteId` **from the request body** — the site’s identity was asserted by the caller, not proved. Probed from outside the cluster on 2026-09-03: an unauthenticated POST reached the handler, while a nonsense sibling path returned 404. So the route was genuinely live and genuinely anonymous.

## The mechanism

Chat signs a short-lived assertion per call — HMAC-SHA256 over a payload naming the site, 60s TTL, `X-Ago-Module-Credential`. This product validates it **with its own code**: no shared package, because `adr/0012` and `adr/0027` give no precedent for one, and a comment in each validator naming its twin is a more honest coupling than a dependency between products.

Verified rather than taken on trust: the comparison is `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, not the `SequenceEqual` shape an inline check reaches for.

The route keeps `AllowAnonymous` and validates in the handler rather than joining the authentication pipeline — this is a machine-to-machine header, not a user principal — and the refusal stays a **401**, distinguishable from the 404 an unmapped route gives. That distinction is what lets a smoke check tell “protected” from “unreachable”.

## The case this item is actually about

A credential **genuinely signed for site A, replayed against site B’s task**, is refused as if the task did not exist — checked against the persisted task, not just the wire body. That is the one the brief called easiest to leave untested, and it was proven failing before the fix (`200 OK` where `404` was expected).

## Rollout

`RequireCredential` defaults to **true** — the state this item demands, shipped as the steady state rather than something an operator must remember to turn on. Setting it false lets a *missing* header through for the length of a rollout where the two images cannot move together; a *wrong* credential is refused either way.

Safe order: chat first (it starts sending a header that is harmless against a still-anonymous endpoint), then the module.

## Verified independently

```
format clean · build 0 warnings 0 errors
Domain 9 · Application 25 · Integration 32 — all three assemblies, 0 failed
```

## Not done here, and needed before this can be deployed

The shared secret does not exist yet. It has to be generated, placed in the node’s `.env`, referenced from the manifests, and matched by the `EnabledModule.Credential` row on the chat side — operational work in `ago-deploy` and the live database, outside this PR and outside a worker’s reach. **The secret never enters a repository.**

`smoke.sh` asserting the anonymous refusal is also still owed; it lives in `ago-deploy`.

## Honest limitation, recorded rather than smoothed over

The secret is **one per module deployment, not per site**. So “site A’s token cannot act for site B” holds for the token — which is what travels and what these tests attack — but a leaked secret mints any site. Harmless today, since one deployment serves exactly one tenant by configuration. It stops being harmless in `22-04`, which makes a deployment multi-tenant, and a per-site secret belongs in that item’s scope.

body:
Refs #641 — Collector copied every PR comment body verbatim into the model context and the receipt; discussion-heavy PRs blew up context, and quota-notice templates with zero findings rode along. Owner ruling: capture findings, by pointer.

## What landed
- Chain ①: collector receipt carries model-submitted findings, each with a machine pointer (repo / PR / comment id / url / author / kind / time); observe view is bounded (512-byte heads), full bodies opened on demand by evidence pointer (`ak_collector_read`); projection has one authoritative implementation; splitting/classification stays with the LLM (no markup parsing in code).
- Chain ②: a normal completion that misdeclares `infrastructureFailure` is bounced as a correctable submission instead of being settled as `host_failure`.
- `souls/collector.md` bullet 4 replaced per ticket (finding + pointer; bodies reachable by pointer, not copied).
- Read-pointer failure contract covered on the real entry; dead test helper removed.

## Court
- 票庭 r1–r3 (r3 `01a06752` 署) → coder r1/r2 (inspector bounces resolved) → reviewer r1 → judge r1 (continue: soul bullet + dead helper) → fixer r1 → judge r2 `01a067ed` converged (notary pass).
- Live acceptance (35-evidence real PR run; glm leg yields a lawful receipt) is the ticket's remaining acceptance item and the condition for lifting the collector seat pause; to be run on this PR's build.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes collector receipt shape, evidence projection, and settlement paths for infrastructure vs correctable errors; behavior is heavily tested but downstream consumers of full bodies in receipts must use pointers/volume.

> **Overview**
> Collector no longer copies PR comment bodies into model context or receipts, and no longer auto-extracts provider inline findings in code. **Chain ①** caps observe output to 512-byte UTF-8 body previews plus pointers, adds **`ak_collector_read`** to open full text by `evidenceId`, and lets the model submit **`findings`** as pointer refs that the runtime validates and enriches with machine locators (repo/PR/comment id/url/author/kind/time). Settlement distinguishes **`ak_collector_read`** pointer bounces from real infrastructure failures via typed facts on errored results.

author: alynnyree
body:
He spotted the flaw: when a full test runs at a random minute, there may be no setup for the AI to read — and the reading step showed that as a **failure**, which would have him chasing a bug that isn't there. The AI honestly finding nothing is the transfer *working*, not breaking.

The setup step now shows **three** states, not two:

- **Gold dash** — the chart was read and answered but no setup was clear at that exact minute, with a line saying so plainly and nudging him to pick a time he knows had a setup.
- **Red cross** — kept only for the AI genuinely not being reachable.
- **Green tick** — a confident setup was named.

The heading says "Every part worked. One had nothing to show" so a dash is never mistaken for a fault.

### Verified

**57 browser checks**, including: a no-setup reading shows a gold dash and not a cross; the run still reads as working; no combo is invented onto the screen; and a truly unreachable AI still shows as failed and is counted among the parts that didn't work. Existing suites re-run green.

**Not verified:** a live run on his phone against the real AI.

body:
## What & why (remediation item 6a — report before deleting)

Item 6 removes duplicate silo-hub pages. Because it's destructive, this first PR is the **read-only verification pass**: it changes nothing, and its output is what we review — with real production counts — before any cleanup runs.

### The problem (investigated, not yet touched)

A silo hub is a `Content` `kind=page`, `page_type=Hub` pinned to a `silo_id`. The system assumes **one hub per silo** (nesting keys hubs by `silo_id`), but nothing enforces it — there is no unique index on `(site_id, silo_id, page_type)`. A structure rebuild (`ServiceStructureWriter` deletes + recreates spokes → new ULIDs) produces new `BuildPage` rows with `content_id = null`, which fall through `PageMaterializer`'s `content_id`-anchored idempotency to an **unguarded `Content::create`** → a second Hub row for the same silo. Origin is the protected trio (`PageMaterializer` / `ServiceStructureWriter` / `RebuildReconciler`), so the durable fix is proposed later (6c), not applied here.

## Changes (all read-only)

- **`DuplicateHubReport`** (`app/Build`) — groups a site's Hub pages by `silo_id`, keeps only silos with more than one hub, and for each reports:
  - the **keeper** (the same furthest-along-then-oldest canonical `DuplicateTownSweeper` uses: published > drafted > earliest);
  - **removable** extras (empty + unpublished — what a sweep could safely soft-delete) vs **blocked** extras (published or carrying a real draft — never auto-removable, need manual review);
  - **`children_to_repoint`** — child pages whose `parent_content_id` points at a non-keeper hub. This is the hub-specific risk that makes hubs different from towns: `parent_content_id` has no FK cascade, so a cleanup must re-point these to the keeper or orphan them. The report surfaces the count up front.
- **`launchpad:report-duplicate-hubs {--site=}`** — renders the report as a per-site table + portfolio totals. **No `--apply`, no deletions.**

## Also in this PR

- A one-line **flake fix** for the item-5 test `it tracks compromised connections` (merged in #700): it created two connections for one site without pinning providers, and `(site_id, provider)` is unique, so faker's random provider intermittently collided. Now pins distinct providers — deterministic.

## Cross-check answer (relay 6d — reported, not built)

The **3,847 location-page duplication is an independent root cause.** Location `page_key = CoverageArea id` is *stable* across rebuilds (a structure rebuild churns only spokes), so it does not mint duplicate location pages the way hubs are minted. That duplication came from a different, already-guarded mechanism (multiple CoverageArea rows for one town in a pre-dedupe materialize → fixed by the assembler's `townDedupeKey` + `DuplicateTownSweeper`). **A single fix does not cover both.**

## Next steps (each gated on explicit go-ahead — no production rows touched without it)

1. **Run `launchpad:report-duplicate-hubs` against prod**; I report the counts.
2. **6b** — `DuplicateHubSweeper` + `launchpad:dedupe-hub-pages --apply`, mirroring the town sweeper **plus child `parent_content_id` re-pointing**. Not executed against prod without your go-ahead.
3. **6c** — durable fix, **propose-only** (touches the protected trio): guard the hub `Content::create` on the natural key + clean stale `BuildPage` rows.

## Checks

- `pint` ✅  ·  `phpstan analyse` ✅ (0 errors)  ·  `php artisan test` ✅ (3173 passed, 12137 assertions — 4 new)

## Constraints honored

No protected file modified. Read-only — deletes nothing. Platform-wide, no tenant-specific branching.

CC:

### Description
Adds pixels for the new Create Image flow to mimic iOS.

### Testing Steps
Use a macOS debug build with `updatedCreateImage` enabled and inspect outgoing PixelKit events.

1. Select a model without image-generation support, then choose Tools → Create Image → `m_mac_aichat_addressbar_create_image_model_switched` fires with the previous/new model IDs, privacy flag, and `entry_point=tools_menu`.
2. Dismiss the resulting model-switch notice → `m_mac_aichat_addressbar_create_image_model_switch_notice_dismissed` fires.
3. Stub `/models` with an unsupported selected model and no accessible image-capable model, then choose Create Image → `m_mac_aichat_addressbar_create_image_unavailable` fires.
4. Keep Create Image active while stubbing the selected model as unsupported, then submit a prompt → `m_mac_aichat_addressbar_create_image_submitted_with_unsupported_model` fires.

### Impact
Low. Telemetry-only changes behind the existing Create Image flow.

---
###### Internal references:
[Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

> **Overview**
> Adds **telemetry-only** tracking for the macOS Duck.ai address bar **Create Image** flow, aligned with iOS payloads and firing frequencies. There are no user-visible UI changes.
> 
> **Model switch and notice:** When `updatedCreateImage` auto-switches from an unsupported model, the omnibar fires `create_image_model_switched` with `from_model_id`, `to_model_id`, `from_model_privacy_preserving`, and `entry_point=tools_menu`. author: maffemuis
body:
## Purpose
Freeze the legacy FLEX-1600 ALPHA message path before fragment-reassembly or decoder refactoring.

## Fixture
Fully synthetic, privacy-safe FLEX-1600 2-level transmission:
- capcode 123456 (`0123456` in legacy formatting)
- valid sync, cycle information, BCH/ECC and interleaving
- one short address
- ALPHA vector
- legacy fragment number `3` standalone form
- message `FLEX GOLDEN OK!`
- generated WAV SHA-256 `315a0a3a12efc99df1fb9ee199f0625732d079855b362e1c851fb174e74a98cc`

## Legacy behavior captured
The first 7 bits of the first post-header ALPHA word are skipped when fragment number is `3`. The generator therefore models that historical header slot explicitly and uses ETX padding for unused visible positions; the golden is not weakened to accept a truncated message.

Expected output:
- mode `FLEX-A`
- type ` ALPHA `
- bitrate `1600`
- message `FLEX GOLDEN OK!`

## Privacy
No off-air/received pager traffic is included; the waveform is generated from fixed protocol data only.

## Validation
GitHub Actions run `33774440430` is fully green for:
- Win32 VS2022 build
- 4/4 preservation tests
- silence replay
- POCSAG 512/1200/2400 alpha matrix
- POCSAG tone-only replay
- FLEX-1600 tone + alpha matrix
- artifact upload

Stacked on PR #10 (`modernization/flex1600-tone-golden`).

author: danigio15
body:
> «si ma mi devi dare la possibilità di eliminare anche la conversazione»
>
> «la risposta non si refresh devo uscire e rientrare»
>
> «passiamo alla versione 1.4.5 ed elimina tutte le beta, lascia solo ultima»

## La versione

Il manifest dice **`1.4.5`**, senza suffisso: la release che ne esce sarà **stabile**, non una pre-release — `release.yml` lo decide guardando se il tag ha il trattino.

**Il CHANGELOG si unisce.** Le tredici sezioni da `1.4.5-beta.1` a `1.4.5-beta.13` diventano una sola, `## 1.4.5`, coi blocchi rimessi in fila per argomento invece che per data: Aggiunto, Cambiato, Rimosso, Corretto, Da sapere.

Non è cosmesi. Le note della release le estrae `release.yml` dalla sezione che porta il numero della versione: lasciando tredici sezioni, la pagina della 1.4.5 avrebbe raccontato **un tredicesimo di sé**, e le altre dodici — cancellate insieme alle loro pre-release — non sarebbero state più da nessuna parte. Nessun punto è stato riscritto: cambiano solo i capitoli sopra di loro. Le tredici introduzioni lasciano il posto a una sola, che riepiloga la versione.

**La pulizia delle release sa fare il suo mestiere.** `cleanup-releases.yml` cancellava soltanto la numerazione pre-1.0 e le beta/rc della 1.0.0: le `1.4.5-beta.*` non le riconosceva, quindi lo strumento che esiste apposta per questo non sarebbe servito proprio adesso. Adesso è cancellabile **ogni pre-release di qualunque versione**, e nient'altro.

La garanzia resta intatta: una versione stabile non ha il trattino, non corrisponde a nessuno dei pattern, e questo workflow **non sa cancellarla nemmeno per errore di battitura**. Resta anche il controllo che impedisce di restare senza nessuna release stabile.

## Il cestino

Ogni riga della scheda «Conversazioni» ne ha uno, e ce n'è uno anche sopra il filo aperto. Cancella per davvero e per tutti e due: `DELETE /console/conversazioni/:linea` toglie la linea e i suoi messaggi dal centralino, e la casa se ne accorge e manda via la propria copia (vedi sotto).

Serve perché una coda dove non si butta via niente si riempie di prove, di domande già risolte e di righe aperte per sbaglio, finché quella vera non si trova più. Ed è il verso giusto della promessa fatta prima della prima riga: quello che si scrive lì non resta in giro per sempre.

**Due tocchi e non uno.** Il primo arma il cestino e chiede conferma sul tasto stesso, il secondo cancella. Una conversazione cancellata non si rimette a posto, e in un elenco dove si scorre col dito un cestino che cancella al primo tocco butta via prima o poi quella sbagliata.

Sul centralino la chiave della console è obbligatoria come per rispondere, e una linea già andata risponde di sì lo stesso — chi cancella vuole che non ci sia, e se non c'è già il risultato è quello: un 404 lì direbbe che qualcosa non ha funzionato mentre era a posto.

## La finestra che non si aggiornava

Leggeva una volta all'apertura e poi restava ferma: la risposta arrivava solo chiudendo e riaprendo. Il giro dei cinque minuti del backend c'era già, ma quello serve al campanello — suona e basta, non ridisegna niente.

Adesso guarda ogni quindici secondi e **ridisegna soltanto quando è arrivato davvero qualcosa**: rifare la casella quattro volte al minuto sotto le dita di chi scrive è il modo di rendere la finestra inusabile. E se ridisegna, il cursore torna dov'era.

Chiusa la finestra — o con la pagina nascosta — non chiede più niente. L'intervallo è dichiarato in `runtime-import-graph.test.js` accanto agli altri otto, con la sua ragione scritta.

## Le bolle stavano dalla parte sbagliata

Nella coda le domande della casa comparivano a destra e in verde — come se se le fosse scritte da solo chi stava leggendo — e le proprie risposte a sinistra e in grigio: una conversazione letta al contrario. «Mio» dipende da chi guarda, e questa finestra la guardano in due.

## I quattro rilievi di Codex, tutti veri

Due dicevano che questa PR **prometteva il falso**, e avevano ragione.

1. **La cancellazione non arrivava alla casa.** «Cancella davvero e per tutti e due» era scritto qui sopra e il codice non lo faceva: sparivano le righe dal centralino, e la casa si teneva la trascrizione intera per sempre. Il centralino risponde già `aperta: false` a chi chiede una linea che non c'è più, e `async_leggi` quel dato lo buttava via. Adesso diventa un `ChatError("gone")` e chi lo riceve manda via la copia. In più lo sportello della casa dice se la linea è **nata con questo messaggio**: chi scrive prima di aver riletto la riapre senza accorgersi di niente, e senza quel segnale la copia vecchia si sarebbe incollata sotto le frasi nuove.

2. **La scheda in fondo si mangiava le campanelle.** Con la finestra dimenticata aperta in una scheda nascosta, il giro dei quindici secondi leggeva — e leggere è aver letto: la risposta finiva in copia e segnata come vista, e il giro dei cinque minuti che deve suonare non trovava niente di nuovo. A pagina nascosta il giro adesso sta fermo.

3. **Un messaggio poteva sopravvivere alla linea.** Fra «la linea esiste?» e «scrivi» ci sta una cancellazione, e `messaggi.linea` non ha un vincolo verso `linee`: la riga restava orfana e la potatura notturna non la raggiungeva più. La scrittura è diventata un'istruzione sola col controllo dentro (`INSERT … SELECT … WHERE EXISTS`), e la potatura raccoglie anche gli orfani nati prima.

4. **Il filo di una casa poteva finire sotto il nome di un'altra.** Il giro assegnava le frasi di A mentre la finestra mostrava B. Adesso si appunta da dove è partito, e un giro per volta.

## Cosa cambia

| Dove | Cosa |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.json` | `1.4.5` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | tredici sezioni beta unite in `## 1.4.5` |
| `.github/workflows/cleanup-releases.yml` | sa cancellare ogni pre-release, mai una stabile |
| `centralino/src/index.js` | `DELETE /console/conversazioni/:linea`, scrittura con controllo dentro, `nuova`, potatura degli orfani |
| `chat_client.py` | `async_cestina`, il segnale `gone`, `nuova` |
| `chat.py` | `async_butta`, e la copia che se ne va quando la linea non c'è più |
| `websocket_api.py` | `dashboardmodern/chat/drop`, dietro la chiave della console |
| `bridge-socket.js` | il tipo nell'allowlist del ponte |
| `assistenza-section.js` | cestino, giro dei quindici secondi, verso delle bolle, cursore |
| `docs/CHAT.md`, `centralino/README.md` | il perché, e il cron che va aggiunto a mano |

## Prove

- **centralino** 31/31 — sette nuove
- **Python** 261/261 — sei nuove
- **frontend** 2116/2116 — otto nuove
- `ruff check` e `ruff format --check` puliti, `check:i18n`, `check:moduli`, `format:check` verdi

La chiave nuova `Confirm?` è nei tredici cataloghi.

## Due passaggi fuori da qui

1. **Il Worker su Cloudflare va ridistribuito** con questo `centralino/src/index.js` (che porta anche il tetto sulle linee nuove della beta.12). Il database non si tocca. Senza, il cestino nella plancia non ha nessuno dall'altra parte. E il **Cron Trigger** `0 4 * * *` va aggiunto a mano dalla pagina di Cloudflare: `[triggers]` in `wrangler.toml` vale solo per chi distribuisce con `wrangler`.
2. **La pulizia delle release** si lancia da Actions → «Pulizia release» → Run workflow, prima in anteprima e poi con la spunta. Va fatta **dopo** che la 1.4.5 è pubblicata: cancellare le beta prima lascerebbe la 1.4.4 come cosa più recente installabile.

author: makenowjust
body:
Fixes #418.

`parseBracedNewConstructorField` switched on `:` and `{` but had no `default` case, so a field followed by anything else (e.g. `NEW A00{A0}`, where the field is followed by `}`) produced a `BracedConstructorField` with a nil `Value` — and `err == nil`. `SQL()` and the position accessors then dereferenced the nil value and panicked.

A braced constructor field requires a value, so the parser now reports it as a syntax error:

```
syntax error: :1:15: expected token: {, :, but: }
  1|  NEW foo { bar }
   |                ^
```

Error recovery wraps the expression in an `ast.BadExpr` as usual.

## Tests

- New testdata case `testdata/input/expr/!bad_new_braced_constructor_field_without_value.sql` (`NEW foo { bar }`) with its generated result, alongside the existing `!bad_new_braced_constructor.sql`.

author: sherifomarsaleh
body:
## What changes

Per instruction, 3 September 2026: *"If fair value is above the current price then OK. Hold and challenge if the fair value is ONLY below the current price by more than 10%."*

A study is now **held only where its central sits more than 10% BELOW** the latest known price. Above the price it publishes.

## Why the asymmetry is evidential, not deferential

Errors in a discounted cash flow are not symmetric. A stale base year, an over-charged discount rate, a missed revenue line, a real-terms terminal decline, an unread filing, a terminal charging a capital intensity the company has never operated at — **every one of them pushes value down**. A central far below the price is a high-prior-of-defect region and the price is the only instrument in the room that measures it.

A central *above* the price is the ordinary shape of finding something cheap, which is what this work is for.

## The cost, stated rather than discovered later

An over-optimistic study is no longer **held**. It is still **audited** — `[R-GAP-01]` stays two-sided, so a central more than 10% above the price still owes its eight-heading review before its files are staged, and a study that skips it still goes red in CI.

**Audit both ways, hold only where the errors run.** If a study is ever found badly wrong on the high side, that is the evidence to revisit this clause, and it is written down so the revisit does not depend on anyone remembering.

## Two-sided answers

Held only if **every** branch sits more than the limit below. One branch at or above the price is a study whose answer depends on a decision, and the reader is shown the decision rather than nothing.

## Negative control

The far-above case is **kept and its expectation flipped** rather than deleted — that construction must now publish. Keeping the case and inverting it is the sharpest available evidence the change took effect; deleting it would leave the change untested exactly where it matters. Two cases added for the new edge: a central just above the limit on the high side, and a two-sided answer with one branch above the price. 14 conditions, all behaving.

## Effect on the book

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| may publish | 2 | **4** (TMGH, RIYADHCABLE, PHDC, DU) |
| held | 9 | **7** |
| unreadable (also held) | 13 | 13 |

Still held: ARCC −30.9%, EGCH −56.6% on its highest branch, AMOC −15.5%, SWDY −22.9%, AIRARABIA −16.0%, MODON −11.8%, SAVOLA −10.1%.

Both governing documents to `2026-09-03q`; sync and text gates green.

author: gregheffner
body:
The `default` AppProject was fully open: `sourceRepos: ["*"]`, any destination namespace, `clusterResourceWhitelist: [{"*","*"}]`. ArgoCD's application-controller is effectively cluster-admin, so that project **was** its blast radius.

Scoped to what the 12 Applications actually use, measured from live Application specs and from cluster-scoped objects carrying an ArgoCD tracking annotation:

| | |
|---|---|
| repos | gregheffner/cicd, helm.datadoghq.com, charts.external-secrets.io, kyverno.github.io/kyverno |
| namespaces | cloudflared, datadog, external-secrets, kube-system, kyverno, prod, radar, automation, default, kube-flannel |
| cluster kinds | Namespace, ClusterRole/Binding, CRD, Validating/MutatingWebhookConfiguration, ClusterPolicy, PriorityClass, StorageClass, APIService, IngressClass, ClusterSecretStore, ClusterExternalSecret, policy.kyverno.io/* |

Applied live with kubectl. The AppProject is not itself ArgoCD-managed and must not be, since it governs the things that are; the export under `documentation/cluster-config` is the version-controlled copy.

**Result:** 11 of 12 apps Synced/Healthy. The one exception, `heffner-security`, had a RoleBinding into `kubernetes-dashboard`, a namespace deleted on 2026-09-02. Removed here; the app should go green on merge.

## 概要

author: phrocker
body:
## What this builds

Packages `shoal-explore-web` so the **same image** runs on a laptop and (once shared-instance prerequisites land) in a shared instance, differing **only in configuration**. No external dependency, no external datastore — the embedded backend serves the corpus from Shoal's own storage engine on a declared volume.

- **`Dockerfile.shoal-explore-web`** — multi-stage; runtime is `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` (uid/gid 65532). `/var/lib/shoal/explorer` is a declared `VOLUME`. Default CMD is the safe loopback + `-dev-auth` combination. ~7 MB, no secrets.
- **`deploy/shoal-explore-web/`** — `docker-compose.yml` (one-command local run; host networking for the loopback-gated `-dev-auth` path; named volume `explorer-data`), `.env.example`, `README.md`.
- **`docs/shoal-explore-web-deploy.md`** — image, the configuration seam, the fail-closed unsafe-config guard, the persistence/#284 caveat, shared-instance gaps, and an Azure sketch.

No application code changed. The `-dev-auth` loopback guard and the #284 startup backfill are **verified and documented, not modified**.

## Verification (run, not asserted)

### Image build
```
$ docker build -f Dockerfile.shoal-explore-web -t shoal-explore-web:test --build-arg VERSION=deploy-test .
 => naming to docker.io/library/shoal-explore-web:test  ... done

$ docker image inspect shoal-explore-web:test --format 'Size={{.Size}} User={{.Config.User}} Volumes={{json .Config.Volumes}}'
Size=7097222 User=65532:65532 Volumes={"/var/lib/shoal/explorer":{}}

$ docker image inspect shoal-explore-web:test --format '{{json .Config.Env}}'
["PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin","SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"]
```
Exported filesystem contains only the binary + distroless `etc/passwd` (the `nonroot` account) — no keys/tokens/`.env`.

### Container run (host networking; port 8098, not 8080)
```
$ docker run -d --name shoal-explore-test --network host -v shoal-explore-data:/var/lib/shoal/explorer shoal-explore-web:test
$ docker logs shoal-explore-test
Authenticating every request as development principal development-principal@localhost
Granted 0 pre-existing document(s) in /var/lib/shoal/explorer to development-principal@localhost ... (issue #284)
Shoal Explorer listening at http://127.0.0.1:8098

$ docker run --rm --network host curlimages/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8098/api/v1/meta
{"max_page_size":100,...,"capabilities":{...,"ingest":true}}
```
(Docker Desktop maps `--network host` to the Docker VM, so the API is hit from a host-network helper container — exactly how a browser reaches it on a native Linux host.)

### Restart-persistence test
```
# seed one document
$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/ingest -H "X-Shoal-Workspace-Request: 1" -F "file=@seed.md;type=text/markdown"
{"snapshot":{"id":"2ab74122b4f13cb59c6dc13e8b41c5a856649374741fb7f12a19911f6047d036",...}}

# before restart: 1 document served
$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/documents -H "X-Shoal-Workspace-Request: 1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"page":{"limit":10}}'
{"snapshot":{"id":"2ab74122...",...},"documents":[{"document":{"title":"seed.md",...}}]}

$ docker restart shoal-explore-test
# logs after restart:
Granted 1 pre-existing document(s) in /var/lib/shoal/explorer to development-principal@localhost ... (issue #284)
Shoal Explorer listening at http://127.0.0.1:8098

# after restart: SAME snapshot id 2ab74122..., document still served
$ curl -X POST .../api/v1/documents ... -d '{"page":{"limit":10}}'
{"snapshot":{"id":"2ab74122...",...},"documents":[{"document":{"title":"seed.md",...}}]}
```

**What it proves:** the named volume preserved the corpus on disk (identical snapshot id; post-restart log finds 1 pre-existing doc) and the local `-dev-auth` profile serves it again.
**What it does not prove:** that authorization persists. The policy catalog is in-memory and is rebuilt by the dev-only backfill each start (#284). Without that backfill (any non-dev authenticator), a restart would preserve the corpus on disk but serve an **empty** set until re-ingested.

### Unsafe-configuration guard (fails closed)
```
$ docker run --rm --network host shoal-explore-web:test -data /var/lib/shoal/explorer -listen 0.0.0.0:8099 -dev-auth
shoal-explore-web: refusing to serve 0.0.0.0:8099 with -dev-auth: the development-principal@localhost development principal is granted the whole workspace corpus and is only safe on a loopback listener; bind 127.0.0.1 or [::1], or supply a real authenticator
# exit code 1

$ docker run --rm --network host shoal-explore-web:test -data /var/lib/shoal/explorer -listen 127.0.0.1:8099
shoal-explore-web: refusing to serve 127.0.0.1:8099 without authentication: no authenticator is configured; pass -dev-auth ...
# exit code 1
```

### One-command compose path
```
$ docker compose -f deploy/shoal-explore-web/docker-compose.yml up -d --build
$ docker run --rm --network host curlimages/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8098/api/v1/meta
{"max_page_size":100,...,"capabilities":{...,"ingest":true}}
$ docker compose -f deploy/shoal-explore-web/docker-compose.yml down -v
```

### Tests
```
$ go test ./cmd/shoal-explore-web/...
ok  github.com/phrocker/shoal-oss/cmd/shoal-explore-web  5.751s
```

## Gaps between local and shared I could not close (by design)

1. **No non-dev authenticator is wired** — without `-dev-auth`, startup fails closed demanding a real authenticator. Blocked on edge identity (**#278**).
2. **`-backend remote` is deliberately refused** (no on-the-wire `auth.Decision`, #278) — multi-node is out of scope; target is single instance, many users.
3. **Host-authority binding** — the handler requires request `Host` == the listener's resolved address, so a `0.0.0.0` public bind rejects real `Host` headers. A shared instance needs a configurable external authority (config seam not present yet).
4. **Durable policy store (#284)** must land before restarts serve a shared corpus without the dev-only backfill.

These are fail-closed behaviors, not packaging defects; I did not work around any of them.

## Notes
- Azure hosting shape is left undecided; the docs sketch Container Apps / App Service / AKS as options, gated on persistent-volume semantics.
- Cleaned up all containers, images, and volumes created during verification.

Do not merge — for owner review.

author: ehofesmann
body:
## 🔗 Related Issues

No related issues to link

## 📋 What changes are proposed in this pull request?

In the Annotate edit panel, a `list<str>` / `list<int>` / `list<float>` attribute rendered with the `checkboxes` component could render but ignore clicks, with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'map')` in the console.

Two pieces disagreed about what "empty" means for a list attribute:

- When an attribute's `when` condition stops being satisfied, the edit form writes an explicit `null` so the autosave delta carries an unset. When the condition is satisfied again, a value was only restored if the attribute defined a `default`, so list attributes were left as `null`.
- `CheckboxesWidget` used a destructuring default (`value = []`), which only covers `undefined`. The render path tolerated `null`, but the toggle handler called `values.map(...)` directly and threw.

Changes:

- `CheckboxesWidget`: normalize any non-array value to `[]` before the render and toggle paths use it. This also covers labels written from the SDK with a list attribute set to `None`.
- `applyConditionalOwnerChange`: when a defaultless `list<*>` attribute becomes visible again and was nulled by the hide branch, restore `[]`. Values that were never set stay `undefined`, so fresh labels don't persist empty arrays they never touched. The hide behaviour (writing `null` rather than deleting) is unchanged.

### Reproduction

The script below builds a dataset with a conditional checkbox-list attribute and seeds one detection with the attribute set to `None`, which is the state the UI leaves behind after hiding and re-showing the attribute.

```python
import fiftyone as fo
import fiftyone.zoo as foz

dataset = foz.load_zoo_dataset("quickstart", dataset_name="checkboxes-repro")
dataset.persistent = True

# Declare the list attribute on the detections
dataset.add_sample_field(
    "ground_truth.detections.issue_kind", fo.ListField, subfield=fo.StringField
)

# Ontology: `issue_kind` is a checkbox list shown only when label == "glitch"
ontology = fo.AnnotationOntology(
    name="checkboxes-repro",
    attributes=[
        fo.AttributeSpec(
            name="issue_kind",
            type="list<str>",
            component="checkboxes",
            values=["missing", "duplicated", "jitter"],
            when=fo.WhenEquals(field="label", value="glitch"),
        ),
    ],
)
ontology.save(overwrite=True)

label_schemas = {
    "ground_truth": {
        "type": "detections",
        "component": "dropdown",
        "classes": ["glitch", "other"],
    }
}
dataset.set_label_schemas(
    fo.apply_ontology(label_schemas, "ground_truth", ontology.name)
)
dataset.activate_label_schemas(["ground_truth"])

# Seed the broken state directly: an explicit None on the list attribute
sample = dataset.first()
det = sample.ground_truth.detections[0]
det.label = "glitch"
det["issue_kind"] = None
sample.save()

session = fo.launch_app(dataset)
```

Then in the App: open the first sample, switch to Annotate, select the first `ground_truth` detection, and click any `issue_kind` checkbox.

- On `main`: nothing happens and the console shows the `TypeError`.
- With this PR: the checkbox toggles and the value saves.

To reproduce through the UI alone, skip the seeding block: select a detection, set its label to `glitch`, change it to `other` (hiding `issue_kind`), then back to `glitch`.

## 🧪 How is this patch tested? If it is not, please explain why.

- New `CheckboxesWidget.test.tsx`: renders, checked state from value, toggling from `null` emits `["value"]` (fails on `main`), add/remove preserves enum order.
- `evaluateWhen.test.ts`: four cases for the list re-show path (restores `[]`, prefers a configured default, leaves `undefined` alone, hide still writes `null`).
- Manually reproduced with the script above and confirmed the console error before the fix.

- [ ] Yes. Give a description of this change to be included in the release

author: lucasmundim
body: All three tests in `tests/integration/test_tracing_export.py` have been failing. Two unrelated causes, neither of them a library bug — both are in the fixtures. ## 1. The exporter TLS-handshook a plaintext receiver The jaeger fixture handed out `localhost:`. `infer_otlp_insecure` only treats an explicit `http://` scheme as plaintext — a **bare `host:port` infers TLS**, deliberately, matching the OTel SDK's secure default. So the exporter opened TLS against jaeger's plaintext OTLP port and died: ``` SSL_ERROR_SSL: error:100000f7:SSL routines:OPENSSL_internal:WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER ``` No span ever arrived, so `assert services, "jaeger never saw trace ..."` failed. The fixture predates that inference (#90, `28b4d70`) and was never updated — #99 later touched this directory without catching it. The comment at `observability/tracing.py:132` already warns that a bare host:port against a plaintext collector needs `insecure=True`; the fixture just never got the memo. **Fix:** give the endpoint its `http://` scheme. Two of the three tests go green on this alone. ## 2. The IPC socket path was too long on macOS `test_per_frame_trace_context_crosses_mq_hop` put its ZMQ socket under pytest's `tmp_path`. A unix domain socket path must fit in `sockaddr_un.sun_path` — **104 bytes on macOS** — and there `tmp_path` resolves under `/private/var/folders/<...>/T/pytest-of-/pytest-//`, landing the socket at **138 characters**: ``` /private/var/folders/m7/6f_4w35d3xz7rgc29x39n0hm0000gn/T/pytest-of-/pytest-999/test_per_frame_trace_context_0/mq-hop-test.sock ``` The bind fails and the only symptom is `AssertionError: receiver thread never started` — which reads like a hang, not a path problem. Linux has short `/tmp` paths and a 108-byte limit, which is why CI never saw this and it only bites locally on macOS. **Fix:** a `short_ipc_dir` fixture that `mkdtemp`s under `/tmp`, keeping the per-run uniqueness `tmp_path` was there to provide. `/tmp` is hardcoded rather than `tempfile.gettempdir()` (which returns the long `/var/folders` path on macOS); safe because `ipc://` is POSIX-only to begin with. ## Verification - `pytest tests/integration/` — **3 passed**, three runs in a row, with the plain invocation and no `--basetemp` workaround. - Temp dirs cleaned up, nothing left in `/tmp`. - Tests only — no library code touched. Unit gate unchanged: **827 passed, 1 skipped, 2 deselected, 0 failed**. ## Not included `tests/test_benchmarks.py::TestZmqIpcBenchmarks::test_zmq_roundtrip_report` also fails, and is **not** fixed here — it is a separate problem. Reproduced standalone: the stall point is non-deterministic (frames 15/25/30/35/45/50, and some runs complete all 60) and it happens on both `ipc://` and `tcp://`, so it is neither the socket-path limit nor the transport. It looks like a lost-wakeup race in the strict send-one/recv-one lockstep the benchmark drives, which is not how a real filter runs. `TestPipelineSimulation::test_pipeline_simulation_report` is the flaky sibling, roughly 1 failure in 9. Both are `slow`-marked and excluded from `make test`. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: uniqbrio
body:
## Summary

Implements the 3-Sep design canvas revision. Six sections are new — **Course detail**, **Delete course confirm**, **Branches**, **Notifications**, **Confirm send**, and an **Audit log** rebuilt as a scrollable table — and eighteen existing sections changed. `design/RosiFit App.dc.html` is updated to that revision and is the spec the rest of this is measured against.

Two defects were found while building it, and both are the reason parts of this diff are larger than the canvas asked for.

## The two defects

**A genuine Google Meet export was being rejected** — `RC-009`, S1. `parseMeetCsv` read `lines[0]` as the header row, but a Meet attendance export writes the meeting code and the created/ended times *first*. So a real export was refused with *"That file has no 'Full Name' column"* — the file was correct, the reader was wrong, and the message sent the operator to check Meet rather than RosiFit. S1 because attendance is the product's one irreplaceable input, and this blocked it entirely for the file the product tells people to use.

No test could have caught it: the parsing lived in `src/data/csv.ts` beside `document` and `FileReader`, outside `scripts/tsconfig.json`'s DOM-free program. The pure parsing is now `src/data/meetCsv.ts`; `csv.ts` keeps only the browser halves. Same split as `csvFormat.ts`, same reason.

**Reports was not counting anything** — `RC-010`, S2. Every figure on it was a literal: `COURSE_BARS` and `BRANCH_BARS` were hardcoded arrays, the headline said "Attendance across 4 courses" whatever the academy ran, the total said `61%`, the period said "1–24 Aug" forever, and the Members scope read the `MEMBERS` fixture rather than the live query. Found while adding the **export** that was actually requested — which is what made it urgent, since a CSV becomes a document somebody keeps and acts on months later.

## Key changes

**New screens**
- `app/branches.tsx` — add/remove a branch, per-branch course and member counts, removal blocked while a branch is in use
- `app/course/[id].tsx` — course detail: roster, week strip, per-member missed/consecutive counts, branch filter, delete confirmation
- `src/components/Notifications.tsx` + `src/data/notifications.ts` — the tray, derived from data the app already loads rather than a new backend concept
- `app/audit.tsx` — rebuilt as a horizontally-scrollable five-column table with CSV export

**Migrations** — both are triggers and constraints, deliberately *not* RPCs: `0005` already states who may write these tables as RLS, and an RPC would restate that rule in a second place and need its own grant.
- `0019_branch_add_remove.sql` — derives the unique `code` from the branch name in a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger so two clients adding at once cannot collide; adds a partial unique index on `lower(name)` because every filter in the app addresses a branch *by name*; and refuses to soft-delete a branch that still has live offerings or scopes a holiday, since both would go on affecting sessions at a branch no read can see. Removal is an `UPDATE` to `deleted_at` through the existing policies — no new grant or policy.
- `0020_delete_course.sql` — course deletion that keeps attendance history and removes the schedule.

**Reports, now live**
- `src/data/report.ts` + `report.test.ts` — aggregation where it can be tested. Groups **sum** expected and attended rather than averaging their members' percentages (averaging 75% and 100% gives 87.5% where the truth is 9 of 10), and return `null` — never `0` — where nothing was expected, because a course with no sessions and a course everybody skipped are different facts.
- `app/(tabs)/reports.tsx` — reads the same member rows the dashboard reads (guardrail 1, one member source), a real period control instead of a caption, and an export that writes what is on screen *including the words*: a row the screen calls "no sessions scheduled" is not exported as `0%`.

**Dashboard simplified to what the canvas draws** — `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` keeps the scope tabs, the filters and the attendance distribution. The hero "N members need you" card, the "What needs you" list, the two quick links, the week table and the week strip are gone. Each was a second place a figure lived; the week table counted from a *different query* than the chart beside it while admitting in its own caption that the filters did not reach it; and the week strip rendered `WEEK_STRIP`, a hardcoded fixture, on the live dashboard. Everything removed is still reachable elsewhere.

**Smaller, from the same revision**
- `app/(tabs)/courses.tsx` — a branch filter that asks the *offerings*, so a course running at two branches appears under both
- `app/upload.tsx` — the Meet format explainer, the empty state, and a "Mapped to this session" panel: the last point in the flow where a wrong file can be caught, since everything after it matches names without looking at which meeting the rows came from. A definite date mismatch warns; an unreadable or absent date says it cannot check, because warning when nothing can be checked trains people past the warning that matters.
- `app/appearance.tsx` + `hueFromHex` in `src/theme/tokens.ts` — a hex field that contributes its **hue and nothing else**. The generator darkens that hue until white text clears 4.5:1 and `check-contrast.ts` verifies all 360, so a hex taken verbatim would walk straight round guardrail 2. Typed as pure green it ships as `#148514`. Plus the numbered preset/custom headings.
- `app/member/[id].tsx` — had **no way back at all**; now `router.back()`, since it is reached from three different places
- `app/match.tsx` — was `router.replace('/upload')`, which discarded the history entry so the upload screen it landed on had no way back

## Verification

- `npm run check` green — **113** unit assertions (57 added), **2836/2836** contrast pairs, **75/75** icons
- `npm run audit:all` clean, ratchets **paid down rather than baselined**: colours 13 → 11, test ids 26 → 24 in `app/`
- `bash db/harness/test.sh` — **215 assertions pass**; `0019` and `0020` replay clean from scratch; the two new specs green at 11/11 and 16/16
- Fail-first evidence for all four new unit specs in `TEST_SUMMARY.md` — two were run against the real code they replace, two against injected defects, each with the failure it produced
- Every changed screen driven in a browser in **both themes**, including the export downloaded and read, and the upload map against three real Meet-shaped files

**CI is red and it is not this PR's** — both jobs fail in 3 seconds without running a step, as have all 7 runs in the repository's history including 5 pushes to `main`. Detail in the comment below. Two `db-harness` specs will also stay red for pre-existing reasons named there.

## Not in this PR

Left from the canvas revision, by explicit decision: **ADD COURSE per-course wording** (needs a migration for course-scoped subject/body and a judgement on guardrail 5, "messages go out through stored templates only"), the **COMPOSE/MODAL** send-flow states, and the **SIGN IN** restructure. The holiday screen is kept although the canvas drops it — removing a working, tested, migrated feature because a canvas revision omits a screen is a product decision, not a design-sync one. `app/member/[id].tsx` still reads the `MEMBERS` fixture, same class as `RC-010`, noted in the register rather than left silent.

author: joyaltitus
body:
S2-G (#284 comment 10), with the session addendum: S2-A (#306) and S2-D (#309) are merged,
**S2-B D-META is not built**, so LeadSources covers D-FORM and D-EMBED (plus the plain-POST
api door) and leaves a labelled empty slot for Lead Ads.

## Lead sources — what the screen can do, and why that is not a design choice

Migration 077 grants the browser `SELECT` on `intake_source_configs` and **nothing else** —
no INSERT, no UPDATE — plus exactly two RPCs: `pm_intake_rotate_key` (client_admin, plaintext
returned once) and `pm_intake_activate_source` (named refusals). The create/rotate/set-template/
set-rep-pool management RPCs the session brief points at were **S2-B's** deliverable, and S2-B
is deferred.

So this screen **lists, issues keys and activates**, and renders phone field, template, cap and
rep pool **read-only** rather than painting inputs whose save button cannot exist. When those
RPCs land, those four lines are where the editors go. The sources themselves are provisioned by
the operator today, and the screen says so in the operator's own words.

Per door: D-FORM gets the `/f/:slug` link, D-EMBED gets a paste-in iframe, the api door gets the
POST URL and — the moment a key is issued — a curl carrying that key. The key is shown **once**,
with a copy box and the warning, because 077 stores only its sha256; a key nobody copied is gone.
Every refusal `pm_intake_activate_source` can name is glossed in plain language, and an
unrecognised code still renders raw, so a hub-side addition is never swallowed.

Lead Ads is a **deliberate empty slot**: it is the door tenants ask for first, and a screen that
simply omits it reads as "not supported" rather than "not yet". It names the workaround (point
the ad at the hosted form — same pipe, same attribution).

## Import — the guard is the database's, and this screen says so

Every write is one authenticated hub call; every read is the `import_batches` row, which **is**
the state machine and carries the counts and the guard state. The screen therefore polls the row
rather than asking the API what it just did — one source of truth, and a reload after a browser
crash resumes exactly where the operator left off. Polling stops when nothing is in flight; an
idle tenant makes no requests.

The lift dialog mirrors `pm_allow_import_messaging`'s own wall — the first eight characters of
the batch id typed back plus a non-empty attestation — so the operator is not sent to the server
to be told. The database still decides, and its refusal is rendered verbatim. A `purchased_list`
cohort is never offered a lift at all, and the "can never be messaged" warning sits on the upload
radio, **before** the file goes anywhere.

One trap found while shooting the screenshots and fixed: `label-caps` uppercases its content, and
the DB compares against `left(id::text, 8)` — a lowercase uuid. An operator typing back exactly
what they saw would have been refused with no way to tell why. The code now renders outside that
span, and the typed value is lowercased on the way out.

## The website widget

A `wa.me` link with the campaign's code word pre-typed **is** the attribution: the customer sends
the word and the existing trigger matcher claims the conversation, so nothing new has to be built,
deployed or kept alive. Plus a ten-line floating button that survives being pasted into a Wix
footer or a hand-written `index.html`. A missing `channel_accounts.display_number` says so instead
of putting a dead link on a customer's website — which is live's current state on all four rows.

## hub-service #276 — the sales-app half

`src/lib/flags.ts` is **deleted**, not rewired. `featureOn.ts` already reads `feature_grants` —
the C3 entitlement source PR #278 exposed — so `RepShell`'s `product_ai` door now asks that
instead of a second door register nobody could audit. Same key, same "no row = hidden" default,
plus the role test the grants table carries (five cases pinned in `RepShell.door.test.tsx`:
granted+enabled+role opens it; no row, `granted:false`, `enabled:false` and a role outside
`enabled_roles` each keep it shut).

`git grep feature_flags -- src tests` is **empty** — the two remaining hits are prose in a dated
security-review table, whose row now points at the new reader. **hub-service can take migration
080 once this is deployed**; I will comment on #276 when it merges.

## Evidence

- 95 suites / **688 tests** green (33 new), `tsc -b` clean, `npm run build` clean at 177.0 KB gz
  against a 200 KB budget, `check:no-service-role` and `check:tokens` clean.
- 16 screenshots in `docs/ui-review/2026-09-03-intake` — both themes, 1280 and 390 — each

  survived, which is the check #59's mock data escaped.

author: muqsitnawaz
body:
**Plan only — no behavior change.** Commits the rendered PHNX-3899 plan under `.agents/artifacts/2026-09-03/`. Implementation is not dispatched until the owner reviews.

**Rendered plan:** https://share.agents-cli.sh/muqsitnawaz/phnx-3899-codex-dispatch

## What this changes about the ticket

PHNX-3899 bundles three unrelated faults under one "codex is broken" symptom. Live probes across six fleet devices (2026-09-03) correct two of its hypotheses.

### macOS was misdiagnosed

`pinnacles` is not failing on the `default_permissions` config keys or a shim/PATH version split. Its managed codex binaries are **killed by Gatekeeper at `exec`**:

```console
$ agents ssh pinnacles '... "$B" --version; echo "EXIT=$?"; spctl -a -t exec "$B"'
0.125.0: exit=137 out=[]
    spctl: CSSMERR_TP_CERT_REVOKED
0.130.0: exit=137 out=[]
    spctl: CSSMERR_TP_CERT_REVOKED
```

`exit=137` is `128 + 9` — SIGKILL, before `main` runs, which is why there are zero bytes. `zion` and `mac-mini` run codex 0.147.0 fine, so this is a **stale install on one box**, not a macOS fault. The `codex-cli 0.39.0` on `PATH` is an unmanaged `bun` install the CLI never invokes (`pinnacles` has no `~/.agents/shims/` at all), so `codex --version` reports a binary that is not the one being launched.

### The load-bearing defect is not codex-specific

`cli/src/lib/exec.ts:2380`:

```js
const exitCode = budgetKilled ? BUDGET_KILL_EXIT_CODE : (code ?? 0);
```

Node's `close` event is `(code, signal)`. A signal-killed child reports `code === null`, so `null ?? 0` yields **0**. Any agent killed by SIGKILL, SIGSEGV, or SIGTERM currently reports **success with zero output** — every harness, for `run`, `teams`, and routines alike. `exec.ts:1430` in the same file already does this correctly.

This is why two loud environment failures presented as one silent one, and why it is recommended as P0 shipping alone.

### Linux: confirmed, plus a constraint the ticket did not have

`userns` is blocked fleet-wide as reported. New fact — `sudo` is **not** passwordless on 2 of 3 sampled boxes (`yosemite-m2`, `mark-1`), so a `agents setup` phase cannot provision this unattended. The plan designs the phase to prompt or fail loud rather than silently no-op.

## On the owner's framing

The plan separates the two axes the question conflates:

- **Approval policy** (does codex *ask*) — already set correctly by `codexPolicyArgs` (`cli/src/lib/codex-policy.ts:70`). This *is* the Claude-style auto-approve. Not implicated.
- **Sandbox** (what a tool can *touch*) — enforced by codex's bundled bubblewrap, which needs an unprivileged user namespace the kernel denies. **No config value can flip a kernel sysctl**; that needs root, once, per box.

## Verification

`artifacts check` passes; both figures inspected at the pixel level on `zion` (architecture SVG and the current/proposed CLI behavior figure — an overflow in the proposed panel was found and fixed), no console errors, share URL returns HTTP 200.

## Note

`agents artifacts share` hit a managed-tier `413 storage limit reached`; published via the BYO Cloudflare backend instead. The managed share quota is full and will need attention separately. The OG preview card is absent (this Linux box lacks `libatk` for the headless capture) — the link itself is fine.

author: mickeyzzc
body:
## Summary

Closes #685 (and the log side of #651). Per the issue's spirit — measure first — I sampled **24h of production logs on M5** (18,462 lines) before touching anything. The field evidence overturned the issue's assumptions:

| Source | Share of volume | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Mangled double-wrapped lines (`level=INFO msg="ERROR …entire line…"`) | **32%** | **Bug fixed** (see below) |
| Routine 2xx request logs (99% `/api` polling, NOT static assets) | 26% | Level-based: Debug/Info/Warn |
| Repeated `auto-remediate skipped` (blacklisted cams, every scan) | 10% | → Debug |
| `pushed video to vision` (per segment) | 10% | → Debug |
| GB28181 REGISTER churn (one device re-registers ~30s despite expires=3600) | 14% | Out of scope — lives in the gb28181-go lib; the storm itself looks device-side |

### The 32% bug: init-time logger capture

51 package-level `var x = slog.Default().With("component", …)` loggers initialize **before** `main()` calls `slog.SetDefault`. They hold the pristine default handler, whose output routes through the `log` package — which `SetDefault` has redirected into the new handler. Every record re-emerges as `level=INFO msg="ERROR connection error, reconnecting component=… camera_id=…"` — **wrong level (ERROR→INFO), attrs unparseable**. Reproduced in a minimal test; mechanism proven.

Fix: new `internal/slogx` leaf package — `slogx.Component(name)` wraps a deferred handler that resolves `slog.Default()` at **call** time, so the configured handler/level/format always apply. All 51 sites migrated mechanically (call sites unchanged).

### Level policy

- `RequestLogger`: 2xx/3xx → **Debug**, 4xx → Info, 5xx → Warn. (The issue's static-asset skip-list idea turned out irrelevant: only 30/4,714 request lines were static assets — the real source is `/api` polling.)
- `auto-remediate skipped` → Debug (identical line per camera per scan cycle; blacklist state transitions remain logged where they happen).
- `pushed video to vision` → Debug.
- `tutk: keepalive tick` → Debug (#651's second noise source; ticks per second per stream).

## Tests

TDD: `internal/slogx` proves the SetDefault-swap survival, level filtering, and no double-wrap; `TestRequestLoggerLevels` pins the Debug/Info/Warn contract; updated assertions in middleware/health tests to the new levels.

`go test -race ./internal/... ./pkg/app/` — **5,324 passed in 58 packages**; `make lint` clean.

author: ericlenzi
body:
El front ya se deployaba solo con Vercel; la API era la mitad que quedaba a mano. Este PR la mueve a
GitHub Actions, con el gate donde tiene que estar.

## ANTES DE MERGEAR

**Hay que crear el environment `production` con required reviewers primero.** Un environment que no
existe se crea solo en la primera corrida, y se crea **sin protecciones**: si se mergea antes, el
primer deploy corre sin que nadie apruebe. No puede hacer dano —falla en el paso de SSH porque no
hay secret todavia— pero el gate no existiria.

Los cuatro pasos de puesta en marcha estan en [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md) y se hacen una
sola vez: clave SSH dedicada para el CI, instalacion del script privilegiado, regla de sudoers, y
el secret + el environment en GitHub.

## Como queda

* **Dispara en push a master** y **queda esperando aprobacion** en el environment `production` antes
  de tocar el VPS. Ese click no es ceremonia: es donde se decide el orden contra una migracion
  destructiva, que es la unica parte del despliegue que automatizar empeora en vez de arreglar.
* **Construye desde un commit**, no desde el working tree de quien deploya. Es la trampa que
  `deploy-api.ps1` no puede evitar.
* Corre los mismos tests que `ci.yml` antes de publicar. Repetidos a proposito: "otro workflow ya
  los corrio" es una garantia mas debil que correrlos aca, y son 40 segundos.
* Replica los excludes del estado de runtime **y el guard**: si un `switch_state.json` se cuela en
  el paquete, se planta antes de subir nada.
* `workflow_dispatch` con un `ref` a eleccion: es el rollback de hoy.
* Si algo falla, imprime `journalctl -n 80` en la salida del workflow. Sin eso, un deploy fallido no
  deja nada para diagnosticar.

## El paso privilegiado

El CI corre **un** comando con sudo: `/usr/local/bin/galecore-deploy`, un script de root que vive en
el servidor, **no toma argumentos** y hace exactamente stop -> extract -> chown -> start. La regla de
sudoers esta acotada a el.

La alternativa era darle `NOPASSWD` a `tar` y a `chown` con argumentos libres, que es darle root
entero a quien deploya. La copia versionada esta en [`deploy/galecore-deploy`](deploy/galecore-deploy)
para que se pueda revisar y diffear; el script **no viaja en el paquete del deploy**, porque un
deploy que pudiera reescribir su propio script privilegiado no tendria ningun limite.

Ademas valida antes de parar el servicio: que el paquete no traiga archivos de estado de runtime
(defensa en profundidad, del lado del que extrae) y que traiga `DataFeed.Api.dll` (un paquete vacio
no vale bajar la API). Y al final chequea `systemctl is-active`, porque un servicio que arranca y se
cae al instante se reportaba como deploy exitoso.

## Seguridad

* **No dispara nunca en `pull_request`.** El repo es publico: un workflow que corre sobre un fork
  con acceso a los secretos regala la clave del VPS.
* La regla de sudoers de los logs es de **comando exacto, sin comodines**: no sirve para leer ningun
  otro journal.
* La clave del CI es dedicada, no la personal del operador: si se compromete, se revoca sola.

## `.gitattributes`

`core.autocrlf=true` sin `.gitattributes` significa que el script de shell se checkoutea con CRLF, y
al copiarlo al VPS el shebang queda como `#!/bin/bash\r`. El error que se ve es
`bad interpreter: No such file or directory`, que no menciona los saltos de linea por ningun lado.

## Lo que NO cambia

* **Las migraciones siguen manuales**, con `migrate-db.ps1`. Automatizarlas exige poner en GitHub
  una credencial que puede `DROP TABLE`, y todo el diseno de dos roles existe para que esa
  credencial no viva lejos del operador. Son 5 migraciones en 4 meses: no lo vale.
* **`deploy-api.ps1` no se elimina.** Es el camino para desplegar una rama sin pasar por master, y
  la salida si Actions no esta disponible.
* **Sigue sin haber rollback real.** `tar` extrae encima: redesplegar un commit viejo no es lo mismo
  que restaurar lo que habia. La solucion es `releases/` con symlink y cuesta editar la unidad de
  systemd; queda anotado en `deploy/README.md`.

## Verificado

`bash -n` sobre el script y parseo del YAML del workflow. **El deploy end-to-end no se pudo probar
desde aca**: no hay acceso SSH al VPS en esta sesion, y los cuatro pasos de puesta en marcha son
tuyos. La primera corrida real es la prueba.

author: lbibollet16
body:
La première relève réelle a échoué sur **les 23 documents**, avec une cause unique et étrangère au code :

> *A positive credit balance is required for all requests, including BYOK, so fallback providers remain available.*

Le solde du **Vercel AI Gateway est à zéro** — aucun appel n'est parti. Les durées de 86 à 967 ms et la colonne `modele` vide le confirment.

## Le défaut que ça a révélé dans ma conception

Les 23 messages ont quand même reçu le libellé « Booking traité » dans Gmail. Comme un message étiqueté ne ressort plus de la recherche, **leurs programmes devenaient définitivement inaccessibles alors qu'aucun n'avait été lu**. Une coupure de service de dix minutes suffisait à vider la boîte.

Je n'avais pas distingué deux échecs de nature opposée :

| Échec | Sort du message |
|---|---|
| le document n'est pas un programme | définitif → on étiquette |
| l'extraction n'a pas pu tourner | passager → **on laisse en vue** |

`pannePassagere` fait maintenant ce tri : solde de crédits, quota, 429, 5xx, timeout, coupure réseau, clé d'API refusée. Un message touché par l'une d'elles n'est pas étiqueté et repasse à la relève suivante. Les documents déjà extraits du même courriel ne seront pas dupliqués — l'index unique `(gmail_message_id, nom_fichier)` s'en charge.

## De quoi rattraper ce qui est déjà étiqueté

`?relancer=1` repart des lignes en erreur, **retélécharge la pièce jointe par son id Gmail** et refait l'extraction en place. C'est ce qui sauve les 23 documents de cette première relève.

Un bouton **« Relancer les N échecs »** apparaît à l'écran dès qu'il y a des erreurs.

## Et le dire une fois plutôt que vingt-trois

Quand toute la relève bute sur la même panne, la réponse la remonte **une seule fois, en clair**, avec ce qu'il faut faire. Vingt-trois lignes « Échec » identiques n'apprennent rien.

## ⚠️ À noter

`lib/commandes-pdf-ai-parser.ts` passe par le même gateway. **Il échoue donc lui aussi en production** tant que le solde est à zéro — ton parseur de PDF de commandes Traction est hors service sans avoir rien dit.

## Pas de migration

Merge, redéploie, charge des crédits, puis clique **« Relancer les 23 échecs »**.
