author: hasezoey
siomkin
body:
## Summary

Every Tauri command now rejects with a serialised `CommandError` (`kind` + `message` + optional `code`/`detail`/`hook`/`path`) instead of a bare string, classification happens in Rust next to the failure, redaction happens once at the command boundary, and failed secondary refresh reads are surfaced instead of rendering their section as empty.

OpenSpec change: `openspec/changes/unify-error-model` (spec delta `ipc/commands`). No Jira key.

## What changed

**Rust**
- `git/types/error.rs` — `CommandError` / `CommandErrorKind` (`git`, `hookRejected`, `auth`, `network`, `staleLease`, `indexLock`, `conflict`, `notARepository`, `missingPath`, `forge`, `internal`) with `From` impls for `String`, `git2::Error`, `RepoOpenError`, `GithubError`, `HttpError`, `SecretError`, `CaptureError`.
- `git/write/classify.rs` — the regexes the frontend used to run over raw git output, ported verbatim with their fixtures as Rust tests.
- `commands/mod.rs` — `blocking` / `sync` / `boundary` adapters are the only error producers (convert + redact once). The registration test now fails any `Result<_, String>` command and any `Result` command whose body skips an adapter. All 181 commands migrated (`updater.rs` included); `forge::ipc`/`context` return `CommandError`.
- `thiserror` added (proc-macro only); derives on `HttpError`, `SecretError`, `CaptureError`/`ReaderError`.

**Frontend**
- `lib/api/invoke.ts` — `CommandError` class (`toString()` = message), `toCommandError`, wrapped `invoke`; all wrappers use it; eslint confines raw core `invoke` to this file.
- `lib/gitError.ts` formats copy from `kind`/`code`/`hook` only; the classifier exports are gone. Toasts attach “Fix authentication…” / “Remove lock & retry” by `kind`; the missing-repo screen branches on `missingPath`/`notARepository`.
- `store/repoRefresh/sectionFailures.ts` + `unavailableSections` on `useRepo`: worktrees/stashes/forge/remotes/operation reads that fail keep their last data, toast once per transition, and clear on recovery — `UnavailableRow` in the branch navigator, `OperationUnavailableBanner` in the app shell.
- Docs: `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture-rules.md`, `architecture-rules-rust.md` §4.

## Design notes / deviations from the proposal
- The classifier lives in `git/write/classify.rs` and runs from `CommandError::from(String)`; the write layer stays `String`-typed internally.
- `GithubError` keeps a manual `Display` over `to_ipc_string()`; `LeaseError` is untouched (message-free by design).
- `CommandError` is 128 bytes, so `clippy::result_large_err` is allowed in `commands/` and `git/forge.rs` rather than boxing the failure path.
- `StackedReview.test.tsx`: the wrapper's extra promise hop exposed a FIFO-eviction timing dependency; the test's viewport is now wider than the cache cap so the assertion is about policy, not batching. No product code changed there.
- `invoke.test.ts` isolates the mock in `afterEach`: with a `beforeEach`, vitest 4.1 re-reported converted rejections as unhandled (cause not identified).

## Validation
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint`, `bun run test` (289 files / 3490 tests), `bun run build`, `bun run sizes`
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` (1093 passed)
- `openspec validate unify-error-model --strict`

body:
### Summary

Adds a `brand/` directory containing a first-pass brand kit for Bundle of Rays, derived from the existing primary mark rather than from a generic XR/healthcare palette.

The mark is a brush-ink drawing on paper, and that constrains everything else: the system is flat, unmixed colour and print-derived texture. Gradients, drop shadows, glassmorphism, glow and bevel are prohibited outright, because each of them visibly fights a hand-drawn ink logo.

> **Licence blocker — the most important thing in this PR.** The mark is not a Bundle of Rays commission. It is Jean Jullien's existing artwork *Us*, and the permission on record (Studio Jean Jullien, 02 Jun 2025) reads *"Jean is happy to let you use US, It would have to be limited to this project only, ie not used again over consecutive conferences etc. If you're ok with that, no fee for you."* That project was *The Just Us Show*, a monthly VR gathering for nurses and teachers. The studio then asked how long the show would run; the reply proposed a year (or an initial six months) and raised use *"potentially as an implied logo for the show"*. There is no further reply on record, so neither the term nor the logo use was ever agreed.
>
> Using it as company identity differs on every axis: a different entity (Bundle of Rays Academy Pty Ltd rather than a community show), indefinite use, trademark use, and a derivative work, since a "BUNDLE OF RAYS" wordmark has been added beneath the artwork. A written licence for company identity is needed from Studio Jean Jullien — or a new mark commissioned — before this kit is applied to anything.

**What's here**

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `brand/BRAND.md` | Guidelines — leads with the licence position, then colour, typography, texture, logo use, XR notes |
| `brand/tokens.css` | CSS custom properties, including a dark-ground inversion |
| `brand/tokens.json` | The same values as design tokens, with contrast ratios, warnings and a machine-readable status block |
| `brand/brand-kit.html` | Self-contained visual kit, built in the brand itself |
| `brand/logo/` | The mark (placeholder raster — see open issues) |

**Colour.** Ink (`#14110F`) on Paper (`#F6F1E7`) at 16.70:1 carries the brand. Four flats — Ray, Pulse, Breath, Deep — are fill colours that take black type, except Deep which inverts to paper. Three deepened variants exist for coloured type on the paper ground. Every ratio was computed against WCAG 2.1, not estimated, and each is stated alongside its conformance level so a pairing can't be used outside where it passes.

**Typography.** Archivo for display, Source Serif 4 for body, IBM Plex Mono for data. All three are SIL OFL 1.1, deliberately: they can be embedded in Unity and Unreal builds without a licence problem, which commercial foundry EULAs routinely prohibit for application binaries.

**Texture.** Three permitted textures, all print-derived — paper grain, brush edge, risograph misregistration — each demonstrated live in the HTML kit rather than described.

### Screenshots (optional)

`brand/brand-kit.html` is self-contained and renders offline in any browser; the logo is embedded as a data URI. It demonstrates each colour pairing at real size with its computed ratio, shows the three textures as live effects, and marks the grounds the logo may and may not sit on.

### Documentation checklist

- [x] Self-contained addition under `brand/`; no existing pages renamed, moved or modified, so no redirects are required.
- [x] `tokens.css` and `tokens.json` formatted with tabs per `.prettierrc.mjs`, so the CI `format:core:check` step passes.

### Open issues blocking sign-off

1. **Licence.** As above — the mark is not licensed for company use, and the wordmark lockup is an ungranted derivative. This outranks the other two.
2. **The logo file is a 225 × 224 px raster with a baked white background.** A web thumbnail, not master artwork; the white is worked around in the HTML with blend modes. Vector art has to come from Studio Jean Jullien, which is the same conversation as the licence.
3. **The palette is proposed, not approved.** The four flats are one defensible reading of the mark's flat-colour method, and they pass contrast, but they need sign-off before anything is printed.

### Note on placement

This repository is a fork of Cloudflare's documentation site, which is not a natural home for this content — it will conflict or be buried on upstream syncs. The kit is deliberately self-contained in `brand/` so it can be lifted into its own repository without changes. Worth moving before it grows.

body:
* 🚨 Severity: HIGH
* 💡 Vulnerability: The automated test scripts `test_clear_log_file.sh` and `tests/test_log.sh` used predictable filenames (like `/tmp/test_conky_gui.log`) and easily guessable PID-based names (`$$`) in the world-writable `/tmp/` directory. This constitutes a CWE-59 vulnerability where a local attacker could pre-create these files as symlinks pointing to sensitive system files.
* 🎯 Impact: When a developer or CI environment runs the tests, the scripts would unknowingly write test output to the attacker's symlink target, leading to arbitrary file overwrite or corruption of critical system data.
* 🔧 Fix: Replaced all predictable and PID-based temp file creations with secure `mktemp` invocations. Removed pre-emptive `rm -f` commands that introduce TOCTOU race conditions.
* ✅ Verification: Ran the full test suite (`./run_tests.sh`, `./test_clear_log_file.sh`, `./test_clear_logs.sh`, `./test_plan.sh`, and `bash tests/test_log.sh`) and confirmed all tests pass using the newly secured temporary file logic.

author: grtwrn
body:
Comment-only follow-up to #40, which I verified before merging.

Its distribution claim for Red at 344 Winchester reproduced almost exactly over 813 visits in 30 days:

| | p10 | p25 | median | p75 | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #40 claimed | 3.1 | 5.5 | 8.3 | 10.7 | 12.6 |
| re-measured | 3.3 | 5.4 | 8.2 | 10.7 | 12.9 |

But its tail figure did not. "One visit in seventeen is under two minutes" is actually **one in fifty-eight** — too high by three and a half times — and it appears in two permanent code comments as justification.

The conclusion is unaffected, and the correction says why: the case for a low quantile is the **width** of the distribution (a rest runs 3 to 13 minutes, so the median is two minutes wrong in one direction or the other most of the time), not the frequency of the short tail. So this changes no behaviour — two comments and a note recording the re-measurement, so nobody later reasons from a number that is 3.5× off.

Also verified while reviewing #40, for the record: the median-to-p35 gap is **11 seconds** at ordinary stops versus **64 seconds** at rest stops, which is why the change is nearly inert where most trips live. And measuring single dwells independently of #40's chain method, p35 moves ≥2-min pessimistic from 10.8% → 6.3% and ≥2-min optimistic from 18.8% → 24.6% — a roughly 1:1 count trade, so the case does rest entirely on a missed bus costing a headway while a wait costs three minutes.

author: mgoldsborough
body:
`check:codegen` regenerates into `web/src/_generated/` and ended in `git diff --exit-code`. That compares **tracked** paths, so it caught a generated file that drifted and was blind to one that does not exist yet — a PR adding a schema source under `src/tools/platform/schemas/` passed with its `.d.ts` missing, and the artifact then landed in whatever unrelated PR next ran `codegen`.

The check is now `scripts/check-codegen.ts`, which runs `git status --porcelain -uall` over that directory and reports clean **only** when git exited 0 and named nothing.

**Why a script and not a shell one-liner.** The first cut of this was `! git status --porcelain -uall … | grep .`. A pipeline reports grep's exit status, not git's — so a git that cannot answer at all (no repository, unreadable index) writes nothing to stdout, grep finds no match, the negation passes, and the guard reports a clean tree it never looked at. That is the same defect one layer over: a guard saying "fine" about something it could not see. `spawnSync` lets a spawn failure, a non-zero exit and a signal each be a failure, with git's own stderr attached.

**Why not `git add -AN`.** The issue offered both. `add -AN` catches the file but mutates the index, leaving stray intent-to-add entries behind after a developer's local `bun run verify`. Reading status is read-only.

**What the reader sees.** `describeCode` turns a porcelain code into a reason, so an untracked artifact reports `generated but never added to git` rather than `??` — naming the fix as `git add`, not another regeneration.

## Verification

The real trigger is a new schema **source**, not a hand-edited artifact — `codegen` wipes and repopulates the whole directory, so tampering with its output proves nothing. Five cases, each run end to end:

| case | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| clean tree | pass | pass |
| new schema source → untracked `.d.ts` | **pass (blind)** | fail, names `web/src/_generated/platform-schemas/probe.d.ts` |
| modified tracked file | fail | fail |
| deleted tracked file | fail | fail |
| `GIT_DIR=/nonexistent` (git cannot answer) | fail (129) | fail (1, with git's stderr) |

One behaviour changed beyond the untracked case: regenerated output that is **staged but not committed** now fails. `git diff` compares worktree-to-index, so `git add`ing it used to pass. It is a true positive by the check's own definition and invisible in CI, but it does mean the local loop is `codegen` → `verify` → `add` → commit, not `add` → `verify`.

`bun run verify:static` exits 0. `bun run test:unit`: 5,253 pass / 0 fail (+13 from the new test file). Lint reports the one pre-existing warning outside this diff.

## Tests

`test/unit/scripts/check-codegen.test.ts` — 13 tests. Moving the check out of `package.json` is what made this possible: the verdict logic is now an exported function over a git result, so the fail-closed property is pinned directly rather than by mutating the working tree mid-run. The load-bearing case is `verdictFor` on a non-zero git exit with **empty** stdout — exactly the state the pipeline form reported as clean.

`web/package.json`'s `check:theme` does not share the original defect and is untouched — it watches a single tracked file that its generator always overwrites, so no directory can gain an unseen member.

Closes #1073

author: kamikaze011001
body:
Two consequences added to ADR-0010, both decided while implementing the screener.

**Resolution failure fails closed.** An unresolvable host is refused, not accepted. Creation is not latency-critical, and accepting links to nowhere is worse than occasionally refusing a domain whose DNS is having a bad day. The cost is stated rather than hidden: a valid destination can be rejected because *our* resolver was unavailable, not because anything was wrong with the destination.

**DNS resolution is bounded to 2 seconds.** `InetAddress.getAllByName` has no timeout of its own, so a slow resolver would otherwise hang a request indefinitely — on a process that also serves Redirects. A timeout counts as a resolution failure, so it also fails closed.

Also names the case the tests exist to pin down: `localtest.me` is a public domain whose A record is `127.0.0.1`. A screener that checks the hostname *string* passes every other check in the suite and still lets an attacker reach the private network — which is why the rule runs on resolved addresses.

author: jaryl
body:
Closes #39.

## What

Cruciform's "Send to <app> on this phone" reverse handoff (ADR-0006) used a **hard-coded** `RpPairHandoff.KNOWN` registry (`heyarr-mobile`, `All Thing`) plus one manifest `<queries>` entry **per RP scheme**. So a new relying party needed a Cruciform release, and the visibility query had to exactly mirror each RP's filter (we already shipped one scheme-vs-host bug this way in 0.5.1/0.5.2).

This replaces the registry with **runtime discovery** (ADR-0009): an RP advertises itself, Cruciform finds it.

## How discovery works

- **Category** `one.rarebit.voidbind.category.RP_HANDOFF` — an RP declares it on a **data-less** `ACTION_VIEW` intent-filter to mean "I can receive a same-phone Voidbind pairing handoff", alongside a `<meta-data android:name="one.rarebit.voidbind.rp.pair_scheme" .../>` naming its pair scheme.
- **Cruciform** issues `PackageManager.queryIntentActivities(Intent(VIEW).addCategory(RP_HANDOFF), GET_META_DATA)`, then for each resolved activity takes the **label** from `ResolveInfo.loadLabel` (`android:label`) and the **scheme** from the `META_PAIR_SCHEME` meta-data, mapping each to `RpPairTarget(appName, "<scheme>://pair")`.
- **Why data-less filter + meta-data scheme** (not the category on the `scheme://pair` filter): Android intent matching won't match a data-less probe against a data-bearing filter, and a generic probe can't know the RP's scheme in advance; and `queryIntentActivities` doesn't expose the activity's *other* filters' data. So the RP advertises capability data-less and states the scheme in meta-data. Documented in ADR-0009.
- **Fallback**: nothing resolves -> empty list -> QR/Sharesheet only. Missing/blank/`voidbind` scheme adverts are dropped.

## Unchanged

`RpPairHandoff.uriFor` / `percentEncode` and the one-tap `cruciform://pair-joined` / `<scheme>://pair-done` contract (ADR-0008) are untouched — only the **source** of the target list changed from `KNOWN` to discovery. Versioning is git-tag-derived, so no manual bump. The two app-repo PRs add the category + meta-data to their manifests (rarebit-one/heyarr-mobile, rarebit-one/allthing-android).

## Tests

- `RpPairHandoffTest` — pure JVM coverage of the advert -> target/identity mapping (dedup, ordering, lowercase scheme, refusing our own/blank scheme, return-leg package lookup) + the unchanged URI encoding.
- `RpPairManifestQueriesTest` — asserts the real manifest declares the generic `RP_HANDOFF` `<queries>` entry (data-less).
- `:androidApp:assembleDebug` + `:androidApp:testDebugUnitTest` green, incl. a `--no-build-cache --rerun-tasks` run.

body:
## Änderungsbericht

**Agent / Autor**: Claude Code
**Branch**: `sec/runtime-sanitizer-token-prefixes`
**Phase**: P7
**Task-Typ**: fix

### Was wurde geändert?

#849 hat die CI-Wache repariert; sie kennt seither alle sechs GitHub-Präfixe.
Dieselbe Lücke stand aber ein **zweites Mal** im Repository — in der
Laufzeit-Redaction `app/audit/sanitization.py:93` mit
`\bghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b|\bgh[osr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b`. Durch fielen `ghu_`,
`github_pat_` und jede Länge außer exakt 36, also insbesondere jeder
fine-grained PAT. Der Kommentar darüber sagte `ghp_…, gho_…, ghs_…, etc.` und
behauptete damit mehr, als das Muster leistete.

Am Mainline `afd84af2` geprüft: durch #850 (KAI CORE v1) **nicht** geschlossen —
es ist genau eine Fundstelle im ganzen Baum.

Der eigentliche Defekt ist nicht das eine Muster, sondern **zwei Listen** für
dieselbe Sache. Solche Listen driften unbemerkt, weil jede für sich plausibel
aussieht; genau das ist passiert. Ein PR, der nur `ghu_` und `github_pat_`
nachträgt, stellt denselben Zustand wieder her, aus dem der Fehler entstand.
Deshalb ein gemeinsamer Katalog plus ein Test, der eine dritte Liste
strukturell verbietet.

**Warum es so lange überlebt hat:** `tests/unit/test_audit_sanitization.py`
hatte für `github_token` **null** Tests. Acht der zehn Default-Muster waren
abgedeckt, dieses nicht.

### Spec-Referenz
- Referenz: Operator-Directive — strukturierte Logs dürfen keine Secrets
  tragen (`app/audit/sanitization.py`, Abschnitt „Goal"); Folge-Arbeit zu #849
  und zur Aufarbeitung in `SEC_TOKEN_ROTATION_20260902.md`.

### Dateien erstellt
- `app/security/secret_patterns.py` — der einzige Katalog. Sechs
  `TokenShape`-Einträge, aus denen beide Verbraucher ihre Form ableiten: die
  CI-Wache pro Präfix einen sprechenden Typ, der Sanitizer eine Alternation mit
  Wortgrenzen und der einen Marke `[REDACTED:github_token]`. **stdlib-only**,
  weil der CI-Hygiene-Job nichts installiert.
- `tests/unit/test_secret_pattern_parity.py` — der Drift-Wächter. Tokenisiert
  jede Datei unter `app/` und `scripts/` und fällt, sobald ein
  GitHub-Token-Regex als String-Literal außerhalb des Katalogs auftaucht.
  Bewusst nur String-Literale, keine Kommentare: `sanitization.py` beschreibt in
  einem Kommentar, was dort früher stand — Historie darf man aufschreiben, ein
  zweites lebendes Muster nicht anlegen. Ein reiner Textscan könnte beides nicht
  unterscheiden und würde das Dokumentieren des Vorfalls bestrafen.

### Dateien geändert
- `app/audit/sanitization.py` — `github_token` bezieht sein Muster aus dem
  Katalog statt aus einem eigenen Literal.
- `scripts/secret_guard.py` — dito; dazu ein expliziter `sys.path`-Einschub, weil
  `python scripts/secret_guard.py` `sys.path[0]` auf `scripts/` setzt und nicht
  auf die Repo-Wurzel. Neue Testdatei in `ALLOWLISTED_PATHS`.
- `tests/unit/test_audit_sanitization.py` — die fehlende Abdeckung: sechs
  Präfixe, zwei Regressionen (fine-grained PAT, den `{36}` nie traf; klassisches
  36-Zeichen-Token, das weiter treffen muss), sechs Fehlalarm-Kontrollen,
  Idempotenz. 23 → 38 Tests.

---

## Quality Gates

- [x] `pytest` grün — `tests/unit` vollständig: **8827 passed, 38 skipped,
      0 failed** (17:44). Keine neue Skip-Markierung im Diff (`grep` auf
      hinzugefügte Zeilen: 0 Treffer für `skip`/`xfail`).
- [x] `ruff check .` grün — ebenso `ruff format --check`.
- [x] Keine Secrets oder API-Keys im Code — alle Fixtures synthetisch;
      `secret_guard --tracked --workspace` meldet `clean` (exit 0).
- [x] Keine nackten `dict` oder `Any` in öffentlichen Interfaces — der Katalog
      exportiert `TokenShape`, `tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` und `str`;
      mypy über 638 Dateien clean.
- [x] Failure-Pfade explizit behandelt — der Import des Katalogs ist bewusst
      **nicht** in ein `try/except` gehüllt: ein Guard, der bei fehlendem
      Katalog stillschweigend mit weniger Mustern weiterläuft, wäre schlimmer
      als einer, der laut abbricht.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` aktualisiert — nicht nötig, kein Interface nach außen geändert.

**Zusätzlich, weil es hier den Kern trifft:**

```
python -S -E scripts/secret_guard.py --tracked --workspace   clean (exit 0)
```

Das ist der eigentliche Beleg für „stdlib-only": ohne `site-packages` und ohne
Umgebungsvariablen läuft der Guard trotzdem durch. Wäre in die Importkette eine
Drittabhängigkeit geraten, wäre er hier gescheitert — im CI erst irgendwann
später, und dann als Ausfall der Secret-Wache selbst.

God-file-, Aggregate-Decomposition- und paper-audit-reader-Ratchet: clean.
`kai_preflight.sh`: `PREFLIGHT: PASS`.

---

## Risiken & Annahmen

- **Weitere Länge `{20,}` statt `{36}`.** Scheinbarer Widerspruch zur
  Vorsichtsregel im Modulkopf von `sanitization.py` („lieber ein verpasstes
  Geheimnis als Über-Redaction"). Der Widerspruch ist keiner: jene Regel wurde
  für das **präfixlose** 40-Zeichen-AWS-Muster geschrieben (Neo-F-004), das auf
  SHA-1-Hashes und Commit-IDs anschlägt. Hier trägt das Präfix die Trennschärfe.
  Belegt statt behauptet: ein Grenztest zeigt 19 Zeichen → kein Treffer,
  20 Zeichen → Treffer. Ohne diese Kontrolle könnte `{20,}` unbemerkt zu `{1,}`
  verrutschen.
- **Neue Import-Kante** `app.audit.sanitization` → `app.security.secret_patterns`.
  Zyklusfrei, weil `app/__init__.py` leer und `app/security/__init__.py` nur ein
  Docstring ist. Wer dort später Submodule importiert, bricht diese Annahme —
  mypy über den ganzen Baum würde es fangen.
- **Der Drift-Test ist bewusst streng** und wird fallen, sobald jemand ein
  GitHub-Muster woanders anlegt. Das ist der Zweck, nicht ein Nebeneffekt. Die
  Fehlermeldung nennt die Datei und verweist auf den Katalog.
- **Keine Rückwirkung auf Bestandsdaten.** Bereits geschriebene JSONL-Zeilen
  werden nicht nachträglich redigiert; der PR wirkt ab dem nächsten
  Schreibvorgang.
- **Der Drift-Test hat beim ersten Lauf gefeuert** (zwei Regex-Literale im
  Docstring des Guards). Behoben wurde die Ursache — umformuliert zu Prosa.
  Keine Baseline angehoben, kein Skip erweitert, keine Warnung unterdrückt.

---

## Nächste TODOs

- [ ] `slack_token` ist das zweite Default-Muster ohne Test. Beim Zählen der
      Abdeckung gefunden, gehört nicht zu diesem Vorfall — hier gemeldet statt
      stillschweigend miterledigt.
- [ ] #848 auf den dann aktuellen Mainline rebasen und die offenen Punkte
      P1-A/B/C schließen.

**Ausdrücklich geprüft und NICHT nötig:** `app/ai/` aus #850 ist keine zweite
Leck-Fläche. `app/ai/audit.py` schreibt über `record_llm_call` nur Zähler,
Modellnamen und eine geschlossene Fehler-Taxonomie — keine Prompt-Bodies, keine
Exception-Texte. Deshalb kein Sanitizer-Aufruf dort.

---

## Testbefehl

```bash
pytest tests/unit/test_secret_pattern_parity.py tests/unit/test_audit_sanitization.py tests/unit/test_secret_guard.py -v
python -S -E scripts/secret_guard.py --tracked --workspace --root .
```

author: chiaotung97
body:
# Description

This PR integrates **KDA (Kimi Delta Attention, a recurrent linear attention mechanism)** into MaxText end to end: the attention layer, the tokamax-backed Pallas TPU kernel, context parallelism (CP), and **decoder wiring via `attention_type='kda'`**. KDA updates its recurrent state with the Delta Rule:

```
S' = S * exp(g_t)
residual = v_t - k_t^T @ S'
S = S' + beta_t * k_t ⊗ residual
o_t = scale * q_t^T @ S
```

The layer follows the Megatron KDA reference and delegates kernel execution to tokamax's Pallas TPU implementation, keeping MaxText free of low-level kernel code.

## Key Changes

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `src/maxtext/layers/attention_kda.py` | New `KimiDeltaAttention` layer and `ShortConvolution`: QKV/beta/gate/output-gate projections, depthwise causal 1D convolution, SiLU activation, always-on QK L2 normalization, per-head RMSNorm + output gate, gate parameters `A_log` / `dt_bias` (matching the Megatron reference); also hosts `halo_exchange_for_conv` for CP |
| `src/maxtext/kernels/kda/` | New `chunk_kda` entry point + tokamax adapter: `[B,T,H,D]` ↔ `[H,B,T,D]` layout translation, lazy import of the KDA API, explicit `mosaic` implementation selection inside `shard_map` |
| `src/maxtext/common/common_types.py` | `AttentionType.KDA` |
| `src/maxtext/configs/types.py` | New `KdaAttention` config (`linear_conv_kernel_dim`, `use_kda_safe_gate`, `kda_lower_bound`, reserved `use_kda_lora`) + validators; `attention_type` Literal gains `"kda"`; `attention_type='kda'` with `scan_layers=true` is rejected at config time |
| `src/maxtext/configs/base.yml` | KDA flags registered; `attention_type` supported list |
| `src/maxtext/layers/nnx_decoders.py` | `NNXDecoderLayer` gains a per-layer `attention_type` override and a KDA branch: builds `KimiDeltaAttention` (no KV cache — recurrent state is carried by the kernel); non-KDA types are untouched |
| `tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py` | Layer/kernel/CP suite (see below) |
| `tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py` | Decoder-integration suite: config guards + a real-decoder training run |
| `docs/reference/kda_cp_support.md` | Design doc, linked into the Reference toctree |

## Using KDA

Select it like any other attention variant — this mirrors how `attention_type='mla'` is consumed:

```yaml
attention_type: kda
scan_layers: false        # required (KDA layers are not validated in scanned stacks yet)
use_kda_safe_gate: true   # recommended: bounded-decay gate, keeps the recurrence stable
kda_lower_bound: -5.0     # common choice, required in [-5, 0) when the safe gate is on
```

Notes:
- KDA always L2-normalizes Q/K — this is part of the KDA architecture (the Delta-Rule recurrence diverges with unbounded q/k), independent of the shared `use_qk_norm` flag which belongs to dot-product attention.
- `context_parallel_load_balance` is rejected with KDA+CP (token order is load-bearing for the recurrent state).
- KDA has no KV cache; autoregressive decoding is not implemented yet (raises a clear `NotImplementedError`). Train/prefill paths are supported.

## Context Parallelism Support

- The CP mesh axis is taken from `cfg.context_sharding` (default `"context"`; `"expert"` works for expert-as-context) and is threaded consistently through the conv halo exchange, the T-axis partition-spec injection, and `ContextParallelMetadata`
- Under CP without user segments, an all-ones segment tensor is synthesized outside `shard_map` so the kernel can always derive per-rank `cu_seqlens` / chain fields
- `ShortConvolution` pulls `kernel_size-1` left-context tokens from the previous CP rank via `ppermute` inside a dedicated `shard_map`; a clear `ValueError` guards the `kernel_size-1 > T_local` case (multi-rank receptive fields are not implemented)

## Tests and Validation

**Unit tests — 35 TPU tests + 23 CPU tests, all passing** (4×TPU v6e, 2026-09-04):

- Layer/kernel: forward/backward (activations + weights), determinism, padding, packed-segment isolation (cross-row and within-row), precision vs a pure-XLA recurrent reference (FP32/BF16, ULP-based fallback)
- CP: kernel-level equivalence parametrized CP=2/CP=4, CP backward, full-layer CP without segments (dummy synthesis path), **full-layer CP with real packed segments** (segment spanning the rank boundary + boundary exactly at the split; fwd + input/weight grads vs non-CP), oversized-halo rejection, load-balance rejection, CP metadata-missing refusal
- Composition: full-layer **Mosaic vs tokamax XLA reference parity** (same weights, fwd + grads)
- Kernel guards: `initial_state` / `output_final_state` rejected with clear errors
- Markers: `tpu_only` is applied per-test, so the pure config/pure-op tests also run in regular CPU CI

**Decoder integration** (`tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py`):

- CPU-runnable: config acceptance, `scan_layers` guard, dispatch of `NNXDecoderLayer` to `KimiDeltaAttention` (and unchanged default for other types)
- TPU: a real-decoder training run (`decoder_block=default`, 2 layers, delayed-copy task — i.i.d. tokens with `t[i] = t[i-delay]`, `delay=5` beyond the conv receptive field, so only the recurrent state can solve it; masked loss): **loss collapses from 5.28 to < 1.0 in 400 steps** through the actual decoder

### Reproducing

On a TPU host (Python ≥ 3.12; verified on 4×TPU v6e):

```bash
# 1. TPU-capable JAX (validation used JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1)
pip install "jax[tpu]" -f https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/libtpu_releases.html

# 2. MaxText with TPU dependencies
pip install -e <maxtext checkout>
pip install -r <maxtext checkout>/src/dependencies/requirements/generated_requirements/tpu-requirements.txt

# 3. tokamax with the KDA kernels — the KDA API has landed on openxla/tokamax
#    main but no release contains it yet; install from source:
git clone https://github.com/openxla/tokamax.git && pip install -e tokamax
#    (or the equivalent branch validated here: -b antgroup/kda-pallas-kernel, tip 939da5c)

# 4. Tests (kernel/CP tests are tpu_only and skip cleanly elsewhere)
pytest tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py -v
```

## Dependencies

- The KDA kernels come from [openxla/tokamax#1103](https://github.com/openxla/tokamax/pull/1103) (Kimi Delta Attention Pallas kernels, by @Fred33146). **Status**: the code has landed on openxla/tokamax `main` (signature-compatible with this PR's adapter, verified), but **no public tokamax release contains it yet**. MaxText's pin therefore cannot express the dependency; the adapter imports the KDA API lazily, so installs without it are unaffected until KDA is actually used (clear `ImportError` with instructions at that point). Once the first release ships, the `tokamax>=` pin and derived requirement files will be bumped.
- Validated with JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1

## Hardware / Shape Constraints (mosaic kernel)

The adapter selects the `"mosaic"` Pallas implementation explicitly (no silent fallback). Constraints — surfaced as clear `NotImplementedError`s from tokamax at bind time:

- TPU generation ≥ 6 (validated on v6e)
- Key dimension ≤ 256
- Under CP: key and value head dims must be multiples of 128
- Sequence length padded internally to a multiple of chunk size 64

## Known Limitations / Follow-ups

- Autoregressive/inference path not implemented (train/prefill only; AR raises a clear error)
- `initial_state` / `output_final_state` not yet supported (explicit `NotImplementedError`)
- `scan_layers` must be `false` with `attention_type='kda'` (scanned KDA stacks not validated yet)
- bf16 training-recipe tuning for KDA models (the integration test validates in fp32 with the safe gate)
- Hybrid per-layer KDA + softmax models (e.g. Ling-style interleaving) and a production KDA model config
- tokamax version pin bump once the first public release with the KDA API ships

# Checklist

- [x] I have performe

author: astro-han
body:
## Summary

Dependabot applies its default labels to every update PR because neither block in `.github/dependabot.yml` sets `labels`: `dependencies` plus a language label, `javascript` for npm and `github_actions` for github-actions. The `javascript` label exists only because of this default. It appears on dependabot PRs (36 PRs, 2 issues) and nothing else: no workflow filters on it and no maintainer uses it. The `github_actions` label does not exist in the repository at all.

This PR sets `labels: [dependencies]` on both the npm and github-actions blocks so dependabot stops applying language labels. `ignore`, `groups` and everything else are untouched.

The config change has to land first: deleting the `javascript` label today would only get it recreated by dependabot on its next update.

## Follow-up after merge

- [ ] A maintainer deletes the `javascript` label from the repository.

## Verification

- `npm run format` and `npm run lint` run clean (YAML is outside Biome's scope, so this only confirms no side effects).
- Dependabot behavior cannot be exercised locally. The `labels` key follows the documented `dependabot.yml` schema.

  - permanent repo-guard stays outside the product CI aggregator
  - component workflows remain available for existing push-main execution until #9
```

Trusted GovernanceGrant is in #88 and authorizes exactly these workflow paths. `allow_policy_relaxation` is empty.

The final `ci.yml` keeps its fail-closed result truth table inside the governance-owned workflow and self-tests that table at runtime before evaluating actual reusable-job results. `repo-guard` is not called or aggregated by `ci-required`.

Settings-level branch protection is not claimed here: #3 remains open until `main` separately requires `ci-required` and `repo-guard` and blocks direct push.

author: chozandrias76
body:
The Bash branch of the no-tmp-scripts guard could not tell a read from a write.
It asked two independent questions -- does an interpreter-ish word appear
ANYWHERE in the command, and does a /tmp path with a source extension appear
ANYWHERE else -- and denied when both were true. Neither question is about
direction, so reading data out of /tmp was indistinguishable from authoring a
script into it. Two commands measured today, both denied, both reads:

    python3 - <<'EOF' ... glob('/tmp/planner/*.js') ... open(p) ... EOF
    mkdir -p target/planner-bundle && cp -f /tmp/planner/*.js target/... && ls

The second is the worse one: it runs no interpreter at all. The alternation had
no word boundaries, so `bun` matched inside the substring "planner-bundle" and
the following `.*` walked to the /tmp path. The same trap was live for `cat`
inside "concatenate", `node` inside "node_modules", `tee` inside "committee".

Both halves are fixed by dropping the interpreter alternation entirely -- an
interpreter NAME carries no direction -- and binding a real write operator
directly to the path it writes: redirection, tee, -o/--output/-O, a cp/mv/
install destination that must be the LAST argument of its segment, and a
write-mode open()/write_text(). Each command word is anchored on both sides, so
a substring inside an unrelated word can no longer arm the rule, and the path
the decision names is now the one being written rather than the first one seen.

The Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit branch is untouched: those tools always
author the file they name, so no write test is needed there.

check.sh never ran this policy's unit tests -- the one policy whose tests it
omitted, and the one whose Bash branch has now been wrong twice (first inert
against `regex.find_n`, then over-firing on reads). Wired in.

Verified in the real cupcake WASM runtime, not just the OPA interpreter: both
false positives now allow, and redirect/cp/tee writes still come back with the

---
**Lingering-branch triage, 2026-09-03.** Branch was last pushed 2026-08-25 and is 260 commits behind `main`; it has never had a PR. Opened as a draft because the work is finished and self-contained (3 files, +173/-15, with the policy's first unit tests) and the bug it fixes is still live on `main` today -- this session hit it: authoring a helper script into the session scratchpad was denied by the Bash branch of the same guard.

Conflicts with current `main` in `scripts/check.sh` only (`git merge-tree`), i.e. the step-list append, which is a trivial resolution.

author: watus44
body:
Victor, on the annotated My Market screenshot: "Over the same rule elsewhere is so cryptic. We need to be a lot more precise here. What's the context? Is it because Montreal is a tier one city?"

It was cryptic because "elsewhere" named nothing. The multiplier is not measured against everywhere else; it is measured against exactly one thing, the rate card's own baseline row, which is the secondary-market tier.

```
before   You are in Montreal
         which pays 18.2% over the same role elsewhere

after    You are in Montreal, a top-paying metro
         which pays 18.2% more than the same role in a secondary market
```

The city line also says what kind of market the city is, which answers his third question without printing our internal label at somebody. "Tier1" is our word, not a seller's, and swapping one piece of jargon for another is not an improvement, so the four phrases say what each tier is.

The tier was already in the payload (`baseline.tier`, with `location.tier` as the fallback), so nothing new is computed or stored.

Consumed by the frontend's `EstimateExplained`; both repo pointers move with it.

body:
## What

Simplify the `frontend-pr-screenshot` skill to attach the screenshot directly to the PR comment instead of hosting it via a GitHub release.

## Why

[GitHub CLI 2.99.0](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-01-github-cli-media-in-issues-pull-requests-and-comments/) added a repeatable `--attach` flag to `gh pr comment` (and `gh issue comment`, `gh pr create`, etc.). It uploads a **local** image/video and rewrites the matching Markdown reference in the body in place — so we no longer need a public URL to embed a screenshot.

## Changes

- Replace the entire "Upload screenshot to a GitHub release" step with a single `gh pr comment --attach '/tmp/frontend-screenshot.png#App screenshot'`.
- Remove the now-unnecessary machinery: the dedicated `pr-screenshots` release, the per-PR file copy, `gh release upload`, the `releases/download/...` URL construction, and the `curl` verification.
- Drop the `REPO=$(gh repo view ...)` lookup (only used to build the release URL) and the `cp`/`mkdir` entries from `allowed-tools` (only used by the removed step).
- Net: 6 steps → 5, `+11 / -24` lines.

## Notes

- Requires `gh ≥ 2.99.0` (noted inline in the skill).
- The stale `pr-screenshots` release and tag created by the old flow have already been deleted.

author: lukidzi
body:
## Motivation

`xdsServer.dataplaneConfigurationRefreshInterval` defaulted to `1s`. The dataplane watchdog is a plain ticker with no event-driven fast path, so every connected proxy had its whole xDS snapshot rebuilt once a second regardless of whether anything changed. That is a constant CPU floor on the control plane that grows linearly with the number of proxies, and 1s is far more aggressive than any realistic propagation requirement.

Fixes #14948

## Implementation information

Default raised to `10s` in `DefaultXdsServerConfig()` and in `kuma-cp.defaults.yaml`, with the generated docs copy and the config golden file updated to match. `UPGRADE.md` gets a 3.0.0 entry stating the new worst-case propagation latency and how to restore the old value. `monitoringAssignmentServer.assignmentRefreshInterval` is left at `1s` — out of scope here.

Worst case for a mesh, policy, or service change to reach a proxy goes from 1s to 10s. E2E specs use a 30s default `Eventually` timeout, so there is headroom, but a spec that chains several config changes could get tighter. If that shows up in CI the fix is an explicit `KUMA_XDS_SERVER_DATAPLANE_CONFIGURATION_REFRESH_INTERVAL=1s` in the E2E framework env rather than walking the default back.

## Supporting documentation

- Issue: https://github.com/kumahq/kuma/issues/14948
- Watchdog: `pkg/xds/sync/dataplane_watchdog_factory.go`

body:
## Intent The developer wanted the `iOS Verify (Staging)` CI job cut from roughly 40 minutes to about 30 without modifying any test file, and wanted a hung run to conclude `failure` rather than `cancelled`. Working from a completed runtime audit as the source of truth, they specified five changes in one PR: step-level `timeout-minutes` plus a silence watchdog and per-test execution-time allowances in `scripts/ci/run-ios-test-passes.sh`; `-Onone`/single-file/dwarf/active-arch overrides passed only on the xcodebuild command line so the project's Staging configuration and TestFlight archives stay at `-O`; pre-booting the simulator during compile; replacing the zero-test enumeration run with `-only-testing:` groups plus one `-skip-testing:` remainder pass guarded by per-pass xcresult checks and a 1,900 executed-test floor; and resolving Mixpanel build settings once per job instead of three times. Constraints: don't touch the memory-grouping work a sibling worker was landing (rebase onto it and consume its isolated groups), keep the coverage baseline of 1,999 executed tests, keep the derived-data-path contract test and CLAUDE.md commands in sync, file rather than fix any test-coupling defects the new pass shape exposes, and back every claimed number with a named CI log or job timestamp read from the jobs API. Mid-task the developer asked the agent to stop using `rm -rf` (which triggers a permission prompt) in favor of `rm -r` or fresh paths. On the two escalated review-gate questions they decided to lower the `Run tests` step cap to 34 minutes and to approve the sibling-rebase note as informational, deleting the sibling's splitter test at rebase time while keeping its path-filter change. ## What Changed - The `ios` path filter in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now includes `scripts/ci/**` and `scripts/lib/**`, so a PR that only changes the scripts the iOS jobs run no longer routes as "not iOS" and skips `iOS Verify (Staging)` / `(Release)` - the hole that let #570's test-split change read green with the one job that could prove it never scheduled. - `scripts/test/ci-workflow-contracts.test.mjs` derives that coverage instead of restating it: it scans the required-check iOS job block for every `scripts/...` path referenced there and asserts each one is matched by the `ios` filter patterns, reusing `matchesAny` from `scripts/lib/required-check-routing.mjs`. Verified by two negative controls - deleting `scripts/ci/**` from the filter, and adding an iOS step that runs a script outside the covered globs - each of which fails the assertion by name. - Added `scripts/lib/ci-annotations.mjs` to the `remote_config` filter, since `report-kill-switch-changes.mjs` imports it and an edit to that module alone would have skipped `remote-config-verify` the same way. `.claude/skills/ascend-deploy/SKILL.md` records both the widened `ios` gate and the derived contract behind it. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: One added path-filter entry plus a CI-contract test assertion that reuses the existing glob matcher, passes against the current workflow, is guarded against vacuity, and can only fail closed. ## Testing Exercised the CI path-routing change end-to-end as the developer experiences it - which jobs GitHub schedules for a PR - rather than only as unit assertions. Real Actions history on PR #570 is the primary artifact: at head 3a42303d, with the old `ios` filter, a diff whose substantive files were `scripts/ci/run-ios-test-passes.sh` and `scripts/ci/split-enumerated-tests.mjs` had both iOS Verify jobs skipped and the run still concluded success; from head e067121d, the first push carrying `scripts/ci/**` and `scripts/lib/**`, both iOS jobs are scheduled. I reproduced that flip locally by replaying ci.yml's `ios` and `remote_config` filters at the base and target commits over that same real changed-file list, and proved the new derived contract test actually guards it with two negative controls - one dropping the filter entry, one wiring a script outside the filter into the iOS job, which failed with the intended explanatory message. Targeted Node suites (ci-workflow-contracts, ci-required-check-routing, and six adjacent CI script suites) all pass. This is a CI-routing change with no rendered user surface, so the artifacts are CLI transcripts and GitHub job outcomes rather than screenshots. Two things I could not close: the un-skipped `iOS Verify (Staging)` job was still in progress when testing finished, so its final conclusion is not in evidence, and `Functions Verify` on that run fails at `Audit dependencies` with a transient npm registry error unrelated to this diff. Transient artifacts (scripts/node_modules, temp copies) were removed; the worktree is clean.

author: hcekne
body:
Implements [`docs/next-development-actions.md`](docs/next-development-actions.md) in full, and
admits it as Phase 12 of the consecutive development plan.

## Why

The fixed fresh-eyes recipe from Phase 10.7 ran three times over snapshot 1058 with two providers
(Codex `gpt-5.6-terra`, Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, Claude `claude-fable-5-1`). The recipe worked. The
evidence around it did not:

- Claude usage was recorded as **2 input tokens per stage**, because the adapter ignored cached
  prompt tokens, so no cost or effort comparison between executors was possible.
- Earlier generations were reachable only by SQL. Status exposed one generation and a bare pointer.
- Nothing said whether a review came from a committed checkout. The whole experiment ran dirty.
- Nothing checked whether a recommendation still matched the code. One generation recommended a
  prepare route that already existed, and all three led with a hazard the source rules out.

This branch repairs that evidence layer. It adds no provider, scheduler, workflow engine, job kind,
dashboard journey, or MCP tool.

## What landed

**Confirmed defects and trust gaps (§12.1).** The 1 MB submission limit counts UTF-8 bytes as its
constant always promised. Two AI request builders share one target-file guard; stored module
identity uses the same function as fresh analysis, each behind an equality test written *before* the
refactor. The Claude executor accepts and forwards a reasoning effort and counts cached prompt
tokens. A second host worker is told `busy` rather than `complete` while a peer holds a review
stage. Proposal diversity is computed from executor family, so `cross_provider` can finally be true.
Claim, complete and fail writes are guarded by status and worker. Task-group failures surface their
leaf cause instead of `unhandled errors in a TaskGroup`. The fresh-eyes start timeout exceeds the
index busy window and says the service may still be planning. Every sidecar write-back retries lock
contention. MCP can request a rerun like the CLI. Additive columns reach an index opened at its
current version.

**Reproducible and comparable reviews (§12.2).** Schema 11 records cached and uncached prompt
tokens, an explicit usage state instead of one inferred from a zero, and the executor effort.
Generations are enumerable with per-stage wall time, output volume and attempts, and selectable by
number through REST, CLI, MCP and the dashboard. Every review and Charter names its checkout and
warns when it was dirty. Declared context reaches the comparison and mission-filter packets while
proposals and adjudication stay implementation-blind. A live scan bounds its own working-tree drift.
An unknown graph snapshot id fails loudly. The local `understand` path can plan without rescanning.
A non-loopback bind says what it exposes. The plan transaction's lock wait and hold are measured
before anyone proposes splitting it.

**Comparison without judgement (§12.3).** Two generations are aligned by deterministic lexical
signals into agreed, conflicting and unique recommendations, read side by side in the existing Fresh
eyes view, labelled `lexical` with the caveat that it cannot detect the same intent in different
words. Each recommendation carries a grounding report — confirmed, needs a test, already satisfied,
or stale — computed against the reviewed snapshot. A principal can refute an inferred Charter claim
without deleting the inferred evidence. One review can pin a different executor family per proposal
slot, with family-filtered claims, a named waiting state, an explicit unpin, and per-executor
background run slots.

## Two defects found while building this

- **Index compaction was silently wiping fresh-eyes job metadata on every index open**, ignoring the
  retention marker. That is why generation-1 jobs in the live index carry empty metadata, and it had
  been emptying `input_manifests` in the existing review payload. Fixed in `bfb44de`.
- A hand-resolved merge of mine dropped a closing brace in `fresh-eyes.css`, silently disabling nine
  rules. Caught and fixed before it shipped.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Python suite | **901 passed** (646 on `main`) |
| Total coverage | **93.2%** (floor 80%) |
| Changed-line coverage | **97.8%**, 1801/1841 lines (target 85%) |
| Deterministic self-analysis | **6 governed findings, 0 issues** |
| Module size / architecture / code quality | **0 errors** |
| Playwright dashboard contracts | **39 passed** |
| Complete quality gate | **passed** (`run_quality_gate.py --base origin/main`, incl. Docker sidecar smoke and benchmarks) |

Three self-analysis regressions this work introduced (a test-support import cycle and two functions
crossing the branch-count threshold) were **repaired, not accepted into the baseline**. When the last
item pushed two modules past the 500-line ceiling and three shared modules past the fan-in cap, the
answer was to extract `semantic_fresh_eyes_jobs.py` and `semantic_fresh_eyes_payload.py` and split
the stage fixtures from the two-executor harness — **no limit was raised to fit the work**.

The production-source ratchet is ratified from 58,346 to **62,746 lines** for 16 new production
modules, with the acceptance evidence recorded in the Phase 12 record.

## One thing left for you

Precondition P3 asks to commit or drop `docs/capabilities.md`, `docs/capabilities-brief.md` and the
uncommitted `examples/maxos-agent.anaxigraph.yml` semantic block. Those are your working files, so I
left them untouched and untracked; nothing in this branch depends on them. Note that the example's
`max_parallel_jobs: 1` would prevent two concurrent host workers, which the new cross-provider docs
say need 2 or more.

Deliberately **not** implemented, each with the evidence that would justify reopening it: an AI
adjudication job kind across generations, stable evidence identifiers, and feeding corrections into
Charter synthesis.

`files[]` and could look nothing up. That left grep-read-grep -- the research shape
this project needs most often -- reachable only through `delegate`, which can write
and therefore has to stop and ask in plan mode. The cheap, safe tool was the one that
could not do the work.

Offering it `read_file` and `search_files` is not a loosening, because the promise was
never what the empty list implied. ADR-0042 declared the tool read-only so a client
gating writes on that declaration could run it unattended; that claim is about what
the delegation can DO, not how many tools it holds. Neither tool can write.

`search_files` runs in the server process under the same four-layer path policy as a
read -- never the sandbox, since only `run_bash` is ever confined (ADR-0010). Matches
come back as a file name, the word `line`, and a number, so the model can read the
part it wants and cite it.

Three supporting pieces, each because reusing what existed would have been wrong:

`resolve_permitted` is the same four layers with the other disposition. `resolve_all`
refuses the whole call if any path fails, which is right for paths a caller NAMED --
six asked for and five returned reads exactly like six. It is wrong for candidates a
walk enumerated, where one declined file would fail the search. Two functions over one
policy rather than a flag, because the lenient one applied to a caller's path is a
silent drop.

`resolve_search_root` checks a directory against `workspace_roots`. `_one_path`
refuses a directory at layer 1, correctly, and `resolve_workdir` checks one against
`workdir_roots` -- a separable surface, governing a read-write sandbox bind rather
than what may be read.

`writes` on `RegisteredTool`, with the read-only set derived from it. A hand-kept list
is the shape this project keeps finding and naming a check that cannot fail: add a
writing tool, forget the list, and the annotation stays advertised while false.
Verified by injecting that exact mistake -- `write_file` with its declaration removed
fails four tests, one of them asserting the executor refuses a write.

Two things the tests found rather than review. The scope resolution used `_one_path`,
so `path` failed for the one argument shape the tool exists to accept; caught by
running in WSL, where the path tests execute rather than skip. And the gate blocked
the first draft of a test docstring that spelled out the name-colon-number shape in
order to explain why it is refused -- CLAUDE.md says the rule cannot show you the
shape it forbids, and the check proved that on a file arguing for it.

Costs accepted: a read-only delegation now spends turns and can hit `max_turns`,
which is why that became a per-call argument first and reaches this tool too. The
one-shot path is kept, not deleted -- `delegate` with an empty toolset is still the
honest shape when nothing needs looking up.

ADR-0048.

author: skaba89
body:
## Contexte

Suite du Lot 1 (`docs/21-FONDATIONS-ENTREPRISE-NIVEAU-2.md`, fusionné dans #49). Ce lot couvre le **premier point explicite de la section 5 (« Lot 2 ») de la mission « FODIP Digital 2030 vers le niveau SaaS entreprise critique »** : un rapport de couverture combiné (unit + intégration PostgreSQL/MinIO fusionnées en un seul rapport texte/LCOV/HTML/synthèse GitHub) avec des seuils anti-régression initiaux. Détail complet dans **`docs/22-COUVERTURE-COMBINEE.md`**.

**Explicitement hors périmètre de cette PR** (« jamais une PR géante ») : les cibles finales de couverture de la mission (80/80/75/75 %, 90/90 % modules financiers/RBAC), et les tests d'intégration supplémentaires listés par la mission (PME, agent, scoring, OIDC Keycloak réel, pannes simulées, etc.) — chacun en PR de suivi séparée une fois ce socle de reporting en place.

## Pourquoi

`apps/api/jest.config.cjs`'s `coverageThreshold` (posé au Lot 1) ne voit que la suite unitaire seule. Une ligne uniquement exercée par un vrai test d'intégration (ex : un conflit de contrainte unique sous verrouillage PostgreSQL réel) compte comme non couverte de son point de vue alors qu'elle l'est réellement. Jest n'a aucun mécanisme natif pour fusionner la couverture de deux invocations séparées (les suites unitaire et intégration sont des configs Jest distinctes, exprès).

## Ce qui change

- **Nouveau `apps/api/scripts/merge-coverage.js`** : fusionne les `coverage-final.json` bruts des deux suites via `istanbul-lib-coverage` (épinglé aux versions déjà résolues comme dépendances transitives de Jest — `pnpm-lock.yaml` : 9 insertions, 0 suppression, aucune nouvelle résolution), écrit `coverage-combined/` (text-summary/json-summary/lcov+html), ajoute une synthèse Markdown à `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, et applique un seuil anti-régression sur les nombres combinés.
- `apps/api/jest.integration.config.js` : collecte de couverture (`coverage-integration/`, dossier distinct pour ne jamais écraser celui de la suite unitaire).
- CI : `unit-tests` ajoute le reporter `json` (donnée brute) à sa collecte existante ; `integration-tests` lance désormais `--coverage`, relance la suite unitaire dans le même job (~15 s, négligeable à côté du démarrage Testcontainers déjà payé), fusionne, et uploade `coverage-combined/`. Fait dans ce job plutôt qu'un troisième job séparé : éviter d'introduire `actions/download-artifact`, sans SHA épinglé vérifié dans ce dépôt aujourd'hui.

## Bug réel trouvé et corrigé en cours de route

`pnpm --filter @fodip/api test:integration -- --coverage ...` (la même forme qui fonctionne pour le script `test` du job `unit-tests`) échoue silencieusement pour `test:integration` précisément : pnpm insère un `--` littéral supplémentaire avant les arguments transmis, que Jest interprète comme « tout ce qui suit est un motif de chemin de test » → `0 matches`. Reproduit localement (`--listTests`, avec ou sans `--filter`), non expliqué par le contenu des scripts — seul le nom change le comportement. Contourné avec `pnpm --filter @fodip/api exec jest ...`, qui bypasse la transmission d'arguments de pnpm — vérifié (58/58 tests, `coverage-final.json` produit correctement) avant utilisation dans le workflow.

## Tests ajoutés

8 tests unitaires (`apps/api/test/merge-coverage.spec.ts`) : fichier de couverture manquant → erreur explicite ; fichier vide → refusé plutôt que fusionné silencieusement ; **fusion réelle prouvée** (deux fixtures construites à la main, chacune ne couvrant qu'une des deux instructions d'un même fichier fictif → la fusion des deux donne bien 2/2) ; seuil anti-régression testé dans les deux sens (passe au plancher, rapporte chaque métrique en dessous par son nom, ne compte jamais `pct: "Unknown"` comme un succès).

## Résultats exacts

```
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile        → OK
pnpm audit --prod                     → No known vulnerabilities found
pnpm test:prepush                     → OK
pnpm --filter @fodip/api test         → 131/131 passed (24 suites, incl. les 8 nouveaux)
pnpm --filter @fodip/api test:integration → 58/58 passed
node scripts/merge-coverage.js        → Statements 74,57 % / Branches 56,38 % / Functions 56,1 % / Lines 75,87 % — seuil (74/55/55/75) respecté
pnpm lint                             → OK
tsc --noEmit                          → OK
pnpm --filter @fodip/api build        → OK
pnpm --filter @fodip/web build        → OK
docker compose config --quiet         → OK
```

Seuil vérifié dans les deux sens, pas supposé : élevé temporairement à 99 % → échoue avec le message attendu ; fichier de couverture d'intégration supprimé → erreur explicite, jamais un rapport partiel silencieux.

## Limitation

`docker compose up`/Testcontainers réels non exécutables dans ce bac à sable (registre Docker bloqué — limitation déjà documentée pour tous les lots précédents). Vérifié à la place : `docker compose config --quiet`, et la chaîne CI complète simulée localement (PostgreSQL natif + `s3rver` en substitut MinIO) dans l'ordre exact du job. Le job CI `integration-tests` de cette PR reste la vérification de référence.

## Prochaine PR recommandée

Tests d'intégration supplémentaires de la mission (section 5), un groupe cohérent à la fois (PME/agent/scoring d'abord, OIDC Keycloak réel ensuite). Lot 3 (refonte UI/UX) reste hors de portée tant que Lot 2 n'est pas validé.

author: kentqian
body:
## Background

The MIGraphX plugin EP wheel could not be installed and loaded reliably with ONNX Runtime 1.27:

- The wheel did not declare the separately packaged `migraphx-libs` dependency.
- `libmigraphx-ep.so` could not locate MIGraphX and ROCm libraries installed in sibling Python packages.
- During plugin detection, ONNX Runtime may load, unload, and reload the library. Unloading MIGraphX/LLVM caused duplicate LLVM initialization and a process abort.

## What changed

- Add `migraphx-libs` to the MIGraphX EP wheel dependencies.
- Add a build option to disable the `migraphx-libs` dependency when necessary.
- Set a site-packages-relative RUNPATH on the packaged `libmigraphx-ep.so`.
- Link the MIGraphX EP with `-z nodelete` on Linux to prevent unsafe unload/reload. (Cursor assisted)

## Validation

- Built and installed the wheel successfully.
- Verified the wheel dependency metadata and ELF RUNPATH.
- Verified that plugin registration and MIGraphX inference complete without the LLVM initialization core dump.

author: bmc08gt
body:
Follow-on to #717. Five fixes to the blur an edit holds past the context menu, and to how the edited message reads against it.

**The blur stopped at the composer.** Its background gradient clears at its own top edge and its controls are glass, so both sampled sharp transcript. Held, the blur now moves into the composer's superview just below the bar and fills it, so the transcript stays soft to the bottom of the screen.

**The floated copy vanished for about a second** on the way into an edit. The clip's bottom edge tracks the composer bar as the keyboard returns, and for a beat the copy's last reported frame sat below an edge that had already moved — `clipsToBounds` cut the whole thing away rather than trimming it. Its origin is now clamped so it hugs the composer for that beat instead.

**A swipe-back carried the screen away mid-edit.** The blur and the copy are hosted by the navigation stack, so they survived the pop and sat on whatever screen it landed on, eating taps with nothing left to dismiss them. Every enabled pop pan on the navigation view is suspended for the length of an edit and exactly those restored — every pan, because a sheet-hosted stack carries a second one and it is the untouched twin that pops.

**The backdrop read as near-black:** a full-strength material on a 0.48 dim chosen to match the menu's dimming exactly. Android frosts the same screen with a 25dp Haze and no scrim, which is the target. `UIBlurEffect` exposes no radius, so the effect goes on through a `UIViewPropertyAnimator` paused at 0.4, and the dim drops to 0.2. One consequence: an edit is now lighter than the menu it comes from, so there is a slight brightening as the menu gives way — the menu's dimming is UIKit's and can't be lightened to meet it.

**The same message rendered three different ways.** A bubble's fill was translucent white, so it took the colour of whatever sat behind it, and that is not always the transcript: measured rgb 43 in the transcript, 34 under the menu, 57 in an edit. It now carries its own ground — an opaque base with the wash composited over it in its own layer — and reads 43 in all three.

Neither lifted state cast a shadow either. A `UITargetedPreview` with a clear background casts nothing, with or without `shadowPath`, so the dimmed transcript sat flat at rgb 17 right up to the lifted bubble's edge. The elevation is now set explicitly and shared by the menu's lift and the edit's floated copy, and taken off again when the menu goes so a recycled cell can't carry it back into the transcript.

author: colemurray
body:
## Summary

Roadmap **P-4 / COL-85** (Control plane on AWS, epic E1, milestone M0). No dependencies; unblocks N-9 (the in-process runtime client) and P-5 (the `Env` split).

`SessionRuntimeClient` is the port that hides how the Worker reaches a session runtime. Five call sites bypassed it and used `env.SESSION`, a Durable Object namespace that exists only on Cloudflare. Each is now a call through the port. No behavior change.

### What changed

- **Abandoned-draft sweep** (`session/abandoned-draft-sweep.ts`, `index.ts`): `SessionDraftExpiryClient` takes a `SessionRuntimeClient` and posts `expireDraft` through it, keeping the per-request timeout and the 404-means-missing contract. The cron entry builds the client with a fresh correlation id.
- **Scheduler prompt enqueue** (`scheduler/scheduler.ts`): `enqueueSessionPrompt` uses the client with the run's correlation context (`automation:<id>` / run id) and the typed `SessionInternalPaths.prompt` instead of a hand-built stub and URL string.
- **Session initialization** (`session/initialize.ts`): `/internal/init` goes through the client, which sets the trace and request headers the function used to set by hand.
- **Child-to-parent status rollup** (`session/session-status-service.ts`, `session/components.ts`): the service takes a `SessionRuntimeClient` from the composition root, correlated to the child's object id, and the parameter is no longer nullable. `env.SESSION ?? null` is gone from the root.
- **GitHub webhook** (`webhooks/github.ts`): the `if (!env.SESSION) return;` guard is dropped; the binding is non-optional in `Env`.
- **Kept by design**: the worker-level WebSocket forward in `index.ts` still resolves the object directly, with a note. The 101 must carry the object's own `webSocket`, which only that Cloudflare-side hop can return.

### Done when

- [x] `grep -n "env.SESSION\|\.SESSION\b" packages/control-plane/src` → only `src/index.ts` (the WebSocket forward) and `session/runtime-client.ts`, plus `types.ts` until P-5 and one test-support fixture.
- [x] Existing tests for the draft sweep, scheduler prompt enqueue, initialize, and child-status flows pass. The scheduler and initialize tests pass unchanged (their `env.SESSION` fakes are reached through the client); the draft-sweep and status-service tests now fake the client directly and assert the session id, path, and init.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck -w @open-inspect/control-plane`: clean
- Unit: 3,646 tests pass
- Workerd integration: full suite green

Closes COL-85.

// app/App.js

author: jimmycallin
body:
## Problem

Each published package had four tsconfigs: a `tsconfig.json` solution referencing `src` and `test`, a `tsconfig.build.json` solution referencing only `src`, the `src/tsconfig.json` that actually emitted, and `test/tsconfig.json`. The root had two, `tsconfig.base.json` and `tsconfig.build.json`, which disagreed on `target` and `noUnusedParameters`. Which root config governed a package's emit depended on what its `src/tsconfig.json` happened to extend. That produced a set of bugs nobody could see from any single file:

1. **Inconsistent published output.** Only core's `src/tsconfig.json` extended the root `tsconfig.build.json`, so core emitted `esnext` with declaration maps. The other 14 extended `tsconfig.base.json` and emitted ES2018 with JS source maps. (Every package's own `tsconfig.build.json` extended the root one too, but those are solution files with no sources, so it changed nothing.)
2. **`tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` is published.** TypeScript places the build-info file under `outDir` at the config's position relative to `rootDir`. With the emitting config inside `src/` that is `lib/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, and `files` publishes `lib/`. On npm, 6.8.0 of `@rjsf/antd` carries a 446 kB `tsbuildinfo` in a 959 kB package; `@rjsf/mui` 265 kB of 856 kB.
3. **Tests were never typechecked.** CI only ran `tsc` on `src`. Vitest strips types without checking them, so the 15 `test/tsconfig.json` files were editor-only.
4. **The root solution was wrong.** It referenced `snapshot-tests` twice and omitted `mantine`, `primereact`, `validator-ata` and `validator-cfworker`.
5. **Chakra's `type-check` checked nothing.** `tsc --noEmit` resolved to a solution config with `files: []`.
6. **Libraries saw every hoisted `@types/*` package**, so library code could compile against Node globals it must not use.
7. **Bloated reference graph.** Source projects referenced their dependencies' `tsconfig.json` solutions, which include the test project, so building core pulled `utils/test` and `validator-ajv8/test` into its graph.

## Fix

One source project per package at `packages/<name>/tsconfig.json`, one test project at `packages/<name>/test/tsconfig.json` extending a shared root `tsconfig.test.json`, and one root `tsconfig.base.json` with one deliberate value per option. The root solution lists every source and test project once, and a root `typecheck` script (`tsc --build`) runs in CI.

Decisions made along the way:

- **Target is `esnext`.** Every theme depends on core, and core already shipped `esnext`, so consumers already had to run it. Core's `lib/*.js` is byte-identical to main apart from a new `sourceMappingURL` trailer. Of the others measured, utils, mui and antd shrink 1–4% and validator-ajv8 grows 0.4%.
- **All packages ship `.js.map` and `.d.ts.map`.** Source is published, so both resolve.
- **`"types": []` in the base.** Packages that use Node APIs opt in.
- **`verbatimModuleSyntax` on.** Zero cost: the source already used `import type` wherever required (oxlint's `consistent-type-imports` enforces it). The one import it would have stopped eliding, `import React` in utils' `shouldRender.ts`, is used only as a type and is now `import type`, so emitted output is unchanged.
- **Validators compile without the `DOM` lib.** `@rjsf/validator-ajv8`, `-ata` and `-cfworker` override `lib` to `["ESNext"]`, so a validator cannot accidentally depend on browser globals.
- **`build:ts` is plain `tsc -b`.** The old `rimraf ./lib` only guarded against stale outputs from renamed or deleted sources, which cannot reach a release because CI builds from a fresh checkout. It also forced deleting `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, since TypeScript trusts the build-info over the presence of outputs ([microsoft/TypeScript#50646](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/50646), Working as Intended), so every build was a full rebuild. `--force` is not a substitute: it rebuilds every referenced project too (building mui rebuilds utils, validator-ajv8 and core), which races under Nx's parallel builds. The build-info is now an Nx `build` output next to `lib/`, so a cache restore keeps the incremental state coherent.

Typechecking tests for the first time surfaced stale tests, which are fixed here: chakra's test wrapper passed a prop `EnvironmentProvider` does not have, `validator-ata`'s test passed an AJV-only option its validator silently ignores, antd and shadcn used jest-dom matchers without their types, and two playground samples had drifted from the core API.

## Effect

Same machine and run, clean outputs before each cold build. Main is `e0f36c943`.

| | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| tsconfig files / lines | 66 / 1173 | 36 / 447 |
| projects in `tsc -b packages/core` graph | 14 | 6 |
| `tsc -b packages/core`, cold | 6.1 s | 2.9 s |
| all 16 source projects, cold | 18.5 s | 15.4 s |
| root `tsc --build` (now includes tests) | red | green |
| `@rjsf/antd` tarball | 130 kB | 45 kB |
| `@rjsf/mui` tarball | 104 kB | 57 kB |
| `@rjsf/utils` tarball | 280 kB | 279 kB |
| `@rjsf/core` tarball | 194 kB | 208 kB |

Core grows because it gains the `.js.map` files the other packages already shipped, minus its 60 kB `tsbuildinfo`. `dist/` is untouched.

## Next steps

Each of these builds on the topology in this PR and is kept separate so it can be reviewed on its own merits. Items 2, 3 and 5 are where this setup still deviates from current guidance (the [TypeScript handbook's library recommendations](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/guides/choosing-compiler-options.html), the `tsc --init` defaults since 5.9, and [Nx's project-references setup](https://nx.dev/docs/technologies/typescript/guides/switch-to-workspaces-project-references)).

1. **Let tsdown emit JavaScript; `tsc` emits only declarations.** Today `tsc -b` produces `lib/*.js` file by file while esbuild and rollup produce the `dist/` bundles from the same source, so two toolchains have to agree on target and module settings. Moving all JavaScript emit to tsdown leaves `tsc` as the typechecker and declaration emitter only, which also turns the root `typecheck` into the `tsc --build --emitDeclarationOnly` shape Nx infers. Config cost after this PR: `emitDeclarationOnly: true` in `tsconfig.base.json`, one line. It cannot land here because until tsdown is wired up nothing else produces `lib/*.js`.
2. **Check published ESM with Node's module rules (`module: nodenext`).** The handbook calls `moduleResolution: bundler` "infectious" for libraries: it accepts specifiers Node rejects, so `tsc` cannot tell us when `lib/` is unloadable by Node. Trying it already found three shipped defects: `@rjsf/react-bootstrap` imports `react-bootstrap/Col` and an extensionless icon path, so Node cannot load its `lib/index.js` at all; `@rjsf/antd` imports the directory `antd/es/select`; and `@rjsf/validator-ajv8` default-imports AJV whose declarations disagree with its CommonJS runtime shape. Config cost is a few lines (the base plus `bundler` overrides for tests, the playground and chakra-ui, whose own declarations are not Node-resolvable). The source fixes are the real content and deserve their own review.
3. **Turn on `erasableSyntaxOnly`.** This is the flag that actually delivers the spec's "runnable under Node's native type stripping" goal by rejecting enums, namespaces and parameter properties. Enabling it today produces exactly four errors, all exported enums: `TranslatableString` and `AdditionalItemsHandling` in `@rjsf/utils`, `GridType` and `Operators` in `@rjsf/core`. Replacing them with `as const` objects changes public types, so it needs its own changelog entry and review.
4. **Move the shared test helpers in `packages/utils/test` into a package export.** The validator packages' tests import them, which is why `utils/test/tsconfig.json` is the one test project that still emits (declarations into `lib-test`) and why validator test projects reference another package's tests. Nx's recipe for this is a `./testing` subpath in the pac

author: vibeatscoder
body:
Minor bump: two defaults changed in ways an operator will notice.

**The forest is scored on the origin.** Not one of the 935 legitimate training rows carries a URL path while 153 of 845 phishing rows do, so it had learned the collection artifact and flagged every subpage of every legitimate site. On identical HTML: `aparat.com/` 0.074 vs `aparat.com/home` 0.962. Live: aparat 0.963 → 0.084, namava 0.952 → 0.081.

**eNamad verification is on**, having never run once. The badge is absent from server HTML but present in the rendered DOM — digikala, alibaba, tapsi, sheypoor and zarinpal all expose one, and 3 of 10 currently-abstaining sites carry a verifiable seal. A breaker stops asking an unroutable registry, so enabling it costs three timeouts per cooldown rather than one per review.

### The one-liner is now genuinely one line

`install.sh` finds a token where the machine already keeps one: exported `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` → `gh auth token` → git's credential helper → an export in a shell profile.

Profiles are read with `sed`, **never sourced**. A value that is a variable reference is skipped — a profile commonly holds both the real token *and* `export GH_TOKEN="$GITHUB_TOKEN"`, and taking the last match handed back that literal string, failing as a 401 that looks like a bad token rather than a parsing mistake. `NO_TOKEN_DISCOVERY=1` opts out.

Also here: the images compose references the tags releases actually publish, checksum verification is opt-in rather than a hard stop, and `scripts/evaluate_persian_clear_rate.py` measures the clear rate against 281 live Iranian commercial sites instead of the academic corpus the threshold was tuned on.

author: simplykryssie-blip
body:
## Summary
The real cause of "Flag as Needs Info" not opening its note box: `busy` was computed as
`busyItemId === "field:instance" || busyItemId === item.infoRequestItemId`. For any question that had never been flagged, `infoRequestItemId` is `null`, and at rest (nothing in flight) `busyItemId` is also `null` -- so `null === null` evaluated `true`, making `busy` true and the button disabled from page load, for every never-flagged question, everywhere. Clicking a disabled button does nothing: no note box, no error, no feedback -- exactly the reported symptom.

Fixed both occurrences (the plain-question list and the repeating-section list) by only comparing against `infoRequestItemId` when `busyItemId` is actually non-null.

This is a separate, more fundamental bug than the hidden-question one fixed in PR #187 -- that one only affected conditionally-hidden questions; this one affected every question, always.

- [x] `npx eslint` on the changed file

body:
# Session 3 - Shell Scripting

**Name:** Pratyush Mishra
**Roll Number:** 10486

## Task: System Information Script

Write a shell script that:

- Prints the current date.
- Prints the hostname.
- Prints the username.
- Prints the disk usage.
- Prints the running processes.
- Uses variables to store and use data.
- Takes user input using `read -p`.
- Creates a directory using `mkdir`.
- Creates a file using `touch`.
- Stores the running processes information in the file using `>` output redirection.

---

## Submission

Script and write-up are in `session3-shell-scripting/tasks/`  - 
[README.md](session3-shell-scripting/tasks/README.md) has the requirement-to-code
table, the script, terminal screenshots and the explanations.

| Requirement | In the script |
|---|---|
| Current date | `current_date=$(date)` |
| Hostname | `host_name=$(hostname)` |
| Username | `user_name=$(whoami)` |
| Disk usage | `df -h` |
| Running processes | `ps` on screen, `ps aux` into the file |
| Variables | nine, including the three captured by command substitution |
| `read -p` | five prompts |
| `mkdir` | `mkdir -p "$dir_name"` |
| `touch` | `touch "$dir_name/$file_name"` |
| `>` redirection | `ps aux > "$dir_name/$file_name"` |

Blank answers to the directory and filename prompts fall back to defaults via
`${var:-default}`, so pressing ENTER can't collapse the path into a directory.

Run on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (WSL2).
