## Summary

Spike 3 structural raster-guard extension (tsp-op5a.382) — closes the three honesty gaps between the plan's structural guard list and what launcher HEAD actually enforced. No frame-hash literals changed and no baseline records were regenerated (the rebaseline set stays empty), per the coordinator ruling.

- **Gap 1 — frame-hash rebaseline had no structural precondition.** All three frame-hash tests now build their offscreen command through one shared `frame_hash_command` helper that always sets `PF_RASTER_INK_GUARD=1`, so an expected-digest update can no longer land without containment / occlusion / target-size firing on the same command. A unit test asserts every frame-hash command carries the env var.
- **Gap 2 — minimum focus/touch target size was not enforced in production.** New `assert_focusable_targets_meet_minimum_size` in the `raster_guard_record` chain requires every actionable node's target box to meet the 48px minimum — now a single shared source of truth (`pf_shell_core::MIN_TARGET_SIZE_PX`) used by both the production guard and the Taffy spike's `validate_geometry`. **The guard's first full sweep FOUND nineteen real sub-minimum targets at 100% scale**, across three routes: Library toolbar/chips (5, 44px), Quick overlay rows (6, 40px), and Search result rows (8, 44px). Per the coordinator ruling these are handled as a **documented-baseline gate** (the same mechanism as Gap 3): the known owner-gated sub-minimum targets are documented in the guard, and the guard FAILS on any sub-minimum actionable node not matched by the documented set — a new route, a new control, a changed height, or a count excess — so regressions fail while known state is documented, never suppressed. Library and Quick are keyed by stable exact node ids; Search is keyed by control class (id prefix `search-result-` + height 44 + exactly 8 rows) so a fixture slug rename passes untouched while a ninth row or a changed height fails. The whole 19-target set is owner-gated (shipped look vs the D011 mockups) and tracked in tsp-op5a.387, which ratifies/parameterizes the minimum and removes the documented entries.
- **Gap 3 — committed baseline records could be FAIL.** `committed_baseline_records_have_raster_guard_outcomes` now rejects any committed record that is not PASS, unless its path is in an explicit frozen legacy-failure allowlist enumerating exactly the nine pre-Taffy Spike 0/1 documentation captures (each entry pinned to its documented failing node id). author: h1994st
body:
Closes #62, #63, #64.

One theme: **rllvm becomes a real drop-in replacement for `gclang`.**

### #63 — usable directly as `CC`

`CC=rllvm-cc ./configure && make` now works with no shim script. Previously every user needed `exec rllvm-cc -- "$@"` for the most basic invocation there is.

The wrapper's own options are long-only and prefixed `--rllvm-`, so they cannot collide with a compiler flag. Everything else reaches the compiler, including `-c`, `-v`, `--help` and `--version`.

That last part is the subtle half. CMake and autoconf identify the compiler by running `$CC --version`; if clap answered it, they would misidentify the toolchain — a failure that looks nothing like an argument-parsing bug. clap's built-in help/version flags are disabled and re-exposed as `--rllvm-help` / `--rllvm-version`.

`--` still works, so existing shim scripts keep working.

**Breaking:** `-c` and `-v` now belong to the compiler. Use `--rllvm-compiler` and `--rllvm-verbose`. Because there is no short form to spare, verbosity takes a level (`--rllvm-verbose=3`) rather than repetition; `require_equals` keeps the bare form from swallowing the next compiler argument, which is covered by a test.

### #64 — relocatable bitcode paths

Objects recorded an absolute bitcode path, pinning them to the directory that built them. That breaks under `mv`, when artifacts are copied out of a container, when a compiler cache replays an object into a different tree, and when CI hands objects to another job.

Setting `RLLVM_BITCODE_ROOT` (or `bitcode_root` in the config) records paths relative to that root; `rllvm-get-bc --bitcode-root` supplies it again at extraction.

Opt-in and back-compatible: without a root, paths stay absolute, and the extractor tells the two forms apart by the leading separator — so both can appear in the same binary with no version marker.

This is the one change that puts rllvm ahead of gllvm/wllvm rather than at parity; both of those embed absolute paths.

### #62 — `rllvm-init` ignores `RLLVM_CONFIG`

It hardcoded `~/.rllvm/config.toml`, so it could report writing a config the rest of the toolchain would never read, while silently overwriting the real one.

Fixed by extracting the path decision into `config::config_filepath()` and having both the loader and `rllvm-init` call it, so they cannot drift apart again. An explicit `-o` still wins.

### Tests

59 → 68. Every new test was confirmed to fail before its fix, including the relocation pair, where the negative control asserts that absolute paths **do** break under `mv` — without it the positive test would be vacuous.

### Not included

No performance work. The 2× clean-build cost is inherent to the approach and shared with gllvm/wllvm; see #51 for why the apparent cheap wins do not address it.

author: kallb123
body:
Fires Out! was the only `available` game with a board screen but no game guide. This adds one, refreshes its share card, and closes the wiring/documentation gap around the guide registry.

## The guide

`src/games/FiresOut/guide.ts` + one line in `GAME_GUIDES`, then the same six lines every other guided board uses: `useGameGuide('firesout')`, a `key: 'guide'` options row between "Show last recap" and "End game", and `{gameGuide.open && <GameGuideModal …/>}`.

Five sections, `Goal` then `Your turn` — all six existing guides are exactly that shape. Every figure is checked against the code rather than the GDD prose (`VICTIMS_TO_WIN`, `VICTIMS_LOST_TO_LOSE`, `DAMAGE_TO_COLLAPSE`, `AP_PER_TURN`, `MAX_BANKED_AP`, the `AP_COSTS` table, the 10/5 POI split). Two things a first review caught, both now in the guide because they're what a new crew gets wrong:

- **A wall takes two chops to open, not one.** `applyChop` places one damage marker and an edge only opens at `damage === 2`, so a way through is 4 AP.
- **Your own chopping spends the collapse budget.** `isBuildingCollapsed` sums damage across *all* edges, player-made included, against the same 24 the Goal section names. That coupling is the game's central tension.

It also splits the two rulesets honestly. In the Family game `isRescuePoint` is true for any exterior space, so a knock-down while carrying actually *completes* the rescue (`deliverCarried` runs on every knocked-down firefighter) — an earlier draft had this backwards. Only in the Experienced game, where the ambulance is the sole rescue point, does the victim still have to be walked out. Likewise the Experienced difference isn't "the building starts burning" (the Family game has ten printed fire markers too) but that the fire comes from explosions rolled at setup that damage walls before anyone moves, plus the difficulty tier.

## Share card

`npm run icons` redraws `public/icons/og-game-firesout.png`. Worth explaining, since the picture looks the same:

The script skips share cards unless Bricolage Grotesque is installed as a system font, which it wasn't here — so the font was built from the `@fontsource` package and installed before running. With it in place **eight of the ten cards came back byte-identical** to what's committed, which is only possible if this environment rasterises the same font as whatever produced them. Of the two that changed:

- `og-game-firesout.png` differs in *every* text region **including the shared "Async Games" wordmark**, which is drawn identically on all ten cards. So the committed card was rendered with a different Bricolage build than its nine siblings. The regenerated one is in line with the set. **Included.**
- `og-game-snakesandladders.png` differs *only* inside its `1→100` glyph plate, with all text byte-identical. No Bricolage subset contains U+2192, so that arrow comes from a system fallback that varies per container — not staleness. **Reverted, deliberately.**

The board art (`public/art/fires-out/board.png`) was already present and correctly wired into `ag-theme.css`; nothing needed doing there.

## E2E — a CI failure this would otherwise have introduced

The guide auto-shows once per account, and a Bootstrap modal backdrop swallows clicks underneath it. `firesout-turns.spec.ts` is the **first signed-in turn spec for a game that has a guide** (Snakes & Ladders and Solitaire have none; the Outbreak spec is a signed-out guest, whose `/api/gameguides` call never marks it unseen), so no existing spec had to handle this. It would have failed on the first PR run twice over: on the board clicks, and on `getByText('Fires Out!')` matching the guide's own title as a second element.

Rather than a second local copy, the `/api/gameguides` settle and the dismiss-if-shown step moved into `e2e/helpers.ts` as `gameGuideResponse` / `dismissGuideIfShown`, now shared with `game-guides.spec.ts` (which also stops naming the "Got it" label in a second place). The dismiss waits a beat for React to render rather than reading the screen the instant the fetch response lands — `gameGuideResponse` resolves before `useGameGuide`'s `.then` has run, and the turn spec has nothing awaited in between to absorb that tick.

Fires Out is also added to `game-guides.spec.ts`'s coverage list. Note Outbreak isn't in it either, so this is coverage rather than required wiring — happy to drop the line if you'd rather not spend the CI minute.

## The unguarded registry

`GAME_GUIDES` was the one registry a game folder joins with nothing checking it. The failure is quiet and quite bad: a game shipping a `guide.ts` but missing from the record still *shows* its guide (the board imports it directly), while `/api/gameguides` validates with `body.game in GAME_GUIDES` and rejects the "seen" write — so the popup re-shows on **every single visit**, forever.

Adds the opt-in guard test beside the existing recap-adapter one (verified it fails, naming the exact import line to add, when the registry entry is removed). With a guard behind it, the registry now also appears in ARCHITECTURE.md §12's "what guards each" table, in `docs/new-game.md`'s wiring table and UI section, and in AGENTS.md's new-game paragraph — none of which mentioned guides at all.

## No "What's new" line

Fires Out has never shipped (`origin/main` has no `src/games/FiresOut`), so per AGENTS.md this stays inside the single New games entry the parent branch already carries. Adding a second line would have evicted a shipped feature players can still see.

## Reviewed

`caveman` (twice — app wiring, then the e2e extraction) and `rulebook`. Every finding above the "judgement call" line is fixed; the guide's chop, knock-down and Experienced-setup corrections and both e2e fixes came from those passes.

`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings 0`), `npm test` (1255 passing, +1 for the new guard) and `npm run build` all clean; `npx playwright test --list` collects all 11 specs.

# Pull Request

Thanks for wanting to improve Open WebUI. The most useful contribution is usually a clear, well-written Issue, not an unsolicited code pull request.

Open a code pull request only when a maintainer asks for one, or when the change is only i18n/localization. For real, reproducible bugs, start with a well-described [Issue](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues). For feature requests, UI/UX changes, behavior changes, architecture changes, suspected fixes, or unconfirmed approaches, start with an active [Discussion](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions).

Before continuing, make sure the linked Issue or Discussion explains the user-facing problem, the expected outcome, the affected workflow, and any examples, logs, screenshots, constraints, or reproduction details needed for maintainers to evaluate it.

If you have implementation notes, include them as reference in the Issue or Discussion. If you want to share code as reference, include it there as a local diff, patch, or branch note. Do not open a pull request for reference code.

Unsolicited PRs may be closed without review, especially when they introduce product, architecture, compatibility, dependency, or maintenance decisions that have not been discussed.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR targets the `dev` branch.

- [x] A maintainer explicitly asked me to open this PR, or this PR only updates i18n/localization.
- [x] The change is one logical unit with no unrelated commits.
- [x] I matched nearby code patterns and avoided unnecessary new settings, abstractions, or dependencies.
- [x] I manually tested the changed workflow and any nearby behavior that could be affected.
- [x] I updated relevant docs, including the [Open WebUI Docs Repository](https://github.com/open-webui/docs), if needed.
- [x] I added screenshots for UI changes, and a recording when motion or interaction matters.
- [x] I reviewed any AI-generated code before submitting it.
- [x] The PR title uses one of the prefixes listed below.

## Title Prefix

Use one of the following prefixes:

- **BREAKING CHANGE**: Changes affecting backward compatibility
- **build**: Build system or dependency changes
- **ci**: CI/CD workflow changes
- **chore**: Refactoring, cleanup, or non-functional changes
- **docs**: Documentation additions or updates
- **feat**: New features or enhancements
- **fix**: Bug fixes or corrections
- **i18n**: Internationalization or localization changes
- **perf**: Performance improvements
- **refactor**: Code restructuring

## Summary

Added missing translations.

author: kemetra
body:
## Summary

**OWNER DECISION filed, not taken.** `#361` recorded U1's next actionable task as drafting an `RRA-010` amendment for "journey adoption of the component layer". Drafting it began by asking what a `/beta` page would then *do*, and the tree answers: nothing.

- **No journey page renders anything the component layer presents.** `RRA-012`'s seven components present bundle properties — governed figures, section states, citations, formula versions, coverage identity. The five `/beta` steps render an intake form, `RRA-003` admission states (already worded in `JOURNEY_COPY`), a job state, artifact links, and a terminal message. Table in the document.
- **The macros could not render there even with the data.** Every journey state is fetched by JavaScript after the page is served; the macros are server-side Jinja over a bundle at materialization time. Adoption means either a JavaScript rebuild of the markup (the "fourth hand-built block" `RRA-012` exists to prevent) or page routes reading session state at render time (`RRA-010` excludes it as a backend change presented as UI).
- **The only real consumer is `R8-10`, and its data side is met.** The web report opens with the quality summary since `#350`; the report step links it before the downloads. What remains is presentation — equal cards — which active `RRA-010` already authorizes.

## The question and the three answers

Should `RRA-010` be amended so a `/beta` page loads the component stylesheet and renders bundle state through the layer?

- **A. No amendment** — recommended. `R8-10`'s journey half becomes a bounded `RRA-010` presentation slice on the report step. Forecloses nothing.
- **B. Admit one asset and one read**, rendering the quality summary in JavaScript. Lifts three `RRA-010` exclusions, moves component CSS out of `report.css` (an `RRA-012` Scope change), and creates a second rendering path for the summary.
- **C. Server-render the report step** through the macros. Right shape if the journey ever becomes server-rendered; wrong to do for one summary.

## What changes here regardless

The U1 row of roadmap §16 records the finding, points at the filing, and **keeps the amendment pending on U1's path until the owner answers** (review fix). The R8 row records `R8-10`'s journey half merged at `#363` and the attachment finding it surfaced: every surface, the web report included, is served `Content-Disposition: attachment` (`report_api.py:562`) — whether the HTML surfaces should be inline is an `RRA-006` reading for you. No specification is touched. `RRA-012`'s Scope note 1 and precondition 4 stay accurate as written — they say adoption *would need* an `RRA-010` slice, not that one is owed.

## Test plan

- [x] `khepri-gov validate`, `ruff check` — green locally
- [x] Docs only; no test reads either file

author: stephenberry
body:
Reading doubles goes from 58% to 87% of Glaze's speed on the benchmark documents, mixed documents from 78% to over 100%, and signed integers, bools and strings move up with them. String writing goes from 91% to 94%.

- The float reader is inlined into the array loop rather than called per element, and out-of-line helpers take the cursor by value so it stays in a register.
- Digits are folded a word at a time through one shared `fold_digits`, used by both the integer and float scanners. Integers of up to fifteen digits stay on the inlined path.
- Signs and bools are read without a branch on the data.
- Strings are copied as they are scanned.
- The float scanner is checked bit for bit against the standard library on 200,000 generated literals in the new `tests/atof.rs`.

Output and accepted input are unchanged. `docs/performance.md` carries the measurements and mechanisms.

author: timothyyao
body: ## Summary Two entity-info / rates quality display bugs from #25: 1. **Legendary outputs never appeared** in the item detail (entity info) panel — even on Per hour. 2. **Quality recipes** showed quality badges on outputs but not on ingredients. ## Causes `qualitySplitResults` rounded each tier’s per-second amount to 3 decimals, then dropped anything `< 0.0005`. The legendary share is `Q × 0.001` (e.g. `0.31 × 0.001 × rate`), so it always lost that filter before the `/h` multiplier could recover a visible number. Ingredients never received `recipeQuality` — only split outputs did. ## Fixes - Keep full precision through the quality split; filter with the same `1e-10` floor as `craftingMachineRates`; round only after the `/s` `/m` `/h` multiplier (adaptive digits for small fractions). - Tag non-fluid ingredients with `recipeQuality` in the Pixi recipe row (`CreateRecipe`), effective rates row, DOM sheet projection, and blueprint rates aggregation. Fluids stay unbadged. - Extract `qualitySplitResults` / `withRecipeQuality` to `entityInfoQuality.ts` with unit tests covering the legendary-tail regression. ## Test plan - [x] `vitest` — `entityInfoQuality.test.ts`, `craftingRates.test.ts`, `quality.test.ts` - [ ] Manual: legendary EM plant + 5× legendary Q3 → Per hour list includes legendary - [ ] Manual: set recipe quality (e.g. Uncommon/Legendary) → Recipe and Per hour ingredient icons show matching badges; fluids do not

Keep keyboard focus inside the open mobile navigation overlay without changing route navigation, drawer dismissal, or focus-restoration behavior.

## Scope
- reuse the shared modal focusability filter for the mobile navigation drawer;

- preserve existing Escape, overlay-click, close-button, route-navigation, and downstream-modal behavior;

author: nima-ch
body:
Slice 2 of Wave 2. A new crate, `nils-pack`, that knows nothing about a registry: a pack plus a stack yields facts, which is what makes a pack testable from a fixture and shippable by someone who has never seen our schema.

**It refuses everything that is wrong before anything is classified**, and says where. A contract this engine does not implement, a version that is not semantic, a name that resolves to nothing, a pattern that will not compile, a flag that depends on itself, a parser declared twice. Each by file, line and path, because a pack is written by someone who writes vocabulary rather than Rust:

```
packs/mri/flags.yml:3: flags.is_odd: parser image_type has no predicate no_such_predicate
```

**The pack's own corpus runs at load**, not at test time, and its failure is the load's failure. That is what makes a pack from elsewhere safe to install: a pack that does not do what its own author says it does never judges anything. It earned its keep immediately by catching two wrong expectations of mine while the MRI pack's cases were being written.

**Overlays** (C2) are provenance-scoped and refused when scoped by a selection. The merge is v0's rule exactly: duplicates dropped case-insensitively with the first spelling kept, order of writing preserved, since v0's contrast vocabulary contains terms whose leading space is load-bearing.

### One design error, found by a test failing for the right reason

The first overlay I wrote for a test made its pack fail to load: the pack's corpus said the site's new word was not an agent, and the overlay had just made it one. Running the author's cases against a site's amendment turns the author's claim into a constraint on the site, which is the opposite of what an overlay is for.

So: **the pack's corpus judges the pack, always and un-overlaid; an overlay carries its own cases and is judged by those.** An overlay with no cases is refused, on the same reasoning that refuses a pack with none. §5.3 records it.

### A correction to the C11 report

Finding 2 of the prototype (an unreachable `or` in v0's synthetic test) was filed as a bug the gate would see. It is not. The token test in front of it catches the same values, because the tokenizer strips the parentheses first, so `IR (SYNTHETIC)` gives `has_synthetic=True` in v0 through the first clause. Checked against v0 rather than reasoned about. It is dead code and a defeated intention, and it changes no verdict. The spike report, the spec's declared-difference list and the record are corrected, and two corpus cases pin both halves, including the one input where neither clause fires.

### What is in `packs/mri/` now

The parser and flag layers the prototype verified against v0 over 518,365 stacks, with the fields renamed to the fingerprint's, two buckets opened for editing, and 18 cases of its own. `nils pack list | show | validate` read them.

Tests: 14 unit, 14 loading refusals, 8 overlay, 1 MRI pack, 2 through the CLI. Whole workspace green on SQLite and on a real Postgres 16 before pushing.

author: kamoras
body:
## Summary
- New confirmed-candidates strategy for Kentucky (19th state on this system)
- KY's own State Board of Elections publishes a certified, county-by-county vote-total PDF for the primary — a genuinely different PDF shape from every other state on file: a candidate is a **column**, a county is a **row**, and Kentucky often rotates the column header 90° to fit a crowded field into narrow columns (the real 2026 US Senate GOP primary had 11 candidates)
- Every header word is clustered to its nearest vote-total column by word **center** (not left edge — a long hyphenated surname like the real PERRY-ADELMANN starts far enough left of its own column that left-edge matching pulled it into the wrong candidate's cluster)
- Within a cluster, only the single ALL-CAPS word is trusted as the surname — Mc/Mac surnames (real: McGRATH) keep their natural lowercase second letter even in this header style, and are matched as such
- **Never guesses**: any column whose header doesn't resolve to exactly one surname skips the whole contest rather than guess

## Adversarial review (fixed before merge)
- A surname-regex bug excluded Mc/Mac surnames, which — verified live — silently discarded the entire real 2026 US Senate Democratic primary as falsely ambiguous, dropping the real winner (Cory Booker) along with Amy McGrath
- Reused the shared, hardened row-clustering helper instead of a naive row-grouping reimplementation — the same class of bug already found and fixed in the NJ candidates module
- Added a defensive guard against a page that both closes one contest and opens another sharing a page, so a future cycle's pagination can't misattribute votes

## Verification
Verified live 2026-09-03 against the real 2026 certification PDF (44 pages, certified 2026-06-01): all 11 real federal contests resolve cleanly — both US Senate primaries plus 6 US House districts across both parties where contested — each cross-checked against the document's own printed county-level tallies.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
ADR-114 puts Documentation, Reports and Features & roadmap in the app's footer, in that order.

## The footer had to be renumbered

It ran at orders **1, 2, 3** — Documentation, Features & roadmap, Restart tutorial — which left no room between the first two for Reports to sit where ADR-114 puts it. So the footer moves to the fleet's usual **90 / 95 / 100**, with Restart tutorial at 105.

Restart tutorial stays *after* the roadmap, which is where it already was. It is a re-entry into the walkthrough rather than a destination, so it does not belong among the three. The spec asserts that fourth position explicitly, so a later tidy-up has to argue with it.

## Three new readings

Opencatalogi had no report surface at all, so nothing is relocated out of the main navigation.

- **Publications** — what is published, what is archived, and what retention says to do next.
- **Usage** — what people looked at and what they downloaded.
- **Catalogs and directory** — how mature the catalogs are and how deeply the directory listings are integrated. `catalog` is what this instance publishes, `listing` is what it has found elsewhere; both on one page because "how far does this catalogue reach" is not answerable from either alone.

All three are declarative `type: "dashboard"` pages over the publication register — no bespoke Vue component, no per-app controller.

## Two judgements worth stating

**Retention is grouped, not filtered on a date.** Scalar equality is the only filter OpenRegister's aggregation endpoint can evaluate, so `retentionExpiresAt` cannot be compared to today here. The honest reading is what each publication's `retentionAction` *says to do* — not which ones are overdue, which this page cannot know.

**Usage sums a stored field rather than counting rows.** `usageCounter` stores a `count` per publication per day per kind. Counting rows would answer "how many days had activity" — a plausible-looking number that quietly answers a different question. The stat and chart widgets both use `metric: sum` over `count` / `sumField: count`.

author: wenxin0319
body:
Summary:
Under CUDA 13, device-side assertions (DSA) were broken: every DSA kernel
launch threw `CUDA error: invalid argument` (`cudaErrorInvalidValue`) instead
of reporting the actual device-side assertion.

Root cause: CUDA 13 changed `cudaMemAdvise` to take a `cudaMemLocation` struct
instead of an `int` device id. D86578286 ported
`get_uvm_assertions_ptr_for_current_device()` to the new signature by encoding
the CPU as `{type = cudaMemLocationTypeDevice, id = cudaCpuDeviceId}`. That is
not a valid location: `id` is only validated as a device ordinal, so the
negative `cudaCpuDeviceId` is rejected and both `cudaMemAdvise` calls fail with
`cudaErrorInvalidValue`. Because `C10_CUDA_CHECK_WO_DSA` throws, the error
surfaced from inside the DSA launch itself, masking the assertion the caller
was trying to report. That diff was validated with `buck build` only, so the
runtime failure went unnoticed.

The fix addresses the CPU via `cudaMemLocationTypeHost`, matching how
`fbgemm_gpu`'s `memory_utils.cu` (`new_mem_location_cpu()`) already encodes it.
`id` is ignored for host locations, so it is set to `0` rather than the
negative sentinel.

The change is confined to the `CUDART_VERSION >= 13000 && !defined(USE_ROCM)`
branch, so CUDA 12 and ROCm builds are unaffected.

This unblocks the CUDA 13.3 wave-2 upgrade for `fbgemm` (D118062393), whose
`KernelLauncherTest.throws_dsa_exception` failure was the visible symptom.

Test Plan:
The repro from D118062393's failing signal. At master (CUDA `12.4`) the test
already passes, confirming the breakage is specific to the CUDA `13.3` switch:

```
buck test fbcode//mode/opt fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:kernel_launcher -- --exact 'fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:kernel_launcher - KernelLauncherTest.throws_dsa_exception'
```
`Pass 1. Fail 0.`

With `deeplearning/fbgemm/PACKAGE` locally pinned to `cuda: "13.3"` (i.e. the
codemod applied) plus this fix, the same command passes, and so does the
broader DSA matrix:

```
buck test fbcode//mode/opt \
  fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:kernel_launcher \
  fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:assert_pass_dsa_compile_runtime \
  fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:assert_fail_1_dsa_compile_runtime \
  fbcode//deeplearning/fbgemm/fbgemm_gpu/test/utils:assert_fail_2_dsa_compile_runtime
```
`Pass 12. Fail 0.`

author: yochze
body:
## Summary
Extends the ServiceNow connector with file tool capabilities to expose record attachments (Knowledge Base articles, incidents, etc.) as readable files through the standard file interface (list_files, read_file, search_files).

## Key Changes

- **File capabilities integration**: Added `LIST_FILES`, `READ_FILE`, and `SEARCH_FILES` capabilities to ServiceNowClient, with `cheap_live_listing=True` since attachment metadata queries are lightweight
- **Attachment API support**: Implemented methods to query and download attachments via ServiceNow's `/api/now/attachment` endpoint:
  - `_list_attachments()` - queries attachment metadata with filtering
  - `_attachment_meta()` - resolves file IDs (sys_id, path-shaped IDs, or bare filenames)
  - `_download_attachment()` - fetches binary content
- **Smart file parsing**: `read_file()` intelligently handles different file types:
  - Documents (PDF, Word, etc.) → extracted text via DocumentText wrapper
  - Tabular formats (CSV, TSV, Excel) → pandas DataFrames
  - JSON → parsed objects
  - Plain text → strings
  - Everything else → NamedBytes for vision/preview fallbacks
- **Configurable scope**: New config options:
  - `enable_attachments` (default: True) - toggle file capabilities on/off
  - `attachment_tables` (default: "kb_knowledge") - comma-separated list of tables to expose
- **Capability gating**: When `enable_attachments=False`, capabilities are narrowed to `{QUERY}` only, allowing runtime rejection of file calls
- **Enhanced system prompt**: Added documentation section explaining attachment access patterns, including how to query `sys_attachment` directly for files on arbitrary records
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 14 tests covering metadata queries, file resolution, parsing, scoping, and error cases

## Implementation Details

- Attachment metadata is never indexed into the catalog; listings are served live from the connection
- Inline images embedded in KB article HTML (stored with "ZZ_YY"-prefixed table names) are automatically filtered out
- File IDs support three formats: canonical sys_id (32 hex chars), path-shaped IDs from listings (table/record/name), or bare filenames searched across configured tables
- The `file_version()` method returns a staleness token combining `sys_updated_on` and `size_bytes` for caching
- Respects instance ACLs for the authenticated identity on all attachment operations

## Summary

`build.gradle.kts` applied `kotlin("plugin.spring")` but not `kotlin("plugin.jpa")`
(kotlin-noarg configured for `jakarta.persistence.Entity`). Without it, Kotlin classes
annotated `@Entity` (`Tender`, `Subscriber`, `InterestProfile`, `NotificationRecord`,
`WaitlistEntry`, `DigestQueueEntry`) don't get a synthetic no-arg constructor, so Hibernate
can't instantiate them against a real (non-mocked) database — every `save()`/read 500s with
`org.hibernate.InstantiationException: No default constructor for entity`. Adding the plugin
fixes this; a new `@DataJpaTest` round-trips every entity through a real H2-backed JPA context
so this class of bug cannot silently reappear.

author: newky2k
body:
Fixes #23.

Initialising a single `DatePickerView` rebuilt the 42-cell calendar grid eight times — once from the constructor, then once for each of the seven colour properties a themed picker sets. Every rebuild tore down and recreated ~126 views. A form with eight date fields paid that ~8,000 times, and paid it even for pickers that were collapsed and never opened.

## Changes

**Reuse the day cells** (3f1df34)

The 6×7 skeleton and its 42 cells are created once and then re-stamped in place. Every cell now has the same shape — a container `Grid` holding a centred `Border` around the day `Label` — so selection, range, today and disabled states are all expressed as a change of colour. The plain look is that same `Border` with a transparent background and zero stroke thickness.

That lets all thirteen properties wired to the old rebuild callback repaint instead: none of them can change the grid's shape or the dates it shows. Month paging and date picking no longer allocate either. Disabled dates are gated when the cell is tapped rather than by adding and removing the gesture recognizer.

This also fixes a bug the issue didn't mention: `HeaderBackgroundColor` and `DayNameColor` were wired to a callback that rebuilt the *day grid*, which never touched the header or the day-name row — so after construction both properties were inert. They now take effect.

**Build the layout lazily** (d2e991d)

`BuildLayout()` moves out of the constructor to the first point at which the control is both visible and attached to a handler. Construction allocates no child views, so a picker that is never shown costs nothing, and one that is shown builds exactly once, after its initial property values have landed. Every callback that can fire before the build already no-ops on the null fields.

**Repopulate on an overflow-day tap** (a541d18)

Tapping a day from an adjacent month moved `_displayedMonth` and updated the header label but left the grid rendering the previous month. Range selection used to get the repopulate for free from the rebuild callback that now repaints; single selection never did, because `OnDayTapped` moves `_displayedMonth` before assigning `SelectedDate`, so `OnSelectedDateChanged` takes its same-month path. Repopulating where the month actually changes covers both.

## Not included

Dispatcher-tick coalescing of structural rebuilds (issue item 2b) is no longer worth it — a burst of property sets now costs a few colour assignments each.

## Testing

- `DSoft.Maui.Controls` and `MauiSampleApp` build clean for `net10.0-maccatalyst` (0 errors).
- Sample app's Date Picker page checked in the iOS simulator: today's ring, selected fill, range band and overflow-day taps all render as before.

README's "How It Works" section is updated — it still described the per-date view cache and the three cell shapes this PR removes.

Release plan, phase 2 (task 2.2) — the audit of the most privileged path a door carries, as a test. A door composes `ACL SESSION '<h>' ` and nothing else, so spec 009's gates decide on the session's principal with its scope resolved per statement. Pinned in `test_acl_session.cpp`: no scope → management and native SQL both refused; `manage` → administers (write lands in the catalog), refused native SQL, cannot self-escalate; `passthrough` → native SQL incl. the node's control surface, while ordinary statements still resolve inside its grants.

**Decision** (spec 009 addendum): passthrough over a door *is* the operator path — god mode by definition — not a surface to narrow. Backlog blocker 4 closes.

author: hackshaven
body:
## Summary

`docs/MULTI_MONITOR_PLAN.md` had been written and rewritten twice without a single one of its platform assumptions ever being executed. A throwaway spike ran the load-bearing ones on real hardware, and two of the plan's load-bearing claims came back wrong.

The biggest is the cross-window decoder budget. §3 reasoned from one iPhone 16 measurement to a fixed ceiling of **4 concurrent decoders**, and described the failure as a hard crash boundary on any machine. On a Windows 11 laptop (Intel Raptor Lake-S + RTX 4090 Laptop, packaged build, real `HLSService` → hls.js → MSE playback), **sixteen** output windows — each holding a WebGL2 context, a 128 MiB 8192×4096 render target and a live decoder — ran at **30.7 fps, 1.00× realtime, zero dropped frames**, *identical* to the eight-output case rather than merely close. Four times the proposed budget at four times the default pixels. The only cost the spike could measure was ~160 ms of extra startup latency.

This PR is documentation only. No `src/` changes, no ladder code.

## Related issue

No issue. This amends the design doc merged in https://github.com/zyra-project/terraviz/pull/205 with measurements taken after it landed. Related context: terraviz#229 (playback rate) and terraviz#230 (the phone decoder ceiling the old budget was extrapolated from) are both cited in the doc and neither is closed by this.

The one code change the amendment identified landed separately as https://github.com/zyra-project/terraviz/pull/419, since that bug is reachable on `main` today and isn't multi-window-specific.

## Changes

Eleven commits, one file, +501/−74. Each is one section.

**The amendment itself (7):**

| Commit | What, and why |
|---|---|
| `4eeed4d0` | **Decoder budget.** Records the 8-vs-16 comparison and three corrections. `MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODERS = 4` becomes `DEFAULT_CONCURRENT_DECODERS`, a seed raised per-machine. Adds a **Health signal** row (steady fps + media-clock ratio) and a **Spawn pacing** row. |
| `dc9fb50d` | **Placement.** New "Monitor geometry and placement" section: signed monitor origins, the physical-vs-logical coordinate trap, and the two clean results. Persistence gains a signed `monitorOrigin`. |
| `458786d0` | **§6 verified.** Marks the ACL reasoning confirmed, and names two hazards it hid. Narrows Open Question 1 to Linux. |
| `76f86ff4` | **Ceiling reconciliation.** Brings three Risks bullets, the MVP scope line, and the GPU-context-loss rationale in line with the measurement. |
| `40cee550` | **GPU selection.** Records it as a deployment concern with no code fix, and gives it a home: the renderer string in the debug overlay, plus a new commit 15 for `docs/MULTI_MONITOR_OPERATIONS.md`. |
| `6a6f0394` | **`dev:desktop` can't play video.** Corrects Appendix B, which told a qualifier to iterate there. |
| `e8a38842` | **Header.** A "What has actually been executed" table, one row per assumption with its verdict. |

**Review fixes (4)** — all four Copilot threads were verified against source and all four were right:

| Commit | What, and why |
|---|---|
| `0258b57f` | **The placement fix wasn't implementable.** `WindowOptions` types `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` as bare `number` in logical pixels (`window.d.ts:1542-1548`); only `setPosition`/`setSize` take the physical wrappers (`:822`, `:870`). Boot-flow step 3 now spawns hidden and without fullscreen, places via the physical setters, then fullscreens, then shows. **This costs a fifth capability grant, `core:window:allow-show`** — see below. |
| `f3ce08dd` | **Restore contract agreeing with itself.** The name+origin rule had been added to §Persistence while four other sites still said name-only — including the paragraph directly above it. Launch flow, monitor reconnect, delivery commit 10, and Appendix A's example all fixed. |
| `614e553d` | **The per-machine budget had nowhere to live.** No schema field, no panel control, no delivery owner — a budget nobody can change is a constant wearing a different name. Adds `concurrentDecoderBudget`, the panel control, delivery ownership in commit 11, and acceptance case **S5b**, because S5 only ever exercised the seeded 4 and so could not detect the budget being unsettable. |
| `0cb1d076` | **ACL hazard scoped to windows that can hit it.** v1's outputs run `datasetMirror` and invoke no commands, so "this feature walks straight into it" was wrong. Narrowed to any window running the *main app bundle* — what the spike's own preflight windows were — rather than removed. |

### The fifth capability grant

§6 asked for four permissions; it now asks for **five**. `core:window:allow-show` is needed because placement cannot be expressed at construction, so an output is spawned `visible: false` and revealed after being positioned. `visible: false` is a free constructor option, but showing is a command, and `core:window:default` is getters only — its 28 identifiers include `allow-is-visible` and no `allow-show`, checked against Tauri 2.11.2's permission table.

It is flagged **untested** in the doc: it came from a code reading *after* the spike, so the header's "four grants, confirmed" result does not cover it. It is now the one line of §6 still in the state the rest of the section was in before the spike ran.

### Deliberate non-changes

- **16 is not written in as the new constant.** Treating it that way would repeat the original mistake with a different number. Every measurement came from one 4090 laptop; a museum is likelier to deploy an Intel-iGPU NUC, where the original cliff may well be real. The doc says so explicitly.
- **No claim about the failure's *shape*.** The old text described a crash boundary; that framing is inherited from a phone. This machine was never taken close enough to find its limit, so cliff-vs-gradient is recorded as **unknown here** — an honest gap rather than a resolved one. A design assuming a cliff will watch for the wrong symptom on desktop hardware.

### Findings the plan did not predict

Folded into the relevant sections rather than appended as a list:

- **Signed monitor origins.** `\\.\DISPLAY1` sat at `x = −1680`. Placement worked, but persistence must store `x`/`y` signed — and Windows display names are *positional* and reassignable across an unplug/replug, so a name-only restore can put an output on a different physical monitor while looking like it worked.
- **GPU selection is not the app's to make.** The webview first landed on the iGPU of a machine with a 4090. `probeGpuSelection()` settled the confound inside one run: `high-performance` and `low-power` returned the same adapter, `powerPreferenceWorks: false`. The driver decides above the app. An earlier spike note proposing `additional_browser_args` with `--force-high-performance-gpu` is **superseded by that measurement** and is explicitly not written in as a fix.
- **An ACL denial looks like a data bug** in a window running the main app bundle. It turned out to affect three surfaces, not the one §6 originally named: `datasetLoader`'s two load paths, `downloadUI`'s `renderPanel` (blank panel, no error, not even the empty state), and `browseUI`'s badge loop. Fixed in #419.

## Impact & risk

**Blast radius: none at runtime.** One markdown file. No schema, no migration, no deploy ordering, no behaviour change for publishers or end users. Nothing under `src/`, `functions/`, `cli/` or `src-tauri/` is touched — the five capability grants §6 asks for are still only *described*, not added.

What this does change is what a future implementer will build. The budget constant, the persistence record shape, the health signal, the window-spawn sequence, and two new delivery-ladder items (the budget control in commit 11, the operator runbook as commit 15) all move. If the amendment is wrong, the cost is paid when the ladder starts, not now.

One risk worth naming: the measurements generalise less than they read. They bound what is **possible**, not what is **portable**, and the doc repeats that at the header, in §3 and

"PDF Archiver" could break across lines anywhere it was set, which reads as two products.

- The name holds a non-breaking space in the site copy, the page titles, the meta descriptions and both press kit READMEs — 93 occurrences, `\u{00A0}` in Swift, the character itself in Markdown
- `site.name` keeps a plain space: it feeds `og:site_name` and the JSON-LD `"name"` field, where the name is an identifier a machine reads rather than a line of type
- The coverage tables keep a plain space too — those are the headlines of other publications, quoted, and theirs to spell

Every remaining plain space in the built site is one of those two: `og:site_name` on each page, the JSON-LD name on the home pages, and the seven quoted headlines on `/press/`.

body:
Faltava justamente o que mais se pergunta no dia a dia: quem faz aniversário, quem completa tempo de casa, quem chegou agora, que campanha está no ar e o que saiu de comunicado. Entram no corpus `announcements`, `campaigns`, `culture_events`, `recognitions` e `onboarding_materials`.

Aniversariantes, tempo de casa e novas admissões entram como documentos agregados — um por assunto, montado na hora com o recorte do mês — e não como uma linha por pessoa. "Quem faz aniversário este mês" é pergunta temporal, não lexical: full-text sobre 135 fichas nunca responderia, mas um documento chamado "Aniversariantes de setembro" responde. De quebra, só quem é do mês chega ao modelo, em vez do diretório inteiro.

A origem é `employee_directory`, a mesma view que o portal já usa: sem e-mail, sem telefone, sem data de nascimento completa. Ainda assim, agora saem nomes de colaboradores para um provedor que treina com os dados — está escrito no README da pasta, porque é o tipo de coisa que se esquece.

author: jerome-benoit
body:
## Description

Harden file-data handling in `src/convert-to-sap-messages.ts` so invalid runtime payloads fail fast instead of reaching SAP as `base64,[object Object]` (root cause of #177).

- Drops the Node.js `Buffer` global and encodes bytes with an Edge-safe, chunked `btoa` path. `Buffer` remains supported through its `Uint8Array` inheritance.
- Accepts genuine `ArrayBuffer` values, including values created in another JavaScript realm; rejects prototype and `Symbol.toStringTag` impostors and reports detached buffers through the AI SDK error contract.
- Preserves the documented buffer-like `toString("base64")` contract only for canonical RFC 4648 base64.
- Validates multi-megabyte base64 iteratively in O(n) time and O(1) stack space, including padding and unused-bit canonicality.
- Reads typed-array backing bytes without invoking overrideable `length`, `subarray`, or iterator hooks, preserving byte identity for valid subclasses.
- Rejects plain objects, provider references, malformed/non-string encoder results, and never fetches them.
- Warns (`unsupported`, deduplicated) instead of silently dropping assistant file parts, unsupported user parts, and non-tool-result tool parts.
- Covers the contract in Node and Edge environments and documents supported/rejected file data.

## Validation

- `npm run type-check`
- `npm run test` — 16 files, 1,355 tests
- `npm run test:node` — 16 files, 1,352 tests
- `npm run test:edge` — 15 files, 1,353 tests
- `npm run prettier-check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build && npm run check-build`
- `npm run build:v2 && npm run check-build:v2`
- Targeted converter tests — Node 132 tests; Edge 130 tests

author: fac07
body:
## Summary

Phase **D4** of `boleta-renderer-offline` — the offline-first local server now speaks the `valores` (EAV) contract end to end: form resolution, typed create/close validation, EAV persistence, and `valores` in the Outbox sync payloads.

Stacked on `main` after D3 (#16, merged @ `eefa414`). Depends on D1 (mirror schema) + D3 (TS MotorCampos port + `resolverCamposLocal` / `validarValoresLocal` / `validarCierreLocal`).

## Tasks

| Task | What |
|------|------|
| D4.1 | `GET /tipos-movimiento/:id/formulario` → `resolverCamposLocal(id, now)` as `CampoAplicable[]`, resolved entirely from the local SQLite config mirror (no central call). |
| D4.2 | `POST /boletas` accepts `valores: ValorCampoDto[]`; runs `validarValoresLocal` → **400 + `ErrorCampo[]`** on failure; persists Encabezado + `BoletaValorCampo` rows in ONE transaction; `SeccionId` derived server-side from `Campo.SeccionId`; local `numeroBoleta` correlativo authority unchanged. Validation and persistence share one frozen `asOf`. |
| D4.3 | `POST /boletas/:id/cerrar` runs `validarCierreLocal` → **422 + `ErrorCampo[]`** and the boleta stays `EnTransito`; success → `Cerrada`; non-`EnTransito` → **409**; no override path. |
| D4.4 | Already done in D1 — the `calidad \| compostera \| detalle-fruta \| caracteristicas` extension routes were removed with their tables; every verb now falls to the generic Express 404. Confirmed. |
| D4.5 | `crearBoletaLocal` persists `BoletaValorCampo`; new `listarValoresLocal(id)`; `Crear` and `Cerrar` Outbox payloads include `valores` (camelCase, `valorNumero` as a JSON number for central's `LeerValores`). |
| D4.6 | RED→GREEN regression spec (`vitest.electron`): a required-section boleta is created + closed + synced offline-first → the `Crear` Outbox payload carries `valores`, no `ErrorCentral`, boleta reaches `Cerrada`. |
| D4.7 | Gate. |

## BasculaId decision

Carried forward the D1 decision unchanged: the local `Boleta` table has **no `BasculaId`** (one install = one báscula). Central's `POST /api/boletas/sync` "Crear" branch already sets `BasculaId = bascula.Id`, resolved from `request.BasculaCodigo` at upload time — the dispatcher sends `basculaCodigo` from local config. No wiring needed; no schema change.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `frontend/electron/db.ts` | `crearBoletaLocal` takes `valores` + persists EAV rows in-txn (`persistirValoresBoleta`, `seccionIdDeCampo`); `listarValoresLocal` + `ValorCampoLocal`; `Crear`/`Cerrar` payloads include `valores`; honors caller `fechaHoraIngreso`; `_inyectarDbParaPruebas` Node test seam. |
| `frontend/electron/local-server.ts` | `GET /tipos-movimiento/:id/formulario`; `POST /boletas` valores + `validarValoresLocal` → 400; `POST /boletas/:id/cerrar` rewrite → `validarCierreLocal` 422 / 409 / 404; `normalizarValores` body helper. |
| `frontend/electron/boletas-valores.spec.ts` | New — D4.6 offline-first create → close → sync regression. |

## Test plan / gate evidence

- [x] `npm run electron:compile` → exit 0
- [x] `npm run test:electron` → 3 files, **22 passed** (3 config-sync + 18 motor-campos + 1 D4.6 regression), exit 0
- [x] D4.6 confirmed RED first (`listarValoresLocal is not a function` / missing `valores` in payload) then GREEN after implementation

## Size

~410 authored changed lines (forecast ~360). `size:exception` — coherent non-splittable slice (routes, EAV persistence, and Outbox payload move together; the regression spec proves the round trip). Precedent: E1 #13 ~1029, D1 #14 ~951, D2 #15 ~527, D3 #16 ~1113.

## Notes

Repo uses no issues/labels — following the convention of PRs #13–#16 (no issue link, no labels).

author: nikcio
body:
## Problem

#182 added `NUGET_PACKAGES` and an explicit restore step to the docs deploy — the restore step **succeeds**, but the deploy still fails identically:

```
Failed to restore src/OpenApiCodeGenerator/OpenApiCodeGenerator.csproj (in 60 ms).
/usr/share/dotnet/sdk/10.0.400/NuGet.targets(198,5): error MSB4181: The "RestoreTask" task returned false but did not log an error.
```

## Refined root cause

With assets already restored by the workflow step, the restore inside `dotnet publish` should be a fast no-op — instead it fails in 60 ms, silently. The remaining variable is the **execution context**: the failing `dotnet` invocation is spawned as a node/pnpm child process inside the Astro action (`execSync` in `build-wasm.mjs`), while the direct workflow step restores fine with the same env. NuGet restore fails silently when `dotnet` runs as a node/pnpm child process on the Linux runner (this does not reproduce on Windows — local runs of the same script work).

## Fix

Keep all dotnet invocations out of node in CI:

- **`docs.yml`**: new `Publish WebAssembly playground runtime` step (`dotnet publish src/OpenApiCodeGenerator.Wasm -c Release`) directly in the workflow, and the Astro action now runs `pnpm run build:ci`
- **`docs/package.json`**: `build:ci` = `node scripts/build-wasm.mjs --skip-publish && astro build`
- **`docs/scripts/build-wasm.mjs`**: new `--skip-publish` flag — skips the in-script `dotnet publish` (requires an existing publish output, with a clear error if missing) and only copies the bundle + runs the Node smoke test. Local usage (`pnpm run build` / `build:wasm`) is unchanged and still publishes itself.

## Testing

- `node scripts/build-wasm.mjs --skip-publish --force` (the CI path): copies the bundle and passes the smoke test
- `pnpm run build:wasm -- --force` (the full local path, dotnet publish under pnpm/node): publishes and passes the smoke test on Windows
- `pnpm lint` passes in `docs/`; workflow YAML validated

author: jessl101
body:
## Summary

A cinematic redesign of douliesleep.com in the palette and typefaces the site already owns. The page becomes one night told in hours: it opens at the 2:47 AM wake-up, rewinds to bedtime, returns to the wake-up, lifts to the morning read, and closes at tonight's projected bedtime. Each beat has its own sky, one light source, and one glass prop showing a real app state.

The creative direction and the prototype the page was built from live under `concept/`.

## Changes

- **index.html** rebuilt. Hero, bedtime, the wake-up, the morning read, a quiet stages list, the close, and the FAQ. Head metadata, disclaimers, legal links and every waitlist test id are preserved. The six-card grid, the stages carousel and the join card are gone; the stage content moved into a plain list and the FAQ into a plain list below the close.
- **landing.css** is a new hand-written stylesheet. It replaces the last of the Next.js build CSS under `_next/`, which nothing else referenced. Includes the frosted form row (email, stage, "Save my spot"), a CSS-only still sky as the no-JavaScript fallback, and a reduced-motion path that renders a single still frame.
- **site.js** keeps the Supabase waitlist flow unchanged apart from the button verb. The carousel code is replaced by the night sky: a 3D Canvas star field with depth of field, scroll dolly, cursor pan and an occasional shooting star, the bedside clock with scene switching, and a few degrees of prop tilt. The frame loop pauses in background tabs.
- **Copy** rewritten for a warmer, more relaxed marketing voice. Benefits as relief, options never orders, no promised outcomes. The medical disclaimer wording is unchanged.
- **README** updated for the new structure and history.
- **concept/** adds the direction document and the prototype for reference.

## Verification

Checked in a headless browser at 1440px and 390px widths: no script errors, no horizontal overflow, invalid emails show the error state, the clock steps through 2:47, 11:40, 6:10 and 7:05 on scroll, and the sky crossfades to dawn on the morning beat.

Not verified: the sandbox blocks Google Fonts and Fontshare, so renders used fallback faces. Please confirm Instrument Serif and Satoshi load on the Cloudflare Pages preview and that the hero headline sits at three lines on a laptop.

## Deploy

No build step. Cloudflare Pages serves the repo root as before.

author: chriscarrollsmith
body: ## Problem `resolve_key_domain` / `catalog.build_catalog` silently omitted missing key labels and `schedule._compute_preferred_fields` then dropped the whole series to expansion order. After #610 the schedule joins on key values, so a half-resolved key aligned by position against neighbours that aligned by key. ## Fix - A declared key that does not resolve on every member raises `PartialKeyDomainError` (wrapped as `InvertedTreeExportError` from the catalog), naming the series and the unresolved data cells. - Expansion order remains the schedule only when no key is declared (`key: []`). - `_execute_bind` raises `UnknownBindKindError` instead of a `ValueError` whose message was string-matched. - `_compute_preferred_fields` no longer falls back to `TIME_PERIOD`-only or expansion order for a partial domain. ## Tests - A `TIME_PERIOD` series with one blank header cell fails closed with the cell named. - A series with `key: []` still emits on expansion order (schema still requires a non-empty key on non-scalar layouts, so that emit case is catalog/codegen only). - Unknown bind kinds are classified by exception type, not message text. Fixes #620

author: whispersofj
body:
## Summary

Re-adopts Bazarr per TODO #4 and the lifecycle re-adoption policy — a fresh, tracked implementation, not a copy of the pre-slim config. Takes the stack from 8 to 9 always-on services (≈12.9g of 22GiB host RAM in caps).

## The service

| | |
|---|---|
| Image | `ghcr.io/hotio/bazarr:release-1.6.0` (matches the hotio pin convention) |
| Cap | 768m / 1 CPU — **174 MiB steady-state observed on this host**; 4.4× the 128m cap it OOM'd under in the pre-slim stack |
| Healthcheck | `curl http://localhost:6767/ping` — verified 200 unauthenticated on a live probe container |
| CVEs | Local trivy run: **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH** (`--ignore-unfixed`); baseline entry added |
| Mounts | Exactly mirror Sonarr/Radarr (`/mnt/remote/nzbdav` + `/data/shows` + `/data/movies`, all `:rslave`) — path parity, no mapping |

## Designed around the landmines

- **Read-only over the fragile trees**: Bazarr only writes subtitle files beside the media; it can never write into mount internals.
- **No `depends_on` on `nzbdav_rclone`** (only sonarr/radarr, service_healthy): mount-owner restarts (landmine #2) and NzbDAV recreations (landmine #4) never touch it.
- **No new env vars**: Bazarr has no `BAZARR__*` env surface upstream — connecting Sonarr/Radarr is a documented one-time UI step (Settings → Sonarr/Radarr, `http://sonarr:8989` / `http://radarr:7878` + API keys from `.env`).

## Wiring (the exhaustive checklist)

- `docker-compose.yml` — service + header comment
- `scripts/audit_residue.py` — `bazarr` removed from `RETIRED_SERVICES`; its registry↔lifecycle cross-check enforced both sides of the move at CI time; test fixtures swapped `bazarr`→`lidarr` (with a new pin that the re-adopted name must never flag)
- `docs/services/lifecycle.md` — removed from the retired table; full re-adoption record added
- `tests/health/run-all.sh` — `bazarr` check + case entry
- `scripts/backup.sh` — `config/bazarr` in the backup list
- `.github/trivy-baseline.json` — `ghcr.io/hotio/bazarr:release-1.6.0: 0`
- Counts 8→9: README, AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, service-registry, expansion checklist, imagemaid.md, API.md, github-profile README
- New `docs/services/bazarr.md` + new Bazarr section in `docs/API.md` (healthcheck endpoint, auth family, canonical docs)
- `TODO.md` #4 closed out with the observed numbers

## Verification

- `docker compose config --quiet` ✓
- image pulled, probed live (`/ping`=200, root=200, API 401 unauth'd as expected), torn down
- `bash -n` + shellcheck on the two touched scripts ✓
- all offline unit tests pass (audit_residue, compose mounts, config drift, digest, secret drift, alias candidates) ✓
- actionlint ✓ · ruff ✓ · audit-residue repo scan: AUDIT OK ✓

## One-time post-merge step (on the host, not in git)

After `docker compose up -d bazarr`: open `http://HOST_IP:6767`, set the API-key auth form, and connect Sonarr (`http://sonarr:8989`) and Radarr (`http://radarr:7878`) with their `.env` API keys.

author: loxybee
body:
## What's in this batch

Three bodies of work plus the docs to match. 35 commits, 39 files, all 115 test suites green, smoke-launch clean, `replay-log.js` invariants held on every detection-adjacent change.

### 1. The full EQEmu buff-stacking engine, ported

`src/shared/spellStackingEngine.js` is a complete port of EQEmu's `CheckStackConflict` â€” every mechanic, not the old effect-slot heuristic: same-slot collision, the `SPA 148/149` block/overwrite directives the client itself enforces, bard-song separation, rank ladders, and the `calcSpellValue` formula table. Parity-verified **100% over 6.75M verdicts** against the reference implementation (`tools/stacking-parity.js`, `test/spell-stacking-engine.test.js`).

- `src/main/stackingService.js` binds it to the live roster (`verdict` / `planConflict` / `wouldOverwriteLive` / `invalidate`).
- The roster now carries per-spell stacking data, written by `tools/build-roster.js` into `buffs.json`.
- The old `spellStacking.js` is **deleted**; `spellEffects.js` gets its stat magnitudes from the ported engine's `calcSpellValue`.
- **Curated data proposes, the engine vetoes.** In `buffEngine._land`'s stale-tile sweep and in the Buff Planner, a curated `overwrites` only removes a tile if the engine agrees the two don't stack â€” AEM's full parse found ~104 curated `overwrites` pairs the real game stacks fine, where tiles were vanishing mid-buff. The reverse too: a *weak* `coexist` (different curated headings, no recorded conflict, no authored `stacksWith`) is overruled when the engine says the pair collides (Cantata of Soothing vs Cassindra's Chorus of Clarity â€” owner-confirmed in-game).
- **Yaulp stacks** with the Shielding line / armour coats / Armor of Protection now â€” it sits on its own AC slot (owner tested in-game).

### 2. Buff duration formula 50 = permanent

45 real long buffs â€” Armor of the Faithful, the whole Shielding line, the damage-shield coat line, permanent wolf/vision forms â€” were being read as ~0s duration and disappearing off the overlay about a minute after they landed. EQEmu's `CalcBuffDuration_formula` case 50 returns the "doesn't tick" sentinel *before* field 12 is consulted; the published EQL spell references render every formula-50 spell as permanent. `build-roster.js` now marks these `infiniteDuration`. Two entries with a genuine field-12 value are left finite pending a live report.

### 3. Buff Planner rework

The Planner page is still **LOCKED** (no nav button) until the `buff-loadout` aura ships â€” but the engine underneath was reworked substantially:

- **Balanced / Melee / Caster are stat-toggle presets, not a hidden weighting.** Picking Melee un-ticks the caster-only stats; Caster un-ticks the melee ones; the user sees exactly which stats got dropped and can re-tick any. Resists and rune stats have no toggle chip â€” they still score, at their low weight.
- **Spell AC is stored 4Ã— the applied value** â€” divided down, floored, to match the in-game tooltip and the published EQL references (Verses of Victory +50 â†’ +12, Yaulp III +40 â†’ +10).
- **A Combat-buffs pool** â€” short buffs (â‰¤5 min) and proc innates (Spirit of the Puma, Ward of the Divine) are the burst-swap loadout, kept out of the standing 14 and out of the totals sheet.
- **No "always worth taking" list** â€” the flat proc score boost is gone ("if it needs an always-worth list the weights are wrong").
- **An X on every slotted row** removes a buff and pulls the next-best up into the slot; a **Reset removed** button in the loadout header restores them.
- **A "why this one?" hover** per slotted buff â€” every buff it beat, their stats, and any blocked-pair reason.
- **Amplification** is pinned as a reference row at the top of the song list (a multiplier on other songs â€” not something to score); **song rows show the instrument type** (Brass / Singing / Stringed / Wind / Percussion, from `spells_us.txt`).
- Magic resist weighted above other resists; Rizlona's Embers scored as a spell-damage focus; a weaker haste/cast-speed source loses that stat's weight (EQ applies one at a time).
- Accordion sections, all open except "Priority order" and "Won't fit".

### 4. Detection fix â€” 1 song vs 1 buff

When exactly one bard song and one non-song buff share a landing text, the 6-second song pulse is the only thing that tells them apart â€” so that check now runs *above* the renewal / spellbook / gem tiers. A now-permanent Frenzy sharing `"You go berserk."` with McVaxius' Berserker Crescendo was absorbing every pulse as its own renewal, so the song was never recognised (owner report).

### 5. Add Aura restructure + misc

- The choices screen is the **original four buttons plus one new "Standalone tools" button = five, grouped under three headings** (Standalone tools / Premade & custom / Import) â€” not sub-menus, not one scrolling page.
- **The aura-name field is removed** from Add Aura entirely â€” auras are named by their kind.
- **A per-aura "Hide permanent buffs" toggle** for the Self Buffs aura (drops Yaulp, Fury, the Shielding line etc. from that aura's list).
- **The in-app changelog was scrapped** at the owner's request (`src/shared/data/changelog.js`, the About-page card/modal, the IPC and its test all deleted). `package.json` version bumped to `1.1.0` (it had been stuck at `1.0.0`).

### 6. Docs

body:
## Summary

Optimizes `/model` picker latency and catalogue resolution so OpenRouter and Radient models show up immediately and live updates complete faster:

1. **Immediate Initial Paint with Cached Aggregators**:
   - Aggregator providers (`openrouter`, `radient`, `radient-key`) have no hardcoded models in the static registry. Previously, `static_catalogue()` returned 0 models for aggregators on the opening keystroke, leaving the user waiting for `live_catalogue()` to finish.
   - Introduced `cached_available_models(provider_id)` in `local_operator.model.discovery` using `peek_listing()` (synchronous, local disk-only, non-blocking, no network).
   - Added `initial_catalogue()` to `ProviderController` and updated `OperatorApp._populate_model_picker()` to use it. On the very first frame of `/model`, cached models from disk (e.g. 425 models from OpenRouter and Radient) paint immediately in <10ms.

2. **Parallel Live Catalogue Resolution**:
   - In `ProviderController.live_catalogue()`, fetching models across all 19 registered providers previously ran sequentially in a `for` loop with individual `asyncio.to_thread` calls.
   - Refactored to fetch all providers concurrently via `asyncio.gather`. The worst-case refresh latency is now bounded by the single slowest provider rather than the sum of all provider round trips.

3. **Aggregator & Public Listing Consistency**:
   - Added `radient-key` to `AGGREGATOR_PROVIDERS` in `local_operator.providers.registry` and `PUBLIC_LISTING_PROVIDERS` / `LISTING_CAPTURE_VERSIONS` in `local_operator.model.discovery`.

## Testing Evidence

- **First frame initial catalogue execution**:
  ```
  1. First frame initial_catalogue: 967 entries, 442 selectable rows in 7.49ms

     - radient        : 425 models immediately offered
  2. Parallel live_catalogue: 1037 entries in 42.11ms (cached) / 1.91s (ttl_s=0 cold parallel vs 5.42s sequential)
  ```

author: juargo
body:
Production was running code against a schema it did not have.

| Migration | In repo since | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `20260821000000_us058_manual_movement` | 2026-08-21 | not applied |
| `20260901000000_categoria_unica_por_bucket` | 2026-09-02 | not applied |

US-058 sat unapplied for twelve days, so manual movements (ADR-039) and `DELETE /api/movimientos/:id` (ADR-040) returned 500 the whole time. ADR-042 then deployed on top of the same gap and turned a clean `409 NOMBRE_DUPLICADO` into an unhandled P2002 → 500.

Both are applied now. Verified against the database, not against the command output:

- `_prisma_migrations`: 15 → **17**, none unfinished
- `Categoria_userId_bucketId_nombre_key` present, `Categoria_userId_nombre_key` gone
- `Categoria_id_userId_key` (ADR-036 composite FK) untouched
- `Transaccion.origen` present, `ingestaId` nullable, `Transaccion_origen_ingesta_consistency` active
- 508 `Transaccion` / 26 `Categoria` — unchanged

### Why keep the runbook

The trap it documents will outlive this incident.

`apps/api/prisma.config.ts` imports `dotenv/config` and resolves `url: process.env.DIRECT_URL ? env("DIRECT_URL") : env("DATABASE_URL")`. `apps/api/.env` points `DIRECT_URL` at localhost (ADR-029), and dotenv fills in what the shell does not set. So:

```bash
DATABASE_URL="<prod>" pnpm exec prisma migrate deploy   # migrates localhost, silently
```

The runbook sets both variables. It also records the pre/post checks, why each migration is safe on the current data (0 rows with `ingestaId IS NULL`, 0 collisions on the new index), and the rollback — including that the US-058 rollback stops being possible once the first manual movement exists.

### Still open

Render's `buildCommand` runs `prisma generate` but not `migrate deploy`. That is what let the drift go unnoticed, and it is unchanged by this PR — recorded as the last step so the decision is explicit rather than silently made here.

author: kagebinary
body:
## Why

Ix ships `install.ps1`, `uninstall.ps1` and `bootstrap.ps1`, runs a
`windows-2022` CI leg, and has a documented Windows install path — and could not
read a line of any of it.

Measured on `scripts/install/install.ps1` (602 lines), which the grammar parses
with `hasError: false`:

```
defs   : Pause-On-Failure, Write-Ok, Write-Warn, Remove-InstallerScratch,
         Write-Err, Test-Healthy, Get-LatestVersion, Resolve-Version,
         Test-DockerRunning, Get-BackendLatestVersion
calls  : 31 distinct, incl. Remove-InstallerScratch and Pause-On-Failure
```

Those last two are calls between functions in the same file, so the graph gets
real intra-script edges rather than a flat symbol list.

## Loading

Through `tryImportGrammar`, not `tryLoadGrammar`. The package publishes ESM
bindings with top-level await — the same shape as SAS/Lua/CSS — so `require()`
throws `Top-level await is currently not supported`. It is also a directory
`main` with no `"exports"`, so it is imported by explicit file path for the same
DEP0151 reason Lua and CSS are; verified the warning count is 0.

Prebuilds cover all six platforms (`darwin-arm64/x64`, `linux-arm64/x64`,
`win32-arm64/x64`) — broader than `tree-sitter-sas`, which is the grammar the
existing comment notes has no win32 prebuild. So this is present on every CI leg
rather than degrading to unparsed.

## Query set

Functions, filters and workflows share one `function_statement` node, so one
pattern covers all three. Plus classes, class methods, enums, calls, and imports.

Imports cover the three ways a script pulls in code — `Import-Module`,
`using module` / `using namespace`, and dot-sourcing (`. ./common.ps1`), which is
how most scripts actually share helpers.

**Both keyword forms needed anchoring.** `using module Ix.Common` puts the scope
keyword in a `generic_token` of its own, and `-RequiredVersion 5.0` contributes
another, so the unanchored patterns emitted `module` and `5.0` as imported
modules. There is a test asserting
`Import-Module Pester -RequiredVersion 5.0 -Force` yields exactly `[Pester]`.

**Class properties are deliberately not captured.** The `variable` node keeps its
`$` sigil, so `$Root` would never join to the `.Root` that references it, and
there is no name-normalisation hook to strip it. Better absent than joined to
nothing — worth revisiting if such a hook ever lands.

## Lockfile

Additive only — one `tree-sitter-powershell` entry. This npm strips `libc` from
the six `@rolldown/binding-linux-*` packages on any write; those fields are
restored here so they do not silently regress. Verified with `npm ci`.

## Verification

- `core-ingestion`: 366 passed (6 new)
- `ix-cli`: 1510 passed + parser smoke
- lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, knip no new findings

author: mascwa200-beep
body:
## The defect

`captainLeads` is a whole mechanic, and every piece of it existed:

- two separate parsers hear **"I'll lead"**, **"with me"**, **"myself"**, **"personally"**;
- it is worth **+2 on every check** in `modifierFor`, itemised for the UI as *"captain leading"*;
- `check()` rolls a wound for the captain at **35% of the officer death chance**.

None of it reached the game.

**The order was parsed and dropped.** The `away_team` case passed `order.captainLeads` to `buildAwayTeam` on exactly one branch — the one that says *"Away team assembled and standing by. There is nowhere to send them, Captain"* and then does nothing. Wherever there **was** somewhere to send them, `awayMission` built the team with `captainLeads` hard-coded `false`:

```js
const team = this.buildAwayTeam(stations, false,
  { boarding: template.id === 'boarding_action' });
```

So saying you would go down only ever took effect when nobody went anywhere.

**And the risk was computed and read by nobody.** `result.captainWounded` was set in `away.js` and appears nowhere else in `src/` — no casualty, no log line, no entry in the record, not a sentence in `buildCheckText`. Measured over 600 lethal checks with the captain leading:

```
captain wounded on 2 of 600 checks while leading

captain wounded. result.text: "Spock could not make it work. We are coming back empty."
  game log mentions the captain being hurt: false
captain wounded. result.text: "Spock is hurt — and we got nothing for it."
  game log mentions the captain being hurt: false
```

Both times the report talked about the science officer.

**Taken together, the +2 was free.** Leading from the front was strictly better than staying aboard — and there was no way to ask for it.

## The fix

The order reaches the mission now, through the *"Where To, Captain?"* question as well, so "away team, I'll lead" survives being asked where.

**A captain who goes down ends the landing party.** Not a new rule — it is the rule already written three lines above, for a team with nobody left standing: whoever is still on their feet is carrying somebody. It is said in the ship's log, on the mission report, and in the record. That is what the +2 is paid for.

## Found alongside

The outcome counted the objectives **attempted**, not the ones the mission had:

```js
const outcome = won === steps.length ? 'success' : ...
```

So a party that broke off after one success out of three read as a **clean sweep**. That was already true for a wiped-out team — the captain going down is simply a second way to break off, which is how it surfaced. Now measured against `template.steps.length`.

## Six tests

| test | why |
|---|---|
| the order line hears a captain saying they will go | the positive case, first — otherwise everything below tests a road nobody can drive down |
| and a landing party the captain leads knows they are on it | ✗ |
| and one they do not lead still does not take them | must not misfire |
| a captain who goes down is said to have gone down | ✗ |
| and an unhurt captain does not stop the mission | must not misfire — >20 clean parties in 60 |
| a mission broken off is not reported as a clean sweep | ✗ |

**Three separate controls, each confirming its own guard:** `captainLeads` forced false (fails 2 and 4), the wound consequence disabled (fails 4), the denominator put back to objectives attempted (fails 6).

The wound is a roll, so the suite scans seeds for a mission where it actually fired rather than pinning one — pinning a seed would pin every other roll in the mission with it. Breaking off early is proved separately from being wounded, because a captain hit on the third of three steps is a real case that looks identical from the outside.

## Verification

- `node --test tests/*.test.js` — **1142 pass** (1136 before).
- `tools/verify-app.mjs` — **349 checks, all passing**, run alone.
- `dist/` and the APK rebuilt. Permissions: `VIBRATE` only, no `INTERNET`.
