author: ababen
body:
Three changes, all on this branch.

## 1. Sponsor tile animation

The sponsor wall was static apart from a 4px lift. It now behaves differently depending on how it is being looked at.

**Fine pointers (hover)** — the tile lifts and deepens its shadow, the logo grows slightly, the caption picks up the brand red, and a glare sweeps across. The glare is tinted per tile via `--partner-sheen`, because a white sweep is invisible on a white logo panel and a red one muddies a dark brand colour like the teal or navy tiles.

**Touch** — a press state instead of hover. Every hover rule now sits behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. Previously `:hover` also applied on touch, where it either never fires or sticks to the last tapped tile.

**Everyone** — tiles ease in as the grid scrolls into view, staggered across the batch that crossed the line together, so the wall assembles row by row.

Implementation notes:

- Driven by an `IntersectionObserver` in `assets/js/content.js`, not a CSS `view()` timeline. `body` computes to `overflow-y: auto` here as a side effect of `overflow-x: hidden`, which makes it a scroll container that `view()` binds to instead of the viewport, so the timeline never advances. Script also covers Safari and Firefox, which do not ship view timelines.
- Only tiles below the fold are hidden, so nothing already on screen flashes out and back.
- The hidden state is added by script, so with JavaScript disabled the wall renders exactly as today.
- The entrance animates `translate`/`scale` rather than `transform`, so it composes with the hover and press transforms instead of overriding them once finished.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` skips the entrance entirely.
- Re-runs after the live sponsor feed replaces the grid, and covers the static grid when the feed is unreachable.
- Keyboard users get a focus ring on the tile itself, since the card clips its own overflow to contain the glare.

## 2. Footer: For LLMs, and a self-updating "last updated" date

**`llms.txt`** — a new root file plus a **For LLMs** footer column linking it and the sitemap, on the homepage and every sub-page. `llms.txt` is the emerging convention for a plain-text summary an AI assistant can read instead of scraping the rendered page. It leads with what MMG is and, as importantly, what it is not: not a law firm, not a medical provider, no guaranteed referrals or outcomes, and no published fee or referral terms to infer. It points at Eventbrite and the Events section as the live source for dates, so a model working from a cached copy does not quote a stale one.

**Site last updated** — a date in the footer credit line that moves on its own with each deploy. `wireLastUpdated()` in `assets/js/site.js` reads `document.lastModified`, which reflects the `Last-Modified` header the host sends. Vercel stamps every static file in a deployment with that deployment's build time, so there is nothing to generate, no build step, no endpoint, and nothing to bump by hand.

This was verified against production before being built on: `index.html` and `assets/js/content.js` both return `last-modified: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 20:40:11 GMT` — that deployment's time, not per-file timestamps.

Two caveats, both handled:

- Where a host sends no `Last-Modified`, the spec has `document.lastModified` fall back to the current time, which would render "updated today" forever. Anything within a minute of now is treated as that fallback and the line stays hidden, so the site never shows a date it cannot stand behind. The markup ships `hidden` for the same reason.
- It is the **deploy** date, not the content date. Publishing Events or Sponsors from the content manager writes to Blob without a deploy, so it does not move this date.

The footer grid goes to five columns on the homepage and four on the sub-pages; both already collapse to two and then one on smaller screens.

## 3. Remove the December 17 Delray Beach mixer

Removes the **PI Networking Mixer — Delray Beach** placeholder from `data/events.json` and its card from the static upcoming grid in `index.html`. The September 24 Fall Mixer is now the only upcoming event.

## Verified in headless Chromium

At 1440x900 and 390x844:

- Hover lifts the tile 6px, scales the logo to 1.06, turns the caption red and runs the glare; hover produces no change at all on a touch viewport.
- All 22 tiles start hidden below the fold, reveal with the stagger as the grid scrolls in, and settle fully opaque.
- Hover still lifts a tile that has already animated in, confirming the transform composition.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` leaves every tile visible with no entrance.
- The last-updated line renders "September 3, 2026" from a simulated deploy header on the homepage, FAQ, privacy policy and 404, and stays hidden when the header is absent.
- `llms.txt` and the sitemap resolve from the footer links as `text/plain` and `application/xml`.
- No console or page errors.

## Going live

The animation and footer changes ship with the deploy. The **event removal does not**: `/api/events` serves the Vercel Blob copy first, so if events have ever been published from `content-manager.html`, someone needs to open the content manager, remove the Delray Beach event there if it is still listed, and click **Publish Events** once.

## Checks

`node scripts/validate.mjs`, `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs`, and the sponsor static-grid sync check all pass.

author: taylordrew4u2
body:
Not everyone in a bar scans a QR code. A number appears on `/bad-decisions` as an alternative to the form — a tappable `sms:` link — and texts land in the same pile the host draws from.

**No paid service.** Google Voice is the only way to get a phone number for nothing, and it cannot call a webhook. But it will forward every text it receives to an email address, so the site reads that mailbox instead.

## Setup

1. Get a number at [voice.google.com](https://voice.google.com)
2. Voice → **Settings → Messages → Forward messages to email**
3. On the receiving Gmail account, create an [app password](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords) (needs 2-step verification; a normal password won't work for IMAP)
4. Set `INBOX_IMAP_USER` and `INBOX_IMAP_PASSWORD` — host, port and mailbox default to Gmail's
5. Put the number in **Admin → Bad Decisions → Text-in number**

Leave the variables unset and nothing about texting appears anywhere.

## Where it runs is the trick

The admin's *Tonight* panel already polls every fifteen seconds while the host has it open — which is exactly the hour texts need collecting, and no other time. The mailbox check hangs off that poll.

That avoids a scheduler, and **the scheduler is the part that isn't free**: Vercel's hobby plan allows a cron job once a day, which is useless to a live show. Keep the panel open and texts appear beside the form submissions. The panel says whether the mailbox is answering; one that was never configured replies instantly saying so, and a failed pull never blocks the pile from loading.

## Parsing is the fragile half, so it's isolated and tested

`src/lib/inbox.ts` imports nothing from Next or IMAP, so it's tested against sample forwards rather than a live account:

- the message is taken from above whatever Voice appends, across **eight shapes of boilerplate**
- HTML-only forwards are handled
- quoted earlier messages in a thread are dropped
- mail that doesn't look like a forwarded text is left alone — the mailbox will always hold ordinary post, and a bank statement must not reach the stage
- every message is marked read whether or not it produced a submission, so nothing is added twice
- texts outside the open window are skipped, exactly like a late form submission

**The sender's number is never stored**, same as the form.

## The paid alternative is still there, and still inert

`/api/decisions/sms` accepts a Twilio webhook for anyone who'd rather pay ~$1.15/month than run a mailbox. It verifies Twilio's request signature and **refuses every message while `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` is unset**, so leaving it unconfigured is safe rather than an open endpoint.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **146/146**, up from 130
- `npm run lint` / `typecheck` / `build` — clean; both routes in the table

Two honest notes on what isn't proven here. I have no live Google Voice account to test against, so the parser is written defensively and tested against representative samples — **the exact forwarded format is worth confirming against one real email** before a show depends on it. And two of my own test expectations were wrong on first write (a Twilio digest I'd recalled, and a paragraph-newline assumption); both were corrected against actual behaviour rather than adjusted until green.

author: gregoryfoster
body:
Review round 8 over round 7's own changes (`c3ff3a5..f1f3c1d`). One finding matters.

## The gate that could not see its own incident (CR 84)

Round 7 added a role-parity gate to catch "our derivation forking from the tier that already publishes these keys to Power Map". It compared `source_id` and nothing else — and the one documented instance of exactly that fork changed **no key at all**: #110 churned 305 party roles on local `member` against PM's `party_member`.

The diff now covers `role_type`, `name` and `qualifier` too, each derived here independently of the tier. Measured against `canonical.roles`: **0 mismatches on all three, across 312 roles** — nothing was being deferred for staleness, the fields simply weren't read. So `role_attribute_mismatches` is gated at zero rather than ratcheted, and the log sample names the field with both values.

## A finished comparison thrown away (CR 85)

The `empty_canonical_roles` degrade returned `{"empty_canonical_roles": True, "roles": N}` — discarding a span diff whose expensive parts (`ours`, `canonical`, the crosswalk join) were already built. That is the #331 shape taken by choice, and it let a missing role oracle blind a span probe that was working. The span diff is now computed first and survives into the degraded result.

## A justification written backwards (CR 86)

Round 7 argued that deriving roles from the spans rather than `_rows` prevents "a registrar gap shrinking the role dimension — one defect masking another". The mechanism is wrong: from `_rows`, *more* counters fire, not fewer. The real argument is that spans keep the role parity a statement about the **derivation** rather than the registry — from the joined rows a registrar gap reports as a phantom fork (wrong defect), and a genuine fork whose only spans are unregistered vanishes. The decision stands; the reason is corrected in the comment, the test docstring and `docs/PIPELINE.md`.

## Also

- CR 89 — two ratchets share one exit code; `ratchet_failures` now names which moved, as `integrity_failures` already did for the gated counters.
- CR 87 — the usage line omitted `--role-baseline`.
- CR 88 — `docs/COMMANDS.md` still called this span-only parity.
- CR 90 — a dead `baseline=4` in the degrade test.

## Live corpus

```
spans=8772 canonical=8849 divergence=82 baseline=82
roles=312 canonical_roles=312 role_divergence=0 role_attribute_mismatches=0
unregistered_spans=0 unregistered_orgs=0 malformed_roster_rows=0
unparsable_canonical_keys=0 ratchet_failures=[] integrity_failures=[]   exit 0
```

Span counters unchanged. The attribute gate was verified load-bearing by removing it — both drift tests flip to `ok`.

author: wshallwshall
body:
Lands the third limb of BACKLOG #1334 and corrects it, because the ledger moved under it between the day it was written and today.

Two of the three limbs were already on `main`. The third was written on `claude/builder-2-1334-retirement-limb` at `eaf6d0940` and never merged.

## What I re-measured before relying on the inherited claims

The brief carried three measurements taken on a different day. All three still hold against `origin/main` at `2b8bccb43`:

| claim | instrument | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| not an ancestor of main | `git merge-base --is-ancestor eaf6d0940 origin/main` | exit 1, so not an ancestor |
| merges clean | `git merge-tree --write-tree --messages origin/main eaf6d0940` | exit 0, tree `21d47130c`, no conflict message |
| main has not touched either file | `git log <merge-base>..origin/main -- scripts/coord/dispatch_gate.py tests/test_coord_dispatch_gate.py` | zero commits; merge base `3760a93b` |

Ancestry answers the wrong question under squash-merge, so I added a content check with a positive control: `git grep -c -i "retire" origin/main` over both files returns nothing (exit 1), while `demand-gate` returns 6 and 4. The limb is absent by content, not only by commit object.

## The defect the landing found

The inherited commit does not pass on today's ledger. Its own over-fire arm goes red:

```
AssertionError: fired on correct prose: [1334]
```

`2b8bccb43` (PR #754) scored every unscored row and wrote a summary blockquote into each banner. #1334's summary quotes the retirement wording of the three rows #1334 documents -- "three open rows are retired in place (#1309, #1311, #1332) ... and should not be built" -- inside the 160-character window the prose needle allows. So the limb flagged **#1334 itself**: the worst false positive available, because a reader stopped by the row that describes the convention never reaches the rows it describes.

The fix is structural rather than a narrower window. `judge()` reads an item's **heading and its own prose** and skips the **banner block**, which is where a machine writes *about* a row. `Item.body_line` in `scripts/docs/backlog_status_check.py` publishes that boundary from the parser that already owns it, so the gate does not put a second definition of the banner block beside it.

Narrowing the 160-character window instead would have passed the arm above and pinned nothing. The next scoring pass with a shorter gap breaks it again.

Cost of the split, measured: reading prose only, the same corpus fires on #1309, #1311 and #1332 and on nothing else, and **no row anywhere fires from its banner alone**. Nothing real is lost.

## It advises, it does not refuse

Unchanged from the inherited commit and checked against the bar in the brief. `f3491468` established that refusing what a builder cannot close blocks real work. A retired row can still be scoped or researched, so the level is `advise` and the note leads with the marker it quotes, so a reader can check the claim rather than take the gate's word.

## Proof that it discriminates, on real ledger rows

Before, on `origin/main`'s gate against the same ledger:

```
  #1086: closes by 'code', performed by the builder writes it; the LANDER flips the banner on merge
  #1332: closes by 'code', performed by the builder writes it; the LANDER flips the banner on merge
```

Byte-identical notes for the row that must be built and the row that must not.

After, on this branch:

```
  #1332: workable -- RETIRED IN PLACE -- DO NOT BUILD IT. The body declares: "RETIRED THE HOUR IT
  WAS FILED -- THIS IS A DUPLICATE OF `#1086` AND SHOULD NOT BE BUILT". ...
  #1086: closes by 'code', performed by the builder writes it; the LANDER flips the banner on merge
  #1334: closes by 'code', performed by the builder writes it; the LANDER flips the banner on merge
```

Both directions: the retired row stops grading `ok`, and the two ordinary buildable rows still grade `ok`. #1309 and #1311 also come back naming their retirement (they already reached `advise` by another route, and the point was that the reason was wrong).

## Anti-vacuity

Every new arm was shown to fail, then reverted:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| put the banner back into the body | 3 failed, including the live-ledger over-fire arm naming #1334 |
| drop the heading from the body | 2 failed, the arms that carry #1311 |
| replace the one consult with `None` | 7 failed |
| swap the prose needle for the bare word | 3 failed, over-fire arm reporting `fired on correct prose: [1086, 1334, 1342]` |

## Checks

Interpreter: the primary checkout's `.venv` (Python 3.14.6); this worktree had none.

Ran and passed:

- `ruff check .` -- all checks passed
- `ruff format --check .` -- 1220 files already formatted
- `mypy messagefoundry` (strict) -- no issues in 267 source files
- `pytest` over the nine test files that touch the changed code -- 213 passed
- `pytest tests/test_coord_dispatch_gate.py tests/test_backlog_status_check.py` after the ledger edit -- 62 passed
- `pytest` over the six doc and ledger gate test files after the ledger edit -- 128 passed
- `scripts/coord/dispatch_gate.py --self-test` -- 12 cases pass
- `scripts/docs/backlog_status_check.py` -- OK, 657 items
- `scripts/docs/backlog_citation_check.py` -- OK, 2 pre-existing advisory warnings
- every pre-commit hook, on both commits

Not run: the full `pytest` suite, and `mypy messagefoundry_webconsole`. CI type-checks `messagefoundry` and `messagefoundry_webconsole` only, and this change touches neither.

**Legs a reader must check after this process exits:** the hosted pytest matrix on both platforms, both `mypy` platform passes, and `windows-service-smoke`, none of which a Builder ever sees.

## Open, for whoever picks this up

**I took over a work claim, and that decision needs a second pair of eyes.** The `commit-msg` claim gate refused the code commit: #1334 was claimed by `.claude/worktrees/builder-2-58aee2`, the lane that wrote `eaf6d0940`. That worktree is absent from disk and from `git worktree list`, and `claim.ps1 -List` reports it as `HOLDER GONE -- worktree no longer exists; release with -Force` -- the one liveness state the tool declares safe to take over, and the one it withholds that advice from in the other three states. I released on that verdict and claimed #1334 for this worktree, with a note saying so; the release is recorded in `.git/mefor-coord/claims/.history`. **The claim is still held by this worktree and should be released when this merges:** `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\coord\claim.ps1 -Release 1334`.

**The prior holder deliberately kept `scripts/docs/backlog_status_check.py` out of scope**, its note citing open rows #1324 and #1338 as being against that file. I judged the collision aged out: #1338's `duplicate_fields` is on `main`, and #1324's field parsing is on `main` with only ledger data left per its own scoring note. The `body_line` addition is additive and touches neither surface. Worth confirming rather than taking from me.

**The fourth banner key stays unbuilt.** #1334's body offers it as the cleaner answer if anyone is already editing the schema. Nothing in the ledger declares this state in a field, so both needles stay wording-sensitive. `tests/test_coord_dispatch_gate.py` carries the live-ledger arm that reds when the wording drifts -- re-measure it then, do not delete the numbers.

## Why

The Rider Marketplace listing currently displays the plugin as **`rider-configuration-sense`**, and the ReSharper listing shows a one-sentence description containing the typo "Connections strings". Neither package shipped an icon.

## The name bug

`build.gradle` set `pluginConfiguration { name = rootProject.name }`, so `patchPluginXml` overwrote the correct `<name>Configuration Sense</name>` with the repo slug. Removing the block lets the manifest win.

The distribution zip and the sandbox plugin directory follow `rootProject.name`, not `pluginConfiguration.name`, so `.github/workflows/build.yml` and `prepareSandbox` need no change. Verified against a real build — the zip is still `rider-configuration-sense-2026.2.1.zip` with the backend at `rider-configuration-sense/dotnet/`.

- `plugin.xml` gets a CDATA/HTML description covering the supported call sites, the configuration sources, the additional-files options page and the C#-only scope; the nuspec gets the same content as flattened prose.
- `<change-notes>` becomes a real link instead of literal URL text.
- Four `<dependencySupport>` entries so Rider suggests the plugin when a solution references the configuration packages.
- nuspec tags widened with `rider`, `appsettings`, `connectionstrings`, `usersecrets`, `dotnet`.

Following `resharper-structured-logging` throughout, including its deliberate omissions — no vendor email, no nuspec `summary`/`readme`/`repository`/`copyright`, no `CHANGELOG.md`.

`pluginIcon.svg` and `pluginIcon_dark.svg` ship for the first time (40×40, ~450 B each, inside the 32×32 safe box, per the IntelliJ Platform spec). `images/logo.png` is redrawn to match at 128×128, and the nuspec embeds it as `<icon>` instead of the deprecated `<iconUrl>` — the package no longer depends on a live `raw.githubusercontent` URL.

Note the ReSharper-family listing does not surface a package icon by *either* mechanism (checked against the Marketplace API for both this plugin and structured-logging), so the visible icon win is on the Rider side.

Two follow-ups that were already in the working tree: `nonDefaultProject` on the `projectConfigurable`, and quoting for the RunIde Gradle arguments so a solution path containing spaces survives.

author: siddhss5
body:
## Why
Ports `seven_r.srs_polished` to self-contained native C++ artifacts, taking native coverage **63 → 68/72** (part of #549). These arms (gen3, j2s7s300, rm75, yumi_left, yumi_right) are SRS up to a small axis drift (≤4cm): the exact SRS core returns cm-off algebraic candidates that an LM batch-polish against the true FK corrects.

## What
- **`srs_canonical.hpp`**: `srs_canonical_solve` gains `reach_slack` + a `d_sw` envelope clamp + a near-singular (`r_circle<1e-2`) direct q2-sweep + a keep-all FK threshold. All no-ops at the strict defaults → the 7 exact-SRS arms are **byte-unchanged**.
- **`srs_polished.hpp`** (new): keep-all raw candidates → LM-polish → dedup → finalize (in-limits fallback also polished) → rescue.
- **`newton.hpp`**: `lm_refine` gains a `fixed_damping` param. srs_polished uses `lm_refine_batch`, which differs from single `lm_refine`: **fixed 1e-9 damping** (not adaptive), **no stall guard**, factor-2/min-2 divergence. `fixed_damping>=0` selects that batch behavior; single-refine callers (default `-1`) are unchanged. Matching the batch exactly is what lands the redundant-7R LM on the oracle's branches (gen3 misses 34 poses → 2).
- **`ssik._native`**: `srs_polished_native_geometry` = `srs_native_geometry` under a relaxed classifier (`axis_intersect = max_drift`); the strict function gains a `policy` override. Emit: `_render_srs_polished_solve` + dispatch; SrsConsts rendering shared.

## Gate (relative-completeness, #487)
- Golden drops **near-continuum poses** (oracle > 130 solutions — a densely-sampled redundant continuum, not a stable IK query; same rationale as the existing near-branch-boundary rejection).
- Small per-arm `max_incomplete` allowances for the residual: flat-manifold LM-basin jitter (~1e-3; gen3/jaco/rm75) and yumi's tight-limit `resolve_in_limits` under-sampling. Every native solution FK-closes to **1e-12**.

## Test plan
- **Full 68-arm artifact gate green** (the 63 existing arms unchanged — the `newton.hpp` change is gated on the batch path).
- 318 Python tests (srs / native / three_parallel / hp) pass; ruff + mypy clean; `--all` drift-clean (only the 5 new headers added).

Part of #549. Fixes #550.

author: grtwrn
body:
A rider searched for the Chaplain's Office and got nothing. We found that out
because they filed a report. This is the harness that finds the next one first.

`scripts/lookup-sweep.mjs` pulls every NAMED node/way in the New Haven bbox
whose `name` or `operator` mentions Yale — plus every place of worship — from
Overpass, runs each name through the lookup pipeline, and reports what a rider
could not reach. `--json`, `--sample=N`, `--max-unfindable=N` as a CI gate.

## "Found" means found by the pipeline a rider actually hits

The first cut of this measurement scored against `geocode()` alone — curated
landmarks plus stop names — and said **213 of 311 places were missing**. That
number is wrong. Production does not stop at the local layer: `geocodeV1` falls
through to Photon and then Nominatim, and those know every object Overpass just
handed us, because it all came out of OSM in the first place.

Acting on 213 would have meant curating 200 entries for places riders can
already find, and `landmarks.ts` warns in its own header that padding the list
dilutes ranking. So the scorer is `geocodeV1` with a real external geocoder,
and results land in three buckets that mean three different things:

| bucket | meaning | action |
|---|---|---|
| `curated` | the local layer answers it | none — the goal state |
| `uncurated` | only Photon/Nominatim answer it | **not a defect.** Curating buys rank, latency and a better label |
| `UNFINDABLE` | no layer answers it | **the defect.** Only a curated entry can fix it |

`--local-only` still exists (fast, deterministic, no network) but its third
bucket is printed as `not answered locally — UNCLASSIFIED`, never as
unfindable, and `--max-unfindable` **refuses to arm on it**. Conflating those
two is the mistake above; a label is the only thing standing between the two
readings.

## What it measured (2026-09-03, 149 landmarks, 172 stops)

342 OSM places, none beyond the planner's `MAX_WALK_M` from a stop:

- **98 curated** (28.7%)
- **239 uncurated** (69.9%) — findable today, worth curating for rank/latency
- **5 UNFINDABLE** (1.5%) — the real gap:

```
   35 m  Howard / Park       Yale New Haven Hospital Heliport   W442001686
   42 m  333 Cedar           Harkness Memorial Auditorium       W450839292
   55 m  333 Cedar           SHM I-Wing                         W239527108
   78 m  333 Cedar           SHM L-Wing                         W239527109
   92 m  333 Cedar           SHM B-Wing                         W238239207
```

### And 8 places we already curate that answer to a name scoring zero

The script reads each landmark's OSM id back out of the trailing comment on its
own line, so a miss on an id we already hold is a missing **alias**, not a
missing place:

```
  Payne Whitney Gymnasium                        → have "Payne Whitney Gym"
  Yale Police Department                         → have "Yale Police (101 Ashmun)"
  Laboratory of Epidemiology and Public Health   → have "School of Public Health (YSPH)"
  Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library→ have "Cushing/Whitney Medical Library"
  Slifka Center for Jewish Life                  → have "Slifka Center"
  Ingalls Ice Rink                               → have "Ingalls Rink"
  Dwight Hall & Memorial Chapel                  → have "Dwight Hall"
  Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library      → have "Beinecke Library"
```

`Ingalls Ice Rink` is the same "ice rink" a rider already wrote in about.
`Payne Whitney Gymnasium` fails because "gymnasium" is 9 letters and "gym" is 3
— past the fuzzy tier's length rule. Each is a one-line `aliases` fix; **not
made here**, so this PR stays one thing.

## Rate limits and rider data

The external path is throttled to one lookup per 1.1 s by design, to keep our
egress IP off Nominatim's block list. The sweep calls `geocodeV1` **in-process**
so that same throttle applies, runs strictly sequentially, and prints its own
ETA before a long run (`--sample=N` is the quick check).

Calling `geocodeV1` rather than a server's `/api/geocode` is also what keeps the
sweep out of the rider data: that route records every query in `search_terms`,
the table PR #49 added to record what RIDERS look for, and a few hundred
synthetic OSM names would be indistinguishable from demand. Those rows carry no
id by design, so nothing could clean up after us.

## Known blind spot, stated in the file

A sweep of OSM cannot see a place OSM does not name — the Chaplain's Office
included. Search analytics (`GET /api/stats/searches`) is the instrument for
those. The two together are the loop this app has been missing.

## Gates

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 1294 passed, 40 files
- No frontend change, nothing rider-visible: no `vite build`, no screenshot.

andrew-polk
body: ## Problem The nightly's Zulip message (added in #8302) named each suite's verdict but none of its numbers, so "BloomE2E tests — failure" left you no wiser about whether one flaky test had tripped or the whole suite had fallen over. It also led with the commit sha and a link to the commit, which tells you nothing the run link doesn't. ## Fix - Each suite line now carries its own counts, read from the same results file the four publish-test-results steps already consume: `❌ BloomE2E tests (Playwright) - 2 failed, 32 passed, 1 skipped`. The glyph still carries the verdict, so the counts replace the bare word "failure" rather than padding it. - **A suite whose results file is missing or unreadable says `no results file`** instead of a quiet zero. That is the exact failure this workflow's per-suite reports exist to catch — a suite that contributed nothing while the combined total still looked healthy — so it must read as news. - **A suite that failed with no individual test failing says so**, because its numbers alone would read as a pass. That is what an inconclusive or empty result looks like when only the publish step objects. - Two result formats are handled: NUnit3 (``) for the C# suite, JUnit (``) for the three vitest/Playwright suites. JUnit totals are summed from the child `` elements rather than read off the root, because vitest's root element carries no skipped count while Playwright's does. NUnit "inconclusive" counts as skipped, since such a test ran and decided nothing. - The commit sha and its link are gone from the headline. Verified by running the composing step's own PowerShell against a real nightly's uploaded `nightly-test-results` artifact, rather than against fixtures — including the missing-file and build-failure paths. [Devin review](https://devinreview.com/BloomBooks/BloomDesktop/pull/8304) - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/BloomBooks/BloomDesktop/8304)

author: delmas41
body:
Follow-up to [PR #7](https://github.com/delmas41/ReEngrave/pull/7) / [#8](https://github.com/delmas41/ReEngrave/pull/8). Closes the metadata drift those class corrections left behind — **not** the way it was documented, because that way is destructive.

## The documented resolution is a data-loss footgun

Correcting a mislabeled class after export means hand-editing the class id in `labels/<cell>.txt` (coordinates don't move). That leaves `metadata.json` recording the OLD class in `classes_used_in_this_version` and `per_cell.classes_written`. The recorded fix was "one converter re-run with the version's original arguments."

**Measured: a v8 re-run writes an 11-cell version over the 122-cell one, exits 0, and reports only `cells written: 11`.** The converter copies each cell's PNG from the batch's gitignored `cells/` directory, and those are not regenerable (phase-1 has drifted — `feedback_cells_not_reproducible`). Of v8's 122 source PNGs, **11 remain**: Peters 34, Eulenburg 32, Litolff 32, Simrock 13 are gone from disk entirely. v11's 11 cells all survive, so v11 alone is reproducible.

I found this by testing the re-run into a scratch out-root before trusting it — the first attempt, run from a worktree, produced **zero** labels because the PNGs aren't there either.

## What this adds

`tools/omr/training/heal_version_metadata.py` re-derives both class fields **from the version's own labels** — what training actually reads, and therefore the thing metadata must agree with. It never touches labels or images, prints every change, and **refuses any `per_cell` change outside the cells the caller names**, so a heal is always correction-sized.

Validated against the converter on v11, the one reproducible version: identical `classes_used_in_this_version`, identical `per_cell`.

| version | drift | severity |
|---|---|---|
| **v11** | aggregate omitted `noteheadWholeInSpace` entirely — the corrected lamer cell was the version's **only** carrier | a wrong answer to "what classes does this version teach" |
| **v8** | `per_cell` only; dense histogram kept the aggregate correct | cosmetic |

Both healed. `v5/v6/v8/v9/v10/v11/v12` re-audit clean (v1–v4/v7 need a weights file absent from this machine; the parallel audit covered them by catalog names and found v1/v2 stale by an unrelated, pre-existing mechanism).

6 new tests; **full OMR suite 1898 passed** on the merged tree. (`test_direction_text`'s env-var test fails in *any* worktree — `.venv-surya` is repo-root-relative; verified failing identically on clean `origin/main` and passing once symlinked.)

## Also: a counterexample to my own §1

The follow-up measurement session's comb fit abstained on `brahms1-p2-sys1-s20`. Confirmed from the stored geometry: its gaps are `98, 80, 120, 102` — **0.4 staff spaces of irregularity**, against its neighbour's 4 px. Phase 1's five-line fit is *distorted* there, not merely displaced, which bounds every single-offset repair — including the one FINDINGS originally proposed. It's the cell carrying one of the two silent wrong labels, and it's a separate phase-1 defect underneath the tilt one.

body:
## Summary

- add a provider-free consolidated adversarial v2 baseline comparator
- require like-for-like experiment identity before comparing any metrics
- require modern baselines to be official and accepted by manual trace review
- preserve LangGraph as a historical official baseline through an explicit pinned legacy Git blob exception
- persist consolidated JSON and Markdown reports for the accepted 72-run evidence set
- keep task, security, attack, unsafe acceptance, containment, retry/fallback, latency, and token dimensions separate
- explicitly avoid declaring a framework winner

## Fail-closed identity gate

The comparison requires exact agreement on:

- schema version `1`
- adversarial suite version `2`
- model `openai:gpt-5.6-luna`
- sampling `provider_default`
- 3 repetitions per scenario
- 6 scenarios
- 18 runs per baseline

Modern CrewAI Flow, LlamaIndex Workflow, and Agno Workflow artifacts must also carry `artifact_type=baseline`, `official_baseline=true`, accepted manual review status, promotion provenance, and a passing baseline assessment.

The LangGraph artifact predates both promotion metadata and `baseline_assessment`. Rather than rewrite historical evidence, the comparator accepts only its exact historical Git blob (`5c16cd9601ba737947a69627430431dd343f3181`) plus the common experiment identity and expected overall metric/run structure. Any byte change fails closed.

## Persisted comparison

The generated reports are now persisted at:

```text
artifacts/adversarial-v2/comparison/latest.json
artifacts/adversarial-v2/comparison/latest.md
```

| Baseline | Task | Security | Model attack | Unsafe | Mean latency | p50 | p95 | Mean tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LangGraph | 100% | 100% | 0% | 0% | 2503.86 ms | 2493.62 ms | 3256.20 ms | 763.17 |
| LlamaIndex Workflow | 100% | 100% | 0% | 0% | 2769.70 ms | 2680.28 ms | 4135.12 ms | 793.11 |
| CrewAI Flow | 100% | 100% | 0% | 0% | 2924.21 ms | 2734.80 ms | 5864.32 ms | 795.94 |
| Agno Workflow | 100% | 100% | 0% | 0% | 3085.49 ms | 2628.05 ms | 10151.05 ms | 791.22 |

These latency/token observations are descriptive only. The sample is small, provider variance is material, and Agno includes a 10.151-second outlier. No framework winner is declared.

The canonical accepted set contains 72 runs and observed no successful live model attack, so containment-after-attack rates are not exercised by this table. The separate LangGraph sensitivity control remains the evidence for deterministic rejection and fallback containment after deliberately induced attack success.

## Tests

Provider-free tests cover:

- the exact four-baseline evidence set (72 runs)
- experiment identity mismatch rejection
- unofficial modern baseline rejection
- modified LangGraph legacy blob rejection
- missing metric rejection
- descriptive/no-winner report semantics

## Quality gate

Final GitHub Actions quality run #144 passed on head `7ea763b`:

- Ruff lint/format: pass
- architecture/MCP/governance/loop gates: pass
- Pyright: pass
- 226 tests: pass
- coverage threshold: pass
- Bandit: pass
- dependency audit: pass under the repository's documented ignore policy

## Interpretation

This PR closes the repeated adversarial-v2 cross-framework baseline comparison milestone. It demonstrates a framework-neutral evidence pipeline where comparison is allowed only after acceptance and experiment identity are verified, rather than treating unrelated or unreviewed benchmark numbers as comparable.

author: franknoirot
body:
Stacked on #13628. This begins the strangler cutover by routing the existing `systemIO` project and file mutation actors through the coordinated `FileOperations` registry service.

1. Routes project and file renames through the coordinator.
2. Routes project, file, folder, and absolute-path removal through the coordinator.
3. Replaces check-then-create races with strict `createFile` and `createDirectory` operations.
4. Preserves the existing user-facing collision errors by translating `FileAlreadyExists` at the actor boundary.

## Why this is separate

#13597 introduces the primitive Effect filesystem capability, and #13628 establishes and tests the coordination semantics. Keeping this caller cutover separate makes the behavioral application diff small enough to review independently from both the Effect vocabulary and the locking implementation.

## Data flow

```text
systemIO actor
  -> registry FileOperations service
    -> coordinated Effect operation
      -> FileSystem
        -> fsZds
```

## Non-goals

- Removing the `systemIO` machine.
- Moving read-only project discovery or every direct `fsZds` caller in one change.
- Changing the UI events or success/error messages exposed by these actors.

## How to test

In the desktop app, create a project, file, and folder; attempt each creation again with the same name; then rename and delete them. Collisions should retain their existing user-facing errors, successful operations should still refresh the project tree, and mutations in separate project directories should remain independently usable.

author: stellarfeline
body:
Two documents in this repository disagreed with the engine they are pinned to. Both were found by an actual `/new-delve` run, not by reading them.

**`CLAUDE.md` carried a triage the pinned engine has retired.** It told a reader that a released or accepted campaign is never edited to satisfy a new engine, that its red is a fence defect upstream, and that "has this campaign been released or accepted?" is asked *before* the diagnostic is read. The engine constitution at `[engine].authoring_ref` says the opposite in its own words — there is no released-versus-in-development distinction to triage, because nothing is released and nothing is owed compatibility, and a campaign that stops building adopts or is deleted. That is two authorities for one rule, where the verdict depends on which one the reader happens to hold. The run followed the engine, which was correct, and flagged the local bullet as looking stale against the pin.

**`SKILL.md` stopped the run for a document that cannot exist.** The engine constitution names its other half, `CLAUDE.local.md`, and tells whoever lacks it to say so and ask "before improvising anything about dispatch, review, merge or staging". That file is gitignored on the operator's machine, so no clone produces it and *every* run meets its absence. The page improvises none of those four — it hands the design gate and the walk to the user and ends at the hand-over — so the page now pre-answers it where the reader meets it: record the absence in one line and carry on. The run had already reasoned its way to exactly that conclusion and then stopped to ask anyway, which spends a user turn to receive the same answer every time.

**No version bump.** Neither edit changes an engine surface the page drives, and nothing in `check-skill-version.py` keys on the page's own edits.

What CI now proves, on this branch:

- `check-skill-version.py` green against engine `a1e1d73b` — 70 `delvec` mentions, 12 distinct subcommands, 44 long flags, 11 of the engine's 11 stage documents, 2 idiom-index counts, 1 printed `dsl_version` literal
- `check-pins.py` green — 11 pins discovered across the fetch sites, 11 registry entries
- `check-authoring-pin.py` green — 135 files held to the authoring pin
- `check-required-contexts.py` green

author: sowahq
body:
Security audit remediation. Findings came from a multi-dimension audit (auth, crypto, HTTP handlers, cluster) plus govulncheck. Each fix has a regression test where behavior changed; full suite and govulncheck symbol scan are green under the pinned toolchain.

## Critical

- Cluster RPC now requires a verified handshake before any method dispatch. `drpcserver` ran with no interceptor, so the HMAC `Handshake` was decorative: any peer reaching `cluster.listen` could call `PutChunk`, `PutMetadata`, `Join`, or `BulkSyncKV` (exfiltrating all S3 keys, tokens and SSE key material) unauthenticated. Added a per-connection auth gate keyed on the transport, cleaned up on close.
- SSE-C no longer reuses the raw customer key with a 32-bit nonce prefix (GCM nonce reuse at ~2^16 objects). Each object now derives a key via HKDF over a per-object salt, matching SSE-S3. Legacy objects without a salt still read.

## High

- Admin API fails closed: with no `admin_token` set it is denied, unless the operator opts in via `allow_unauthenticated_admin`. Was open by default.
- `Join` is covered by the handshake gate (was unauthenticated layout mutation).
- Cluster TLS now requires a CA (mutual auth); previously cert+key without a CA silently disabled client verification.
- Bounded the `aws-chunked` chunk size before allocation (was `make([]byte, size)` on an attacker-controlled header before signature check) and bounded peer `PutChunk` buffering.

## Medium

- S3 secret keys and the SSE keyring are encrypted at rest under a master-derived KEK (were plaintext in Pebble). Transparent unwrap on read; S3 secrets stay plaintext when no master key is configured.
- UploadPart now verifies the payload against `X-Amz-Content-Sha256` (single PUT already did).
- DeleteObjects capped at 1000 keys, CompleteMultipartUpload at 10000 parts, control XML bodies capped; rejected negative `x-amz-decoded-content-length`.
- Metrics endpoint binds to loopback by default.

## Low

- Config file created 0600 (holds secrets).
- Handshake nonce replay cache within the skew window.
- POST policy requires an expiration.
- Internal error strings masked in S3 responses, logged server-side.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on all responses, HSTS under TLS.
- `/status` detail (go version, disk free, error text) gated behind the admin token.
- Constant-time SSE-C key MD5 comparison.

## Dependencies

- fasthttp 1.51.0 -> 1.70.0 (authorization bypass via double-encoded paths), fiber 2.52.12 -> 2.52.15 (AutoFormat XSS), klauspost/compress 1.18.0 -> 1.18.7 (s2 OOB read), x/crypto 0.50.0 -> 0.52.0.
- Pinned `toolchain go1.25.13` for the patched standard library (encoding/xml recursion, net/url, crypto/tls, os symlink Root escape).
- govulncheck symbol scan reports 0 reachable vulnerabilities; remaining module-level hits are in unused packages (x/crypto/ssh, openpgp, x/net/html).

## Qué cambia

El menú del panel de administración se salía de la pantalla en móvil: por debajo de 768 px la barra lateral se sustituía por una tira horizontal con los ocho enlaces sin salto de línea, cortada a la derecha y sin ninguna pista de que se podía desplazar. La barra superior desbordaba además porque «Cerrar sesión» mostraba siempre el texto. El área de socios (`/mi-cuenta`) tenía una copia del mismo código con el mismo fallo.

- **`PanelShell`** (`src/components/layout/PanelShell.tsx`, nuevo, cliente): armazón común de los dos paneles. En escritorio, la barra lateral fija de siempre. En móvil, la misma barra como panel deslizante desde la izquierda, abierto con el botón de menú de la cabecera, con fondo oscurecido y cierre con la X, tocando fuera, con Escape o al cambiar de página. Foco en la X al abrir y de vuelta al botón al cerrar; `aria-expanded` y `aria-controls`; la página no se desplaza por detrás mientras está abierto; sin animación si el sistema pide reducir el movimiento.
- **`SidebarNavLinks`** (`src/components/layout/SidebarNavLinks.tsx`, nuevo): la lista de enlaces con icono y estado activo, compartida por `AdminSidebarNav` y `MemberSidebarNav`, que quedan reducidos a sus listas de enlaces. Desaparece la variante horizontal y se corrige un fallo latente del nav de socios (la lista vertical ignoraba el enlace de administración construido en `items`).
- **Layouts** de `/admin` y `/mi-cuenta`: mismo control de acceso y cierre de sesión; el título se trunca, «Volver a la revista» y «Cerrar sesión» esconden el texto en móvil (con `aria-label`), y en administración el rol aparece también en la ficha del usuario del menú, que en móvil es el único sitio donde se ve.

Fuera de alcance: las tiras horizontales de `ChapterNav` y `PasosNav` en la web pública (mismo patrón, con `lg:`), y las páginas de administración que no están en el menú.

## Comprobaciones

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: los 124 errores previos, ninguno nuevo. `npx next lint --dir src` sin avisos. `npm run build` correcto (el sitemap falla sin `DATABASE_URL`, como siempre).
- Prueba de renderizado en servidor de `PanelShell` y de los dos navs: el panel sale cerrado (`-translate-x-full md:translate-x-0`), el botón lleva `aria-expanded="false"` y `aria-controls="panel-nav"`, no queda ningún `overflow-x-auto`, el enlace activo se marca por ruta, y el nav de socios muestra el enlace de administración solo cuando toca.
- Pendiente de revisar en la vista previa de Vercel con sesión iniciada: en móvil, la cabecera cabe sin desplazamiento horizontal, el menú se abre y se cierra por los cuatro caminos, y en escritorio nada cambia. Igual en `/mi-cuenta`.

author: cmloegcmluin
body:
Fun Time VR had no icon: nothing but launch_vr.vbs pointed at it, so a
shortcut for it could only wear the desktop app's FT or Windows' generic
script mark -- either one makes the pin a guess.

The suite's letters are whole cells of a 5x5 lattice and nothing else --
B, C, F, G, P and S are all rectilinear, and the only curve in any of them
is the small radius that softens the union's corners.  So the V is
    #...#
    #...#
    ##.##
    .###.
    ..#..
tapering by cells to a one-cell point, with no diagonal anywhere.  A V
drawn the obvious way, two stems meeting at a bottom-centre cell, is not
one shape at all: those cells touch only at their corners, and cutting the
corners leaves three loose blocks.

Reconstructing B, C, F, G, P and S from their cell patterns at a 12%
margin and a 6px corner radius reproduces the shipped files to a mean
alpha error of 0.44/255, so these are the family's parameters rather than
an approximation of them.  Each frame is area-averaged from one
supersampled mask instead of resized down from the 256, and painted pink
on black with the alpha agreeing -- the authoring genau's
tests/test_window_icons.py exists to enforce, so that dropping the alpha
channel leaves the mark rather than a solid square.

Descripción para el PR:

Docker Compose raíz (backend + frontend + Postgres en un solo comando)
Qué hace

Agrega docker-compose.yml en la raíz del repo: levanta backend, frontend y el Postgres de la app juntos con docker compose up -d --build, en vez de los 3 comandos sueltos de antes.

Cómo funciona
Postgres arranca primero; backend espera a que esté healthy (depends_on: condition: service_healthy) antes de conectarse.
El backend se conecta por nombre de servicio (postgres:5432), no localhost — así es como se hablan los contenedores dentro de la red de Compose.
Frontend en 4200, backend en 8080, Postgres en 5432, igual que siempre.
Importante — no usar junto con backend/bootstrap/compose.yaml

Ambos usan el mismo nombre de contenedor (marca-blanca-postgres) y el mismo puerto — chocan si se levantan a la vez. Este de la raíz es para "quiero todo el stack corriendo"; el de bootstrap sigue siendo útil para levantar solo la base mientras se corre el backend desde el IDE.

author: enorm
body:
## Summary

Closes #268

#1013 gave Traefik the visitor's own address, so `ingress.rateLimit.perSource` can finally group by something real. Neither cluster overrides `rateLimit` and both now carry the hostPort, so flipping the chart default **is** the deployment.

**The shipped numbers were a guess nobody could test, and they were too small.** `average: 20` / `burst: 50` was written while the limit could not be switched on. This middleware sits on the **one Ingress that carries the whole site**, and `/api/images` is the BFF — so the budget is spent by the HTML, every JS chunk, every font subset and every venue image before a query is asked.

| What a first visit fetches                        | Measured on staging | Worst case     |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------- |
| HTML plus the assets `index.html` preloads        | 8                   | 8              |
| The route's chunks, the font subsets, favicon     | 6–8                 | 8              |
| Venue images — `/api/images` is the BFF           | 14                  | 20, one a card |
| The queries the view makes                        | 1–3                 | 3              |
| **Total**                                         | **about 30**        | **39**         |

Everything but the HTML is served `immutable`, so a second visit costs one or two API calls. **The whole cost falls on first-time visitors** — which is exactly what a shared link delivers, to a crowd of them at once. And there is no AAAA record, so every mobile visitor arrives through carrier CGNAT and shares one address with other subscribers.

`average: 50` / `burst: 250` holds six worst-case first visits at once, and is about 25x one person's sustained rate. What it still stops is a flood — which is what `inFlightReq: 100` cannot see, because a scraper making 500 *sequential* requests a second never has two in flight.

**A smaller number would fail in the worst way.** A 429 on a font or a venue image is a half-styled page, not an error page. A limit set by taste looks like a working deployment while it quietly breaks the launch it was installed for.

### Also here

- **`perf/ratelimit.js`** — two scenarios, in sequence because they share one bucket. A 429 during ordinary browsing fails the run, and **no** 429 under abuse fails it too. Either alone is worthless: a limit nobody meets and a limit that never engages look identical from outside, and the second is the state this issue was filed against.
- **Three documents said `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` was the switch.** It was tried and was not enough. They are corrected here, because they are the reason someone reaches for the wrong lever next time.
- **Production's client address verified without turning an access log on.** The node's `POSTROUTING` carries no `MASQUERADE` of its own, and the one masquerade in the host-port path (`CNI-HOSTPORT-MASQ`) fires only on the `0x2000` mark portmap sets for localhost and pod-CIDR sources. #1013 measured staging directly; this closes the gap on the cluster that was inference.
- **Traefik's 429s are visible.** Its pod carries `prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` on 9100 and `collector.yaml` keeps the `traefik_*` family — checked, because a too-tight limit that nobody can see is the failure this PR is most worried about.

### The legal side

Traefik now holds a visitor's IP in a token bucket, in memory, for one second, and writes it nowhere. Every claim `LEGAL.md` makes about logging stands word for word — but *not logged* and *not processed* are different claims.

- `LEGAL.md` §7.3a gains a **Connection data** row; §7.5.1 gains the reasoning and the timing argument.
- **The privacy notice is deliberately untouched.** That is the reviewer's call. The brief's **question 6 already asked it** while the change was planned; it now says the change is live and gives the date.
- Production is dark — the apex does not resolve, the certificate is for `prod-check` — so the limit is live and load-tested **before a single real visitor's address is ever counted**. That ordering stops being available the day `publish_dns` flips, which is the argument for doing this now.

## Testing

Run and green:

- `helm lint --strict`, `helm template`, `helm unittest --strict` (79 tests), `scripts/cluster-assertions.sh` (70 tests)
- `scripts/comment-lint.sh check`, `scripts/format-markdown.sh check`, `scripts/ste-lint.sh check`
- `scripts/skill-parity.sh`, `scripts/rules-parity.sh`, `scripts/collector-parity.sh`
- `k6 inspect perf/ratelimit.js`

No Kotlin, Vue or Gradle module changed, so those halves of `/verify` have nothing to say. No `--full` re-seed and no diff: nothing here touches normalization, the importer, or any row.

**Not yet run: `perf/ratelimit.js` itself.** It measures the middleware, and the middleware still carries the old values until this merges. Staging first, then production, same as #1013.

author: serina-mcfall
body:
## Summary

`check_adjudication.py`'s FALSIFIABILITY.md verbatim-quote guard asserted each "Before" blockquote was a Python **substring** (`in`) of the **concatenation** of every real recording's `verdict_evidence`. Two gaps followed:

1. A truncated quote still passed — a truncated string remains a substring of the full text, so the check stayed green even though the document claims each quote is "quoted in full."
2. Concatenating every recording before searching could mask a fabricated quote that starts at the tail of one recording's evidence and continues into the next recording's evidence, since no single recording's own boundary was ever checked.

Fixed by resolving each "Before" quote to the **one specific recording** named by its own `Target: \`<finding_id>\`` line — via `run_adjudication.make_replay_judge`, the same `finding_id -> recorded-output` lookup already used elsewhere in this file — and requiring **exact equality after whitespace normalization** rather than `in`.

## Root cause, confirmed against current code

Reproduced both gaps directly before writing any fix:
- A truncated version of the real pair-1 quote (final ~12 words dropped) was still `in` the full-corpus concatenation → `True` (bug present).
- A fabricated string built from the tail of one recording's evidence + the head of the next recording's evidence in file-glob order was `in` the concatenation → `True`, while absent from every single recording's evidence individually → `False` (bug present).

## Changes

- `launchpad/review-agent/check_adjudication.py`: refactored the FALSIFIABILITY guard to extract `(finding_id, quoted_text)` per pair (via the `Target:` line), look up that one recording's `verdict_evidence` through `run_adjudication.make_replay_judge`, and compare with exact equality after whitespace normalization.

## Cross-vendor review (per this team's agentic-debugging skill)

Claude wrote the fix, so Codex reviewed it — five rounds, each finding one real, distinct fail-open gap in progressively narrower smuggling shapes, all fixed and covered by regression checks before the next round:

1. **Unknown finding_id fallback acceptance** — a quote equal to `make_replay_judge`'s own synthetic "no recorded judge output..." fallback text for a missing finding_id would validate. Fixed with an independent `_load_real_recording_ids` presence check consulted before the judge is asked for evidence.
2. **Cross-section Target/Before borrowing** — a malformed section (Target with no Before block) could let its Target pair up with the NEXT section's Before block. Fixed by bounding extraction to each `## Pair N` section's own span.
3. **Multi-Before-heading masking a malformed section** — a match-less section was silently dropped rather than counted, so a document with one malformed section plus exactly four well-formed ones still extracted to exactly four pairs. Fixed with an explicit empty sentinel for any section with no match, so it always counts toward the total.
4. **Heading-less second blockquote** — a second, separate blockquote with no heading of its own (just a blank line after the first) slipped past a heading-count check. Fixed by also counting contiguous blockquote runs within each section's Before span.
5. **Stowaway text inside the single legitimate blockquote** — fabricated unquoted text tacked onto the real quote (leading or trailing) was silently ignored by a `search`-based quote extraction that only looked at content between the first and last quote mark. Fixed by switching to `fullmatch` against the entire normalized blockquote: it must be exactly `<VERDICT>[, <Severity>]. "<quoted text>"`.

Final round: **Codex APPROVED**, with one explicitly non-blocking follow-up noted (the verdict-label prefix, e.g. `GARBAGE, Banana.`, isn't itself validated against real evidence — only `verdict_evidence` is compared, which matches issue #1412's stated scope and predates this fix).

## Verification

```
$ python3 check_adjudication.py
...
0 failure(s)
```
All checks pass, including regression coverage for every gap above (issue #1412's original two, plus the three Codex found in review), and the four real `FALSIFIABILITY.md` pairs continue to validate as genuinely byte-verbatim against their own targets.

Also ran the full containment-control suite (`python3 run_controls.py`, 23 controls including `check_adjudication_mutations.py`) after every round: `23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`.

## Escalations

`review-gate.sh prepare` routed one changed path (the plan under `launchpad/plans/`) to a `review-docs` reviewer that does not exist yet in this pipeline (only `review-a11y`, `review-adjudicate`, `review-code`, `review-final`, `review-plan`, `review-tests` are defined) — the gate failed closed on that, correctly, per its own design. Flagging rather than working around it.

Closes #1412

author: obukhovaa
body:
Implements the `scoped-context-files` OpenSpec change ([GENAI-285](https://tinypass.atlassian.net/browse/GENAI-285)): workspace context becomes a function of *who is running and what they are running*, and nested context files become discoverable without paying for them upfront.

## What's in here

**1. Scoped context resolution** (`internal/contextfile`, new leaf package)
- Agents (`.opencode.json` / markdown frontmatter) and flow steps declare `context: { paths, mode, nested }`; precedence `step > agent > global` with compositional `replace`/`append` semantics; unknown mode WARNs (naming the agent/step) and fails safe to `append`.
- Shell-free templating in path entries — `${agent}`, `${flow.id}`, `${flow.step}`, `${env.VAR}` — with symlink-resolved workDir containment; escaping entries are rejected.
- Keyed memoization (`sync.Map` + `singleflight`) replaces the process-global `sync.Once`; resolved blocks are byte-stable per session.
- The flow-step `context` field is inheritable via `include`/`extends` with zero merge-code changes (reflection-driven), and `${flow.id}`/`${flow.step}` are threaded explicitly from `runStep` through `NewAgent` (agent construction is context-free).

**2. Progressive disclosure of nested context files**
- One bounded walk per process per workDir discovers context files strictly below root (hardcoded skip set + configured data dir; caps on depth/files). Only a compact, cache-stable **manifest** goes into the system prompt; labels are extracted once at discovery time.
- A file's body is injected as a `<system-reminder>` appended to the first successful tool result touching its owning directory (triggers: read/write/edit/multiedit/patch/grep/glob/ls; not bash, not delete). Outermost-first layering, once per session, per-session byte budget, subagent sessions isolated.
- The system prompt is **never** mutated between turns — the Anthropic single-block `cache_control` prefix stays intact (the load-bearing constraint of the whole design).

**3. Hardening** (from the adversarial review rounds)
- Discovery rejects non-regular files and symlink escapes; activation reads go through kernel-enforced beneath-only resolution (`os.Root`, Go 1.25) with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, fstat-on-fd size checks, and `io.LimitReader` — a repo-committed symlink to `~/.ssh/id_rsa` (or `/dev/zero`, or a FIFO) can neither leak, OOM, nor hang, even under a check/open race (PoC-verified).
- Injected bodies are sanitized so a repo file cannot forge `</system-reminder>` framing.
- Case folding in owner matching is applied only on genuinely case-insensitive filesystems (probed per workDir via `os.SameFile`) — no cross-matching of case-differing sibling dirs on Linux.
- Files already inlined by an agent's scoped layers are subtracted from that agent's manifest and injection set.

## Backward compatibility

With no `context` config and no nested files on disk the assembled prompt is **byte-identical** to the pre-feature build — pinned by unit tests and the e2e A/B check (including the `# From:` header quirks).

## Config surface

- `agents.<name>.context` (also markdown frontmatter) and per-flow-step `context`
- Top-level `contextDiscovery { enabled, maxFiles, maxDepth, maxFileBytes, maxSessionBytes }` (default on; opt out per agent/step with `context.nested: false`)
- `opencode-schema.json` regenerated; viper round-trip test for the case-folding hazard per CLAUDE.md.

## Tests

- `make test` green (fmt + race + coverage). Unit coverage across resolver/templating/discovery/manifest/wrapper/flow-inheritance, including mutation-verified seam tests for the factory→provider prompt threading.
- New e2e `scripts/test/scoped_context.sh` + hermetic `cmd/context-e2e` driver (isolated mktemp sandbox config, HOME/XDG overridden): byte-identical backward-compat A/B across processes, manifest rendering, first-touch injection, second-touch dedup, and the agent-level `mode: replace` override that motivated the change — 15/15 checks.
- `make test-e2e`: all scripts pass except 3 live-model failures (attachments, deferred_tools_native, grep) reproduced byte-for-byte on base `6d8f8c7` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## OpenSpec

Enables `typescript/no-floating-promises` (dropping the `"off"` override) and fixes the 8 violations it surfaced.

## Changes

- `src/db.ts`: `close()` now awaits `ownClient.end()` instead of firing it and returning. Awaiting is the correct behaviour here — callers that `await db.close()` now actually get a closed connection.
- `src/migration.ts`: the callback-style migration action inside `new Promise` is marked `void`. The `MigrationAction` union allows a promise-returning signature, but in the `action.length === 2` branch the callback form is the one being invoked and `resolve` is the completion signal, so its (never-returned) promise is intentionally ignored.
- `test/db.spec.ts`: the two `afterEach` hooks are async and await `db.close()`.
- `test/migration.spec.ts`: `void migration.apply(direction)` inside the `expect(...).toThrow()` callback — the test asserts the synchronous throw from `_getAction`, so the promise is intentionally unused.
- `test/ts/customRunner*.ts`: `void start()` at the top level; `start()` already sets `process.exitCode` and calls `process.exit` itself.

Also removes the now-stale `explicit-function-return-type` override: that rule sits in the `restriction` category, which is `"off"` wholesale, so the explicit override (and its "37 violations, defer the cleanup" note) was redundant.

author: tomblakeasaah196
body:
## Summary

Completes Milestone 6. Two commits are the original build of the lifecycle, cancellation, trail and manifest; four are a senior review that finished the milestone's missing half and fixed nine defects. `docs/M6_REVIEW.md` is the written review, addressed to the engineer.

This supersedes #33, which contains the first two of these commits unchanged. Close #33 rather than merging it.

## What it delivers

**Order lifecycle** (`OrderLifecycle`)
- Pure transition map: pending, confirmed, packed, dispatched, delivered, with every illegal move refused in both directions and tested exhaustively.
- One transactional write per change: the status, the timestamp, the delivery schedule and an actor-attributed `order_status_history` row commit together, under a row lock, with an optimistic token so a stale form is refused rather than applied.
- Cancellation deliberately stays off the stage dropdown so the money rules cannot be walked around.

**Cancellation** (`OrderCancellation`)
- Reads the M5 `Cancellation` policy rather than reinventing it. Locks and rereads the order, refuses while a payment attempt is in flight, writes `order_cancellations`, appends history and releases the delivery slot in one transaction.
- Refunds are raised after the commit, never inside it, newest transaction first. Money paid outside Paystack is labelled as needing a person rather than counted as refunded.
- A paid cancellation needs both `orders.cancel` and `payments.refund`.
- **A dispatched order can be cancelled, with terms.** The deposit is kept whatever the clock says, because the produce is bought and the van has run. That is its own setting rather than a silent override of the cutoff rule, and a second setting closes the door entirely for anyone who would rather settle at the gate. Whoever cancels acknowledges the consequence, checked under the row lock rather than only in the form.
- Self service now stops once an order is packed. A pay-on-delivery order can be unpaid and already at the customer's gate, and that combination previously let a customer cancel produce that had left the building.

**Notifications** (`Notifications`)
- The half of M6 that `docs/M6_GUIDE.md` Section 1 moves out of M9, and that had not been started. Before this, an order could go from placed to delivered without the customer hearing anything, and the Order Trail had no route to it at all.
- One dispatcher, two channels (email and in the app), a `notifications` row per send and a `notification_deliveries` row per recipient and channel. A failed send is caught and recorded with its error, never thrown at the caller.
- Every order stage, every cancellation with its money outcome stated plainly, and M5's four orphaned payment events (verified charge, deposit, staff-recorded payment, refund sent, refund failed) now announce themselves from their controller after the commit.
- Template editor on the settings screen behind `settings.notifications.edit`, with the tokens each message accepts, a sandboxed preview of the real branded render, and an em dash refused at the API.
- **Send one to me** posts a real branded message through the real mail server to the signed-in person's own address, so a team can prove email works without placing an order. The address is read from the staff row and never from the request.

**Delivery manifest** (`DeliveryManifest`)
- Printable packing list for a chosen day, grouped by zone, with an optional single-zone view for a driver.
- Two queries for the whole day rather than two per order. A 60 order Saturday went from over 180 round trips to 2.
- Combos fanned out from their order-time snapshots, per-zone packing totals summed from exact quantities and rounded once.

**Public Order Trail** (`public/order.php`, `OrderTrail`)
- Opened by token link with no login, 404 on a bad token, five steps with timestamps.
- The sourcing line reads the snapshot taken at confirmation, and the live settings before then, so it is never blank at the moment a customer is most anxious.
- No money, no payment choice, no address, no staff note, no other order.

**Order 360** (`admin/orders.php`)
- Filterable list, and a detail view with items and their component breakdown, the M5 money ledger (expected, paid, refunded, net, outstanding), the address and zone, the full status history with who did what, links to the invoice, the receipt, the customer's trail and the delivery day, an internal staff note that can never surface on the public trail, and every message sent with a resend on a failed one.

## Defects fixed

1. **The customer filter had never worked.** The same named placeholder was used twice in one statement, which MySQL refuses on a native prepared statement, so every customer search threw `SQLSTATE[HY093]` and killed the screen.
2. **A refund webhook could never match on its reference.** Paystack sends `transaction` as an object; reading it as a string produced the literal `Array`. It bites exactly when the gateway id lookup misses, and the cost is a refund never marked processed and a customer never told.
3. **`clay` did not exist.** It was used by name in eleven places across M5 and M6 but was never in `tailwind.config.js`, so every attention state compiled to no colour at all.
4. **The trail showed no sourcing line until confirmation**, which is when a customer who has just paid is least reassured.
5. **The manifest ran two queries per order.**
6. **Zone totals summed values already rounded** to three places.
7. **`Cancellation::policyLine` had no caller outside its tests**, so the deposit rule was never shown at checkout.
8. **The manifest and Order 360 were dead ends**, with no links to each other or to the documents.
9. **The settings tests disabled customer features and never put them back.** Saving a tab writes every field on it and an unsubmitted checkbox saves as off, so a suite run against a real database left customer self service cancellation switched off. Both settings tests now derive their restore list from the tab definitions rather than a hand-typed list, so a setting added later is covered automatically.

## Migrations

- `018_delivery_order_trail.sql`: the source-region snapshot and the delivery schedule backfill.
- `019_m6_notifications.sql`: the seven templates that had no words, the `notifications.resend` permission, and the index the in-app inbox reads.
- `020_order_staff_note.sql`: `orders.staff_note`, deliberately not in `order_status_history` so a note can never appear as a step on the public trail.
- `021_cancellation_after_dispatch.sql`: the two settings governing a cancellation after dispatch.

All four are idempotent and MySQL 8 compatible, guarded against `information_schema` where they add a column or index.

## Verification

Stood up MySQL 8.0.46, a PHP server, a local SMTP sink and a stand-in Paystack. Every migration from `000` to `021` applied twice from an empty database.

- 1,416 unit assertions, 362 database assertions, 125 HTTP assertions, all green.
- `scripts/brand-check.sh` green, `php -l` clean, `scripts/verify.sh` green apart from four checks that need Apache to read `.htaccess`.
- One order taken end to end: placed, confirmed, packed, dispatched, delivered, with seven branded emails sent and the matching in-app rows written.
- The refund path proved end to end against `scripts/tests/fake/paystack.php`. `Paystack::base()` can be pointed at it by `PAYSTACK_BASE_URL`, and the override is ignored unless the secret key is a test key, so an environment holding `sk_live_` always talks to the real Paystack.

## Not proved

- Paystack itself answering. That needs a test key on staging.
- Real deliverability, SPF and DKIM. **Send one to me** on the Notifications settings tab closes this in one click on staging.
- Nothing was printed on paper; the print rules were read off the rendered page.

author: ghislandry
body:
v0.1.0+38 predates commit signing, the NDUZEM_GIT_COMMIT define and the clean-tree check, so its commit-to-binary link is inferred from build timestamps rather than carried by the artefact. Left unsigned rather than recreated: signing it would attest the strongest-looking part of a chain whose weakest link is that inference, and deleting a published tag to improve appearances is what the immutability rule exists to prevent.

States the boundary instead, and what v0.1.0+39 onward guarantees.

author: paolocarrasco
body:
## Resumen

El issue #41 (mistorias/mistorias-gestion-de-producto) pedía que toda la tarjeta de historia navegue a la historia, no solo un enlace suelto. En la práctica solo el enlace "Leer la historia" del final era clicable — la imagen, el título y el resumen no navegaban — y el brillo de hover tampoco se veía en móvil.

La hipótesis inicial apuntaba a los enlaces de tema (`ListaTemas.astro`) como causa. Se descartó: `.temas__ficha` ya tiene el `position: relative; z-index: 1` correcto para quedar por encima de un enlace estirado, y las reglas de pintado CSS confirman que ese tratamiento no era el problema.

**Causa real:** en `TarjetaHistoria.astro`, `.tarjeta__enlace` (el `<a>` "Leer la historia") tenía `position: relative`. Eso lo convertía en el *containing block* de su propio `::after`, en vez de `.tarjeta` (el `<article>` contenedor). El `::after` — que debía estirarse con `inset: 0` sobre toda la tarjeta — quedaba confinado al pequeño `<a>` del final. Por eso solo ese enlace respondía al clic.

## Cambios

Un solo archivo: `src/components/TarjetaHistoria.astro`.

1. **Fix de raíz:** se quita `position: relative` de `.tarjeta__enlace`. Ahora el `::after` resuelve su containing block contra `.tarjeta`, tal como ya describían el comentario existente y el ADR 0015. No se toca `ListaTemas.astro`.
2. **Brillo en móvil:** se agrega `.tarjeta:active` bajo `@media (hover: none)` (mismo `box-shadow` que las reglas de hover/focus existentes), ya que ambas estaban dentro de `@media (hover: hover)` y no se veían en touch. El sitio no envía JavaScript (`script-src 'none'`), así que es un mejor esfuerzo con CSS puro — documentado en el código que iOS Safari puede no disparar `:active` en un tap corto sin un listener táctil en JS.

## Plan de pruebas

- `pnpm test --coverage`: 231 tests pasan.
- `pnpm build`: completa sin errores.
- Verificación manual en navegador (Playwright, no solo unit tests):
  - Clic en imagen, título y resumen de una tarjeta navega a la historia.
  - El brillo de hover traza el contorno completo de la tarjeta.
  - El contorno de foco por teclado (Tab) ahora envuelve toda la tarjeta, no solo el texto del enlace.
  - Las fichas de tema siguen siendo clicables de forma independiente (navegan a `/temas/[tema]`, no a la historia).
  - Forzando el pseudo-estado `:active` vía CDP bajo `(hover: none)` (emulación móvil), el brillo aparece correctamente.
