author: pachaninm-lab
body:
**PASS 127 → 128, FAIL 92 → 91.** V16.5.4 закрыт. Файлы не пересекаются с #4978, #4980, #4982.

## Два процесса держались по разным меркам

`outbox-worker.ts` и `marketing-outbox-worker.ts` ставят `uncaughtException` и `unhandledRejection`, логируют и завершаются осознанно. `main.ts` не ставил **ни того, ни другого**, и глобального фильтра исключений не регистрировал.

Умолчание фреймворка, зачтённое под V16.5.3, — **другой контроль**, и оно остаётся зачтённым: оно ловит исключение **внутри** запроса. Последний рубеж нужен для того, что брошено **вне** запроса — в таймере, в слушателе события, в фоновом промисе, где никто не смотрит.

## Замерено, а не взято из документации

Node v22.22.2, живой `setInterval`, держащий цикл событий занятым:

```
$ node -e 'setInterval(()=>{},1000); Promise.reject(new Error("boom"))'
unhandledRejection exit=1

$ node -e 'setInterval(()=>{},1000); setTimeout(()=>{throw new Error("boom2")},10)'
uncaughtException exit=1
```

Значит прежнее поведение — **не** «Node продолжает работать». Это жёсткая остановка **в обход всех путей завершения**: пул Prisma не закрывался, HTTP-сервер не сливал соединения, OpenTelemetry не отправляла накопленное, запросы в полёте оставались без ответа.

Поэтому заявляется ровно то, что изменилось, и не больше: **меняется форма остановки, а не факт остановки.**

## Что именно делает обработчик

- **причина пишется в stderr со стеком, и запись ожидается.** `console.error` в pipe асинхронен: процесс, выходящий в том же тике, теряет ровно то сообщение, которое объясняет, почему он вышел, — а это и есть отказ, ради предотвращения которого требование существует;
- **приложение закрывается**, чтобы отработали shutdown hooks и слились соединения;
- **процесс всё равно выходит ненулевым кодом.** Обработчик, который залогировал и продолжил обслуживать трафик, **хуже падения, которое он заменил**: он оставляет открытым приложение, чьи инварианты уже нарушены. Это направление проверяется тестом, а не ревью;
- **закрытие ограничено таймаутом**, и код выхода выставляется **до** `close()` — падение или зависание `close()` не должно превращать фатальную ошибку в успешно выглядящий выход.

**Сигналы намеренно не перехватываются.** `app.enableShutdownHooks()` уже владеет SIGTERM и SIGINT для API; воркеры ставят свои только потому, что запускают application context без HTTP-сервера, которому эти сигналы принадлежали бы. Второй обработчик того же сигнала запустил бы два завершения. Мутация, добавляющая дубль SIGTERM, ловится.

`once`, а не `on`: вторая фатальная ошибка во время обработки первой уходит поведению Node по умолчанию, и это правильный исход. Обработчик, зацикливающийся на собственном отказе, — нет.

## Проверено, а не заявлено

**Восемь мутаций обработчика, все восемь пойманы:**

| мутация | падений |
|---|---|
| проглотить фатальную ошибку: залогировать, закрыть, но не выйти | 3 |
| перестать выставлять ненулевой код выхода | 3 |
| перестать сообщать причину | 3 |
| убрать защиту от повторного входа | 1 |
| сделать таймаут закрытия фактически бесконечным | 1 |
| покрыть только `uncaughtException`, оставив `unhandledRejection` | 4 |
| `on()` вместо `once()` | 1 |
| забрать себе ещё и SIGTERM | 1 |

## Одна мутация НЕ была поймана матрицей — записано, а не исправлено молча

Удаление `forceExit` после завершения **оставило V16.5.4 на PASS**: условие искало литерал `forceExit(1)`, который есть и в ветке таймаута, поэтому удаление другой строки его не отменяло.

**Неверна была не мутация, а условие.** Выход после завершённого shutdown теперь использует именованную `FATAL_EXIT_CODE`, и условие закреплено на ней. Повтор той же мутации после исправления:

```
### re-run: remove the post-shutdown exit, with the condition repinned
    V16.5.4 -> NOT_ASSESSED   91 FAIL  88 NOT_APPLICABLE  39 NOT_ASSESSED  127 PASS
### restored
    V16.5.4 -> PASS           91 FAIL  88 NOT_APPLICABLE  38 NOT_ASSESSED  128 PASS
```

Условие, мимо которого мутация может пройти, — не условие.

## PASS отзываем машинно

| мутация дерева | V16.5.4 | итоги |
|---|---|---|
| `main.ts` перестаёт ставить обработчики | NOT_ASSESSED | 127 / 92 / 88 / 39 |
| убрать выход после завершения | NOT_ASSESSED | 127 / 92 / 88 / 39 |
| убрать тест «процесс всё равно выходит ненулевым» | NOT_ASSESSED | 127 / 92 / 88 / 39 |

Одно из условий отдельно требует, чтобы **воркеры сохранили свои обработчики**: это не «покрыли один процесс за счёт другого».

Обратная сторона проверена: без фатального события ничего не происходит — приложение не закрывается, в stderr не пишется, код выхода не трогается.

## Гейты локально

- `pnpm --filter @pc/api typecheck` — exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @pc/api test` — exit 0, **2433 passed**, 0 failed
- `node --test scripts/security/*.test.mjs` — exit 0, 130/130
- `p7-autopilot-guard.sh` — **exit 0** (на закоммиченном состоянии)
- `verify-pc-crop-project-lock.mjs` — **exit 0**

## Что НЕ закрыто

- **V16.5.3 остаётся PASS** и этим проходом не трогается: оно про отказ внутри запроса.
- **V16.1.1, V16.2.3, V16.3.3** остаются FAIL — все три про один отсутствующий документ с набором событий безопасности.
- **V16.4.3** остаётся FAIL: коллектор шлёт в Loki по plaintext http.
- Глобальный фильтр исключений Nest **не добавлен**: он покрывает то же, что уже зачтено под V16.5.3, и добавлять его ради совпадения со словом в условии было бы подгонкой под гейт.

Зависимостей не добавлено, схема БД не менялась, миграций нет, маршруты и политики не трогались. Production / REG.RU / DNS / БД / креденшелы не мутировались. Новые обязательные расходы: 0 ₽.

Refs #4459

author: adamcrofts2-max
body:
`npm test` had been failing on `main`: 4 visible failures and a hard crash partway through, so **only 94 of 408 assertions ever ran**. Everything after the crash — roughly three quarters of the suite, including Phases 123 and 124's new coverage — silently never executed.

**Result: 408 passing, 0 failing, exit 0** (was 94 passing, 4 failing, crash).

Four independent root causes. One of them is a live production bug.

---

## 1. PDF export was broken for every user

**Not a test problem.** `pdf/fonts.ts`'s `loadThemeFonts` embeds every custom cover font on **every** export, whether the book uses it or not — and `@pdf-lib/fontkit` throws `RangeError: Trying to access beyond buffer length` from `TTFGlyph._getCBox` on **Bebas Neue**. So `exportBookToPdf` threw before producing a single page, for every book, regardless of which fonts it used.

Diagnosed rather than guessed:

- **The file is not corrupt.** Its `loca` table matches `head.indexToLocFormat` (short/2-byte) and `maxp.numGlyphs` (497); every table lies inside the file; no glyph offset runs past `glyf`.
- **A freshly downloaded copy from Google Fonts crashes identically**, so re-downloading cannot fix it. This is a fontkit defect on this typeface.
- **The failure surfaces at `doc.save()`, not `embedFont`**, so it cannot be caught per-font at load time — a `try`/`catch` around the embed was tried first and did not work.

**Fix:** `'bebas-neue'` no longer embeds; it resolves to **Anton**, the closest working condensed display sans. Two supporting changes so this is coherent rather than a silent substitution:

- `coverTypography.ts` maps the same id to Anton **on screen too** — showing Bebas on screen and Anton in the PDF would break the true-WYSIWYG guarantee this app treats as non-negotiable.
- Removed from both cover-font pickers so nobody new selects it. **The id is kept** in `CustomCoverFontId`, so a project already saved with it still loads and simply renders in Anton — the codebase's standing "default in code, never migrate persisted data" convention.

`embedOrFallback` also makes an embed-time font failure non-fatal (logged, falls back to a standard face). It doesn't fix Bebas, whose failure is deferred to save — but it stops this *class* of failure from ever taking down a whole export again.

## 2. `runReview` is deferred a tick; the tests asserted synchronously

`virtualEditorStore.runReview` wraps `runPipeline` in `window.setTimeout(…, 0)` so the "Reviewing…" state paints before the synchronous pipeline blocks the main thread. Correct and deliberate — but the tests read the report immediately, found none, then dereferenced it at `smoke-test.ts:621`, killing the run. **This was the crash that hid ~310 assertions.**

Fixed test-side with a `flushReview()` helper awaited after each of the six `runReview` calls. The production deferral is untouched.

## 3. The spell-check dictionary URL was root-relative

`spellcheckDictionary.ts` fetched `/dictionaries/en-gb/index.aff`. Node rejects a root-relative URL (`ERR_INVALID_URL` — no origin to resolve against), so the dictionary never loaded and every spelling-dependent checker silently reported "not analysed".

Now resolved against `document.baseURI`. **Also a real production fix:** a root-relative path breaks the moment the app is served from a sub-path, such as a preview deployment under a prefix. The loader's fail-closed behaviour is preserved.

The harness shim was widened to match — it served only `/fonts/` from `public/`, and now serves anything under `public/`. **The spell-checker is genuinely exercised by the suite for the first time.**

## 4. A stale assertion nobody could see failing

The overall-score test averaged a hardcoded list of four categories. Four more (`developmental`, `typography`, `accessibility`, `commercial`) had checkers registered afterwards, so it went stale and started failing — unnoticed, because the suite was already red further down. It now derives the analysed set from the report itself, so it can't go stale again, with a separate assertion pinning the four long-standing categories.

---

## Verification

- `npm test` — **408 passing, 0 failing, exit 0**
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run lint` — exits 0, **49 warnings before and after**
- The 24 assertions added in Phases 123–124 now actually execute for the first time

## Recommended next

**Phase J's CI pipeline.** This suite was broken across multiple phases without anyone noticing. A GitHub Actions workflow running build/lint/test on every push would have caught it on the commit that introduced it — and would have caught the PDF export regression immediately, since the export integration test was one of the four visible failures the whole time.

author: mphinance
body:
Two changes to the fund data layer. Together because both touch `CLAUDE.md` and the lockstep provider tables.

## 1. Eighteen new funds — 71 → 89, across 12 providers

**Capital Group** is a new provider: CGDV, CGGR, CGGO, CGUS, CGXU. ~$95B of genuinely discretionary multi-manager active equity — the largest uncovered family of that kind. Their holdings page renders client-side with nothing in the HTML, but the Download button hits a plain unauthenticated REST endpoint returning XLSX, so **no headless browser needed**:

```
GET /api/investments/investment-service/v1/etfs/{TICKER}/download/daily-holdings
```

Adds `openpyxl`. It wasn't a dependency anywhere before, and the Vultr one-off Docker command in `CLAUDE.md` hand-listed its packages — that now installs from `requirements.txt` so it can't silently drift again.

**Avantis 3 → 10.** Pure `FUNDS` entries; the existing id-based fetcher already handles them. Ids were recovered from each product page and verified by re-deriving the three known mappings as a control.

The reason this beats its AUM: **AVEM/AVDE/AVDV/AVIV hold emerging-market and developed-international companies, and every ticker in the product until now was a US name.** Every other candidate writes over names already tracked. This actually extends the universe.

**YieldMax 8 → 14.** Same URL pattern, also pure data — but they are not equivalent and the PR shouldn't pretend they are:

| Fund | What's inside | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| CHPY | Micron, NXP, ASML + calls written per name | Real stock picking |
| YMAX | Other YieldMax funds | Allocation across the complex |
| AMDY / AMZY / GOOY / GDXY | T-bills + a few calls on one underlying | None — widens the effectiveness surface only |

YMAG skipped deliberately: the Mag7 by definition, nothing is decided.

**Not added — JEPI/JEPQ ($86B).** They *are* actively managed, contrary to the common belief that they're index funds. But their option exposure is in bank-issued ELNs rather than listed contracts, so the options analysis has nothing to parse, and the equity sleeve is built for low beta rather than conviction. Since `convictionScore` multiplies by AUM, they'd drown genuine small-fund conviction under a mechanical mega-fund reweight. Dimensional skipped on the same reasoning.

Every new ticker is mapped in `FUND_PROVIDERS` **and** `FUND_AUM` in both `api/data.py` and `lib/providers.ts`. Verified all six new YieldMax funds resolve to `option-income` and Avantis/Capital Group to `active-equity` — an unmapped ticker defaults to `active-equity` and would put collateral churn straight into the stock-picking signal pool.

## 2. `holdings.ts`: 1,172 → 425 lines

The file is `@deprecated` and `api/data.py` is the declared source of truth, but it carried a full parallel implementation of the cross-fund signal math with **zero call sites** — the whole app imports only `getLatestHoldings`, `getDailyDiff`, `getLatestHoldingsDate`, `FUND_AUM`, `PROVIDER_ORDER`.

That dead code had already diverged from the Python it claimed to mirror: `getInstitutionalSignals` never excluded option-income funds (`api/data.py:396` documents a real incident where EGGQ/EGGY collateral churn surfaced as the #2 institutional sell signal), and its AUM fallback was `?? 0.1` against Python's `0.01`/`0.0`.

Neither was a live bug, because nothing called it — **which is exactly the hazard.** It reads as authoritative and is wrong; it generated two false-positive bug reports before being understood.

The entire active-weight chain is kept — `/holdings` needs it for the Δ Weight column and it must stay in lockstep with `api/data.py`. `CLAUDE.md`'s now-false claim about those aggregates is rewritten; the "don't simplify back to raw `weightDelta`" warning is preserved.

## Also

Untracks `scraper.log` — in `.gitignore` since May but never removed from the index, so the rule never applied and 73 commits of churn landed anyway. A perpetually dirty tree is what makes `sync_data.sh` bail on the Vultr box.

## Known issue, deliberately not fixed here

**`FUND_AUM` is stale by up to 14×** — AVLV declared at $3.2B against $21.6B of actual holdings on 2026-09-03 — and it feeds `convictionScore` directly. The holdings CSVs already carry the true value per row, so it should be derived rather than hand-maintained. That changes what the product ranks, so it belongs in its own change.

## Verification

187 tests pass · `tsc` clean · `next build` clean · all 18 funds fetch real holdings (AVEM 4,010 rows, AVDE 3,331, CHPY 88).

body:
Adds a session list/switcher panel to the web solo stopwatch page.

## What's in this PR

### `SoloSessionSwitcher.tsx` (new component)
- Modal panel listing all local solo sessions (newest-first)
- **Create**: "+ New session" button with name prompt; switches to the new session on create
- **Rename**: inline edit triggered by pencil icon; Enter to save, Escape to cancel
- **Delete**: trash icon → inline confirmation ("Delete? Yes / No"); red destructive styling per design system
- **Switch**: clicking any session row activates it and closes the panel
- **Session cap** (10): once reached, shows a clear message instead of the create button; cap enforced by `soloSessionStorage.ts` storage layer
- Running/paused/idle status indicator on each row (RUNNING shown in red per AGENTS.md)
- Keyboard: Escape closes the panel; all interactive elements have `:focus-visible` with 2px blue-primary outline
- Backdrop click closes the panel

### `page.tsx` changes
- Session name + chevron in the masthead header → clicking opens the panel
- `handleSwitchSession` callback: saves current session state (with fresh wall-clock anchor if running), switches active session pointer in storage, restores incoming session's stopwatch state (same drift-free wall-clock restore pattern as the page-refresh logic)
- `CountdownTimer` keyed on `currentSessionId` → forced remount on switch, so the timer correctly re-reads its state from the newly active session
- Countdown cancelled, pending stop dismissed on session switch

### `help/page.tsx` update
- Documents the multi-session UI for the stopwatch surface (create/rename/delete/switch, cap, storage scope)

## Design
- Uses only existing `globals.css` tokens (`race-*`) — no new hex values
- Blue-primary (`#0B6FB3`) for interactive/active elements; red (`#CC1A22`) for destructive delete only
- Light-blue accent instrument-surface language preserved on the dial

## Verification
`pnpm --filter web build` ✅ (TypeScript clean, no new errors)

## E2E coverage
Full Playwright E2E coverage tracked in #368 (the dedicated multi-session E2E issue).

Closes #367

body:
Second of two PRs for #1010, stacked on #1019 (which declares the callee-side contract and changes no behaviour). **This is the one that narrows.** Merge #1019 first; GitHub will retarget this to `main`.

`secrets: inherit` → the four names `build-image.yaml` actually references. Ten secrets stop being passed, including `KUBECONFIG`, `ARGOCD_TOKEN` and `HCLOUD_TOKEN` — cluster and infrastructure credentials that were in the environment of a job that checks out and builds *someone else's* repository by design.

## Verified before merge, not after

A missing name here does not fail loudly: `build-image` falls through to a weaker credential tier and logs which one it used, so the failure surfaces later as a registry 403 or a broken package install. A green run proves nothing by itself.

`release-deploy` is `workflow_dispatch`-only, so this branch was dispatched **directly, before merging**, re-using the image tag each component already carried. The bump job then reports `already at <tag> (no diff)` and commits nothing, while the build job still runs end to end.

| run | target | result |
|---|---|---|
| [33817965997](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/actions/runs/33817965997) | `labs/mctl-telegram-preview` @ `main-b1983ba` | ✅ |
| [33818254152](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/actions/runs/33818254152) | `admins/mctl-docs` @ `0.1.38` | ✅ |
| [33818385218](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/actions/runs/33818385218) | `labs/mctl-academy` @ `0.1.50` | ✅ |

All three logged the same tier lines as the pre-change baseline (last release before this branch, run at 2026-09-03T23:04) — i.e. no silent degradation:

```
🤖 Using GitHub App token for checkout     ← APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY arrived
🔐 Using GHCR_PAT for GHCR push            ← GHCR_PAT arrived
```

and all three bumped nothing:

```
platform-gitops/services/labs/mctl-academy/values.yaml: already at 0.1.50 (no diff)
##[notice]No tag change (already at 0.1.50)
```

### `GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` needed a specific target

The three repos on that allow-list are not interchangeable. Checking their Dockerfiles, **only `mctl-academy` consumes the build secret** — `mctl-web` and `mctl-docs` never reference `github_token` at all, so a canary against either would have been green whether or not the secret was passed.

The `mctl-academy` run proves it properly. Layer #16 executed (not `CACHED`):

```
#16 [builder 6/9] RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token  GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/github_token ...)"  sh -c 'cd client && bun install --frozen-lockfile'
```

and `client/.npmrc` binds the `@mctlhq` scope to GitHub Packages via `${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}`, with `@mctlhq/ui` among the client's dependencies. A private-scope install cannot succeed on an empty token, so the secret demonstrably arrived.

## Noted while here, not fixed

- The `GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` allow-list at `build-image.yaml:243` names `mctl-web` and `mctl-docs`, neither of which consumes the secret. Harmless, but it is two more repos than the build-arg needs.
- `GHCR_PAT` is written to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` at `build-image.yaml:204` with no `::add-mask::` (only the Vault PAT gets one, `:141`). Pre-existing and out of scope for #1010.

Closes #1010

author: danvratil
body: There was no way to paste or insert an image into a draft. The `InlineImage` model and `multipart/related` export already existed. ## Change - Paste image files (screenshots, clipboard files) in the compose dialog onto the draft as `InlineImage`s - **Insert image** picker (`accept` limited to PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP; SVG is rejected) - Images show in the existing attachment list (labeled `image`) and can be removed - On send, the plain body is wrapped with `cid:` `` tags so export emits `multipart/related` - Regular **Attach** is unchanged (file attachments, any type) - No remote URL fetch from HTML clipboard (privacy) Closes #20 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds inline image support to the compose dialog: paste screenshots or clipboard images directly into a draft, or pick them via a new Insert image button. Images are stored as `InlineImage`s, shown in the attachment list, and sent as `cid:` parts in `multipart/related`; regular Attach is unchanged. Closes #20. **Behavior** - Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, and BMP are accepted; SVG is rejected, and an explicit unsafe MIME type wins over a safe-looking filename. - Files that would exceed the draft limit are rejected before being buffered in memory. - Images can be removed from the draft like file attachments. - On send, the plain body is wrapped with `` tags so the export emits `multipart/related`. - Remote URLs from HTML clipboard content are never fetched. Written for commit 57912829d40ebdce1b7712b299b74c075c2a9b56. Summary will update on new commits.

author: atom-oh
body:
Closes four gap-audit i18n items (docs/v1-gap-audit-2026-07-19.md) — 3 remain after this (L124/L129 inventory-home, L168 vpc TGW, L228/L229 k8s-eks → 4 lines, some multi-part).

## Why four items in one batch
They share ONE mechanism and were mostly already solved: cloudfront (L186), dynamodb (L207), and waf (L254) all render through the generic `/inventory/[type]` page, and v2's `tt()` translation (SUPPORTED_LANGS ko/en/zh/ja — one MORE language than v1's 3) already covers the Korean strings the audit flagged ('총 N', '검색…', '전체 해제', '로딩 중…'). The items predate the tt() rollout — this batch VERIFIES that and closes the residue.

## What actually changed
- **17 unregistered Korean literals** on the datasources surfaces (DatasourceForm, DatasourcesTab, CardDashboard, ExplorePanel — L206) registered in en/zh/ja.
- **The composed donut title** `'<label> 분포'` (+ optional `' (표본 기준)'`) had no RULE — donut titles now translate instead of passing through Korean-mixed.
- **Lockstep guard** `web/lib/i18n-coverage.test.ts`: extracts every Korean `tt('…')` literal on exactly these surfaces and asserts each resolves in en/zh/ja (`applyTerms` passthrough = named failure); scan-size sanity guards prevent an empty-glob false pass.
- **Disclosed deviations** (in the ticks): spec/column labels deliberately stay English (the repo's technical-identifier convention); the guard scopes these four surfaces.
- Drive-bys: the batch-39 locale guides now name each locale's RENDERED sample qualifier (en 'sampled' / zh（基于样本）/ ja（サンプル基準）— PR #287 round-3 chair note), and the audit's L110 tick gains the batch-39 `view=agg` correction pointer.

## Gates
npm test (2605, incl. the new coverage guard) · tsc non-test clean · next build · pytest scripts/v2/{workers,steampipe} (1348).

author: bobrenjc93
body:
## What changed

Generalize the guarded native torch.compile backend="eager", fullgraph=True frontend from one exact native CPU float32 Tensor input to two positional Tensor inputs. Support straight-line neg/abs/add graphs where binary add exercises real PyTorch-compatible broadcasting (including matrix+vector and tensor-scalar cases), key the bounded cache on metadata for every input, and preserve import-time Tensor method guards, recompile_limit/reset/concurrency behavior, and fail-closed rejection without eager or installed-PyTorch forwarding. Extend the versioned PyTorch 2.13 differential corpus with broadcasting-category and held-out cases that verify values, shape, stride, dtype, device, requires_grad, unsupported forms, cache invalidation, and observable semantics. Run focused and full tests; keep claims narrow and do not add timing claims in this leaf.

Implemented two-input native `torch.compile(..., backend="eager", fullgraph=True)` support.

Changed:
- Generalized compile bytecode lowering and trace execution to one or two positional exact native CPU float32 Tensor inputs.
- Cache keys now include metadata for every input.
- Two-input `add` supports native PyTorch-style broadcasting, including matrix+vector and tensor-scalar cases.
- Preserved fail-closed behavior, Tensor method guards, recompile limits, reset behavior, and no PyTorch/eager forwarding.
- Extended the versioned compile corpus to `torch_compile_corpus_v3` with broadcasting and held-out cases.
- Updated public compile tests and supported-surface docs.

Checks passed:
- `.venv/bin/python -m py_compile ...`

author: tyu41275
body: Follow-up to #59 from the first production attempt. Google Chrome 152.0.7977.82 installed successfully, but its CLI emitted harmless trailing whitespace and the identity regex rejected it before exporting the executable path. This accepts trailing whitespace only; product identity, four-part version, explicit binary binding, version equality, and Chrome >=149 remain mandatory. Run 33818426682 is failed evidence and does not accept #11.
